column9: Tasty and filling, but not low calorie if eaten as a lunch
column10: This is a tasty sweet-ginger curry with chick peas and a few chunks of potato. The sweetness comes from the chick peas themselves, smartly brought out by the spices chosen.  The texture of the vegetables is surprisingly good - modestly firm, not an unrecognizable mush.  Unlike most prepackaged meals, I don't mind it cold, though it only takes two minutes in the microwave.Each package has 480 calories, which is rather incredible for just 10 ounces of Indian food with no ghee or paneer.  In fairness, it is high in fiber and protein and low in bad fats, so it is probably an ideal choice for skinny vegans/vegetarians.  But for those like me that eat plenty of dairy and meat but are trying to keep a few meals light but flavorful and filling, there are better options, particularly the Dal Bukara (340 calories) and Rajma Masala (270) by the same maker and several options from MTR or Tasty Bite.ETA: I understand it's technically 2.3 servings, but my original review was geared in terms of a quick office lunch, which is how I most often consume shelf-stable foods like this.  For me (tall male), 10 ounces of food is about what I expect for lunch.  So I still eat this, but usually as an addition to a family meal with a couple of other dishes and rice.  In that context, I full endorse the recommendation of other commenters to heat with a can of regular chickpeas (drained), ideally after sauteing a bit of garlic or onion.  The flavor spreads nicely, plus it's a bit healthier and cheaper that way.

column9: Very tasty, good quality, Too much salt
column10: I recently ordered a whole bunch of Kitchens of India 6-packs from amazon during a sale.  This is my first dish from this company so I cannot compare it to others yet.Pros:-Very nice combination of flavors, accurate texture similar to making it fresh-10oz serving for just over a buck-fifty, very reasonable for prepackaged food of any quality-No processed ingredients at all, a major plus-You will actually be able to tell what ingredients you're consuming (again, nice texture)-One packet (2.3 servings) on some rice makes a great meal at about 470 calories + rice-about 19 grams protein per package (2.3 servings), 10 grams fiber, 26 grams of fatCons:-about 1900mg sodium per package (2.3 servings)!!  This about ruins this dish for me, and I'm afraid of the other products that are still in the mail-Tastes far too salty (you will notice the 2 grams of salt in there!)Do not add salt to your rice when cooking, when this dish is diluted by the rice it is consumable.  It is very unfortunate they added so much salt, could not decide if 3 or 4 stars is appropriate (5 stars without the excess sodium).  Perhaps they did this for preservation.

column9: not for the faint of palate

column9: An Outstanding Curry But Comes at a Cost...
column10: I must say this is easily my favorite of the Kitchens of India [KoI], Ready to Eat curries that they offer.  The Pindi Chana, chick pea curry takes virtually no time to make.  Either empty the pouch into a pan and heat for 3 minutes; microwave the contents in a bowl (I prefer mine over rice), or just heat the package up in boiling water for about 3-5 minutes dig in without needing a container.  It is an easy, fast meal that tastes delicious!Speaking of taste, the Pindi Chana comes across as a flavorful curry that seems so simple yet can be very complex.  There is a mild ginger flavor to this curry that goes really well with the chick peas and potatoes inside.  The spices are perfectly balanced and do not overpower the flavor of the chick peas, while having a slight spicy after taste.  There is a lot going on with this curry but it comes together really well to produce an outstanding dish that is ready for you in less than 5 minutes!I would gladly give this curry 5 stars in a heart beat but what brings this curry down to 4 stars is actually the Salt and Fat content.  While this curry doesn't taste very salty at all(probably because I eat it over rice), it packs about 830mg per serving of salt and 10g of Fat.  10oz of this delicious curry will cost you over 20g of fat and almost 2 grams of salt; plus around 500 calories just for the entire packet alone (not including any sides).  Of course this delicious curry is worth it, but I personally portion the packet out usually into 2 servings.  For the price you get two fast meals that taste excellent.5 star quality taste, but overall 4 stars due to less than stellar nutritional value....* Nutritional Information ** (Entire packet)Each packet is 10oz (285g) and contains a little less than THREE Servings (~2.5 servings). It doesn't have that much saturated fat in comparison, but it is higher calorie, probably in part because it has a lot of protein (and fiber!) I've never ordered chick peas curry (or whatever you wish to call it) in a restaurant so I cannot compare, but this is a good. The pouch is super-convenient.

For Indians living abroad, it is easy to taste home cooked food by trying this product. It is good in taste and also suitable for maintaing health. Once any one will try it, he/she will become a regular user of this product. Kitchens Of India Ready To Eat Pindi Chana, Chick Pea Curry, 10-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)

Vegan. Natural. Kosher Pareve. Spicy. Tender chana [also known as chick peas or garbanzos] along with some pieces of aloo [potatoes] in a delightful & spicy vegetable gravy. Authentic flavor. Taste the 'kick' from real Indian green chilis. Let your adventurous taste buds travel to India without having to go there. Great with whole wheat pitas, organic basmati rice, or your favorite [Indian] bread.  Made with chick peas, potatoes, onions, sunflower oil, tomatoes, spices, green chilis, salt, ginger, garlic, pomegranate seed powder, and tea leaves extract. 525 calories and 20g protein per package. Product of India. Also really like Kitchens Of India Ready To Eat Rajma Masala, Red Kidney Bean Currry, 10-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6). This review is out there for those for whom this makes a difference. See all of my reviews and the vegancompassion Profile for more great choices. Check out "Vegan Grocery Favorites" and "Vegan Grocery Top Ten" & all the other helpful "Vegan Grocery" Listmania. Your input counts and will be greatly appreciated to benefit the search of others. Thank you.
Tastes pretty good. Spicier than the other packages they have, but I think that makes it tastier.
My family loves the Kitchens of India chick pea curry, butter chicken curry, mild chili pepper curry, and kidney bean curry!
I tried few from kitchens of india and this the best, I liked it a lot.  The quality and taste are very good.

I've had a bunch of these Indian food pouch things, and this is probably the best one I've had. The sodium is a little high, but all of these types of things are. Easy to take to work and reheat, and very very good.
A very good curry for times when you remember to set the rice cooker, but fail to get the rest of the meal ready.  Nothing needed but to heat up this packet.

While I often cook different types of curry from scratch, sometimes we need something quick and easy. These chickpeas became a favorite quick meal in our house. My husband and I will split it and pair it with some basmati or brown rice. Sometimes I even throw in some chicken short cuts that I have on hand. The sodium is high, but if you aren't regularly eating sodium laden foods then once in awhile shouldn't be that big of a deal. I don't think it is overpoweringly spicy, but then again my husband and I love spicy foods so it probably doesn't make me a good judge of the spice level. I think it does take an adventurous palette, as do many things, but I would recommend that it is at least worth a try. I think the price on Amazon is good too, ~$2.66 a box whereas in the grocery store I have paid $3.50-$3.99. Will be ordering from Amazon in the future!

This is a really nice product. Not too spicy, but with very good flavor. You can warm it up and eat it as it is, right out of the package, or pour it over rice or couscous and make more of a meal out of it. My son even liked it! (and that says a lot, LOL)
Really great-tasting....but oily.  Maybe that's what makes it so delicious, don't know.  If you love chick peas, this can be addictive.

column9: The Curry Tastes Okay, Everything quick, but...Nothing Special
column10: I am a single guy in his mid-20's and I buy Kitchens of India curry because it is a tremendously quick, easy dinner idea.  The taste of the curry is about on par with Chili con Carne from the can and is of relatively the same quality.  Nothing to give five stars over as for the price it is not even that good of a deal.  This item, in my opinion, is extremely over-hyped.  Don't get me wrong, not a bad food option, just not a five-star food product.

column9: Not half bad, and super convenient
column10: I recently tried the KoI Chick Pea Curry after being impressed with their Kitchens of India Paste for Butter Chicken Curry, 3.5-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6).  With the Butter Chicken, you have to add chicken and some other ingredients (i.e. water, butter), but with this Chickpea curry it's all inclusive in a pouch - simply squeeze the pasty contents of the pouch into a pan and heat up for a few minutes.  I served over couscous, not sure how authentic that is but it was pretty  good.The nutritional info says one pouch contains 2.5 servings but in my opinion it's only enough to feed one, and even then I'd want some rice or something with it.  It's high in sodium, but unfortunately so are most packaged foods.  I'm normally a big meat eater and even though this is a vegetarian dish I still found it substantial enough for a quick dinner.My only complaint is I'd say it is a little bit mushy, but overall it's not bad and for the convenience it's tough to beat.  Because it's so easy to prepare requiring no outside ingredients and with a shelf live of over 2 years, not only is this a good quick/convenient food option but stocking a few in the pantry in case of emergency (i.e. as part of hurricane preparedness stash depending on where you live) wouldn't be a bad idea as long as you have a way to heat it, like the Coleman PefectFlow 1-Burner Stove, although I'm sure you could eat it cold if necessary - and the pouch packaging is much smaller and lighter than canned food.

this is my injun favorite, rich  and authentic taste, just heat in foil pack and mix with rice naturally! Makes a dull meal into something a little special, chick peas are a nice complimentary protien to the rice and the meat or fish main course... Hmmm talking about Indian food is making me hungry LOL

column9: they emptied out the salt mine into this
column10: One word: SPICY. If you don't love spicy food, don't even have a taste of this. Why? Because it tastes damn good and you will want to eat the whole pouch and then your mouth will be on fire (and in the future your brain will remember "tasty" over "spicy" and you will make this same mistake a second time). The packet says 2.5 servings, but who are they kidding? (I guess if you're cooking for two adults and one child.) The only reason they say that is because the entire pouch *exceeds* the USDA's upper limit for sodium. Ouch. Honestly, I don't even remember it tasting overly salty. At least it's vegan.

column9: Add rice for a tasty meal.
column10: I heat this up and dump it on rice. Makes for a quick, easy, and substantial meal. Nicely spiced. Long shelf life is a plus.

I'd say this is their best "ready-to-eat" meal selection.  The chick peas are very hearty, the spice is a tiny bit above average.  It's best served with something like rice/naan.  I'll definitely be ordering this one again soon.
delicious blend of spices and sweetness... this makes a full meal along with a bit of your favorite bread or rice... 5 stars

I'm not sure how they do it, but this manages to taste fresh--definitely doesn't taste like it came out of a foil pouch! I'm not easily pleased with prepared foods, so I find this dish remarkable. I love the spicy kick too. Try it!

column9: Just had this for lunch - FANTASTIC!
column10: I purchased my Kitchens of India "Pindi Chana" from a local supermarket.  I have been buying this at $3.99 a pouch locally and decided on a whim to check if Amazon carried this.  I am elated that this is available, Prime shipping eligible, and in multi-packs.I have been eating this for years.  I just finished my Pindi Chana for my lunch and it was FANTASTIC.  I must say that if you do not like Spicy foods and if you do not like SPICY HOT foods, then you will not like this meal.  I, however, LOVE spicy and spicy hot meals and this is seasoned perfectly for me.I absolutely love Indian Cuisine with my favorite being Punjabi style.  This is really excellent for a pre-packed meal and tastes like my favorite fine Indian restaurant.If you are one who likes well spiced foods but not spicy hot, I would steer you to Kitchens of India's Red Bean Curry as it is spiced nicely but no heat.This is definitely a vegetarian dish but this meal is not always vegan as it is sometimes made with ghee instead of the sunflower oil.  In my local Indian restaurant, this is vegetarian not vegan.

I combine one package of the KOI pindi chana with my own pre-cooked chickpeas (about one 16 oz can's worth) and then split it into two healthy meals, which reduces sodium intake.  Every couple of months, amazon.com sells it at discount - fabulous deal! Each 6-pak comes to about $8 with the discount code and Subscribe & Save... it's a terrific savings! :-)

This curry is nice and spicy - really a convenient tasty meal on it's own, or (slightly less convenient) combined with some rice.  Packaging is a bit inconvenient for stacking in the pantry, but it wouldn't stop me from buying more.  The consistency of the potatoes, chick peas, etc is pretty good (not real mushy).  Also the ingredients are vegan, although the package does say processed in a facility that also processes milk.

column9: Great Tasting and Fairly Spicy - Highly Recommended
column10: "Pindi Chana, Chick Pea Curry" was one of the meals included in Kitchens of India  Ready to Eat Dinner Variety Pack, 10 Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6). I very much enjoyed this dish, found it to be authentic tasting and fairly spicy.The packet makes about 2 servings for my family. This makes an excellent main course or side dish for an Indian themed dinner and makes for an enjoyable snack as well.It should be stirred very well before serving since the oils do have the tenancy to separate.Recommended!CFH

I'm in love. This stuff is quite spicy (even for an admitted hot food fanatic that doubles the red pepper in every recipe, etc. etc.) and really tasty. You literally dump it in a bowl and heat it and - bam - good generic take-out Indian restaurant quality chick pea curry. Awesome. Now if they only make Jal Farazi!

I've been eating these for years now. I first found them at my local supermarket. Now I order them through Amazon. I don't know if I'm saving any money but it sure is convenient to have them delivered in bulk.Personally I like to have this dish with couscous, raisins, peanuts, and chutney. Yum!

This is my first taste of the Kitchens of India RTE products, but I'm very happy (I've had other KoI products, like the Kitchens of India Paste for Butter Chicken Curry, 3.5-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)).  The chickpeas are cooked very well, neither hard nor mushy, and the curry gravy is very flavorful.  I'm impressed that they actually use real, natural ingredients.  You will find an occasional piece of ginger in there showing you this isn't as industrial as the vacuum foil pouch packaging makes it seem.It's more "medium" than "mild" if you're used to typical American Indian restaurant food.  If you love the taste of chickpeas, you may be a bit disappointed, because the curry gravy does overpower the taste of them a little.

I've loved the Kitchens of India pastes, so took the chance on a dish I like. The chickpeas are mushy and the spicing is horrible. I would not recommend this dish to anyone, and my dog did even eat it. I did try the TASTY BITE CHANNA MASALA and felt it was a much better product for the price. Amazon's having a special on the TASTY BITE meals, which average to over a little under $2.00 a piece. Even though I will not be buying any more Kitchen of India ready to eat meals, I do like their lamb and butter chicken pastes.
I was pleasantly surprised with the authenticity of this dish.  The taste was very distinct and as good as any restaurant dish.
For packaged, microwave food, this is very good.  The ingridients are select, and the armoa is delicate.  Downside--very oily.

Kitchens of India's "Pindi Chana (Chickpea Curry)" was an unexpected surprise. I'm not a fan of garbanzo beans by any means. They have a funky flavor,and I like them best when they're incognito as felafels or hummus. Garbanzos must be seen and not tasted. Kitchens of India succeeds. The tomato sauce is SO SPICY that one can't taste the garbanzo beans. At all. The chickpeas serve as the canvas,the supporting player,while the spicy sauce gets top billing. Indeed,they act like movie extras,which is how it ought to be.It was SO SPICY (there should be a warning label) I should've paired it with rice,or a dollop of yogurt.To put the topping on the curry,so to speak,it comes with a CD of Indian classical music. It's a duet between Ustad Liyaqat Khan (on sarangi) and Pandit Tarun Bhattacharya (on santoor). It's sublime and sensual. This is the sort of easy listening music that 96.5 KOIT should be playing.. it's THAT good. Great music, great food-a sublime combination! All ready-made Indian meals should be this great.
We do not have an Indian restaurant in our town so this is a great substitute.  It is also good when you are short on time to make dinner. Just add rice.
I'm happy for getting these as a deal, but i wont say it tasted AMAZING. it was decent, and no regrets.
The taste of the chick peas was overpowered by the curry and heat.  Definitely not as good as their other products.

column9: Tastes Great but will Kill your Sooner
column10: All of the Kitchens of India products (and in fairness all ready to eat Indian Curries) are loaded with sodium. This particular product has over 800 mg per serving. Each packet is supposed to serve two! I eat one pack as a single person. I have read several people who claim to eat the entire package individually. In effect you are ingesting ~1650 mg of sodium with a single package. The latest recommended FDA sodium levels have been reduced to 1500 mg per daily to avoid heart issues apart from other potential issues. While this product does taste great and is good for busy single people who cannot spend time cooking, it is going to kill you sooner than otherwise. So enjoy the taste as long as you are willing to die sooner as well....

I bought this back in January 2011 because the positive reviews made this sound so yummy...I should have listened to the negative reviews. I think it is an acquired taste. My brother and his wife came down from NorCal (March 2011) and they tried it and liked it so I made them take it with them.  At least someone liked it so I didn't waste my money.
I can't believe that someone would pay sixteen bucks for this! Almost anyone can get it for two at their local Indian grocery store.

column9: Coffee House taste without the cost!
column10: Delicious and affordable. Buy the squirt dispensers and get the coffee house taste without the cost and many, many cups of great coffee!
Da Vinci coffee syrup is the best ever!  I highly recommend this to anyone who enjoys the  flavored taste of coffee anytime in the day.

I was surprised and pleased that I received a glass bottle, rather than plastic, but I know with the nature of the fulfillment structure, you never know what you'll get.  I tried the syrup first in a protein drink (vanilla) and it was excellent.  I've tried the Torani SF English Toffee syrup and like the DaVinci better.  The pump works well with the glass bottle, and 4 pumps in 12 oz. of vanilla protein drink seems optimal.  I've found in the past that when using a pump in the plastic bottle, when the liquid gets down a couple of inches, just the slight compression of picking up the bottle can cause it to send liquid up and out of the pump.
Very well balanced flavor with no after taste.  Syrup does have the tendency to drip down the side while pouring so you may want to get a pump.

As a woman perusing the candy aisle said to me just yesterday, "When did licorice stop being black?"  Sure enough, all of the choices on the shelves were red and had one so-called fruit flavor or another.  Apparently, black licorice has joined muscle cars and drive-in theaters as mostly a memory.It's hard to miss the old stuff when the new stuff tastes as good as this, though!  I shared this package with four people, three of whom are avowed licorice fans.  One had to be strong-armed into trying it because she's from the black licorice camp, but in the end, even the youngest among us liked it.  The tangy flavor sets it apart from the usual very sweet red licorice, and we did like knowing both that it was organic and that it supports the Newman's Own charity recipients.  It also has a somewhat softer chew than the usual twists and the preferences were split, with some thinking this was an improvement and some not.And, as I go to post this review, I see that Newman's Own makes - you guessed it, black licorice!

As with all of the Newman's Own products I have tried, the Organic Pomegranate Licorice Twists are delightful!  Unlike some other pomegranate-flavored products, the Newman's Own Pomegranate Licorice Twists tasted very much like pomegranate, with just the right amount of sweetness.  The twists are chewy, but not overly so, with even flavor throughout the product.  Very tasty!

This tastes like real licorice candy, with a pleasant dash of real pomegranate. It has the right texture, starting out chewy and slowly melting and releasing flavor. While it is candy, not health food, the ingredients are more food and less junk than most candy.My kids didn't like it and I suspect yours won't either. It does not have the intense artificial flavors of more processed candy, and the complex textures are more appealing to adult tastes. No one will pig out on a whole package of these, they are candies to savor. You could serve them after a good dinner with fruit, cheese, nuts and dessert wine without shame (unless your guests see the package, I suggest cutting the sticks into shorter pieces for additional deception).Since I no longer take chocolate GORP on my hikes for health reasons, I tried short pieces of various flavors of this with raw almonds instead. I won't say it delivers the ecstasy of the original, it satisfies both tongue and stomach.

column9: Not terrible, but our kids didn't like it
column10: The Newman's Own line generates some decent food products at reasonable prices.  This one, however, wasn't one of our favorites.  The "licorice" is a bit sticky, and left a sticky residue on our children's fingers.  The pieces are also relatively short.We do eat pomegranates from time to time.  This doesn't really taste strongly of fresh pomegranate.  The initial taste is reminiscent of a sweet-tart apple/pomegranate with berry, but the aftertaste is a little off.  Don't get me wrong.  It's not horrible or anything.  It just doesn't really live up to what we've come to expect from the Newman's Own brand.

I always have a little licorice every now and then to tide me over that starting hunger just before a regular meal. Most often I would do this at work and it has benefited me in a way that I do not overeat during a regular meal. Since I lift weights and do cardio, my system of eating incorporates several small portion eatings to keep my metabolism running and in check. I found that eating licorice works wondersand I have shifted to eating organic and sugar free licorice to maximize the health potentials. When the Newman's Own Organics Pomegranate Licorice Twists came to Vine, I felt I go to have and I haven't regretted it. The pomegranate variety is among my favorites because of the health factors you get from the Pomegranate fruit. This variety though contains corn syrup so I advise you to eat this in moderation. As you very well know, corn syrup plays a huge factor in just about everything we eat nowadays and recent studies proved overabundance of this ingredient is not healthy. So moderation in eating this or any other licorice for that matter is highly recommended. Overall satisfied with the product.

Well this isn't your grandmother's licorice to chew.  In fact, if you check the list of ingredients, you have to read to the end to get to the tiny amount of licorice that us included.  So, if you're looking for whatever licorice does for you you probably won't get it from this.  Still, this is a very tasty snack - nice and sweet with a pleasant pomegranate taste.

This product is the best licorice I have ever eaten.  It's chewy and flavorful, as well as quite a bit healthier than other licorice.  Very addictive!  The pomegranate flavor is so intense, and it is not overly sweet.  Just right.  Perfect. I want more!

column9: Pretty good, although the number one ingredient is wheat.
column10: I must state up front that I am not much of a fruity candy lover.  That being said, the Pomegranate Licorice is pretty good.  You can taste the fruit, but you also get the anise flavor.  That is an important distinction as my wife, who loves similar products, didn't like these due to the anise.  I personally liked them BECAUSE of the anise flavor.I didn't care for the fact that the number one ingredient is wheat, but beyond that it appears to be a quality product.

Who'd ever think of Pomegranate licorice twists? I'm glad it was Paul Newman's Own.They're not just tasty, it's a hearty flavor that goes a long way. And the ingredients are all natural, organic, and bold.Love them. Enjoy!

This licorice is really good! I took it to work and everyone agreed it was really good stuff. A few things I gotta add though... I am not a fan of pomegranate. But I really liked this. I was very surprised that it tasted so good.Also, this stuff was delivered to my house during the hottest weather week of the year - we even came close to setting a record. I did not get a chance to check my mail for a few days, so it sat in the outside mailbox, in >105F degree heat for a day or so. I expected it to be a big lump of licorice.Newman's apparently has the recipe down just perfectly for dealing with temperature - none of it was stuck together at all. (I bet you never expected to read a 'torture test' in a candy review, did you?)So, would I buy it again? You bet I would. Can't wait to try out the other flavors.

I grew up eating Red Vines and I liked them very much, but it's been ages and ages since I've eaten licorice. I don't why, I do eat candy on occasion, but licorice I just stopped eating, until last week when I tried these. They do kind of remind me of Red Vines. The flavor is different, of course, then I remember. These are pomegranate flavored, but it's been ages and ages plus years since I've eaten a pomegranate, so I can't swear that they've gotten the flavor right, but that being said, these are very tasty.

column9: Great for the movies or in a martini
column10: I'm not a big licorice fan, but I do like Paul Newman's food products and pomegranate, so I gave these a try. They have a nice pomegranate flavor, and they are not too chewy as licorice can sometimes be. I like that they are made with organic sugar and wheat flour, and the size is smaller than the usual licorice.I think they'd be perfect in a pomegranate cocktail, like a martini. It would make a festive swizzle stick. They'd also be great to stick in your purse on your way to see a movie. I have to admit that they are addictive too; the serving size is 5 pieces, and  that seems about right to satisfy the candy craving.Licorice lovers should definitely give these a try; they are a worthy addition to the Paul Newman organic family of products.

I ate six of these right off the bat. Delicious but not overly sweet, with only a hint of pomegranate that tastes more like conventional cherry licorice. These are delightfully chewy (and my bridgework is still well intact). I certainly would like to try the other flavors, but finding just a single package at retail would probably be quite pricey. (One 5-oz. package contains eighteen 4-3/8-inch "twisted" sticks.)According the the package, these are made in Mexico and certified to be organic by Oregon Tilth. Ingredients include corn syrup--but not the high fructose type.

Okay, but I don't think I'd buy it if I saw it in the store, natural ingredients or not. However, for those of you who are into licorice, this does taste like licorice, not the licorice I'm used to, there is a hint of something else, pomegranate they say, but I couldn't tell. And I'm wondering if Paul Newman were still with us, if this would be branded Newman's own.

I really wanted to like this product.  I usually like "Newman's Own" items. . . and I really like licorice. . . and I really like pomegranate.  But this item fell short.Pro's:Texture.  Chewy just the way you want it.OrganicCon's:Cost. I know that prices go up-and-down on Amazon. .  but right now the price is CRAZY expensive for a 5oz package.Pomegranate?  Really?  I was in hopes of a real good pomegranate flavor, but it just didn't come through for me.  But I must admit when I eat "red" licorice I don't think it has much of a strawberry flavor either. . . if that's what it's supposed to be.Overall the product is fine. . . but I wouldn't buy it again. . . I would like to try some of the other flavors though, like tangerine.

This pomegranate licorice is quite tasty. The pom is a nice tart yet sweet flavor. The licorice is a bit tougher than some other brands but I preferred it. I like having some to chew on for awhile and suffice my oral fixation

These taste alright, but they're nothing special. Would I order them online? No. But I would buy them at the checkout in my local supermarket if they were priced the same as the licorice that's there now.That being said, these do have all natural ingredients, however natural does not necessarily mean healthy. These are candy, like all licorice.

These naturally-flavored twists are healthier and tastier than the more popular type out there on the market (which taste like plastic)I was hoping not to find corn syrup in these twists, but these days it is almost impossible to find man-made snacks without it.Ingredients:  Organic wheat flour, organic sugar, CORN SYRUP, organic tapioca syrup, vegetable glycerin, sunflower oil, elderberry extract, citric acid, natural flavor, pomegranite juice concentrate, licorice root extract.Made in Mexico. (So much for being "Newman's Own")

column9: My Son Pick Newman's Own over Red Vines
column10: So to the ultimate licorice test. I gave my son one of these sticks and a Red Vine. The Red Vine was longer, so he grabbed it first. It was redder two. After he gobbled it down, he gobbled down Newman's Own Pomegranate Licorice Twist.I went and sat down and waited. There was a pack of each of these on the kitchen counter, by the sink. He asked could he have more licorice and I said yes. He went for Newmen's own. Nuff said.

this is great stuff.  when it comes on the market i will buy it.  the pomegranate flavoring is surpurb.  funny thing it doesn't leave a after taste like regular licorice does.  the taste is smooth and enjoyable.  it does not harden up even after being left open for a week like regular licorice does.

These smell great, but my first impression of the taste was of plastic. If you're desperate for a snack and you keep chewing on them, they kind of get better with time, but I don't think I'll be going out of my way to purchase them.

column9: A healthy version of the red "vines"...but...
column10: I only got a 5 oz. packet of these (~20 of their 6 in. sticks) and gave them out to the crew at home, so it was a small sample...but we all agreed on the following pluses and minuses:+ healthy ingredients...what you'd expect from Newman's Own...especially when compared to the commercial versions+ nice color, obtained naturally...NO food dye!- a bit too waxy for our tastes (as compared to other licorices, like "Panda" Brand)- a bit chewy for our teeth...not very filling-friendlySo, overall, we have a mediocre response to these. If you really love swizzler-type candy, these might be a healthy alternative...but if you are craving a meatier kind of licorice, try some of the other brands (one example already cited above).Thanks for reading!
This licorice is delicious -- very natural tasting and not too sweet at all. Warning, though: these are extremely addictive!Newman's Own delivers once again!

column9: Newman's Own Goodness--a bit of an aftertaste, though
column10: We really like Newman's Own products.  We also like these.  But the taste is not consistent.  It starts out nice, and you can taste the pomegranate, but as it sits in the mouth, it begins to taste like cough syrup a bit.  Just enough to be slightly off-putting.  Overall, good product, but not one you will want to buy multiple packs of.

While I'm not a licorice fanatic like some of my friends, I do enjoy a licorice twist now and then! I really liked the Newman Pomegranate twists. They are sweet, but not too sweet. The texture is smooth and not grainy. The licorice was fresh and tasty. I'll definitely buy this for a low calorie treat in the future!

column9: Good Ingredients But Just Too Sweet
column10: I appreciate the organics of this product but it's just too sweet and the texture is a bit gooey and not licorice like.

I have to say, I'm generally not a big fan of organic food. Especially since the taste of organic food can sometimes leave a lot to be desired.  Another drawback is that organic food is, in general, much more expensive than regular. But I have to say, these licorice sticks were a pleasant surprise. They weren't overly sweet and they have a very strong fruit taste. I enjoyed them a lot and would consider buying them in the store. However, I gave a piece to my mom and she said it was "terrible." She said it had a really nasty aftertaste. This isn't your run-of-the-mill licorice. However, I think this is one of those foods that either you love them or you hate them. Based on the other reviews I read of this product, there doesn't seem to be much in between. I would definitely be interested in sampling other flavors of this licorice.

I've never been a fan of black licorice but find myself enjoying a package of Red Vines every so often - but they MUST be chewy. So imagine my joy happening across this new treat from Newman's Own and having my first bite having the required "chew" without having to let the package stand out in the open for a few days.Yummmmmy. A whole new way to enjoy licorice with a healthful "kick" of tangy pomegranate to stave off the guilt of indulging in some delightfully chewy and delicious candy treats.I'll be sneaking these babies into the movies from now on.

column9: Hit or miss... family is split
column10: So out of 4 of us. 2 Like the licorice, one hates it and one says it is ok...It is pretty much just like regular Licorice, but cool flavors and organic.3 year old hated it and gave it to the dog. (The dog LOVED it).6 year said it was yummy and better than any other licorice he had before.The grownups were split...If you like twizzlers, you will like these. Think of them as fancy twizzlers.

column9: Newman's Pomegranate Licorice tasts natural - not artificial
column10: I shared this package with several work colleagues who have nearly finished off the package as I write this review.  We all agreed the taste is a bit cut above the other popular red licorice vines.  It has a taste somewhere in between the health food store licorice brands, which use all natural ingredients and that other popular red licorice product.  The ingredients list seems to be largely organic and include actual pomegranate juice in the ingredients list. The one oddity is the mix of both sugar AND corn syrup.  It might be nicer to exlude the corn syrup from an otherwise all-natural natural product (I know, I know - corn syrup is natural, etc.  But a lot of people - me included - avoid it.)  Overall, it's flavorful and darn near addictive.  Another hit from Newman's Own, a company you can feel good about supporting.

Although I try to eat healthily, I am a big fan of all kinds of candy, which I try to reserve for an occasional treat. Newman's Own Organics Pomegranate Licorice Twists are a nice compromise--sweet, but not filled with a lot of chemicals. For example, there are eleven ingredients in the Newman's Own Licorice, while Twizzlers has a list of ingredients too long to count.Newman's Own Licorice is shorter in length than typical licorice, and come in a much smaller package. The ingredients are not totally organic, and corn syrup is the third ingredient (it's the first ingredient in Twizzlers). The Newman's Own Licorice is made in Mexico, which is a drawback for me, I prefer my candy to be made in the US, the quality is usually better.The best part of Newman's licorice is the flavor, it is a clear, strong pomegranate. It is really refreshing for a candy to taste like the flavor it's supposed to be instead of being just sweet with no specific taste profile. Two or three of these twists are enough for a snack, which I suspect is because the flavor is so good. The back of the package says that strawberry, tangerine, and black Newman's Own Licorice is available, which I will definitely look for and try.

There isn't much to say about this product besides the fact it's amazing. I have been munching on them off and on for the last week and they taste great! I have the pomegranate flavored but I look forward to trying other flavors too. But in all honesty, I have not had anything of low quality in the Newman's Own brand. So... Enjoy!

Oh, my gosh! This is a virtuous treat. But don't look at the rating I gave Nell and Pa Newman. Not yet.First you should know:1. I am a health nut.2. I know what all the ingredients in these Licorice Twists do for one's body including the Elderberry Extract and the Pomegranate Juice.3. And generally I am not a big fan of licorice sticks of any kind. They're too sticky and I hate that I feel as if I'm eating industrial-strength food coloring.You can't possibly weigh the credibilty of this review without knowing those things. But now you know, here's the scoop. These twists may become my new before-bed snack. I can eat just one and only consume about twenty calories and go to bed happy and yes, feeling virtuous. So in spite of my aversion to anything that sticks to my teeth, I love them and have even become a fan of the last ingredient on the list, Licorice Root Extract.

column9: Nice candy, flavorful and toothsome, but maybe not quite so Green
column10: Newman's Own (Organics) Pomegranite Licorice is a red chewey twisty stick (tube) candy of the sort that most of us remember.  It's sealed in a multilayer plastic-and-foil wrapper, which may lessen its appeal to the sustainable-use folks.The aroma and flavor are clear and memorable.  Had I not known that this was pomegranite-flavored, I might have labelled it black cherry, but pomegranite it is.  It was just chewey enough to resist the tooth pleasantly.The list of ingredients is much as expected, except that the sugar and starch sources are described as "organic" (except for the corn syrup, which follows flour and sugar, but precedes tapioca starch).  The glycerin is listed as "vegetable glycerin" and the package bears one of the familiar Kosher markings, along with the designation PAREVE.This package is marked BEST IF USED BEFORE MAR 11 2012.  I don't know the date of manufacture, but the package says it was made in Mexico and certified organic by Oregon Tilth.So ... this is the familiar candy of your childhood, only a little bit better, or a lot better if you enjoy the aroma first.  There were a generous 18 pieces in the package I received.  They call it "about 3 and one half servings" but I think it could be five or six, even though the sticks are shorter than the candy store variety and maybe a little thinner.I'm taking a star off for advertising it as "organic" (which it is) while sealing it (for good reason) in a foil-and-plastic multilayer pouch.

I like the texture and taste. They firm, but don't have a plasticky feeling, and pomegranate doesn't taste fake (no artificial flavor). Not too sweet - good thing, although there is corn syrup in it, right after sugar. Only 3 out of 9 ingredients are organic (didn't count citric acid and natural flavor as an ingredient).I've tried Twizzlers before and Newman's licorice is way better. In general I am not a licorice person, on top of that whole package is 455 calories, I think I'd prefer M&Ms as a snack (small package 250 calories). But if someone likes this kind of treat than this is the way to go.

Newsman's Own Pomegranate Licorice Twists are out of this world!  I Love that it is made with organic sugar, is low in fat, and absolutely delicious!  The licorice is not overly sweet, there are no ingredients that I cannot pronounce (or any that I would turn my nose up at), it is soft and chewy, and the whole family enjoyed it.  We'll definitely be purchasing more for our home movie nights!

column9: Tasty and less "tough" than most of this stuff
column10: The pomegranate flavor is nice, and while I'm not sure I'd have identified it as pomegranate, it didn't have that fake taste that most of this stuff has.The other nice thing is that while it's chewy, it's chewy in a nicer way than most of this, and not as tough.If you like "red licorice" products, I think you'll like this better than most of them.
Licorice?Maybe.This is very sweet with a definite pomegranate taste.While not unpleasant, this very chewy candy will not appeal to everyone.For those with a very sweet tooth and good teeth.

column9: Best Licorice I have ever had!
column10: I ordered this because I am a fan of licorice and I like the idea of pomegranate flavored licorice.I was not disappointed in the least. Newman's own is known for creating superior products. This is no exception. The flavor is excellent, the ingredients are extremely high quality, and the overall taste experience is well above average.If you like licorice, this is certainly the way to go. Not much more I can say about it other than it blows your typical candy away.If you are a fan, I would highly recommend this!

These Pomegranate licorice twists are excellent.  They have a nice light flavor and a good chewy texture for those who like this type of candy.  They are a bit chewier and tastier than similar brands that are often a bit hard and sometimes have the feel of chewing on plastic.This is a high quality and enjoyable candy.

column9: Pomegranate licorice takes some getting used to
column10: I love pomegranate flavor, so when this came up as a Vine option, I jumped at it.  I got it a few days later, quickly opened it, took a bite, and then stopped.  Wow - this was weird.  I wasn't sure if I liked it.  I took another bite.  Hmm.  Still weird, but not bad.  Last bite (they're short)... I'll need another one to be sure.  Three more later, I've decided to like them.  They are kind of like salt & vinegar chips - odd at first, but addicting.The texture is perfect - soft and chewy, not so chewy that you're afraid of your crowns coming out.  I suspect if you leave them exposed to air for long enough, they'll dry out and get hard to bite, but after 3 days of an open package (clipped closed)the texture is still good.There are no artificial colors (or flavors), so the deep red must come from the elderberry extract and pomegranate juice concentrate.  Cool.  There are actually 2 grams of protein and 2 grams of fiber in a 5-piece serving, and only 1/2 gram of fat.  At 130 calories, it's not exactly guilt free, but the guilt can be rationalized.I like that these are mostly organic - less toxins to dump in the environment when they grow the wheat & sugar.  I like that you can get this on subscribe & save.  I do that for a lot of things.  There are 15 smallish packages (about 18 pieces per package) so they stay fresh.  Twizzlers might be a lot cheaper, but this is a LOT better.  Newman's Own licorice ingredients start with organic wheat flour.  Twizzlers start with corn syrup and contain artificial colors and flavors and there's slightly more fat & calories and no fiber.I'm just not sure I need 15 packages of candy at my house.

For a true licorice lover, these are certainly worth a try.  The pomegranate flavor bursts at the first bite and then subsides toa  tasty licorice finish.  The twists are a bit chewy, but not in the obnoxious way.  This allows for a fuller taste of all the flavors in the twist and not just the before or after, but also the in between slide from fruitiness to licorice tang.  Overall, an interesting take on a traditional treat.  I liked it.

It's so nice to come across an all natural product that really tastes good! I am a huge Black licorice fan so the flavored stix are not usually my thing. These actually do have licorice root extract in them which many black licorice products don't even have, so technically this is real licorice. The bag is 5 ounces and 3.5 servings, each twisted stick is approx 4.5'' long and 5 of them are only 130 calories and just 10 grams of sugar. There is also 2g of protein and 2g of fiber go figure. The flavor is pomegranate/berry  it is flavored with both Pomegranate and elderberry. I like this product and I don't feel like I need to punish myself for snarfing down a 5 stick serving, there is nothing bad in this product. I will try the other flavors too.  Darn, my bag is empty!

Reviewing food is tough -- I didn't like these as much as I had hoped I would, but if they're to your taste, go for them.The box I got had 16 or so 6-inch licorice ropes.  Each piece was firmer and chewier than I expected, but pleasant to eat.  The licorice had a very fruity smell and a sweet, slightly waxy, pomegranate flavor.  It's a Newman's Own product, so the ingredients are organic, and some money goes to charity.If you're intrigued by the idea of a firm, pomegranate licorice, go for it.

column9: Paul Newman had nothing to do with this but it's still good
column10: Licorice is a funny sort of treat, both humble and old-fashioned, and perhaps more relevant than ever in an ever more obese world obsessed with counting calories.  Pomegranate is an interesting choice of flavor; the pomegranate too steps forth from the fringes of fruit consciousness as from the pages of myth, its recent 15 minutes of fame as a super-antioxidant notwithstanding.  I like licorice and I like pomegranates, but I was a bit skeptical that the pomegranate's intense dusky flavor would make a good match.  I'm still not sure--not because this licorice isn't sweet and delicious (it is!), but because I'm not sure it's really fair to say this licorice is pomegranate flavored.  Yes, there is some pomegranate in it, but it's lower on the ingredient list than elderberry.  And sure enough, there is a definite undertone--or is it an overtone?--of the somehow dark, musky sweetness that makes elderberry so distinct.  I happen to love elderberries, so for me this is a happy coincidence.  Whatever your taste may be, it does seem as though the folks at Newman's Own use good ingredients and care about the quality and flavor of their products.  I did notice an odd almost minty sensation at times which is why I give only 4 stars.  More concentrated flavor would have been nice too, but overall a great snack--good flavor, good texture.

column9: Not health food, but a delicious candy
column10: Newman's Own is well known as an innovative company - innovative in their products and innovative in their corporate giving. This interesting snack is a "red licorice" candy that has a deliciously sweet pomegranate taste. It's made with all organic ingredients, including pomegranate juice concentrate.I liked it a lot. Yes, it's candy with five pieces containing 32 grams of carbs(!), so it's not health-food. But nonetheless it is a delicious candy!(Review of Newman's Own Organics Pomegranate Licorice Twists)

I really like this Licorice.It has a great flavor.Does it taste like Pomegranate?I don't really know what a pomegranate is supposed to taste like, so can't really answer if that's the flavor I'm tasting.But if you're looking for a licorice with a nice berry flavor that doesn't turn your tongue colors, this is it.I also like that it's from Newman's Own.  I always purchase their products as I know it's going towards charity.

These are really pretty good. My husband and I both tried them and he loves them. I feel like they have a bit more of a chewy texture than Twizzlers, which is why I gave it 4 stars. However, the flavor is great! Also, the product is made with some organic ingredients (wheat flour, sugar, and tapioca syrup) makes me feel good about it. The pieces are much shorter than Twizzlers, so they make a nice quick snack if you just want one. Overall, a very yummy snack with good flavor, but a bit on the chewy side.

column9: Good, though a little subtle on the Pomegranate flavor...
column10: Got a chance to try these Newman's Own Organic Pomegranate Licorice Twists and I have to say that I enjoyed them, but I didn't love 'em.  I've never been a huge fan of the "red" licorices, finding them a bit bland and much more plastic-y than your standard black anise licorice, and these certainly fall into that camp.  I was expecting more of  a burst of pomegranate flavor, but it's rather subtle unless you really keep it in your mouth and savor it.  Actually the flavor builds with the more you eat, and you taste it more on the back end as an aftertaste.

column4: C. Ball "An idea that is not dangerous is unw...
column9: Tasty and Great Old Fashioned Licorice!
column10: Based on my previous great experience with Newman's Own products, I got the Pomegranate Licorice.  Opening the package treats you to a wonderful aroma.  The licorice itself has a beautiful rich color and is made from cane sugar and tastes like real licorice unlike some which are more waxy and tough and lacking authentic flavor.  This is tender and tasty and a real treat.  The package is just the right size for a snack.  Glad I got them!  Now excuse me I need to get back to chomping licorice.

column9: Newman's Own Organics Pomegranate Licorice Twists
column10: I love licorice!  I was not so sure that was going to be the casewith a POMEGRANATE licorice...but, it WAS!  I just loved this!I am not a consumer of pomegranates usually...so not really surewhat I could expect.  This to me had almost a berry flavor to it.It was chewy and the shorter sticks are nice as you can HAVE thattreat and not go crazy and eat 1/2 of the package.  Really I cannot say anything bad about these...many of the ingredients areorganic too.  If you are going to purchase candy THIS is a goodone to get...plus the added great feeling of knowing that the"Newman's Own" are supporting charities with their profits.

This was surprisingly delicious!  I'm not a big licorice eater but this licorice had a good taste and aroma, and was very satisfyingly chewy.  It's not overly sweet, but just sweet enough for a nice treat.

column9: Red licorice that actually has some taste.
column10: I like to have licorice twists sitting around for an occasional snack. I tend to prefer red. But the problem with the typical red twist is that it has no taste, really.  A vague cherry flavor, perhaps, but predominantly just a sugary taste and a super gummy texture.  In contrast, these pomegranate twists have some flavor. They are tart and tasty and have a substantial feel to them when you take a bite.  The package says that they are made with organic sugar. Makes no difference to me, but some people might care.

column9: Tastes good, not too artificial tasting
column10: I don't have any idea what organic licorice is, but I do know that these strips are pretty tasty. Moreover, they do not have as strong of an artificial taste as Twizzler's. I'd buy them if I had the chance. The pomegranate flavor is good, not tart, just sweet enough. And the proceeds are donated, so what the heck....

column9: Eat This, Not That (for old time flavor)
column10: Do you remember old time, penny candy licorice in flavors like strawberry, and black, and cherry?I do.  We used to get them 5 for 1 cent at the drugstore on the corner. Ate 'em up, loved them.In later years, I tried to substitute those old flavors with a supermarket brand of licorice that (Twi**Elers), in a strawberry flavor.  Pure sugar with that. And some kind of "gum" for chewiness.Let me tell you, as someone old enough to remember real licorice-- these licorice twists, in POMEGRANATE, from Newman's Own Organics, are as chewy, tasty, juicy, and real tasting as candy gets. Takes me right back to the penny candy drugstore.Now, I know, these days, people want carb counts, calories, sugar, etc. So, here's some of that:sugars: 10gcarbs:  32gcalories: 5 pieces, 130 caloriesHey, I'm not your doctor. I'm reviewing a candy. And it tastes GOOD. For those with real health issues with sugar, etc., I recommend reading the ingredients  (see package) in the grocery store. For anyone else who just wants a nice, great tasting, old fashioned treat, get these, and enjoy yourself!

column9: Great snack- perfect for your sweet tooth
column10: I didn't have high expectations when I received this product.  "Healthy" forms of candy and treats are often disappointing-- but this one is not!  It has a great texture and a slightly sour-sweet taste that is refreshing and enjoyable.  Your sweet tooth will be satisfied without an overload of sugar.  It's much better than the regular candy versions of licorice.  I have to admit that I'm not sure I could have identified the flavor specifically as pomegranate-- so if you're worried about not liking an unusual flavor like that, don't.  It just tastes great!  By the way, this candy holds up in all sorts of heat without getting sticky or messy (mine was sitting in a metal mailbox in the Texas summer heat and survived just fine) so I think it would be safe to hand to children without too much worry of sticky hands or other messes.  All the healthy aspects-- low fat, organic sugar-- well that's just a bonus.  Excellent product-- I'm looking forward to trying more Newman's Own licorice products soon.

column9: More pomegranate than licorice - an energizing snack
column10: I was expecting some black licorice with a pomegranate flavor.  I grew up not far from Pontefract in Yorkshire where licorice was a treat for those who couldn't afford chocolate, so I love the black chewy Pomfret cakes and I like to chew real licorice roots. Black licorice is typically made with treacle or molasses, but this like American red licorice with a fruitier, less sweet flavor.On the plus side, it is good and chewy if you keep it in the fridge. To me, it tastes better than red licorice because it is not as sweet and has a delightful taste of pomegranate.On the minus side, I wish there were more licorice flavor. This might be a boon to those who don't like licorice, as I couldn't taste the licorice root extract.The main ingredients are organic wheat flour and organic sugar.  There's even a tiny bit of sunflower oil in the ingredients, above elderberry extract, citric acid, natural flavor (not sure what the flavor is?), pomegranate juice concentrate and last & least licorice root extract.This is an enjoyable candy, good for a hike where you need that little bit of extra sugar.  There are 130 calories in 5 pieces, the bag says it has 3.5 servings (I think there were nearer 4), but still that is 455 calories a bag.For me, I'd like less sweetening and more licorice to make this a truly great snack. I'd also like the texture to be a bit more glazed and springy - like gummy bears, maybe substitute gelatine for flour.

this arrived soft, smelling AMAZING and tasting even better! usually I only like black but this makes me a red lover!  the smell is so amazing too makes you wanna take a bite and the bite does not disappoint loved it!

There isn't much more to say than what has already been said by other reviewers. It is firm but not hard, so you actually have something to chew on and the taste is amazing.My only complaint is the price.

I have never tried the similar candies before so maybe I have nothing to compare these with, but I really enjoyed them. It is not too sweet and just has a pleasant taste overall.I think I will be buying these candies for myself in the future. I tried Newman's Own other products and I am happy that this one has not dissappointed me.

column9: Yummy variation on a classic treat
column10: Fruity, chewy and lovely.  I love black licorace. The good stuffy is a delicate balence of chewy and lush flavor. Newmanns own pomegranate licorace is just right. A lovely variation on a classic. Give yourself a treat!

column9: An adult flavor with the chewy funfilled aspects of ....
column10: I really enjoy Newmans own products and this is no exception.  Though I am not sure why they had this flavor instead of some of the others but it worked and was a tasty treat that really has that complex almost funky quality that pomegrante is known for.

These licorice twists are very tasty. They are soft and pliable but still chewy and firm. The pomegranate flavor isn't strong, but there is definitely a fruit flavor to them though not too sweet. I like the color of the twists, they look like that deep pink of pomegranates. I really liked that the many of the ingredients are organic. I've been happy with many other Newman's Own Organic products and this was no different. This is a good company that supports good causes, and makes great products. These Licorice Twists were enjoyed by me, my husband, and our six year old. I am interested in trying their other flavors as well. If you find these, give them a try!

Even though I consider myself fairly health conscious, I like a treat every now and then. When I was a kid, I ate Twizzlers by the pound and loved the chewy, fruity taste of them. Now that I am an adult I was looking for a healthier alternative, and the Newman's Own fit the bill. As you would expect, this product is free of artificial colors and additives. It is full of taste though, and I esp. loved the pomegranate flavor. One caveat: although this organic, it is still junk food and a serving of these (approximately 5 sticks) have 12 grams of sugar. Still, compared to what is out there, I would buy these in a heartbeat. Lastly, these are somewhat sticker to the teeth than most licorice sticks, so it might be a good idea to have your toothbrush handy after you eat them.

When I received my package in the mail, eager to try these new pomegranate licorice, I just happened to have a gaggle of people at my home who flocked around me like little birds waiting to be fed. So this review is based on a roundtable discussion which then ensued.I got this candy because I really like Newman's Own products and pomegranate, so I thought I would love these. Unfortunately, I did not enjoy them. I am more apt to like the lighter, fresher tasting Red Vine sort of licorice rather than the thick heavier Twizzler kind. These were more like Twizzlers, but tasted more like a fruit roll up. It was also suggested that they taste like the red Vitamin Water.Although I did not enjoy them, there were several in the taste test that did. 4 out of 12 loved them and would buy them again. 2 thought they were so-so and might buy them again. 6 of us didn't care for them. In our numbers were two children who eat every candy imaginable, even fruit roll ups - that these taste the most like, but didn't finish their sticks.All this being said, I like Newman's Own products, will keep buying them and trying new things they bring out. I see that they have a Tangerine version of this same candy and will be buying a pack to try them out!

column9: Delicious, subtle, and not too chewy.
column10: This is a candy that's just a little different, with a true pomegranate flavor and the requisite hint of cough syrup, since it's licorice after all. The consistency was just right... toothy, but no danger of removing your fillings. For fans of the salt licorice, this would be too sweet, but for me it's just right.

This is a very tasty variation of the classic red licorice. It has a mild pomegranate flavor and a very soft, chewable texture. I did initially wonder about the corn syrup that is the third ingredient but a friend informed me that it is high Fructose corn syrup that is bad and considered non-organic. You get 15 half ounce packs which breaks down to $2.70 a pack so it is actually a pretty good deal, especially for an organic product.So if you want to try something new, especially if you prefer an alternative to the old red licorice I highly recommend trying this product.

I shared a package with a friend.  I like pomegranates but thought that the flavor of the twists was bland at best.  I wouldn't actually buy this as a confection.  My friend thought they were frankly awful. This may not have been a good idea for a candy.

column9: Great taste, but a tad chewy
column10: I'm a licorice fanatic, so I was excited to get these in the mail. My daughter and I enjoyed them. The taste was good, but I wonder if they were a little stale. They seemed a bit hardened. Perhaps that's not a reflection of the product as much as a natural staling that might occur in shipping. I do love the pomegranate taste. Fantastic.

These licorice are very tasty, the pomegranate gives it a tangier taste than Twizzlers (they are also a little shorter than the popular brand).  It is one of those treats where you say you will have just one and five of them later; you are hiding the package to avoid being tempted to take more.  The only drawback is that like most licorice, you will be picking it out of your teeth after eating it.

There's a great cinnamon note to these licorice.  You can taste the "realness."  They're also not as sweet as other licorice you might be used to.  They still taste great, and they're organic!  Of course, they're still not "health food," but they might be a healthier choice than twizzlers.

column9: You won't stop at just one!
column10: These are some of the most delicious licorice twists I have ever had! I wasn't sure what they would taste like but was pleasantly surprised when they had a punch of sweet and tangy flavor. It didn't take long to finish off this pack of twists as everyone in the house kept going back for more. Even my son, who has never liked twizzlers, thought these were delicious! I like that they are organic and has a short and simple list of ingredients. They are about 100 calories for 4 twists, which is pretty steep, but worth it I would say!

column9: It could have had more flavor.
column10: I liked this product because I love the flavor of a pomegranate.  It could have had more of the flavor as far as I was concerned, so I gave it three stars.  Not as tasty as some other brands, but you have to remember they are using organic sugar so it is a healthy trade off.  But as a bit less sugary alternative to other candies, not bad.  Myself I like the salad dressings much better.  I am not so sure they should try candies, because let's face it, if people are going to eat candy they are going to go for the favorite sugar stuff that they love, but for those who really have discipline to choose a healthy snack, they will love it.

column9: Sorry, the flavor's not for me
column10: I love licorice and try to drink pomogranate juice daily, but the flavor of this licorice was not for me. It reminded me a little of a 'perfumey' artificial grape taste, perhaps because of the elderberry extract listed in the ingredienct list before pomegranate juice is. I actually like elderberries so am not sure why I didn't like this better than I did. The texture was okay, a bit chewier than traditional red vines and more like those long licorice ropes. I didn't detest it, but I can't say I particularly liked it, either. The product is made in Mexico and certified organic by Oregon Tilth. I'd stick with the black licorice flavor when ordering this brand.

I was pleasantly surprised to find Newman's Own licorice. I've always enjoyed the Newman's Own products, but then realized they are not the same companies. One is Newman's Own who makes the salad dressing, popcorn, etc. while this is another company known as Newman's Own Organics. Either way, I like licorice, and wanted to give it a try. Having picked up a pack, and distributed it to the family, we all enjoyed it, but were somewhat underwhelmed. There wasn't a lot of flavor until quite a bit of chewing. The first bite is definitely disappointing. Having had the pomegranate licorice from Cabela's we expected more flavor. These definitely weren't bad, and we'll eat the entire package easily, but it just wasn't the best pomegranate licorice I've had. Average is the best way I can describe it. If I was offered this licorice in the future, I'd still eat it, but I don't see myself going out and wanting to purchase this again.

I don't like to give anything of Newman's a three star review because this family gives all its profits to charity, but the Pomegranate licorice needs improvement.A nice idea to add a new flavor to licorice, but the flavor of the pomegranate is somewhat on the weak side and needs to be more full bodied, and the twists are a bit too hard and should be softer.Not bad all around but needs a boost.
they are very good, fresh & chewy but they taste more like bing cherries than pomegranate. i like both so doesn't matter but the price is way too high.

When I first opened the bag the delicious aroma was amazing!  These smell very, very good.  The taste was pretty good too, but they did not taste as flavorful as the smell had me thinking they would.  The texture was great and these did make for a good snack - the whole family passed the bag around and had a couple.

column9: Pleasing Overall Except For Odd Aftertaste
column10: I'm a licorice fan, although I tend to only enjoy plain licorice, not the fruit flavors. However, since I also adore tart pomegranate flavoring, I thought I'd try this Newman's Own version.Overall, it had a good, chewy texture without being too hard. It conveyed well the somewhat tart pomegranate flavor I expected, within the limits of what the candy can offer ... which means that licorice twists aren't usually known for sharply focused taste. I enjoyed it quite a bit.The only thing is that there was a brief, odd aftertaste that I couldn't identify but which I didn't care for. As I say, it was fairly brief and faded after a little while. It wouldn't keep me from buying the candy if I was in the mood for pomegranate flavor and licorice twist texture. I mention it to explain why there isn't a higher star rating.

column9: Surprisingly good for a non-licorice flavored licorice
column10: Most non-licorice flavored licorice candy twists or ropes - usually "red licorice" - available are pretty lame.  Mostly sugar, with little flavor other than obviously chemically-induced painfully artificial strawberry basically meant for kids whose only criteria is sweetness. This item from Newman's Own line of products rises above the pack. The texture is firm and chewy - moreso than many of the other licorice "twists" - but it's the flavor that earns the distinction here.  The pomegranate flavor is surprisingly distinct with a tang that is refreshing and not overly sweet-tasting.Being an "organic" product also may appeal to some consumers. Be aware though, that for those sensitive to the corn syrup issue, the third listed ingredient here is corn sugar and not specified as "organic".  These considerations aside, from strictly an enjoyment perspective, this new licorice offering does offer more appeal than most similar products found in the candy aisle.  As may be expected however, price is an issue here.  Enjoyable product but only the individual can decide if this type of non-licorice flavored licorice is worth the money spent here.  It is, however, worthwhile sampling for its distinctive flavor.

This is very good licorice.  The texture is outstanding: soft and chewy, but with some "bite."  The flavor is subtle and pleasant.  There is no cloying, artificial sweetener aftertaste.  The ingredients are mostly organic.  (However, let's not kid ourselves; this is candy, not health food.)The one and only downside is the cost.  It's considerably more expensive than regular licorice.  Whether the better quality overcomes the high price will, of course, be a matter of personal opinion.But it is very good licorice.  VERY good...

Has a nice pomegranate flavor and fragrance and a slightly firmer texture than other licorice that I've tried.I tested this on my other family members and two out of four people liked it and would purchase it again.The other two thought that it tasted a little odd and didn't care for the flavor.

What can I say except that they are delicious!  I love licorice and to get it in the pomegranate flavor is a real plus.  I also like the fact the ingredients are organic and none that I can't read. There are no fillers in this product.  My only objection is the product is made in Mexico and I'm hoping/assuming the facility has been thoroughly inspected and meets the US standards.  And...yes, I will buy these twists.

First, obviously, you've got to like pomegranate.Once you're past that, you have to enjoy this Licorice! It's not too sweet, just the perfect springiness in the bite, doesn't coat and stick to your teeth with no starchy rubberiness unlike some of the others I've tried and it goes down very easy.Thoroughly enjoyed this pack.

column9: Doesn't taste artificial or sugary, but a natural sweet
column10: I love licorice.  I'm not a huge fan of those neon-colored rainbow packs with funky flavors, so I tried not to be skeptical about the idea of pomegranate licorice.  I'm also not a huge organic food person, though I do try to be as natural and healthy as I can pull off.What I got was a cute package of roughly 4.5" licorice sticks.  Opening the package, I was immediately struck by a delightful aroma that smelled fruity and real, not sugary sweet.  Grabbing a piece, I was expecting a texture like Twizzler, but found one more like Nibs.  It isn't sticky, nor is it a challenge to bite through.Flavor -- it doesn't taste artificial or sugary, but just a natural sweet.  I like it.With a candy, I wouldn't normally get into ingredients, but since this is organic, I thought I'd comment.  First, I can pronounce everything on the list, with the most difficult one being vegetable glycerin.  Corn syrup is on the list, along with organic sugar.Overall, I like this.  I cannot imagine this will become a regular purchase, but I don't buy much candy.
I can't decide whether I like this or not. there is a pomogranate taste with lemon and something else i couldn't identify.

column9: Tastes Good and Not Too Sweet
column10: These Newman's Own Pomegranate licorice twists has a very nice fruity taste without being too sweet.I checked out licorice on Wikipedia and I list some information here for your reference.ToxicityExcessive consumption of liquorice or liquorice candy is known to be toxic to the liver[26] and cardiovascular system, and may produce hypertension[27] and edema.[28] In occasional cases blood pressure has increased with excessive consumption of liquorice tea, but such occasions are rare and reversible when the herb is withdrawn.[29] Most cases of hypertension from liquorice were caused by eating too much concentrated liquorice candy.[30] Doses as low as 50 grams (2 oz) of liquorice daily for two weeks can cause a significant rise in blood pressure. The liver effects can lead to a weight gain from fluid retention of 6 pounds 3 kg of fluid in as little as 3-4 days, but immediately when liquorice is removed from the diet the weight just drops off again as the liver once again achieves equilibrium and the body flushes out the excess fluid.[31]

column9: Subtle pomegranate flavor tickles the palate...
column10: It was interesting to see an organic candy, and not only that pomegranate to boot.  I was a little skeptical at first but this pomegranate licorice was able to pull it off.  The flavor isn't too intense, leaving you with a more subtle initial bite with not really a burst of flavor, but a subtle taste when it hits your tongue.  Where you really taste the pomegranate, though, is in the aftertaste.  It felt like I had eaten a whole pomegranate with the amount of flavor that lingered in the aftertaste.  A pleasant surprise.  Not quite sugary sweet, but a subtle flavor that grows on you.

column9: Tasty Candy But A Bit Pricy
column10: This licorice is very much like Twizzlers or Red Vines in texture, which I like. It is chewy without being too much so and not sticky. The flavor is good. It is distinctive without being overpowering, and no aftertaste.I normally don't care what my candy is made of or how many calories it has. After all, it is candy. I don't expect any healthy ingredients. However, since Newman's is promoting the organic aspects of the product I decided to comment on them. While the brand is "Newman's Own Organics," only three of the eleven ingredients in the product are organic. The rest are conventional. At least there are no artificial colors or flavors. Calorie-wise, Newman's comes off slightly better at 3.1 calories/gram vs. 3.6 for Twizzlers and Red Vines.While the foil packaging may keep the candy fresh on the shelf, once opened there is no way to reseal the package. In all fairness, though, neither Red Vines nor Twizzler packages can be resealed after opening.When comparing 5 oz. packages of all three products here on Amazon, you find Newman's costs over twice as much as Twizzlers and over 2.5 times more than Red Vines. Twizzlers and Red Vines are made in the USA and Newman's are made in Mexico.For me, licorice is an occasional treat. Therefore, if I am in the market and craving a licorice type candy, I would probably reach for these, price not withstanding. I like the pomegranate flavor, and I think I would give the black licorice flavor a try as well.

This is the best licorice I've had in years.  It reminds me of the candy of my youth.  The texture, the flavor is perfect.  I just wish the packages were bigger.  Can't wait to try their black licorice.

column9: If you love licorice, then you will love these.
column10: Very strong pomegranate flavor. Very fresh, chewy consistency. Each stick is 4.75 inches long, about 18 per pack.A serving is 5 pieces, for a whopping 130 calories (only .5g fat calories), 8% dietary fiber.Watch out, these little licorice sticks are addictive!

This was my first taste of licorice in a pomegranate flavor and I was not disappointed. These were juicy, sweet and flavorful with just a hint of pomegranate. While I like pomegranate, I don't love it, and was pleased that the flavor was more sweet than strong. If anything it may have been a bit too sweet.While organic, they are not exactly health food, as they do contain corn syrup. Although if I'm eating licorice my first goal usually isn't healthy, it is something to be aware of. Nevertheless, I loved them, gobbled down the entire package in two days and found them to be almost addictive.

I took this to work and shared it. The comments I got were:bland; I wouldn't buy this; the texture is different than "Twizzlers".  Nobody raved.I thought the flavor was mild but pleasant.  The aroma is good.  I might buy this if it was on sale AND I had a coupon for it; Newman's Own stuff tends to be a bit pricy for me.

column9: Extra points for using organic ingredients
column10: Newman's Own products are usually quite good.  I was eager to try out this product because I love fruity licorice twists (and regular licorice,too)and love pomegranates.  I was surprised by my first bite by a slightly bitter taste.  Although that was brief, the flavor was not particular interesting - I couldn't tell that it was pomegranate - it could've passed for strawberry or cherry, in my opinion.  The twists were firm but not stale at all.  They were chewy and I could see getting hooked on eating them, even though the flavor is not anything special.  I might buy this in the store if I was looking for an organic candy snack for the movies.

column9: Newman's Own Organics Pomegranate Licorice Twists, 5-Ounce Packages (Pack of 15)...
column10: Newman's own does it again!These Licorice Twists are the best, most flavorful (Pomegranate, no less!) that I've had in recent memory.My only complaint is that they are...small (but, that in itself, will not detract anything from the score)!I invite everyone who reads this to try them...delicious!I rate "Newman's Own Organics Pomegranate Licorice Twists, 5-Ounce Packages (Pack of 15)"...Five stars!

I love twists. And I love almost anything pomegranate.  So I was predisposed to like Newman's Own Organics Pomegranate Licorice Twists.  However I was a bit taken aback at just how delicious they were.  They weren't too sweet - just right.  They filled my taste buds with a great pomegranate flavor--and when biting down gave an almost liquid like sense of refreshment. I tried to save a few for another day but darn it if I didn't eat the entire package of 15 in one day! The serving size is 5 twists with 130 calories per serving.  Not too bad if you can just eat one serving. These are all natural and darned good.  I highly recommend this for a great, organic snack that should be enjoyed by adults and children alike.  I know I am ordering more.

I thought these twists were simply delicious, but then I love anything that has Pomegranate! At only 25 calories per twist, this is the perfect little sweet to eat anytime. The best part for me is that the sugar is just right and the fact that it's organic is certainly a plus. It still contains Corn syrup but then so does everything around us as well. In short, it's tasty but don't overeat thinking it is organic.

You really need to be a fan of pomegranate to enjoy this product.  These twists are bit tougher to chew than most licorice twist on the market.  I liked them although I would not rush out to get them again.  My husband did not like them at all--he thought they were too hard and had an after-taste.  A friend thought they were good but she is really love the flavor of pomegranate.  So if you like pomegranate and don't mind a chewier twist, this on eis for you.

This candy just tastes fruity. I notice that the last two ingredients on the label (the smallest component of the product) are pomegranate juice concentrate and licorice root extract. There is more citric acid than pomegranate or licorice, and, elderberry extract precedes citric acid. I think that the citric acid gives the candy a bit of tang, but the overall flavor is more elderberry than pomegranate or licorice.This licorice is good enough that I ate the entire 5-oz. package. I didn't notice any after taste, as mentioned by other reviewers. They just tasted like soft, chewy, sweet, fruity licorice - - not bad, but nothing exciting or wonderful.Concerning the organic aspect, the two major ingredients are called organic: wheat flour and sugar.
