The 4th ingredient, tapioca syrup, is also organic. That's nice and makes me happier than if nothing were organic. But, we're really dealing with candy here, junk food to be eaten in small quantity. So, I can't get too worked up about how organic the contents are.

Good tasting licorice in a hard-to-find flavor.  I especially like that it is organic.  It's scary these days reading the long list of ingredients of various foods, many of which are man-made additives that I cannot even pronounce.  I think a lot of the "artificial" foods I consume are wreaking havoc with my poor stomach these days.  That is not the case with this organic licorice.  I would recommend this product.

I'm a fan of many of the Newman's Own products and the philosophy behind them. The fact that the company has donated so much of its earnings to charities is a big plus for me. I wish more corporations were so inclined.Pomegranate Licorice Twists are a tasty addition to the Newman's Own line. They really captured the essence of pomegranate in these twists, something that's not so easy to do. While I enjoy the taste, I found them a little tough, even though the "best before" date on my package is for March 2012. I expected them to be a little softer, but the chewiness didn't hinder my enjoyment of the product overmuch. However, it did cause them to get stuck in my teeth. It was a while after eating before the last traces of these twists were dissolved.Here's a list of the ingredients:Organic Wheat Flour, Organic Sugar, Corn Syrup, Organic Tapioca Syrup, Vegetable Glycerin, Sunflower Oil, Elderberry Extract, Citric Acid, Natural Flavor, Pomegranate Juice Concentrate, Licorice Root Extract.The twists are part of Newman's Own Organics division, started by Nell Newman. Organic is great, but it translate into a costlier product. Comparable Strawberry Twist Twizzlers are about half the price and are fewer calories per piece, yet have half the iron and protein of the Pomegranate Twists. Twizzlers taste about as good and are softer too. Consumers must decide for themselves if it is worth a premium price for a snack product very similar to the competition. If you value (mostly) healthy ingredients and enjoy exotically flavored licorice, then it just may be worth it to you.~ Kort

This was an interesting twist:  The kids loved this one more than the adults.  You could pop-psychologize that one to death (children open-minded vs. adults unable to let go of preconceived ideas of what "licorice" is supposed to be), or we could just have weird kids.  In any case, the reviews (over an empty package) went something like this:Adult 1:  "A little unorthodox, but overall I like 'em."Adult 2:  "They taste like medicine and I didn't finish mine."Teen:  "They're good.  A little weird... but good."Kid 1 (age 8):  "I really, really like them."Kid 2 (age 2):  "..."  (Mouth was full of licorice.)The flavor and texture IS different from the corn-syruped red stuff that we're used to.  If you or your Licorice Lovers wouldn't be able to get past that, click "Helpful" below and move along.  It's not different to the point of unrecognizable, like many "all-natural" products, however.  These licorice sticks are smoother and more dense than traditional licorice, appealingly chewy, and the pomegranate flavor adds a bit of a twist.  They are all-natural (impressively no artificial colors) and you'll be able to read and understand all the ingredients, assuring you that you'll not be ingesting anything that once was drilled out of an oil field.  They've even got a couple of grams of fiber per serving.  AND, all of Newman's Own profits go to charities.Those are a couple of facts that you can feel undeniably good about.

Good Old Paul Newman, not only was he one of the greatest actors ever to grace cinema, he also created his own line of food products.  Sure tons of people in the entertainment business create products for the masses, but it really seems like Paul Newman's food products have done quite well, despite his passing a few years ago. The product of Newman's that I am most familiar with are the salad dressings, they are great.  So I was interested and somewhat eager to try "Newman's Own Licorice", once I saw this product.The flavor in question is pomegranate and this candy is made with organic sugar.  I have some mixed feelings about this product. I want to say first and foremost it is much healthier than most candy out there.  There aren't a million ingredients and the ones that are present can be pronounced.  Also a serving size is five pieces at 130 calories, which I don't think is bad at all.As for the taste, well that is a different tale altogether.  I really don't taste pomegranate in this candy.  The licorice doesn't have a bad taste, per se, yet it isn't exploding with flavor. As for the size of each piece, well it is smaller than your average piece of licorice.  The package itself is also on the tiny size. Each bag is only 5oz, so this equates to a pricey product.Overall, I think the ingredients, serving size and health awareness of this product make it a worthy item.  However, the taste left a little to be desired.  I would eat this product again, but wouldn't go out of my way to find it.

When it is time for an adult licorice, have a Newman's Own.I used to eat packs of licorice as a kid, usually while staying up late watching movies and playing Monopoly.  Well, those days are over. I can't eat a pack of licorice anymore. For one, I would never fall asleep and I would put all of that sugar straight on to my gut.  But it is also that my taste buds are just a bit - a little bit - more mature. I don't like to eat something with all kinds of bizarre ingredients and a chemical aftertaste.  I don't trust a product that looks like plastic and seems to have an odd resin coating.These are worth the calories, and you don't have to regret it later. The flavor of these chews is just so much better than TwizXXX or SwitXXXX. The sweet, dark and tart flavor of the pomegranate is delicious.  It is a genuine flavor. It is also a very substantial chew. You can chew on one of these for quite some time.My wife has no fond memories of licorice. "I can't stand those," she says, when I point to a pack of twizXXX in the candy aisle. "I won't eat them." She means it. But she loved these. She thought that they had more of a cherry taste, albeit a tart cherry.

Newman's has achieved the perfect texture and chewiness of classic licorice, but with a nice flavor twist. The pomegranate tastes real, not overly sweet. It even has a slight bitter note, like real pomegranate. A nice organic treat for classic licorice lovers.

column9: Great for me but not for the Kids!
column10: I enjoyed these licorice twists. Being the first Organic licorice i will order, i was not sure if it would be different from the licorice i was used to or not. As far as i could tell there was no difference. It has the nice chewy texture that makes licorice unique. The flavour is also quite good.Being organic means it should be a healthier option too. I gave it 4 stars because my children don't like it. They took a taste and stayed off the entire pack. So i guess my kids must have noticed a difference but they could not explain to me what the difference was.So, while i consider it good for adults, note that buying it for children might not work.

you know how when you bite into a nice piece of tasty fruit licorice? that exquisite moment when the citrus hits the taste buds and you know that the soft chew soon to follow will release more flavor?that's what you'll get with this pomegranate licorice!thank heavens that Amazon only sent a small bag, 'cause there is no way a big stash would last very long in the casa!this is some good stuff!

I remember, as a little kid, peeling pomegranates by hand - yellow flesh hiding ruby red jewels. Amazing that the authentic flavor of this fruit, densely packed with Vitamin C, has been infused into licorice! It tastes like the "real" thing - without the work. Made with pomegranate juice, and with a great texture, these twists are awesome.

If you're interested in knowing what really good licorice tastes like--buy this!  The flavor is great and the texture is very smooth.  I was a bit concerned because I read earlier reviews that said the licorice was harder than normal licorice.  I found the opposite to be true!

column4: J. W. Kennedy "in statu uiae et meriti"
column10: Chewy "licorice" twists, similar to Twizzlers or Red Vines but made with all-natural ingredients.  The texture is exactly what I expected: sort of resilient and gummy, sticks to my teeth.  The flavor is mystifying ... I'm not familiar enough with pomegranates to tell if it really tastes like one, but it does taste really good - sort of like black raspberry mixed with plum.  It's an unidentifiable fruitiness that resembles the taste of "Mr. Pibb" soda on my palette.  Smells nice too.  It's been a long time since I had Twizzlers but these Newman's twists seem to be less sweet than I remember for this type of candy.  I like them more than I thought I would.

I can highly recommend Newman's Own Organic Pomegrante Licorice Twists!!  Many folk are now turning to pomegrante to lower cholesterol and this is a tantalizing, tasty treat of a healthy pomegrante product.  Portable, no need to refrigerate or heat and delicious on-the-go snack.  A good chew for the pool, lunch box, movies or desk drawer. I am looking forward to trying other flavors.

I have always loved flavored licorice, but have stopped eating them because of their poor nutritional value.  Newman's Own Pomegranate Licorice twists are an answer to my quest for a nutritious sweet.  The pomegranate flavor is very pleasant and real.  The texture of the licorice is smooth and moist. (It doesn't taste like sugary plastic.) Each serving of these organic sweets contain significantly less amounts of sodium than its competitors, and significantly more iron and protein.  The carb to sugar ratio is 3:1 instead of the usual 2:1.  The licorice actually contains dietary fiber!  While this will not be a frequent treat, it is definitely on my list of healthy snack alternatives...which I am continually building.Barbara Lynette PetersAuthor of:  Adulterous HeartAdulterous Heart

Like ever. This Licorice is delicious and didnt last long once i got it home.I find ones like red vine to be overpowering, this one isnt super sweet so thats nice.. It has a very good flavor and i wish more companys made it. I like that its organic. These really are great and i will for sure be buying more. Highly recommended!

I was a little disappointed in the Newman's Own Organics Pomegranate Licorice Twists.  The flavor was just okay and they were quite chewy. I have had lots of licorice that was easier to chew.  They left a slight after-taste which was not all that pleasant.  In fact, it was almost a little bitter.I do like licorice, and I was expecting the pomegranate to be better, but this would not be something I would purchase again.

column9: Nice alternative to traditional licorice flavors
column10: I'm a lover of both red and black licorice - organic or not is not a sticking point for me but a nice bonus if that's how the product is made.I found these pomegranite flavored licorice twists to be a nice refreshing alternative to the traditional licorice flavors of red and black.  The pomegranite had a sweet flavor with a hint of tartness that was enjoyable, and I found the texture to be just right, soft yet chewy and firm.While these might be a bit pricier than most other licorice brands, if you're looking for something a little different, or as a special treat I think these are worth the splurge.  The fact that they are organic, and have Paul Newman's name on it are a good indication of quality, although I was rather disappointed to read on the back of the package that these are made in Mexico.

As far as candy goes, this is a little on the pricey side, coming out to about $2.67 ($2.27 with subscription discount) per 5-oz pack, which nets you about 17-20 4" pieces. That said, the quality definitely stands up to the price. The flavor is good but not overpowering, the licorice is chewy but not mushy, and it leaves no aftertaste, unlike other pomegranate-flavored foods I've had. The fact that it's organic and healthier than other licorice is a bonus.My one, albeit small, complaint is that the packaging isn't resealable. Twenty pieces is a lot to eat in one sitting - in fact, the package has about 3.5 serving in it. With some bending, though, the package fits in a standard Ziploc sandwich bag (problem solved!).Also note that these candies have expiration dates. It's not that you have to eat them as soon as you get them, but I know some people like to buy in bulk and hide the stuff in the pantry for a year - I wouldn't do that with these.

I usually love the Newman's Own products and I had high expectations for the Pomegranate Licorice.  I found the candy to be bland, tough and sort of weird tasting.  Not at all a pomegranate flavor.  One good thing is that these are relatively low-calorie and fat-free, so they can be a satisfying answer for a sweet tooth if you're watching your weight.

Organic licorice in a totally unique flavor..  * sweet w/o being overly sweet.  * Low in both fat and suger  * Low Cal only 130 per serving  * Chewy and light with a nice welcoming fruity flavor.Who wouldnt want this yummy chewy snack thats fun to have around and a prefectly lovely without being overly indulgent treat.
One thought the texture was a bit too hard, one thought the texture was a bit too soft, one thought the texture was just right. All agreed the flavor was great.

I like licorice.  I like the idea, at least.  Usually the licorice I find is too hard, too squishy, smells great but has no actual flavor (twizzlers), makes me sick to my stomach, and/or has ingredients I would never want to ingest.  Newman, that mad magician, has created a product that has none of those problems, and tastes pretty good!The texture is good, a bit harder than perfection, but still good.  The twists are sweet, but not overpoweringly sweet.  Best of all, they actually have flavor, and a very good pomegranate flavor at that!  They're still candy, in this case consisting of flour and various sugars, but at least it's nothing extremely unhealthy.Overall this product did not disappoint and I would recommend it to licorice fans.

I'm not much of a candy eater but these pomegranate twists are much more tempting than standard licorice. Organic is great but it still has sugar and corn syrup. Don't get the idea this is health food, just because it comes from Newman's Own. However, just about everyone deserves some wasted (or waisted) calories now and then. These are small and relatively better for you than most... so go ahead and indulge.I took the package into work. They were gone in a couple of minutes with lots of rave reviews, including my own.

Newman's Own Pomegranate Licorice has a very pleasant bite, both in texture and flavor. The twists are robust in size, not chewy, but rather have a snappiness in texture that creates good mouth feel. There is no oily residue coating the mouth after eating a twist. The flavor of the candy is almost tart, very pleasing. Thoroughly enjoyed this as a mid-afternoon treat!

I usually like my licorice to be "licorice" flavored but Newman's Pomegranate Twists are a step above Vines & Twizzlers in the taste department.  To me Red Vines always tasted, well, Red.  The Pomegranate Twists have a pleasant and distinct taste that can be picked out blindfolded or in a dark movie theater.  A serving size is 5 pieces yielding only 130 calories yet there is only .5g of fat and very low sodium.  Best yet, there is some fiber in them there Twists.  The price is actually quite a bit higher than the competition but I guess you get what you pay for.  (And some of the profits go to Newman's charities).  I think I may sneak some of these in to my next visit to the Cineplex.

First, I love the packaging! It really caught my eye, giving it an old-fashioned twist.  When I first opened the package, the smell was just heaven and the taste was even better.  A chewy stick full of flavor.  The pomagrante flavor I have never tried in licorice before but I'm a new fan.  My husband, on the other hand, thought it tasted like medicine, but still took another piece. It reminds me of the old-fashioned licorice and I would definitely buy this.  I want to try the tangerine next! The only gripe I have is that I wish the package was resealable.  Once you open it, it's hard to preserve the freshness without putting in a ziploc or other container.

It's not bad. My son is picky and didn't like the fruity scent. My daughter was turned off by the scent at first, but then she said it was good. It's soft and chewy, not rubbery. It doesn't stick to the teeth too badly, and it's not overly sweet. It's really not bad at all. I like it better than traditional red licorice and a thousand times better than black licorice. I'm very picky about my candy, though. I wouldn't go out of my way for it.

These had a nice flavor, not overly sweet like the ones we ate as kids.  They contain no HFCS or artificial flavors.  The texture is like traditional licorice, just chewy enough.  I do not eat a lot of sweets, but these were quite enjoyable.

My favorite candy is licorice and this goes above and beyond the "normal" stuff you pick up in the candy aisle.  Most of what you buy just taste like sugar and chemicals while this one has no funny after taste.  I tried the pomegranate which is supposed to have antioxidant properties.  I really had to try hard not to eat the whole thing in one sitting. The best thing about this licorice is that there is real licorice used, which is really rare.  The natural taste of the licorice enhances the pomegranate flavor and doesn't overwhelm it.  I can't wait to try the other flavors.

I love licorice, but I have to admit that my "go-to" licorice is definitely Twizzlers. But, when I heard about this intriguing flavor, I had to try it. And I am glad that I did! It was really tasty! Not overpoweringly sweet, or too overwhelmingly fruity, the balance of licorice flavor and pomegranate fruit was quite perfect. They are also, unlike Twizzlers, already in a perfect straw style, ready to spruce up a summery lemonade as a fun licorice straw! I definitely am not interested in sampling the other flavors.The only downside is that they are rather sticky, both to the touch and to the teeth after eating. These would not be possible for people with braces or fragile dental work! But the strong-toothed will definitely enjoy them!
I love this stuff and it's totally addicting! The big difference is the flavor, totally lacking in the nasty chemical taste that most licorice candy has. I highly recommend it!

I really enjoyed the pomegranate flavored licorice. It had a pronounced and interesting taste.  The quantity in the package made easy to share and being organic makes it healthy then the usual candy.  The only problem I would have is the price, but I would certainly try the other flavors.

Classic licorice this is not. If you're looking for true licorice, a European or Australian brand is better suited to traditional tastes.For you Red Vines lovers, red pomegranate licorice will also be an adjustment in taste and texture. I am a Red Vines fan and when I opened the package, I was disheartened to see what looked like Twizzler-style licorice. I won't really go into my hatred of Twizzler brand "licorice," but suffice to say, when I saw the shiny thin ropes of candy, I didn't know if I should even bother trying it.It took a few bites, but my mouth adjusted and now I like it quite a bit. The flavor hints at pomegranate, but if I took a blind taste test, I'd probably never be able to identify the flavor. The texture is a bit like Twizzlers, but it's fresh and actually tastes like food (unlike Twizzlers, which taste like raspberry plastic.) The fruitiness comes through slowly, so take a moment. No artificial colors or flavors, uses organic sugar. These features had minimal impact on me, because it is a processed food at the end of the day. Still, I liked. I might go for these instead of the Vines at the movies. A good alternative to my old standby. Recommended.

I'm a fan of the entire line of Newman's products. This licorice is slightly softer and easier to chew than other major brands. The pomegranate flavor is original and, I thought, quite good. My one disappointment is that, while the sugar used is organic, there is regular corn syrup used.

I got ahold of Newman's own Pomegranate Licorice and was amazed at the taste.  I love licorice, especially the 'unexpected' flavors. Usually its a blueberry or a strawberry, the occasional peach.Leave it to Newman's Own to come up with Pomegranate. if you are considering buying, I highly recommend it. The flavor is solid (pops nicely in the mouth), the consistency is soft (as opposed to break-your-teeth-twizzler hard) and the packaging kept it quite fresh.  All in all, a win all the way around.From a dietary standpoint, here's what was on the packaging (incomplete, refer to the packaging for complete nutrition facts):Serving size : 5 (there's 15 in the bag so 3 servings)Calories  : 130 Calories from fat 5Sodium  : 5mgTotal Fat  : .5g (1%)Total Carb  : 32g (11%)Protein  :  2gHope this helps!  It was pretty delicious!

column9: My kids liked it, I didn't
column10: I tried this product as did my children, who ended up devouring the entire bag. I had one piece and let me tell you, that was enough for me.  It was soft and chewy, which was good.  Unlike regular licorice that is hard, I really did like the fact that this was kind to your teeth.  The taste was ok, at first, but then it left a really bad after taste in my mouth.  It was just kind of weird.  I liked that this product was made with healthy ingredients, but I didn't like the yucky after taste.  Overall though, as far as my kids go, this is a healthier treat (as compared to pure candy with unwanted perservatives) that they actually like.  Because of that, I did appreciate this product more.

These are so good, and a nice change with the flavored licorice rather then just the red or black you get at the store. I tried these through the vine program, but will buy them again. My son loves them as well!!

column9: Interesting flavor, good quality licorice. Better than Twizzler.
column10: I liked this product quite a bit.  It is a significantly higher quality licorice than typical "Twizzler" fare, and it has a unique tasty flavor.  It also melts in your mouth, which is kinda neat.  Overall I like it quite a bit and would recommend it if you enjoy licorice for both the unique flavor and quality licorice.

If you like licorice, you're bound to like Pomegranate Licorice, a new flavor from Newman's Own Organics. And as candies go, it's fairly healthy with little fat and sodium and not too many carbs. As you would expect from the Newman folks, it's all natural with no artificical flavor or colors. It is simply delicious.In addition to pomegranate, you can get this candy in black, strawberry and  and tangerine as well.If you are looking for items made in the U. S., you will have to look someplace else, however, as the wrapper indicates it was made in Mexico.

column9: tastes very good -- but how good is it?
column10: They're very delicious, so much so that you have to resist eating them all in one sitting.  I ate them over two days.But how healthful are they? They're marketed as healthful. Organic. No artificial colors or flavors.  That's all good.My biggest sticking point is that the ingredients list corn syrup. Perhaps that's not as bad as high fructose corn syrup, but I still don't think corn syrup is too healthful.  That's why I'm deducting a star.Here's a full list of ingredients:  Organic Wheat Flour, Organic Sugar, Corn Syrup, Organic Tapioca Syrup, Vegetable Glycerin, Sunflower Oil, Elderberry Extract, Citric Acid, Natural Flavor, Pomegranate Juice Concentrate, Licorice Root Extract.Serving size: 5 pieces.  130 calories per serving.  (That's 26 calories per twist.)"About 3.5" servings per container.They taste good, if you don't mind the sugar and corn syrup.
This licorice is addictive!  The taste is original and fresh.  What I love the best is the after taste-it leaves you wanting more!A Winner!

Wow.  What an improvement on the old red licorice!  The pomegranate juice, combined with the elderberry extract makes for a truly tasty treat.I used to relish eating the first stick of traditional red licorice, but by the time I'd finished, the artificial flavoring in that one stick alone had turned my stomach.  Not so with these.  A real quality product, as is typical with Newman's Own Organics.My only suggestion would be in improving packaging -- it would be nice to have a resealable package so that these don't go stale, get tough, or lose their intense flavor after being opened.  Opening the package for the first time releases an incredibly intense aroma, and I'd hate for that to fade over a few days.  Not that big a deal, though, and these are just leaps and bounds better in taste than any red licorice candy I've ever eaten.  Fantastic product!

Newman's own Organic Licorice has the taste and texture of old fashioned licorise so hard to find now.  Beyond being good candy it is not only free of things which are bad for you and actually contains several which are good for you! Licorice is a known anti-inflammatory, as is elderberry, and ingredient seldom found in American food products but widely used in Europe is also an anti-infammatory and has recentl7y been found to have anti-viral properties as well.  It also contains fruit and some sugar (not high fructose corn syrup!) as well as some corn syrup (natural, not chemically altered).  I am always happy to find a product I feel good about buying and good giving my kids.  In addition to making healthy and safe products, Newman's philnpthropy is reason enough to support the brand.  This, however, is not something that I would buy out of any any sense of altruism.  Even if you don't care about what you put in your body, or the this of the company producing your food, this is about the best licorice you can get without going to a gourmet store, ethnic market or importing it yourself.  Off to see if Amazon has this available on subscription (though having it around all the time could prove a bit dangerous)!

Has a taste in near red licorice but I like this a tad better.  The problem is that I don't find red licorice that good to begin with -- I'm more of a black licorice person.  It's nice that this is organic and used natural sugar, note.  Also, I shared this with my co-workers.  About 50% enjoyed it, 25% thought it was disgusting, and another 25% thought it was just okay.  Packaging is nice with shorted sticks than conventional licorice packages.  Five sticks is 130 calories.  Contains 4% calcium, 6% iron, and 1% sodium for daily percentage.

column9: Organic Ingredients and Tangy Pomegranate Licorice Chew
column10: Newman's Organic Pomegranate tastes a bit like a tangy twizzler.  They are delicious: each twist is about 4" long and 5 pieces come in at about 130 calories. There are about 20 pieces per pack.  So these candies a great little pick-me-up for my desk drawer.For those of you interested in the organic aspect of Newman's Own, the good news is that the main ingredients are certified organic.  I appreciated that the 3 of the first four ingredients are certified organic (Organic Wheat Flour, Organic Sugar, & Organic Tapioca Syrup).  There is a distinction between organic and "natural" labels on products. Organic certification involves rigorous inspection to make sure the food source is pesticide-free, hormone-free, among other things.  The remaining ingredients were ones that I felt comfortable with eating (Corn syrup, Vegetable Gycerine, Sunflower oil, Elderberry extract--which is great for the stomach--, citric acid, Natural flavor, Pomegranate juice, and Licorice Root extract--also great for stomach ailments).To be clear, organic or otherwise, it is candy. And it has plenty of sugars in it.  But for me, when I'm dragging in the middle of a long day at work, a little piece of candy helps even out my blood sugar and holds me over until I can get home and eat dinner.The distinct flavor of Pomegranate comes through in these tastey licorice twists.  If you're looking for a candy that is a little different but still delicious, I would suggest these Pomegranate twists.  If you like twizzlers, Newman's Pomegranate twists taste even better and their organic source materials mean that you are eating higher-quality foods.

Newman's Own has branched out quite a bit into different types of organic foods since it's beginning, most with a good degree of success. Unfortunately, I can't say the same about this licorice. I am addicted to licorice (yes, even black licorice) and the thought of a pomegranate flavor was pretty cool, since I really like that fruit. So I can say the concept was better than the actualization.This licorice is a bit tough, and doesn't seem to have a very strong flavor. There is a bit of tart pomegranate, but I'm not sure that most people would be able to identify the fruit in a blind taste test. However, the flavor was good enough to keep me eating. What wasn't very good was the after-taste. I'm not sure what in the licorice would cause it, but it hits fairly quickly and does not fade very fast. It's sort of bitter, and is not very pleasant. The semi-good news (I suppose) is that it does not increase with the consumption of more licorice - it just stays constant, there in the background.I haven't tried any other flavors of their licorice (if they have any) to know if there is an after-taste with those as well, or if it's something to do with the pomegranate flavor. But I can say with some certainty that I will not be buying this licorice of my own accord.

column9: Good quality licorice, but the Pomegranate flavor is not for me!
column10: I was excited to try these and when they arrived in the mail I opened the package, closed my eyes and got a whiff of an almost medicinal smell.  The weather is quite hot now, and the package was warm when I opened it so that might have contributed to the smell. The texture was quite nice, chewy, not hard. The taste, however, did not appeal to me and the licorice did have an aftertaste that I did not care for. I liked the packaging, the size of the licorice, and the amount contained within the package - I just did not care for the Pomegranate flavor and would like to try some of the other ones available.I also wish it was made in the USA instead of Mexico, but I have to think that because of the reputation of Newman's Own products that it is being made under the strictest of regulations. That being said, I still wish it was made in the USA.  I was surprised to see that it wasn't when I looked at the packaging.

column4: D.M. (Lover of all things Heart) "laugh a lot...
column10: Simply put, this pomegranate licorice is really tasty and yummy, it's actually some of the best licorice I have tasted. I love its great pomegranate taste, and the fact that it is organic is a nice added bonus. If I were rating this solely on taste, I would give it *5* stars. But then I looked at the price... I mean I am lucky that I got offered this for free thanks to vine, but what about the normal costumer? So I simply have to point out that I feel that the price is expensive for a 5 oz bag, and that's why I can't give it 5 stars.In the end, this pomegranate licorice is one delicious treat!

As a consumer I make a point at eating quality food and care about what I put in my body. I search out organic and I am willing to pay the price for it.I am an avid buyer of Newman's Own products, and like their other products. The pomegranate was high quality and tasty.Compared to the major brand licorice, Newman's own pomegranate has 10g of sugar and 2g of protein compared to 18g and 1.3g respectively. The first ingredient in Newman's own is Organic Wheat Flour while the other licorice is corn syrup.The taste of the Pomegranate licorice is strong and sweet. The Elderberry added is more pronounced than the pomegranate. Non-organic corn syrup is in the product(third ingredient).I can taste the quality in the product and recommend it.

It is not Australian licorice, maybe it was the flavor - pomegranate - but very tasty all the same.  I would buy this, although I question any health benefits from the pomegranate, seriously.  It's the trendy thing for the early 2010's me thinks.  It is fine candy, short pieces.  Australian was the best I have ever had.  I can't help keep thinking of Earth Shoes with the pomegranate, but with the Newman's name, I figured it to be very good, and it is.  It is without question the best pomegranate I ever ate.  I ate the whole bag in about 1/2 hour, yeah, that good. Profits are shared or given I believe, that is good.

These have a softer flavor than what I was expecting. Guess I was expecting something similar to black licorice. I really like the fact that they are organic and are therefore healthier for us when we are wanting a snack.Brandy really liked them when I shared some with her, she kept asking for more. She said it was a unique twist on the flavor, very yummy. I would have to agree with that assessment.Actually, it's a nice sized package, perfect for two people who are wanting to enjoy a healthy snack together.

I really wanted to try these. I love pomegranate and it is truly a very difficult flavor to nail. And I must admit that these do not exactly do the flavor justice. But what it does do right is that it has a linger flavor of pomegranate that seems very natural. Newman's licorice does use concentrated pomegranate juice, and once you get it going, the flavor sneaks up ... and you suddenly find yourself wanting more, almost needing it. It is deceptively refreshing.

I'm a fan of both the late, great Paul Newman and his Newman's Own line of organic food products, if only because the profits from the latter are donated to various charities. It's my understanding that the profits are considerable and I would have to assume that this is due to the fact that so many of the products actually TASTE good; the ingredients are not only organic but are responsibly selected to yield results that are both delicious and as healthful as possible (bear in mind that most of the line consists of snacks and such and that no one is suggesting they should constitute the bulk of one's nutritional intake). Newman's Own Organic Pomegranate Licorice Twists are no exception.One can't get too lyrical about something as prosaic as twist candy but this one really is good. The flavors used are natural and a number of the ingredients used are organic. Please note that corn syrup and HFCS are NOT synonymous and that the inclusion of the former (for chewiness) shouldn't be confused with the latter. The twists taste a lot better than Twizzlers, that's for sure and the texture is licorice perfection: very soft and chewy, even after leaving them in the open package for a few days. My only complaint is that I wish the flavor was both a bit more intense and tart, then I'd rate it "perfect."I have to admit that I wasn't thrilled to read that this product is manufactured in Mexico. I'm sure there are reasons for this, probably economic, but it doesn't make me happy. However, at least it's the same continent so perhaps I shouldn't be slug about it. Regardless, it's still a good product and likely to be enjoyed by kids as well as grown-ups. 4½ stars bumped up to 5.

"Pomegranate Licorice Twists" by "Newman's Own Organics"...  WONDERFUL, GREAT TASTING!  Nice, flexible `almost' soft, very pliable.  Sticks into one's teeth just like the others.  MUCH BETTER than that  red licorice found in that plastic tub offered by the BIG BOX discount stores.  Your teeth can easily cut through this stuff; you don't have to twist it around nor risk ripping your teeth out when you take a `chaw' out of it.  WOW, I just ate 4 of these in one sitting!  The Pomegranate flavor is REALLY flavorful - I wasn't expecting it (also available in Black, Strawberry, & Tangerine - I can't wait to get a hold of those, too).  It is packaged as `organic' - it has organic wheat flour, organic sugar, and organic tapioca syrup, with other suff.... `certified organic by Oregon Tilth' even though it is made in Mexico - may be organic, but it tastes GREAT!  I'm not a chemist so I don't know whether or not that `improves' this treat's flavor or not, or even if it is any healthier -- but the strong, in-your-face, I can tell it's activating my taste buds -- Pomegranate flavor really works for me.  My parents liked them, too.  Good high quality flavor.

I received a pack of Newman's Pomegranate Licorice today.  They are curiously addictive.  I thought the flavor was not that strong, but definitely hit the taste buds.  In the past, I've had licorice that left an aftertaste, but this one did not do that.  They are not high sugar, provided that you do not gobble the entire pack in one sitting.  I do need to say that I have never been a big fan of licorice, flavored or otherwise.  That is why this orginal treat surprised even myself.  I'd definitely recommend it.  Jim Fargiano, author of: The Spoken Words of Spirit: Lessons From The Other Side
Like most Newman products these were good. I really enjoyed them. And I will buy them again. They have a great taste that is enjoyable.

I love pomegranate and I love licorice so I was very excited to try this product. It is very delicious - good flavor and texture - sweet enough but not too sweet.  I'm not sure if I would be able to guess the flavor "pomegranate" if I didn't know that was the flavor - but I feel like I can taste it.  This is not Twizzlers (not that there's anything wrong with Twizzlers!) - it reminds me more of "Australian style" licorice.

I've had many of Newman's Own products & have, for the most part, liked them all.  I love that Newman's Own is totally organic & will continue to buy their products.When I first put the licorice twist in my mouth, It tasted much like any other licorice twist.  Mid way through the twist I got a burst of flavor I couldn't identify.  The package says Elderberry Extract,  Pomegranate juice concentrate, etc.  I didn't care for it, in act, the flavor lingered in my mouth for a short time afterward.  Personally I wouldn't buy again.I will, in fact, try another of their licorice flavors.

column9: Tasty, sweet, brings back memories of childhood
column10: My wife and I use various Newman's Own products regularly, so I thought this might be a good choice for a relatively healthy "cheat". First of all, the taste is great! It's reminiscent of the good old red licorice you may remember as a kid, but has a subtle pomegranate flavor that is quite nice. I set out to taste just a few sticks and ended up eating almost the whole pack--very addictive.For those with wheat allergies, the first ingredient in these is organic wheat flour, followed by "organic sugar" which is too generic a description and could mean anything from raw cane juice to processed sucrose from organic sources. Don't overdo it and you won't overload yourself with too much sugar. The rest of the ingredients follow: Corn Syrup (beware), Organic Tapioca Syrup, Vegetable Glycerin, Sunflower Oil, Elderberry Extract, Citric Acid, Natural Flavor, Pomegranate Juice Concentrate, Licorice Root Extract. That's a lot of different sugar sources, and the "Corn Syrup" is something to be wary of.All in all, it's a slightly healthier sweet treat than buying the usual dime store or movie theatre red licorice, but not much. It does taste very good, and don't be surprised to eat the whole pack once you open it (15 in a pack). Recommended, but watch the sugar intake.

Licorice is a weakness; hard to open a package and not keep continually returning for "just one more."  Newman's organic pomegranate, in that regard, is pretty hard to resist.  Very tasty little treat for adults and kids alike, and the fact that it's organic makes it even more enjoyable.  Tasted a hint of ripe berries, in addition to the pomegranate, and I'm not sure I would have easily identified the flavor without the packaging.

column9: This product is not for me....
column10: I do like licorice.  I do usually like Paul Newman products.  I feel that they can be counted on to be quality products.  However this product was not to my taste at all.  Nice packaging.  Licorice was fresh.  Perhaps a different flavor would be better.  I like pomegranates, I just don't care for the taste of this product.

Newman's Own Pomegranate Licorice Twists are a unique candy, to be sure. I'd never heard of a pomegranate-flavored licorice before, so I was anxious to try it. First the good: The pieces are firm and chewy (I like a little substance to my licorice), they're a good size (about 2 inches shorter than a Twizzler), and the pomegranate flavor is nice. Now the bad: While the flavor is good while you're eating the licorice, a bitter aftertaste lingers (I had to either immediately take a drink or shove another piece of licorice into my mouth to get rid of the aftertaste), and the price is outrageous. At 53 cents per ounce, this licorice is four times the price of  Twizzlers. Is it four times as good? I don't think so. While I enjoyed trying these licorice twists, I won't be buying them in the future.

column9: Stays With You Long After Eating
column10: I love Pomegranate.  I love licorice.  I love organic foods.  So I thought Newman's Own Organics Pomegranate Licorice Twists would be something I could love too.Wrong!The flavor is good.  The texture is as licorice should be.  But the aftertaste is just too much.For several days after eating this Pomegrante licorice, everything I ate tasted like Pomegrante.  EVERYTHING.  Dr. Pepper had an underlying taste of Pomegrante.  Tacos had an underlying fruity Pomegrante taste.Ugh, too much for me.Unless you really, really, really love the taste of Pomegrante and don't mind it being present in the next 10 meals, then I'd recommend skipping this organic treat.

column9: Not too sweet, not too flavorful
column10: OMG! *Another* Vine review of Newman's Own Pomegranate Licorice Twists?  Yeah...Anywho, I'm going to start off by saying: My wife really likes these.  She finds the flavor prevalent but not overpowering and the sweetness isn't cloying like Red Vines.I'll follow that up by saying: I adore Red Vines, I loathe Twizzlers, and these are somewhere in-between.To the reviewer who wrote:  "they had a kind of weird wheat flavor and heavier texture, which is not the kind of thing you want to taste when you're thinking red licorice" I can only say: I 100% agree. I grab a licorice twist and I want that sweet, chewy Red Vines (or even Black Vines) experience.  These do *not* deliver that.  While they do manage to stick to your teeth, they're not particularly chewy; they're somewhere closer to a crumble than a chew.And I was expecting to be wowed by tart pomegranate flavor.  I was completely let down.  The flavor is mild, at best... and reminds me of pomegranate, but not overly so.Anyway, I'd have rated these 1 star, but since the wifey loves them, I'm upping it to 3. Like Twizzlers?  You'll probably like these.

I'm only an occasional licorice eater, but my dad, who loves the stuff, didn't really care for this.  I found the pomegranate flavor unappealing, though I appreciate the organic nature.  I'll stick to Twizzlers.

Sorry, I'm not a huge licorice fan, but I do love pomegranates.  I was looking for a low calorie treat ... to be used while long distance driving to keep me awake.  I often use beef jerkey for this purpose.  Anyway, the licorice is ok and it does taste somewhat like pomagranate - and NOT like regular red licorice.  That is why I gave it three stars... it is what it's advertised to be and is quite chewy.  However, I really did not like the aftertaste and it made me feel a bit nauseated for an hour after I ate the first one.  This is why I only gave it three stars.Now perhaps I just was due for a stomach ache, but I'll be checking other reviews to see if anyone else had this happen....

I have made pomegranate syrup before and it had about the same flavor as this licorice. The problem with pomegranate is  that when it is cooked (reduced) it changes flavor, becoming somewhat bitter in the process. I was hoping that this product wouldn't show signs of that, but I was wrong.The texture is great and if you like the flavor, then this is a fine product. It boasts being organic and uses sugar instead of high fructose corn syrup (there is corn syrup, just not modified), both are plusses in my book. Plus Newman's own donates profits to charity, another plus.But it is a bit expensive for something made in Mexico. At $40 for 15, 5 oz packs, that's about $8.50/pound. A little high for licorice made outside the country.Bottom line is, I ate the whole thing, so it couldn't be too bad. My daughter thought it was OK, too. But I rated it down for the slightly odd flavor, high price, and unnecessary outsourcing to Mexico.

column9: Yummy, Chewy, Tender, Tasty Pomegranate Licorice
column10: I have been eating R** V**** red licorice since 1975 and I wish they tasted like these Newman's Own Pomegranate Licorice. I was very sorry when they were gone.  Newman's own actually has licorice root extract in it and other tasty ingredients. I was interested in the review that elderberry extract was also included and that it was healthy for you. Since the ingredients are listed on the product's web page, I will give you the Nutrition Facts.Nutrition Facts:[Each package is 5 oz., the serving size is 5 short sticks = 42 grams, approx. 3.5 servings which equals 17.5 pieces? -- I didn't count the sticks before I gobbled them down.)Per serving:Calories: 130Calories from fat: 5Total Fat: 0.5g  1% DVSodium: 5mg 0% DVTotal Carbs: 32g  11% DVDietary Fiber: 2g  8% DVSugars: 10gProtein: 2% DV  Iron 4% DVBased on a 2000 calorie per day diet.All a person can say is how something tastes, would they buy it again and is it a good value.I like the taste, would like to buy it again but feel it is a bit "spendy" as they say in North Central Idaho (expensive).

column4: Ursula K. Raphael "AstraDaemon of The Zombiep...
column10: What's not to like?! It actually tasted ike pomegranate juice, five licorice sticks (reasonable size -- not tiny) are only 10g of sugar (which went over well with the diabetics in the house)...calcium, protein, iron -- even fiber!! As a matter of fact, all three generations enjoyed the treat, the youngest being 5yrs, and the oldest being 61yrs.I just wish I could have tried the black licorice too...guess I will have to buy it! =D

column9: Pomegranate is suprisingly good ... but does take a bit like Fruit Roll-ups
column10: As a reviewer for licorice, I believe myself to be well qualified.  Every trip to the store, I go down the candy aisle, to if nothing else, pause to decide if licorice is on the mental shopping list.  I must admit that I've never seen this offering in any grocery store, but on my next trip to Whole Foods, I'll certainly take a look.Overall, the licorice is quite tasty but not what I would call addictive.  It definitely was fresh and closer to "Twizzler" consistency than "Red Vines".  I usually buy Red Vines that are both tasty and inexpensive.  I believe that the makers of this licorice were aiming for the 1930s type of candy store licorice instead of the mass produced taste of Red Vines.  If you examine the price of 40 dollars (Amazon's listed price) for a total of 75 ounces (pack of 15 x 5 ounces per pack = 75 ounces), you'll quickly see that the price per pound is about $4.25 a pound (16 ounces).  This compared with other higher produced licorices is much more than a 3:1 cost of either Twizzlers or Red Vines.  Clearly, Newman's Own Organics is going for the more discriminating licorice consumer.In summary ...ProsVery tastyFreshDecent consistencyOrganic (although I honestly don't know how big a benefit this is for licorice)ConsMay be costly for the average consumerTastes a bit like Fruit Roll-ups (making it a bit of a Fruit Roll-ups for adults)Happy Eating!

column9: Good texture; only for those who like pomegranate taste
column10: Red Vines are one of my "guilty pleasures." I like pomegranates and miss the tree that supplied them to me in Tucson, long before the pomegranate-as-antioxidant craze. I wasn't expecting some pomegranate taste to assuage my guilt about eating what is one-quarter sugar (while not caring if the sugar derives from organically grown sources), and it didn't.I was hoping that the Pomegranate Licorice Twists would have more pomegranate than anise taste, and they did--even with elderberry juice being higher on the list of ingredients than pomegranate juice. (I don't remember what elderberry juice tastes like, but think the twists take like sugar with some pomegranate. I guess that neither the pomegranates or elderberries are organically grown, nor is the corn used as corn syrup...)The twists are about two bites in length (compared to the three of Red Vines). The soft/chewy balance seem right to me. My Costco plastic casks of Red Vines dry out, and I have no doubt that these would if I let them. (Alas, the packages are not resealable.)I like the twists and the philanthropies of the company. Some have complained of an unpleasant aftertaste. I don't experience this, but my mouth feels a bit dry after eating one or two twists.

Pomegranate is an unusual taste but one that you usually find combined with something else.  However here I found myself wishing it was a different licorice flavor.  It's sweet and tangy...but just one of those tastes that neither wows me or turns me off.  Just an average candy flavor in my book...Reading the package states it is made in mexico which when it comes to food I rather not see...especially on organic labeled items that should have a higher health standard.  Organic here of course just refers to the sugar used.All depends what you're looking for but it isn't something I'd choose again because of where it is made.

Newman's Own Organics Pomegranate Licorice met mixed reviews in our home.Pomegranate has become the new flavor of choice with many products--especially beverages and snack foods. This is due to the increased emphasis on the important of anti-oxidents, the anti-oxident benefits of pomegranate, and the cosumer's desire for the "next new thing" in exciting fruity flavors.Newman's Own Organics authentically brings together both the flavor of licorice and pomegranate. The folks in our home that loved pomegranate enjoyed the taste of this treat. The folks less accustomed to this ancient fruit simply felt the licorice was adequate.Most of the complaints about the licorice had to do with texture. This licorice had a mushy quality, which is disappointing those that like a sturdy chew with their licorice. It is braided, but not tightly braided.All in all, this was a fun snack for us to have, but not something we will be looking to buy more of.

Wow, I'm really sorry I tried this product.  Why?  It's too good!  Now I have to order it in every flavor.  It's that good.  And the ingredients, check this out:  organic wheat flour, organic sugar, corn syrup, organic tapioca syrup, vegetable glycerin, sunflower oil, elderberry extract, citric acid, natural flavor, pomegranate juice concentrate, licorice root extract.  Made in Mexico.  Flavors:  black, pomegranate, strawberry, tangerine.  Oh, boy, I've gotta try them all!  So, Amazon readers, this product is fabulous.  I have never had a Newman's Own product that I didn't love.  Still can't believe Paul Newman isn't here.  What a great guy and a great family to be continuing this wonderful line of products.

I wasn't bowled over by this product and probably won't ever buy it. However, there isn't anything wrong with it and I wouldn't turn it away if I was offered some. I just can't see ever wanting it enough to purchase it or crave it.Positives: Perfect texture and 'bite' for a licorice candy. Just chewy enough without killing your teeth. Good flavor, if a bit medicinal. The organic label is nice however not all the main ingredients are labeled as organic although most of them are. No artificial color or flavor. Very low in fat and not too bad in calories - about 26 per piece.Negatives: The flavor doesn't really say pomegranate to me. It's sweet, kind of fruity and a little bit like medicine instead of candy. The package should be resealable as the contents are larger than a single serving and it's a little on the pricey end of things.
These are really good!  I love that they are organic! With these I don't have to worry about my kids eating candy with things that have all those ingredients I can't pronounce.  Love the flavor, too!

I am a fan of Newman's Organic Products, my food COOP carries many of the products, and we had the President of the Organic Branch, Nell Newman, speak at our COOP meeting. The products are more expensive, but on the whole, well worth the price. However, in this case, I am confused about the price of these delicious chews. Amazon advertises 5-ounce package, pack of 15, for $40.04. That would mean that each licorice piece costs over $1.60 a piece. That seems to me to be an outrageous price.The pomegranate licorice twists are delicious. They are advertised as having 70% organic ingredients. There are no artificial flavors or colors and the color is a dark ruby red, the color of pomegranate. Pomegranate is the fruit of the year, and you will find it in many different products. Each twist has 130 calories as stated on the packaging. My package contained 17 twists, and the package states pack of 15.Chewy and good tasting. These organic pomegranate licorice twists have my stamp of approval, as long as I am not buying.Recommended.  prisrob 07-26-11Newman's Own Organics Organic California Raisins, 15-Ounce Cans (Pack of 6)Newman's Own Organics California Prunes, 12-Ounce Pouches (Pack of 6)

I've only ever had strawberry, regular or black licorice before, so I wasn't sure what to expect from pomegranate (the 'in' flavor of the past couple years, I guess). I thought these tasted okay, but I wouldn't buy them instead of any of the traditional flavors. They were a nice, soft texture yet still satisfyingly chewy (without endangering dental work). I do like the fact that they are made from ingredients I can pronounce and recognize-- they actually have pomegranate in them! I give this a three because if I went to the store and found this product, traditional red, or strawberry, this product would be my third choice to purchase.

column9: tastes nothing like pomegranate. save your money
column10: Newman's Own Organics Pomegranate Licorice Twists taste decent but they just don't taste of pomegranatefor starters, a bitter after taste some foods leave in your mouth - that came first. I had to chew a few more pieces to get that to go away. That was unplesantsecond, they taste nothing like pomegranate. They basically tasted like ordinary red licorice. It's not worth the money. don't bother.

column9: I really like licorice and pomegranates, but this is ho-hum
column10: I was excited to try these once I got a whiff of the contents upon opening the package.  I'm a fan of good licorice...note: Twizzlers are just okay to me.The smell and consistency of this licorice are good, but the flaver is quite disappointing.  It has a very weak taste of Pomegranate and for some reason I got a hint of peppermint in every bite.  Maybe just the way my taste buds interpreted the licorice mixed with a little pomegranate juice (can't be much in there).I like these more than Twizzlers, but I would buy a number of other brands before these.FYI: Below are the listed ingredients and nutrition facts.Ingredients-----------Organic Wheat FlourOrganic SugarCorn SyrupOrganic Tapioca SyrupVegetable GlycerinSunflower OilElderberry ExtractCitric AcidNatural FlavorPomegranate Juice ConcentrateLicorice Root ExtractNutrition Facts---------------Servings per container: About 3.5Calories per serving: 130Total Fat 0.5gSodium 5mgTotal Carbs 32g- Dietary Fiver 2g- Sugars 10gProtein 2g

column9: I did not care for them...
column10: I generally like Newman's Own products and I like licorice a lot.  I am also a fan of Pomegranate so I figured these would be a home run. Though they are made with organic sugar instead of high fructose corn syrup, they still tasted almost sickly sweet, cloying to me.  The texture was very nice and these certainly appear to be high quality, but I simply did not like the way they came together.

I love licorice, so am always eager to try something new. This was just barely OK. Organic is a plus, I guess, but honestly, when I search for treats, organic isn't one of my criteria. Taste is King, then as long as the flavor pops, I look for licorice that is as Natural (i.e. fewest ingredients whose names I can't pronounce) as possible. I have found other (supposed) Natural products to have much more intense flavor than this Newman's product, so this will not be a repeat for me.

column9: Not the way licorice should taste
column10: A few good things about this licorice:- it has a fair taste though a bit removed from the taste of real licorice.- It is made with mostly organic products.The bad (in my opinion):- real licorice should taste like licorice first. Why flavoring it? I did not recognize pomegranate either.My conclusion is that there are already some serious licorice makers, using traditional products out there. So why bother with this product which is not up to par?

I adore licorice and pomegranate so I had high hopes for this... especially since Newman's Own is such a great brand. For me, the licorice just wasn't up to par, especially considering the price. The taste is low key (which I was expecting), but the texture was somewhat greasy/waxy, which was a huge surprise. There was also a bitter aftertaste, which to my friend (who loves black licorice) liked enough to give this candy at C+... but for me the texture ruined it completely. I love the concept, I just hope they continue working on the texture in the future.The packaging, I have to say, is pretty awesome.

I love pomegranate, I love licorice, I love natural and organic things, and I love just about every Newman's product I've ever had. And it looks like a lot of other people love these. To me, these taste like medicine. I think it's the elderberry that's in them. When I'm sick, I drink that stuff like crazy so I think for me, elderberry and medicine are inextricably linked at this point.But really, why is there elderberry in these? I really wanted a nice tart pomegranate flavor and I feel like I can barely taste it. Even my sweets-obsessed 3 year old didn't like these. I'll try the black ones next. Hopefully they are better.

I will say this, the licorice is very flavorful, however, it is really hard to gnaw on. Maybe we got a not so fresh pack. Maybe we're use to softer licorice. To be honest, my sons and I prefer Lucky Country flavored Australian licorice more. That licorice is juicy, soft, and more flavorful than Newman's Own.

This is an interesting product. My advice, if you're looking for an alternative to "candy" licorice or twists, you'll want to avoid this. If you're looking for a better type of licorice, than this product might be good for you.I'd describe this product as "old-fashioned". It seems to be made in a way in which many mass-produced licorice products aren't made anymore. Most interesting are the ingredients: organic wheat flour, organic sugar, elderberry extract, and pomegranate juice concentrate. While "organic" isn't necessarily any more healthy for you than non-organic products, the "wheat flour" is very interesting, and probably helps add the 2g of fiber to each serving.If I had to describe the taste -- I'd say "sour". The first piece you eat will be "curious", but if you eat an entire 5-piece serving (3.5 serving in the package), the flavor actually improves. I do think the use of wheat flour makes them a bit "pasty" or "chalky". And pomegranate isn't necessarily sweet -- so expect a tart experience.Bottom line -- the kids won't like this, but health-conscious adults may.

column9: Difficult to Taste Pomegrenate in These Twists
column10: Looking hard for pomegranate flavor, it was really hard for me to find one in these Mexican made twists. They are just like ordinary licorice twists, that are somewhat sticky, and exorbitantly priced for only "70% organic". Carbohydrate content is 11% in these twists, so these are definitely not healthy. But using "organic" sugar  gives them the excuse to charge preposterous price.

column9: Organic licorice?  You can't be serious!
column10: Seems people will buy anything w/ "ORGANIC" stamped on it these days.  This pomtastic licorice was pretty tasty.  I like Twizzlers.  Ok, I LOVE Twizzlers, but this stuff gives the old mystery mouth chomper a run for it's money.  It's licorice, it's organic.  You feel like there's a benefit to eating it.  Try some, maybe you'll live longer because of it.

column9: GOURMET TWIST ON A CLASSIC PRODUCT
column10: When I was a kid, I loved red and black licorice twists. But that kid never imagined there'd be such a thing as an "organic pomegranate" twist! Thanks to the Paul Newman company ("Newman's Own Organics"), there is now!I'd call this a gourmet twist on a classic product. I got a sample of the pomegranate licorice, and saw that there are Black, Strawberry and Tangerine flavors as well. I'd like to try them all.I would have given this licorice 5 stars - it's tasty - but cut two stars for these reasons:1) there's corn syrup in it - and not organic, either. If you use Paul Newman's good name, and then add "Organic" to the title, you'd better be sure that everything in is either organic, or darn healthy. High fructose corn syrup is not it!The other lost star:2) You have to buy more than $40 worth of one flavor of licorice to get this particular product via Amazon! I never bought $40 worth of licorice in my life.Just so you know, each one of 15 packs you get comes in a plastic wrap pack, about 7 x 5 inches, and the twists within are about 4" long (hard to tell from the picture, right?).The product, by the way, is made in Mexico.If you do go for this, once you tear open a bag, and you don't happen to eat all the twists at one sitting, you had better put them in a ziplock. I left mine open a couple of days, and they dried up.Another quibble: the print on the packaging is so small, even with reading glasses, I can barely make it out - I'd guess the point size is 4 or 5? But there's a lot of unused space on the packaging, so "Newman's Own" - would you please increase the font to 10 or 12???Recommended - with reservations.

I'm not a huge candy fan... a little chocolate here, some licorice there.  That's why I tried Newman's Licorice Twists.Twists have always been a favorite of mine.  They harken back to the day of the Saturday matinee at the local theater.  Unfortunately, most of the twists I find today are heavily sugar laden.  They taste good, but I just know I've eaten far more than I should and it's because of the sweetness.Newman's Organics don't contain nearly the sugar I've found in others which makes them taste a little bland yet they are satisfying.  Like most twists, I could eat a Newman's bag at one sitting, but I find that three or four are enough and I don't feel like I've over-extended my craving. The flavor is not as prominent as other flavors, but I don't mark that as a major fault.You can find cheaper versions of candy twists, and we all know that, after all, candy is candy. On the other hand, try these. They are pretty good and you don't feel quite so guilty.

I didn't think it could get better than T*******'s Strawberry Licorice, but somehow, Newman's Own did it.  These are great...The whole family aged 4 - 41 enjoyed them.  Newman's Own continues to develop quality, trustworthy products, and their licorice seems to be the latest.

column4: Karissa Eckert "Devourer of all books fantasy"
column9: Tastes more like cranberry than pomegranate
column10: I love licorice and was curious to try out some Pomegranate licorice.  I got a bag of this licorice through the Amazon Vine program.The licorice is nicely packaged and the package was easy to open.  Everyone in my family tried a piece of it.The licorice is has a tangy taste that everyone who tried it thought tasted more like canned cranberries than pomegranate.  Then there is a slightly perfumey aftertaste, that wasn't unpleasant but just different.I thought the licorice was different tasting but fine.  The texture is similar to Twizzlers, but slightly tougher.My 4 year old thought is was horrible and refused to eat more than a bit.  My co-workers thought it was interesting, but didn't want more than a small piece.So overall an okay product. I personally like it fine, but probably wouldn't go out of my way to buy it again. If you like the taste of canned cranberries and like licorice you should give it a try.

This is a great product, but I expect nothing less of Newman's Own.  It has a real fruit taste, kind of like fruit leather.  It wasn't too sweet and I like that all they use are organic sugar and such to create this product.  The only problem that I encountered was the fact that a serving size had a slight laxative effect.  I would definiately purchase this again.

If there is such a thing as gourmet licorice, this is it.  These taste like red licorice infused with fruit juice.  I can't say that I necessarily recognized the fruit flavor as distinctly pomegranate- it could just as easily be a berry flavor or other similar fruit.  Still, it makes for a tasty combination.  The result is not too sweet, and a bit firmer and chewier than what I was expecting.

column9: A healthier version of regular licorice candy
column10: I've always loved licorice, so I had to try these. I got the pomegranate flavor and really liked them. They're chewy and not too sweet, but full of flavor. The mostly organic ingredients and real organic sugar instead of corn syrup in other brands of licorice makes them a healthier option. They taste a little like fruit strips in the shape of licorice. The bag doesn't have a way to re-seal it or a ziplock on top, which would have been convenient, but as far as the flavor and taste go, they are something I'd buy again.

column9: A little more Licorice would be nice
column10: The taste and texture of the twistsare very good. I enjoyed this candybut it seemed like a pretty smallamount for a package comparedto Licorice I usually buy at the store.

These are sweet, chewy, and delicious. The pomegranate is a unique, but not too exotic or overwhelmingly sweet flavor.  Because these are organic they didn't leave that slightly chemical taste, like some other red twists I avoid.The whole family loves these, which is why I'm happy they come in a large pack of 15!

column9: Twizzlers for grown-up foodies, perfect candy for an indie theater
column10: As a kid, I loved going to movies and chewing on Twizzlers as soon as the previews started.  It has been a long time since I've had the candy, though, and I haven't been tempted by it for years.  These pomegranate licorice twists, though, are bringing back old cravings by updating them for an adult.  When I first started one of the twists, I was not a fan - I didn't think that the pomegranate flavor blended well with the hit of licorice flavor at the end.  I kept going, though, to put in an honest effort, and I grew to love these strangely addictive little candies.  It's not that the flavors don't blend - it's that they're textured and nuanced, rewarding slow contemplative chewing.  The pomegranate taste is juicy (and trendy, yes), and the spices keep things interesting.  I also like that the package has plenty of short twists, so they're easy to share, and each one isn't too much of a commitment if your friend doesn't enjoy the flavors.

column9: A different twist on red licorice
column10: Tired of the same old red licorice?This may be the refreshing change you seek.The pomegranate licorice twists have the same sweetness and texture of red licorice, but the pomegranate flavor is different.Sweet, chewy and tangy.
This is not the best licorice I have ever eaten, but it gets high marks for not being overly sweet. Still, I've had better.  If you're a pomegranate lover, you may really enjoy this.

Let me start by saying I absolutely love Twizzlers.  These are definitely not Twizzlers!  I've never tasted anything Pomegranate before this.  They do have a nice, sweet flavor.  I like it!  I don't usually "do" organic, I couldn't care less, really, so that doesn't matter to me.  I just wanted to see how they tasted.The texture is a little harder (tougher?) than the aforementioned Twizzlers.  LOL!  This results in more pulling on dental work but they're not so hard that it did any damage to my dental work, and I have alot of that to worry about!  I would definitely buy these, just not on a regular basis.  Kind of a treat with a unique (yummy) flavor!

column4: David L. Poremba "the past in review"
column9: where can I get some more?
column10: This stuff is good!  Tastes like pomegranate, not too sweet. Great licorice texture - chewy, not waxy. Although pomegranate is not a particularly favorite flavor (black is the best), I would not hesitate to buy this at the store. To top it all off, it is organic. Can't wait to try the other flavors....

After enjoying the salsa, spaghetti, and other Newman items, I was expecting something a little more than I got.  First taste is pretty good, but then the after taste kicks in.  Not something I really want to remember.  If you want licorice  then go buy some Twizzlers.

Most of Newman's Own products are delicious. I've been a fan of his pasta sauce for several years, so I was happy to try their Licorice Twists. I typically prefer black Licorice and expect licorice to have at least some licorice flavor, if not a texture that is somewhere between chewy and hard. I found the texture of the Newman's Own Licorice to be overly soft, but find the flavor to be overpoweringly sweet. So much so that the pomegranate flavor is nearly undetectable.

I liked these Newman's Own pomegranate licorice because of their organic ingredients, and wonderful smelling pomegranate fragrance upon first opening the package.  However, I almost couldn't taste the licorice, so it would be a misnomer to call them "licorice".  I also found them a tad too chewy, and more importantly, was disappointed by the addition of corn syrup to its ingredients list.However, they are certainly a wholesome alternative to the artificial feeling and tasting Twizzlers.  Additionally, the pomegranate flavor is a nice alternative to the usual licorice flavor (which I don't particularly like).

Because of the Newman's Own brand reputation and that most of the ingredients are organic, many people may be fooled into thinking this product is healthy to eat.This is *candy*.Okay, now that I've hopefully made it clear that this is not a healthy product to be eating. It does make an enjoyable snack!  The flavor is good and the nutritional profile is not terrible. Enjoying a few of these now and then may be a nice break from an otherwise healthy diet (You are eating healthy right?).The soft chewy texture and nice mild flavor is very enjoyable.I like these, but I wouldn't make a habit out of eating them.

I gave these to several members of my family, because they are licorice connoisseurs. Overall, my family and I agreed that these were really differently flavored, but in a good way. They almost had a deep currant type of flavor. They were still sweet, but had a slightly spicy flavor. They were wonderful.

This is a review of the pomegranate flavor of Newman's Own licorice.Basically the two qualities of a licorice twist are flavor and chew, and this product was above average on both counts, though not superb. The flavor is definitely pomegranate so if you like that flavor, you'll be happy with this. I thought this had a teeny medicinal flavor, but I think that is sometimes true of the flavor anyway. The chew was on the chewy end of the licorice twist range, but not unpleasantly so. The twists are shorter than typical, and each stick is about 25 calories, with zero fat and 5mg of sodium. Made in Mexico with organic ingredients. Based on the success of this flavor I'll definitely try the tangerine.

column9: Very tasty, but contains corn syrup
column10: Taste-wise, these are a huge improvement over the popular brand of red licorice sold today. Newman's Own Pomegranate Licorice is firmer and you can actually taste the real pomegranage flavor. These seem more lightly sweetened than Twizzlers, Strawberry, 16-Ounce Bags (Pack of 6), as well. My only complaint is that this Newman's Own product contains corn syrup for sweetener. So if you are going to eat red licorice, these are tasty, but don't think of them as health food! They are candy.

Just because it says its organic you still have to read labels. As an example Newmans Own 'organic' Pomegranate Licorice twists, say organic on the label and notes 'made with organic sugar'. Then you read the label and its lists : Organic wheat flour, organic sugar, corn syrup,organic tapioca syrup, vegetable glycerin, sunflower oil, elderberry extract, citric acid, natural flavor, pomegranate juice concentrate, licorice root extract. MADE IN MEXICO. Notice how few items are organic. And low and behold made in Mexico is a no go for me.

column4: ChibiNeko "Sooo many books, so little time!"
column10: I was sort of excited to try these because licorice is one of my favorite sweets & I'm always eying up new flavors to try out. This just sort of seemed a natural fit for me as far as a vine review goes.The good thing is that the texture to these are pretty good. It's nice & chewy without being too chewy or too soft. It's a happy medium, although I do recommend that you try to get these as fresh as possible since I can't imagine trying to eat these when they've a little old or have been exposed to air & not stored properly.The bad thing is that these just have this funky aftertaste to them. The basic taste is fine enough. It doesn't taste like pomegranate & normally I'd be OK with this since candy often labels things "watermelon" or "strawberry" when it doesn't taste anything remotely like the fruit. Since this is supposed to be mostly organic & natural, I really expected it to taste more like actual pomegranate. Then there's the occasional weird aftertaste these have to them that's somewhat unpleasant. I can't really explain it but it's not a taste that I'd really care to have in my mouth.One thing I do want to mention is that out of the 11 ingredients in this product, only 3 are organic. That doesn't bother me much, but I know that there are some people who get irritated at how some labels mention "organic" but only a small part of it is actually organic. At that point you really can't call the product organic since it has non-organic product in it. (There's no USDA organic label on this anywhere, if you were wondering, which can only be put on if a certain percentage of the product is organic.) Note that this product didn't have "made with organic ingredients" on it, just "made with organic sugar". The people who label watch for organic products will know what that means. I mention all of this because I know some are very picky about product that have organic anywhere on it.Overall I wasn't really that enthusiastic about this product. It wasn't horrible but I can safely say that I probably won't be buying any of these in the future. I might & I stress *might* try one of the other flavors, but that'd only be if the price was right.EDIT:Updated to say that I won't be buying any of this in the future. The licorice I ate later is really making me feel a little gross. Like another reviewer said, it's just sitting there like a pile of lead & is giving me some pretty bad indigestion. If you have a cast iron stomach (which admittedly mine isn't as strong as it once was but is still pretty good), then you probably won't have a problem with this. This has to be the first licorice product that has remained unfinished in my house ever.

I'm not a particularly "organic" kind of person.  I don't have anything against organic products but I don't seek them out nor am I willing to pay a premium for something that is organic as opposed to other products.  I know a good product though when I experience one.This fruit flavored licorice stick simply has more flavor and a more pleasing texture than other types of the more generic, "waxy" licorice twist, rope or nibs that are out there.  Opening the package I was hit by a wave of fruity aroma that alerted me to the fact that this was not like most other twists.  The flavor was strong, bold and not "sugary"  Add to it that the texture was soft but still had a "chewy" quality to it without being overly sticky.  Occasionally such products in the past have been a challenge for crowns and caps and this wasn't the case here.Anyone who values organic products will no doubt be encouraged by reading the ingredient list and I certainly wasn't turned off by that in the least.  In terms of pure taste and quality of the eating experience, the word "organic" never really crossed my mind.  It's just good.5 starsbart breen

With each one that I eat, I appreciate them more! The pomegranate is very good, although I would have been hard-pressed to identify this as pomegranate - more of a mixed berry. This licorice is a little thicker and waxier than your typical Twizzler - more of a sophisticated licorice, but not lacking any of the enjoyment. Okay, so it sticks to your teeth a bit more than the mass-produced variety, but it's worth it... my only complaint... a bit pricey for my taste. If I saw these in the store, they'd have to be under two bucks a pack for me to buy them. But hey, I'm cheap. If you're not, give these a try. Tasty.

column4: Eric DiPier "Life is a gift horse."
column10: Pretty much pomegranate-flavored Twizzlers, except using actual food-related ingredients.  I was impressed with these - they arrived, I tried one...and then two...and then three...it was hard to stop.  They are very chewy, a little chewier than Twizzlers, and the fruit flavor is strong but not overwhelming.  I would say "the pomegranate flavor" but I really have no idea what pomegranate tastes like.  I found it interesting that pomegranate is the next-to-last ingredient - I guess it doesn't take much pomegranate to make a pomegranate-flavored product.All in all, if you like "licorice twists" in general, and you have slightly adventurous taste buds, I think you'll like these.b

column4: Raymond H. Mullen "Trust others, but  pack yo...
column10: Pomegranate 'Anything' didn't even sound good to me.  Was I surprised!!!  I just finished eating three pieces of this stuff and really enjoyed it!!  The only reason I only gave 4 stars was simply because it was soooo sweet. I definately would buy this product.  Roughly only about 130 calories from 5 (five) pieces and only 0.5g of fat.

column9: Addictive --  I had the entire pack for lunch.
column10: Newman's Own Organics POMEGANATE LICORICE TWISTS contains about thirty sticks of pomegranate "licorice." The sticks have the dimensions of 1.0 cm wide by 11.0 cm long.
