I started on these immediately after opening the package, and thus I am only estimating the number of sticks as about thirty. The weight of the contents is 5 oz (141 grams).The uninitiated consumer might find the flavor to be a grape flavor. According to the label, the flavor comes from ELDERBERRY EXTRACT, POMEGRANATE JUICE CONCENTRATE, and LICORICE ROOT EXTRACT. There is no indication that any of the flavors are artificial or synthetic. Based on my experience as a consumer, I sometimes do not like flavorings that are artificial or synthetic, because of the off-taste that comes with them, perhaps due to contaminating by-products made during the organic synthesis. Also, some products such as tea bags containing flavored tea, have an artificial flavor that is over-powering and that contaminates brewing devices, kitchen utensils, and such, in a way that causes them to acquire the chemical flavor. At any rate, Newman's Own Organics POMEGRANATE LICORICE does not contain any synthetic flavors.The licorice sticks are on the soft side. The color is a dull (not glossy) dark purple. This is in contrast to "red licorice" found in drug stores and supermarkets, which is hard and unnaturally glossy (like fingernail polish). Newman's Own Organics POMEGRANATE LICORICE TWISTS is a product that is unusual enough to be used as a component of a gift-basket, for example, as a holiday gift. This kind of gift basket may also include, for example, an expensive silver bell, embroidered note cards, and gourmet chocolates.

Pomegranate is one of my new favorite flavors.  I like pomegranate juice, tea and now licorice. Newman's Own has made a great tasting treat.  It's a lightly sweetened licorice twist, made with all natural, organic ingredients.  It has only a trace of fat and is low in sodium and sugar.  That I definitely like.  When I first tasted it, I thought it was more of a cherry/pomegranate blend.  And after reading the ingredient list, I realized why.  Besides pomegranate it has Elderberry extract.  If you like licorice, I do recommend giving this one a try.

Oh I was so happy to find this. It is so good, and knowing that it is organic is awesome.So good. If you want a comparison the texture is somewhat like Nibs. But way better.At least if I have an addiction to licorice, it is so good.

I adore certain kinds of licorice...I know I got this from my mom...she and I both loved this Englishy licorice called Allsorts.I am not a fan and I do not indulge in foods...is licorice an actual food...that have artificial colors and weird long named preservatives in them...so when this product was offered to me...I pounced!!!It came yesterday and my husband and I each had two pieces after dinner...we were cautiously optimistic because it is aPaul Newman product and we usually love these products.  They are usually excellent.We were not disappointed with this licorice.It is not overly sweet...is 70% organic and just tastes really delicious.  We had the pomegranate ones and again...loved them!!!We actually each had two more pieces before going to bed.  I am counting the ones left in the bag...so that we each get our fair share until I can find them locally.And now I am wondering...is an addiction to this licorice a serious one?Since there are 15 pieces in the bag...who will get the extra one?  Hmmm...

Newman's Organics Pomegranate Licorice is a pleasing upgrade from traditional Red Vines. The candy has a satisfying mouth feel combined with a subtle pomegranate flavor that beats the waxy, sugary cheapness of other licorices. I shared my package with five coworkers and we all loved this candy.

I absolutely love junk red licorice, so I thought that I would try the Newman's Own Organics Pomegranate Licorice Twists since they would probably be a much healthier treat.  The initial taste was okay, yet not quite right... they had a kind of weird wheat flavor and heavier texture, which is not the kind of thing you want to taste when you're thinking red licorice.  But it was the after-taste that left me thinking "yuck!"  It was just plain strange, almost minty, but again with a grain flavor.  I could not put my finger on what the flavor was, but then after looking at the ingredients list, it made sense: the number one ingredient is wheat!  Now this is much healthier than regular red vines that consist of mainly corn syrup, but I would not ever eat these!  Now, I should mention that all the rest of my family tried them too, some who love sweets and some that do not, and they all thought they tasted fine.  So I guess if you are looking for something sweet to munch on that is a little bit healthier give them a try, but don't think that they will taste like red vines.

column9: Can't say I'm a fan.  Oh well!  I still like  lots of other Newman's own products.
column10: I am not a gourmet food expert.  I just know what I like and I didn't much care for the Pomegranate Licorice although in general I like most anything pomegranate flavored.  Even actual pomegranate.  Go figure.Upon first sniff of the product I thought:  This smells just like a scented candle!  It smelled nice.  But smelling a candle and eating a candle are two different things.  Just because something smells nice does not mean it tastes nice.  Anyway it kind of tasted like it smelled... like a scented candle.  It wasn't maybe that unpleasant.  But it was not as good as licorice should be.I thought it had a weird taste to it.  It to me tasted very much like you might imagine a scented candle to taste like.The texture was good- not too sticky.  But the taste was what is making me rate this at only 2 stars.  I just didn't care for it.  Taste is a pretty subjective thing though and I see so many other reviewers are giving it raves so perhaps I am just the odd man out.

Talk about awesome!  This licorice is so tasty, so good, and so satisfying.  It is pomegranate flavored and tastes so good!  Since it is pomegranate-flavored, I guess you could say it is fruity licorice, which, to me, is the best type.  This licorice has a tangy pomegranate flavor.  Heaveny fruity flavor.This licorice is so good, and I've already ate most of it.  I will have to hide the rest from myself.The texture is that of which is normal for licorice.  It is not too sticky.  Just perfect.Perfect texture, perfect taste, perfect flavor.This product is made with organic sugar, organic wheat flour.  It also has other ingredients.These licorice twists are so good, I will definitely be buying more.  Lots more.  It has been many, many years since I have had licorice of any type, but I am already hooked on these pomegranate licorice twists by Newman's Own.

The twists are wonderfully soft and chewy, and they stick in your teeth in a good way. However, the mix of licorice and pomegranate flavor is strangely medicinal, and the twists aren't really sweet enough for my tastes. Still, they're a bit addictive, which makes it impossible to give them a one-star rating.

column4: Meg "Livin la vida loca in Maine!"
column10: I'm very disappointed to have to write this review, I had higher expectations for this product. I love pomegranate, licorice and prefer organic products whenever possible. One would believe that I would love Newman's Own Organic Pomegranate Licorice. Not so! I found it to be bland and tough with a slightly stale flavor that does not taste like pomegranate. I almost lost a filling on these! I would not recommend them at all.

column9: I like Newman's Own but not this product
column10: I am disappointed to have to give this product an unfavorable review. The licorice has barely a hint of pomegranate yet all the calories associated with a super sweet licorice. Also, the licorice in the package I received in July, 2011, which was dated as "Best Before March 2012" I though was kind of stale and a bit hardened.

column9: Somewhat Better Tasting Than Pencil Erasers
column10: I have bought and enjoyed "Newman's Own" brand products for years.  This however has now changed with their "Pomegranate Licorice".  it may be "all natural" but apparently that also means "No Flavor" and a texture that could pull fillings..The smaller print mentions this is the "second generation" so I presume his kids are running it.I love licorice.  This however is only marginally better than gnawing pencil erasers.  The flavor is bland, with only a vague hint of something that might be called "pomegranate" if you had never actually tasted the real thing.  The licorice was stiff and past "chewy" and on into "stale" and is now sitting like lead in my stomach.  I am actually thinking of getting an antacid to counter this stuff.Save your money. "Newman's Own" made a major miss on this one and I don't think their dad would be proud.If you want a really good licorice, try this one on Amazon: Darrell Lea Red Strawberry Soft Eating Liquorice, 7-Ounce Bags (Pack of 8)

I am already a fan of Newman's Own Organics line of products.  I think they are generally high quality, reasonably priced and have a great track record as a charitable organization.  So, I was really looking forward to trying out the Pomegranate Licorice.When you first open the package, you can immediately smell the sweet sugary fruit scent of pomegranate.  The next thing you notice is the rich red, well pomegranate, color.  One thing I liked right off the bat is that the licorice sticks are not super long like a Twizzler.  They are shorter and more manageable to eat.  They are a also not overly sticky and do not leave a sticky residue on your fingers.Taste wise, they are great.  Perhaps my favorite aspect of this licorice is that they are not super sweet.  While they have a strong sugary smell, they are not obnoxiously sweet like Twizzlers.  The licorice has a nice chewy texture and trends towards soft.  The pomegranate taste is subtle.  At first you cannot taste it at all, instead tasting the sugar and gelatin flavors.  As you chew the pomegranate taste grows and by the end has a nice strong flavor.  The pomegranate flavor is also very good.  I haven't ate too many raw pomegranates but I do like the POM juice products.  This licorice compares well against the POM juice products.So, as a nice treat to share with the family, I highly recommend.

column9: It's not my sort of candy
column10: To me, these don't taste at all like licorice and not much like pomegranate. They are quite sweet. It says "Made with Organic Sugar" but it also lists corn syrup as a major ingredient.

column9: Doesn't live up to the Newman's Own name
column10: I have always loved just about any product that Newman's Own has put out but for once, I am disappointed. Everybody in our family sampled Newman's Own Organics Pomegranate Licorice Twists but and the response was tepid at best and 'yuch' at worst. It's not that anyone hates pomegranate either as we often buy pomegranate juice or whole pomegranates.Our biggest complaint is that there was too much chewing involved for too little flavor and even then there was an unpleasant aftertaste. Sad to say, we are not likely to buy this product again.

column9: yummy twist on a childhood candy
column10: I was intrigued by the idea of a pomegranate flavored licorice and wasn't sure at first if I would love it or hate it.  I was pleasantly surprised on my first bite and nearly finished a package all on my own!I like that it has natural ingredients and is low fat.  Not all ingredients listed are organic but on the plus side there are no artificial colors or flavors added.  For a candy it's a relatively guilt free choice and can be enjoyed by kids and adults alike.

I haven't tasted licorice in a long time. What a treat this Newman's organic brand is. They offer a wide selection of flavors, and I found the pomegranate exceptionally good. It has an exotic taste, very deep and rich, and it quicky became evident that you can't eat just one twist. Fortunately, the calorie count is around 130 for 5 twists, so I didn't feel guilty at all. A nice alternative to gum, lasts long and holds its flavor to the last bite.

I love licorice! Red, Black (real stuff!) and sometimes the alternative flavors.  But none of that Twizzler stuff for me, it's just a tease of flavor as far as I'm concerned!I was fortunate to recieve a package of this Licorice from Amazon to try and review.  I love this licorice! It's very flavorful! Has a medium sweetness along with a juicy tartness rather like a real dried fruit roll-up.  I expected it to be soft, like the Aussie licorice, but was pleasantly surprised at how it hits a midline in being firmer than the Aussie but softer than the traditional Red and black Vine.  Yummy! Ooooh! my mouth is watering for more, but mine is all gone!I do like the flavor of Pomegranate and like the medicial properties of the berry and choose this flavor often. So when I had eaten a few pieces of the licorice, I detected another flavor and took a look in the ingredients list, expecting that possibly some cranberry extract would be found.  But instead I was pleasantly surprised to find a listing for Elderberry extract up higher in the content list than the pomegranate! Elderberry is even more healthy...the berries contain more vitamin C than any other herb except rosehips and black currant.Elderberry is often used for its antioxidant activity, to lower cholesterol, to improve vision, to boost the immune system, to improve heart health and for coughs, colds, flu, bacterial and viral infections and tonsilitis. Bioflavonoids and other proteins in the juice destroy the ability of cold and flu viruses to infect a cell. People with the flu who took elderberry juice reported less severe symptoms and felt better much faster than those who did not. Elderberry juice was used to treat a flu epidemic in Panama in 1995.What a fantastic tasting snack, while being healthy organically with an implication of some medicinal properties! I'm going to have to find another bag at the market while I wait for my re-order from Amazon to come!

column9: Great texture, but a tad bland on flavor
column10: I am normally not a fan of licorice, but I was eager to taste Newman's Own Organics Pomegranate Licorice Twists, as I love pomegranate. First, the good news: its evident that these licorice are a quality product. They're fresh, soft, and chewy. And now for the bad news: there's no real burst of flavor. The pomegranate is lacking a prominent presence, making for a dull dessert.Despite the phrase "organic" that appears on the package, only three of the ingredients are listed as organic: wheat flour, sugar and tapioca syrup. Is this a deal breaker? No, but it does seem somewhat misleading, as most will perceive this treat to be entirely organic.Here's a breakdown of the nutrition data:Serving Size: 5 pieces (42g)Servings Per Container: About 7Calories: 130  Calories from Fat: 5Total Fat: 0.5g (1%)Sodium: 5mg (0%)Total Carb: 32g (11%)Dietary Fiber: 2g (8%)Sugars: 10gProtein: 2gINGREDIENTS:Organic Wheat Flour, Organic Sugar, Corn Syrup, Organic Tapioca Syrup, Vegetable Glycerin, Sunflower Oil, Elderberry Extract, Citric Acid, Natural Flavor, Pomegranate Juice Concentrate, Licorice Root ExtractAll in all, there are certainly worse sweets available, so Newman's Own Pomegranate Licorice Twists do make for a healthier alternative. But if you're expecting a sweet, refreshing pomegranate treat, you may be disappointed.

column9: Really tasty, and chewier than most
column10: This licorice has a great pomegranate flavor. I love pomegranate, so I really enjoyed the unique flavor. This licorice is also a bit firmer and chewier than the soft stuff you usually get in stores (Twizzlers, etc.), but I like my licorice a bit firmer and chewier. I also like that it's organic, and part of the Newman's Own line (which donates a lot of it's profits to charity). I will definitely pick this up at the store again, and look forward to trying some of the other flavors (tangerine, strawberry, etc.). If you like licorice and pomegranate, this is highly recommended.

I'd been reading about this product in magazines for almost a year, and couldn't wait to try it. I finally got to and it did not disappoint. Pomegranate is not an easy flavor to capture and somehow they were able to. I have tried all the NEWMAN'S OWN ORGANICS licorices and this was the hardest in terms of chewing, but it was not overly hard. I have had some that I know would put any dental work at risk, and this is a good option if you like slighly harder licorice but still want something that is chewy. Not too sweet, but good if you need a candy fix. And of course, it's got all natural ingredients, so you can get your candy fix as I have been doing without feeling in the least bit guilty!

I am a seriously addicted licorice lover! I buy bags of black jelly beans every Easter, seek out new licorice flavors in the candy stores, and buy a pack of Twizzlers whenever I run out. I was very excited to try the Newman's Own and thought pomegranate would be an awesome flavor to try. WELL...I was very disappointed. I thought the flavor was very strong, and really didn't taste much like pomegranate. It tasted more like liquid cough medicine. I definitely will not look for this flavor again, and may really hesitate to buy the brand.
These are great little snacks when you want a different flavor. Not overly flavored but not weak. Just a nice, different flavor. A departure from the usual. I would definitely get these again.

This Licorice was very good.  The pomegranate flavor was sweet but not overwhelming.  I love that it is all natural.  My kid's really enjoyed the product as well.  Will definatly buy more in the future.

column9: Very good but doesn't justify the price.
column10: We like the licorice we get at TJs in a tub just as well and it's a lot cheaper. But if you want to support the Newman's Own causes this really is good stuff. Just one star off for the price.

These are really good licorice: chewy, sweet, GREAT flavor.  Certainly better than the average store-shelf flavored licorice.  However, they have an odd aftertaste that I could never quite pin down; somewhat biting, somewhat off-putting, but never quite bad.  Not sure where that comes from, but it was the only reason for a 4-star instead of 5-star rating.  Would I get more of these?  Possibly, but if other flavors had that same aftertaste, I wouldn't get them too often.

column9: Great idea, not so great delivery
column10: Simply put the licorice is no good. I like pomegranate juice, I like the fruit, I even like the smell of it in various perfumes and lip balms. This didn't deliver on the pomegranate promise. A little chewy and tough even for licorice just turns you off. Couple that with the medicinal flavoring and it just doesn't add up.

These are certainly interesting candies, and a pleasant alternative to much of the less "natural" that's on the market. The pomegranate taste is unusual, almost a slight bitter-sweet combination that stays around after the candy has gone...although I should add that the liquorice has a tendency to get into your teeth in ways that you almost wish it couldn't. It's very chewy and sticky so be warned.Not the cheapest "candy" on the market, but certainly an enjoyable occasional treat.

Newman's Own Organics Licorice Twists have a lot of things going for them - 70 percent organic, with no artificial ingredients.  The pomegranate flavor was surprisingly good and, while it had a different consistency from the Twizzlers I'm used to, it wasn't a bad change.  Recommended.
Enjoyed them - has exotic flavor and are a bit sweet, if you like sweet. I prefer Strawberry twistzlers. The pomergrante is a nice topuch and I'm not sure whether it has any herbal efficacy.

column9: Newman's Own Organics Pomegranate Licorice Twists, 5-Ounce Packages (Pack of 15)
column10: I wouldn't say I'm a pomegranate fan, but I do like good tasting licorice, and I did like this. It's rich and flavorful but not overpowering or sickeningly sweet like many brands.  The pomegranate flavor is a nice change from the usual "red" flavor twists out there. This is a bit chewier than other brands, however, but it looks like it may be from the ingredients (including organic wheat flour  and organic sugar and corn syrup instead of the usual high-fructose corn syrup), rather than from being stale.  I found it to have a mild sweet and tangy flavor one would expect from a quality licorice. It's a healthier choice, offering fewer calories and some organic ingredients, but be warned, it's hard to put down and easy to overindulge. I think it's one of the better ones on the market. In my opinion, if you're a licorice fan, looking for something a bit different, and want a tasty treat not jammed full of sugar and chemicals, this is worth looking at.

column9: Just like the kind you had as a kid
column10: These tasty treats are absolutely wonderful. I tried the pomegranate variety and they had pretty much the same flavor as cherry, but that is nothing to complain about. The flavor is very addictive. They are sweetened with "naturally dried cane sugar," which is still sugar. I don't think there is any natural advantage to the dehydrated cane sugar fad. Sugar is sugar. The folks at Newman's Own ought to think about sweetening with stevia, which is both natural and free of any calories. Just a suggestion.Even with sugar, this candy is a real delight and something to stock up on for Halloween trick or treat.

I am a big licorice fan, so I thought I'd give these a try.  The best thing about them is that they are made with organic ingredients, which makes them less guilt-inducing than most licorice.  Texture: a bit rubbery/chewy but fine. Taste: Takes some getting used to, but ok, especially because the pomegranate is not overly strong. Aftertaste: my least favorite part, it's pretty chemical and makes me want to drink lots of water.I would be willing to try the other flavors (black & strawberry, probably not tangerine) but I don't think I'd ever buy this flavor.

Not much to add here other than the flavor of pomegranate was distinctive which I liked.I try not to eat or buy anything with corn syrup in it so...I passed it along to someone else.  But for what it is (candy) I thought it was quite good.

I'm not sure I even have the words to convey how good this stuff is. But take note: I say this as a twist purist. As far as I'm concerned, it's not a twist if it doesn't bloody well taste like licorice, or anise, or fennel, or Pernod, or whatever you want to call it and whatever variation of the flavor you're using. I want my licorice. But I figured, "hmm, pomegranate twists, might as well give it a shot. At least it's not those awful red things." And I got them, and I opened the bag, and...Wolfgang Puck recently said of the banana cream pie at Emeril's that "you put the first forkful in your mouth, and you can't think of anything except putting the next forkful in your mouth, and five seconds later there's none left!" Well, that's exactly what happened with these pomegranate twists. Good lord. I ended up wondering where they'd gone, and then going to the store to get more of them (unfortunately, they haven't hit the mistake on the lake yet). Deep, rich pomegranate flavor, perfect texture. Warning: when you go to the store and try these, buy the smallest bag available if you're watching your figure. They'll be gone in five seconds. *****

These didn't last long in this household! We both love licorice, but this was especially nice because it didn't have that cloying, oversweetness that comes with too much sugar or HFCS. That and the pomegranate is a really nice twist, if you'll forgive the pun--much better than artificial strawberry! Really good texture, too, softer but with a good chew to it. We have a winner!

Arrived fast and fresh. They have a unique taste to them and are much better than twizzlers, which have a plastic taste to them. This is what licorice is suppose to taste like - I imagine finding something like this at Cracker Barrel. I loved them, I am sure you will too.
Well, "licorice" is a stretch, but this is like most of the Newman products -- tasty and good quality. Whether YOU like the taste is, of course up to you, but I did.

"Newman's Own" has expanded into candy!Unfortunately, my family found this product to be merely "so-so".  One daughter, who is really into pomegranate flavors really enjoyed it; most of the rest of us could take it or leave it -- at best.  Personally, I found the flavor rather peppery -- not what one necessarily expects from candy.Nothing special here.

delicious flavor and not too sweet that lingers on the palate.  Although I initially received these as a product to review, I ordered some more since the kids love these so much.  Wonderful taste combination.

There are those of us with a sweet tooth, and there are those of us without.  I am of the first category.  I especially love fruity candies, like Twizzlers and gummies, so had to try these out.  They had a nice balance of sweetness, just the right amount of chewiness, and had a little more of a natural fruit flavor to them than any other licorice twists I've tried.  Plus, I'm always happy to try out Newman's Own products based on what I know the company - that they donate a portion of the proceeds to charity.

These didn't do anything for me. I could eat a stick and they weren't bad, but I would not buy them again.That said, I typically do not like licorice products. I would rate these higher than anything else I have tried for what it's worth.I usually like Newman's products and knew I was taking a risk here. I thought maybe they'd change my mind about licorice given the number of positive reviews from others.

column9: Family likes it, me not so much
column10: My boys and husband really liked this licorice.  I found it a little tart for my preference in licorice.  The texture is nice, and the brand is of course respectable. I like that the ingredients are natural.  I'd get it again for the family, and try a different flavor for myself.

Pomegranate Licorice sounds like it might be a unique taste treat, but I didn't find it to be anything special. If you're a fan of pomegranate, you'll find a familiar tang in the taste. It's not bad, but it didn't leave me longing for me.

This is really great tasting licorice.  The pomegranate flavor really comes through unlike many other pom-flavored products I've tried.  I've also had other Newman products and been less than impressed.  This however, has been the exception.  Fresh in the package and wonderful flavor.  I'll be buying this again.
Didn't know what to expect from Newman's own licorice, but I was plesantly surprised.  Great pomegranate taste and not too sweet.  My 10 year old's comment was 'Yummy, Daddy'.  Good stuff

I'm a big fan a pomegranate, but not of licorice... or any candy that is not chocolate. But the double pluses of pomegranate and Newman's got me to try it.My kids, and their friends wanted nothing to do with it. However, after my wife and I let out a few "Wow"s, it got their attention, and one by one, curiosity got the better of them all.A pleasant pomegranate taste, without having too much of a sicky sweet candy taste.

column9: Nice flavor - milder than I expected
column10: I had never had pomegranate licorice, so I didn't know quite what to expect.  What I found with this product was a pleasant, smooth, somewhat milder than I had expected flavor experience.  My expectations were based on traditional black licorice and this is clearly different.  Texture and toughness seemed OK to me, also.If you like licorice and you like fruit flavors, I'd bet that you will like this product.

This is not your average Twizzler, here!  These licorice are different than your regular every day candy! These licorice are way better quality than the kind you grab at movie theaters! Just the right amount of sweetness! Perfectly chewy and a great flavor! I was hesitant about the pomegranate flavor, but its a wonderful change the every day cherry variety! My daughter and I gladly gobbled these up!
I enjoyed these way more than I thought I would. Not very pomegranete-y, but still very yummy. Perfect snack for a movie date.

There were two testers--your reviewer and Family Member X. We deemed this pack of licorice the perfect snack to make us feel a wee bit better about watching a Hoarders Season Two: Part One marathon. We may have needed an Intervention Season 1: Then and Now to get us to stop, but the package was all gone, and we didn't go out hunting for more. And we threw away the wrapper.Fibery, more cherry than pomegranate, but delicious all the same and addictive, these old fashioned licorice twists remind me of childhood and make me salute Paul Newman for the 1000th time...
This licorice has a very good flavor! The only thing I would have liked is it were a little softer.

I LOVE pomegranates and I know that organic things are supposed to be healthier for you, so what's NOT to like about these?  Nothing... they're REALLY good! They're also easy on the sugar (per serving), for those with diabetes, myself included.Okay, I confess... these left me wanting (and having), more than one serving as well as wanting to try the other delicious-sounding flavors!  A not-too-sweet and delicious snack you can feel good about eating.  Yummy... well done!  (... and, uh-oh, this package is gone!)  :)

column9: Just the Right Amount of Sweetness
column10: Pomegranate is a difficult flavor for me to accurately place, so I'm not sure whether these taste a lot like pomegranate or not.  However, the flavor is good and they are pleasantly sweet.  The texture is more like Twizzlers than Red Vines.  The fragrance as you are eating them is also nice.If you like licorice twists, I think you'll like these.

I really hate black licorice and there hasn't been a flavor of licorice I really adored since the old "Pull and Peel" Pech Twizzlers they stopped making roughly fifteen years ago. However, after trying the Newman's Own Organic Pomegranate Licorice, I feel in love with this age old candy once again.I'm always happy when someone creates a candy that is organic and flavorful, so right off, this own the licorice some points from me. Pomegrante has always been one of my favorite fruits long before it became a trendy product so I was happy to see this in candy form. I can't think of any other pomegrante candies that i have tried. Then there is the flavor. It doesn't taste exactly Pomegrante-y if you are comparing it to the seeds or juice of the fruit, but it does taste wonderful. It's a flavor you have to try to truly understand, but it is incredibly delicious.This is another great product by one of my favorite companies and it's definitely a treat I'll pick up again for long plane rides or the like.

I was a bit skeptical...pomegranite licorice? Well let me tell you, this stuff is the bomb! Not too sweet, not too tart with true pomegranite flavor and the perfect consistency and chew. This package did not last long at our house. After this package was devoured, there were lots of requests for "more"!

If you're looking for a Twizzlers type of flavor, this is not it. The sweetness is more natural, and the licorice actually retains a little flour flavor, which I happen to like. Not a bad little sweet treat!

These pomegranate licorice twists were a tasty combination of licorice flavor and fruity pomegranate flavor.  They taste like they don't have as many preservatives as Twizzlers... once you open the package you need to put them in a ziplock bag or they harden up to a rock.  I still like Twizzlers better though.

We enjoyed our package of pomegranate licorice.  I prefer to buy organic and this fits the bill.  It's not too sweet but yet still is candy.  The entire family enjoyed it and it was a nice special treat.  If you are looking for a nice treat that is not too sweet and sugary this works.  I would prefer that they didn't use corn syrup but it is candy.

This is good stuff, especially for those of us who aren't exactly fond of chocolate.  I happen to like Pomegranates, so this is a departure from the cherry twists I usually buy.  Newman's Own Pomgranate Licorice Twists are tasty without being overpowering.  The texture is good, not too chewy, just right.  I like `em.

I've read several reviews complaining about this product not being like the red twists they're used to, but though one might expect that taste based upon the appearance, they are supposed to be different.  I, too, expected a different taste when I took my first bite, but after the surprise...... and another bite, I liked them.  They aren't as sweet as one might anticipate, but they have a nice, tangy flavor and are pleasing to my palate.  I do think they are a little expensive, but the profits go to charity.  I didn't experience the after-taste that some mentioned either.  I think if you bite into one without that red licorice paradigm in your mind you'll enjoy them as I did.  They are definitely worth a try.Recommended.

Upon opening a package of Newman's Own Organics Pomegranate Licorice Twists, one is greeted by an aroma much like red wine. The first bite provides a similar taste experience.Made with organic and natural ingredients (and no animal ingredients, like gelatin), Pomegranate Twists are an acceptable snack for vegetarians and vegans. The best thing about them is that they are not overly sweet, as some brands of fruit-flavored licorice twists tend to be.Low in fat and sodium and only 26 calories per twist, these treats are packed with flavor and are especially recommended for adults (though, kids will like them, too).

This is a great licorice!  Individual pieces are about 5" in length - which is alot handier to eat than the traditional 12" lengths.  The pomegranate flavor is unexpected and delicious!  This licorice has so much more flavor than other brands which to me taste like sugar gel.  We started eating our package and devoured the entire things in one sitting it was so good!  I would give the product 5 stars but for one thing.  The product is manufactured in Mexico.  I'm so much more conscious of the impact we all can have of purchasing products made in America.

I bought these for my hubby because he loves licorice. These tasty twists also have some nutritional value too, BOUNUS! My hubby absolutely Loved them! I very much recommned Newman's Own Organics Pomegranate Licorice Twists.

First of all you need to know that I'm a big licorice fan.  But, I'm really picky when it come to the licorice I chose to eat. I love the Austrian black and strawberry licorice, detest some of the so called licorice that really isn't licorice at all. Some of it leaves a bitter almost chemical taste in your mouth.  I was a little skeptical about Newman's Own Pomegranate Licorice, but when I tried it I was pleasantly surprised.  This is a great flavor and added variety for licorice lovers.  The bonus is that it is made with lots of organic ingrediants, and real pomegranate flavor.  Ironically I just complained to Hansen's Naturals about their pomegranate green tea beverage, which contains no pomegranate at all.  To me if it says pomegranate and has a picture of a pomegranate on the can it better have pomegranate in the product.  So Hansen's Naturals are not natural at all and Hansen's is deceptive and dishonest in the products they offer.  Not so with Newman's Own.  I recommend Pomegranate Licorice Twists.

column9: Okay taste but chewier than normal licorice
column10: Newman's Own Organic Pomegranate Licorice have an okay taste but they are chewier than your standard licorice vines. This could be related to them being organic; I'm not sure.Overall they taste fine but I don't think I would get the Pomegranate Licorice twists again.

I'm a licorice fan, but admittedly a "cheap" licorice fan in that I'd take good ole' Twizzlers above most others. I did like the pom flavor, but thought the toughness gave them a kind of stale texture.
I do love red licorice and these pomegranate-flavored are no exception. Their taste is quite a departure from the standard "red vine" flavor but still very good. I would definitely buy these.

column9: used to love it, but a scary experience for my golden raised questions
column10: I fed my two golden retrievers and cat Wellness products for a long time with good results. I really respect the approach Wellness has tried to take and always thought their ingredients were excellent.  Their ingredient list is outstanding-- human grade meats and veggies/ a holistic health approach.Then we had a strange incident. I opened a new bag and gave it to my dog, and shortly after eating breakfast she became terribly sick for about a week---severe, severe diarrhea. I thought this was a weird coincidence, so I discarded the bag just to be safe, and went through another bag of Wellness with no problems. Then about a month later I again opened a fresh bag and my dog became terribly ill shortly after eating the first bowl-- same symptoms.  (Both bags were not expired.)I can't help suspecting that something about how the ingredients were mixed in those bags made my dog terribly sick. I stopped feeding Wellness to my pets and we have had no further problems over the last 6 months. I should add that my dog had never had any allergy problems of any kind and has always been very healthy. She has never had a bad reaction to any food-- she is a chow-hound and does not have a sensitive system.I reported our experience to the store where I purchased the food and they agreed to notify Wellness. I don't know if the company has looked into this issue or not.If your dog stays healthy on Wellness I would still support it as a good choice given the ingredient list. However, if your dog has symptoms like my dog's symptoms, I'd suggest to you take that seriously and switch foods.

column10: I am disappointed in these. I thought I would try them instead of the greenies, but they dry out quickly once you open the package and to top it off, my dog, who is definitely not a finicky eater, won't eat them.I am back to the more expensive greenies again.
These things dissolve in drool very fast. The dog does not get any benafit from chewing because they are mush in minutes.
I haven't try these yet, but I priced them at Walmart. A pk for large dogs has 32 stix and is $12.00.

I gave a stick to my 1 year old Weimaraner and he got diarrhea!:( I'm very disappointed that Pedigree has not emailed me back regarding the quality of their product. I hope we are the only ones that have had this happen to.

Anyone who would purchase this product from Amazon for the stated price  of $40.43 for 100 stix of 55.7 oz. must have money to burn and probably does not do price comparisons.  I purchase this item at Kroger's.  I pay $6.69 regular price (or $4.99 sale price, which happens often) less the value of any coupons I find on-line or in the Sunday newspaper for a bag of 25 stix (14.1 oz) which comes to a total of $26.76 for four bags of 25.  If I purchase the product here I would be paying the equivalent of $8.19 (which includes my 20% Prime discount) for the same size bag.  And if I read the Amazon blurb correctly this price of $40.43 less 20% is a one-time deal.BTW I think the product is wonderful and deserves 5 stars on that account.  My beagle Bootsie loves them.  And what is more wonderful, no more doggie breath.

column9: If you want an obese dog.....
column10: Just an FYI for the doglovers out there.....per my Vet, each of these chew-sticks has 300 calories each.  That is probably why she called my dogs "obese" on their last check-up.  You'd never know that because nutritional info is not put on the bags like human food....there are much lower-calorie chew sticks out there and they do put their calorie count on the bag (the new ones I buy are 19 calories each....BIG DIFFERENCE)The boys have lost 3 pound each since we dropped the Dentastix a day habit!

I consider myself a huge fan of turkey jerky. I've tried many of the brands with varying results. This is the most tender and delicious brand that I constantly buy. Great flavor, fresh and not all stale / hard as others.

column9: my favorite jerky as a meal helper
column10: i'm surprised to see so many negative reviews. considering this is my favorite jerky i feel obligated to write an review. it is tender, flavorful, and relatively healthy (no artificial ingredients, no preservatives like sodium benzoate except naturally occurring one in soy sauce), and the hint of sweetness is just right. the beef variety sometimes is too hard and dry to my liking. the turkey one is much better.it is probably too salty as a snack but it is excellent as a meal helper and blends well into different kinds of meals. (well it is not that salty considering all the fast food we are exposed to. it contains 470mg (20% daily value) of sodium per serving (1oz/28g) and has 8 servings per bag. so even if you somehow eat the whole bag at once it is just 160% daily value of sodium.)

I enjoy jerky and like to try new kinds and new brands. Last week at the nearby Costco, I found 16-ounce packets of Pacific Gold Teriyaki Turkey Jerky, subdivided into two 8-ounce pouches. It's good! It's tender, but chewy. It has a nice flavor, but it's a little too sweet to be ideal for me. It has a very low fat and cholesterol, but is perhaps a little high on salt. The jerky seemed good and fresh, if you can apply that word to jerky. This stuff is pretty good. I don't think it's going to last long.Gary Peterson

By far the worse jerky I have EVER tasted! Over all flavor - salty to the point of causing my tongue to be raw (in places) after only eating 2 ounces. If I could give it a lower rating than 1 star SURELY I WOULD!I AM SO, SO DISAPPOINTED! :'(For the person who soaked it to give it to their cats, I was just trying to figure out what I am going to do with a pound of junk... No cats to give it to and (really) not good enough to just give to another human being. (And I live in a 3rd world country...)Have written the company. My advice to the majority of you is -- SAVE YOUR MONEY (or buy Jack Links - has never been a disappointment).

dry, stringy and just plain gross. Like eating salty chalk. Ended up soaking it in several water changes to draw out some sodium and fed it to the cats. How in the eff does a jerky company sell something this pitiful. and how did it pass in house taste testing

column9: great product from a good co.
column10: I just want to share with everyone about this item.  I was very pleased with the speed of delivery I think it is USPS not sure?! but the actual product was outstanding.  It is easy to prepare and delivers great taste. Im pretty confident you will be satisfied i checked reviews for other products and have purchased other brands. The Starbucks brand for the price is by far the best you will get to a starbucks latte.

I got an espresso maker a few months ago, I've tried generic espresso, Starbucks loose ground espresso roast, and these pods. These pods are definitely the best! Best taste and much easier to use. Less than 50 cents a pull. Had problems with the filter clogging with the ground espresso, obviously not a problem with these.

Package shipped in good time, however several of the espresso pods were damaged inside of the individual cartons.About half had open espresso pods in each carton.While they were moderately usable, it was a bit of a disappointment.

I'be purchased Starbucks pods for a year and a half, by multiple case lots, and have enjoyed them until recently. After an inexcusably lengthy backorder period the pods I have received on two shipments since then have been poorly formed and seem to tightly packed based on increased flow times (40-50 seconds) to pull a shot from my Breville espresso maker (I'm talking about 12-16 boxes, not just a single bad box). Is my pump going bad? That may be a possibility but during the backorder period I ordered LaVazza pods and they needed tamping because they pulled too quickly. I've also found now that I was forced to try something other than Starbucks I like the tast of the LaVazza (and possibly others) better.

column9: Easy to use and tastes great!
column10: I just bought the DeLonghi home espresso maker from Amazon and purchased these pods plus starbucks flavored syrups.  The quality is amazing!  I can make the same latte at home at a fraction of the price.  The pods are much cleaner than the grounds and the flavor is great, plus they come in decaf.  They are hard to find in stores, so I'll keep ordering here!

As a frequent Traveler to the West Coast, I have found myself in accommodations where there just wasn't a nearby StarBucks location, and I don't have the taste for regular coffee, since there is just too much Inconsistency and reliability of both coffeemakers and coffee/espresso grinds.Plus, I have been Spoiled Rotten by my purchase of the Bosch Tassimo Coffee/espresso maker earlier this year, that currently, I am still working thru my StarBuck's enormous inventory and supply of their espresso's, and then, it's not like I can just take my Tassimo with me on my trips either!I purchased the Hand-powered espresso machine, called the HandPresso Wild - Black model, mainly because it uses the StarBucks Espresso Pods.I will be writing a separate review on the "HandPresso" unit, which I have learn to love!In short, here's the main highlights for the 'StarBucks Espresso Pods' - I Highly Recommend them!* Starbucks Espresso Roast Pods, are each in their own Foil-sealed package, EZ to tear open, with 12-pods in each box, has a dense, caramel-like sweetness and smooth, satisfying finish. I usually take 2 boxes on my 2 to 3 -week trips, and always have some left over.* Price point of only $4.95 is Excellent! That's only 41 cents per shot, AND, it's Human-powered! How Cool is that!* Starbucks coffee pods, filled with fresh-roasted, ground and tamped Starbucks Espresso Roast, so there's no measuring, no grinding, no mess.* The coffee pods can be used with most home espresso machines (must accept E.S.E. - Easy Serving Espresso - pods.)* With a good `Routine', you can make an Expresso in 5-minutes or less!Here is my Recommended AM Espresso Routine:1. Be sure to clean the unit the night before, then leave my Favorite StarBucks Coffee Cup + the  `HandPresso' open in 2 parts + 1 or 2 Espresso Pod(s) + Creamer, and/or Sweetener, if applicable, out on the kitchen counter.2. First thing in the AM, before shaving, I  place a 1 or 2-quart Tea Kettle with or without a Whistle is fine on the stove. Check out the Pedrini model listed here on Amazon, it's Simple and it Works!Use about a quart of fresh or filtered water and bring to a Boil.3. As soon as I return to the kitchen, I hand-pump the HandPresso to the maximum of 16 (top of Green bar), and once you get the hang of it, this only takes 1 to 2 minutes, and is Great Exercise, BTW!TIP - the Handle IS the `hand-pump', and it only takes a Quarter Turn Counter-clockwise to "Unlock", and let the Pumping begin! When done, you may turn it Clock-wise to Re-lock it, but is not necessary.4. I then open the Espresso Pod, place it nearby, AND, place my Powered or Liquid Creamer (&/or Sweetener), in the cup, and pour an ounce or two of Hot H2O, into it to "prep it".5. Then, I pour the Hot, boiling water into the Glass Well opening, on the HandPresso, to at or near the top, I place the  Pod in it, then place the Lid, Pushing down slightly (look for the White line markings), then Turn it Clock-wise and Locking it in place. Important - Don't forget to Push & Place the Actuator Button, into the "On" position.6. I Flip the HandPresso over and directly over my cup, and Press Down on the Button. Watch the Magic Happen! This only takes about 3 or 4 minutes, and at the end you will start to see BOTH the Pressure Needle move to the 0 position, AND there will also be some creamy froth and bubbling from the Pod.7. Stir and Enjoy! Remember, once you have established your `ROUTINE Steps', the whole procedure becomes much Faster, especially when Traveling, Camping or on any Expeditions.Caveats - Use less H2O if you want a Stronger Shot, Use more Creamer to dilute it, thus giving you a fuller cup of coffee/espresso. If you are just going to use a Sweetener, and NO Creamer, I highly using the Organic, Low Glycemic Sweetener, made from Blue Agave Nectar, by Wholesome Sweeteners.

column9: Starbucks Groceries are often close to their expiration date
column10: It bugs me when I buy groceries from starbucks and look at the expiration date on the package and it's very soon.In this case, I got the coffee pods yesterday, and they expire 6 days from today.Not very cool.

I ordered the Starbuck pods even though some of the reviews were not very good.  I took a chance and with the first order the pods were great and so I felt much more comfortable to reorder.  Unfortunately the second order was awful.  The taste was bitter and left a burning sensation in my mouth  I will not order this product again.  I dont know if Starbucks was trying to get rid of defective product by selling through Amazon, but it not only put a bad taste in my mouth from the horrible coffee these pods produced it also shows a serious lack of quality control by Starbucks and the product that bears its name and Amazon that sold this offensive product..

I normally don't buy any coffee as I roast my own, and to me Starbuck's coffee is usually very marginal quality wise at best but these pods are convienent and actually have a pretty good flavor. Would recommend them for the price.
I have had a few pods in the box from an earlier order that did not produce any coffee at all, just warm water. So I have to see if the replacement order turns out to be more consistent.
Starbucks Espresso Pods coffee tastes great, nice bold flavor, easy to make and tastes like an espresso should. I would highly recommend it.Starbucks Espresso Pods (12 count)

Before you jump down my throat and tell me I know nothing about the stuffy habit of espresso, remember what this product is designed for. This is not the world's best espresso, as many of the reviews state, but if I wanted the world's best espresso would I buy pods from Starbucks? Take this product for what it is! A quality espresso that is very easy to make. I think this product is exactly what it intends to be.
Please do not buy this junk. It is the worst coffee you could possibly get. Produces no crema at all and tastes like burnt bitter coffee. The pods have residue coffee on the side not cleanly packed.
I don't drink Decaf, but my Mom does and she loves this coffee. She has used almost the whole box.

Although it says these pods work for almost all portafilters, the instructions on the back say to place a "pressure insert" into the portafilter basket. I have no idea what that is, since there isn't one on my Gaggia espresso machine. The coffee barely trickles out.
I ordered these pods with the espresso machine I gave my husband for Christmas.  They are very bold -- enough to make us both a small cappuccino-- and taste great!  I'll be ordering more of these.
These pods are perfect for larger dinner parties where you have to brew many shots quickly. The flavor is good, the creme is OK and the easy clean up is great. Very happy.

I liked the coffee pods. I bought 3 brands to test which i liked best. as far as flavor, this is good for a production coffee. the only way it cold have been better would have been to grind it 30 seconds before brewing, not what i'm doing here with these. so you can't compare this to your espresso in Italy.My DeLonghi machine didn't seem to like these pods. they are tightly packed and i'm sure, finely ground. i discovered that if i dampened the pod first it would then flow more easily.5 stars for flavor and convenience, 4 for the price.
So much easier than packing my espresso machine with grounds. I highly recommend this product. It is so nice that the pods are wrapped individually so you don't have to worry about freshness.

Fantastic turn-around time!  Shipment arrived about 3 days after I placed the order.  :  Product was as advertised, correct amount, and in good shape.  Will order my espresso pods from Amazon.com again!!

I just love these starbucks espresso pods! They make it easy to have a coffee house experience at home without having to make a mess measuring espresso and tamping the grounds! Compact, easy to use, awesome product! Great job starbucks I will continue to buy these and use for years to come!

Let's face it, it's hard to find good coffee in the States. Your average coffee is little more than dirt water and all Starbucks did was bringing to the mainstream a little better coffee that why Americans who visit Italy and try an espresso in any bar cannot go back to Starbucks. Just today a friend returning from a week in Rome asked me to help him buy an espresso machine. The problem as always is not finding a good machine (plenty choice) but finding a good coffee. I grew up in Italy and when it comes to coffee I don't compromise. I actually get my coffee from Italy. I'm a bit of a coffee connoisseur (check my review of the De Longhi machine as wel), I do know Starbucks coffee well and I don't like it because it's your typical high volume quality. Sometimes away from home I'll go for it because it's either that or a cup of what I call "dish-washing water." Starbucks roasts a high volume of coffee at high temperature to keep up with their demand. If you want a good espresso you have to roast the grains at low temperature for a long time, that's not fast enough for Starbucks and that's why their coffee tastes bitter and burned. I give a generous three stars because the pods make life easier and keep the place cleaner regardless of it being quite expensive; but on Amazon you can get 150 pods of Lavazza coffee for less than $50 and that's a much better coffee even if Lavazza is the high volume of Italian coffee.

column9: Thought it would make faster espresso....
column10: I was kind of disappointed in this product. I was looking for something that would help me make espresso faster in the morning. This actually makes it take longer. Usually I grind up beans and tamp them down and sometimes it takes awhile to get the correct type of grounds. Then I just warm up the machine and it makes dark beautiful espresso.With these pods, the water has to go through the pods several times before I get a dark enough espresso. I'm sorry, but I don't have the time of day to keep running hot water through my machine and into the espresso glasses, waiting for the perfect espresso.Other than that, it's an easy cleanup.

I have a sensitive stomach and cannot use any pregound coffee - decaf or not.  The only thing I can do is grind whole beans - decaf of course. You may do fine with this of course.  Also on a personal basis I do not like Starbucks in general.

Currently[...] is selling this exact 2# coffee for under ten dollars after instant discount. It has a high end restaurant, low acid, wonderful smooth flavor quality about it. It is a very oily instead of dry bean so you may want to just keep a small amount out in an airtight container and freeze the rest. I only purchased one bag to try since I had been disappointed in kirkland's/starbuck's organic gold bag coffee. Now I must hurry back and purchase more before all is sold as it was a limited buy item. I am glad Amazon carries this brand, although it is the non-organic version. I assure you this will be one of the best coffees you will try.Enjoy!

This definetly tastes like coconut water, but because they added sea salt it tends to leave a salty aftertaste. It would be an exact replica of coconut water if they just removed the salt.I guess it is because people use this to replace electrolytes, so unless you are training hard, you might not like it.
Reva Coconut water Instant Natural mix does NOT taste anything like Coconut water.  Reva has added sea salt to the mix and that is all you taste.  Very expensive disappointment!
Bought 3 boxes of Reva packets would be perfect for traveling but I tried 1 packet and it tasted awful, had to give away.

column9: Has SALT and SUGAR added... but tastes great/fast shipping!
column10: HOW can you say it's natural if you add salt and sugar to it? Aside from that, it does taste pretty close to real young thai coconut water, and the ease of mixing cannot be beat! I bought a box of these yesterday for a plane trip I'm off on tomorrow. I'll be spending a week traveling and I'm unsure of the availability of coconut water on my trip. The box arrived in less than 24 hours.

I have tried all the coconut waters and this one tastes great and is so convenient.  I am a runner and I travel a lot so I pay attention to hydration.  This is perfect because I can take it anywhere and just have to get some water when I want it!

I have tried almost all the Coconut Waters in the market and I like this one the best. I usual drink this after I get done with a long ride or after my work outs. I have read that it is very good for hydration and for me, at least, that seems to be very true. I will definately buy this product again because it is easy to take with me to the gym and taste great.

column9: A Rich and Robust Alternative to Coffee
column10: Three years ago I gave up most caffeine in my diet but I've never been able to give up that last little bit contained in a good cup of decaffeinated coffee -- until now.  While the flavor is a little different than that of coffee, its close enough to become my new morning ritual.  Here's what I like about this healthy alternative:  * I brew it in a coffee pot just like usual  * The drink's consistency is similar to coffee and is dark roasted color  * It comes in various flavors just like coffee  * I drink it with about half the raw sugar and cream I used to use  * I'm totally satisfied with my drink; I don't feel cheatedIn addition to cutting on caffeine, I'm also cutting costs.  When I make coffee I use a tablespoon of coffee per cup.  With this stuff I use only a half-tablespoon.

If you're searching for a coffee replacement, something that fools you into thinking you're drinking coffee, this probably isn't it, but if you're looking for a great tasting, healthy alternative to coffee, I don't believe you can do any better.  As I'm typing this, I'm drinking a huge glass of 2 cups brewed Teeccino added to 1 cup light soy milk and a packet of Stevia with ice.  I have it once a day and look forward to it, knowing I'm actually adding something healthy to my body, and there are no sugar or caffeine jitters. I've been buying Teeccino for about 15 years, first at the health food stores and then on Amazon.com where I always get it for the best price. (Love free shipping!!)

One of my favourite herbal coffee beverages. It is caffeine free and actually good for you.  It has potassium, fiber and helps with digestion.I love the Mocha flavour especially since I am a chocoholic.Try it you won't be disappointed.

I love the new teeccino alternate choice tocoffee and/or tea.  Tasty both iced or hotand non acidic and no caffeine.  A nice changeof pace.  An excellent blend of flavors.My favs are the almond and mocha.

The following review is the review I wrote on the vanilla flavored Teeccino. I saw no reason to change it except to mention that I found the Mocha flavor to be even better. It's not nearly as chocolaty or sweet as hot chocolate (thankfully) and it has only 20 calories per cup. It tastes more like coffee then the vanilla and mint and is the flavor smoother. My wife didn't care for the other two but loves the Mocha. It makes for a great, healthy after-dinner desert drink.*This is my second time trying Teeccino and I must say the more I drink it the better I like it. As I've gotten older, coffee is having adverse effects my digestive track and it's not been good so I need something else and tea just doesn't cut it. Teeccino seems to be about as close to coffee as one can get without being coffee. The mint was really good and this vanilla nut may even be better. Teeccino doesn't leave that bad aftertaste coffee gives you (even the really good stuff) and it seems to give a slight energy boost. Nothing like coffee though. No brain stimulation. I think the energy comes from the inulin. I did some research on inulin and I suggest you do the same. I'm still not sure if it's a good thing or not. Some say yes and others no. It doesn't seem to have a negative effect on me as of yet. If you need to get off of coffee or hot chocolate or your just tired of drinking tea give Teeccino a try. I think you'll be quite pleased. Oh yea... I put honey and milk in mine and it's really good that way.I've been making a pitcher at the beginning of the week and keeping it in the fridge. It seems to keep very well. It's easier to heat up a cup on the stove in the morning so I don't wake the entire house with the noise of the coffee maker or microwave.

This coffee has a rich robust taste without all of the acid and no caffeine. I would strongly recommend this coffee if you need to distance yourself from caffeine for health reasons. Not only does it taste like coffee, but it taste better that coffee.

Outstanding robust flavor.  Helps reduce acid reflux caused by regular coffee.  I use half coffee and half Teeccino and love it.  I've been using it for a couple of years.  Amazon also offers free shipping for a large order if you can wait but I still recieve it within a week.
Teeccino as a coffee substitute does take time to adjust to the taste difference; but once one adjusts, the taste is okay; it's just not the same taste as coffee itself.

For those of us that can no longer drink coffee for health reasons, this may be the answer. As another reviewer suggested, I first tried a sample packet of all the Teeccino herbal coffees and this was the one I liked most. None taste like my wonderful coffee but for me this was a pleasant hot drink. If you try the samples, I suggest you try them at different concentrations. My preference is a more diluted drink that the standard recommended. After using it a couple of months I find I enjoy this hot drink almost as much as I did my morning Coffee. It brews the same as coffee and my be used with creamer and sugar. The only reason I gave it 4 stars is that it still isn't coffee.

I have to quit drinking coffee as I have horrible caffiene reactions. I love the taste of coffee though. I've tried hazelnut and mocha so far and both are tasty. Hazelnut has a bit stronger flavor but mocha is good too. Even my kids liked it when they tasted it. I think its a great alternative and better for you.

I've always enjoyed a cup of black, mild-roast coffee in the morning, but found that my breastfed baby's reflux was much worse when I drank coffee- even the occasional treat. A friend had read about this product, suggested it, and I've not been disappointed! I find that if I use an equal amount of Teeccino as coffee, the taste is too strong to drink black. By cutting back the mix just a little, it's the perfect amount. I'm sure I'll go back to coffee at some point, but Teeccino has been a lifesaver for both baby and me during this period!
Teeccino is the best herbal coffee I've tried. It's still not coffee, but it's healthy.

column9: Not as good as I was hoping
column10: ehh, it's ok.  the mocha just did not come out with flavor like i was hoping.

column9: it's delicious. don't think of it as coffee
column10: I take my coffee "white" disguising it with sugar and skim milk.I chose this for a warm drink to drink after meals. I'm breastfeeding and my son doesn't respond well when I have had caffeine. Most decaffeinated coffees are made decaf using formaldehyde so that's a gross option.My favorite is the Hazelnut flavor, mildly nutty (don't expect starbuck hazelnut syrup). I don't like it black but I never drank real coffee straight either. I take mine with either skim milk or half/half.  Sometimes I use coconut flavored powder creamer. It's yummy.I will purchase it again (along with trying other flavors).For those of you disappointed in the taste, it's not coffee. It's better. Diet Coke isn't Coke, so why do you expect fake coffee to taste like real coffee?

I discovered Teeccino when I happened to see it on a huge discount at my local organic grocery. I normally wouldn't entertain the idea of a coffee substitute because I love a good fresh cup of coffee. However, I was pleasantly surprised! This stuff is robust and tasty and very satisfying. There are several flavors though so I started to experiment and found that I prefer the Mediterranean line of Teeccino, specifically "Mocha." So I switched from coffee to Mocha Teeccino and am living happily ever after. :) I now have my Teeccino automatically shipped to me so a package of three bags arrives on my doorstep just as I'm just about to run out. I get a reduced price this way and I'm basically cheap so that works for me.I have a suggestion, though... Like me, you may prefer one or two Teeccino flavors over others so do some taste testing so you can find out your favorite. I think there's a sample pack available so that should help. (Or maybe buy a few flavors and split with friends so you can all taste test). You should also know that the name Mocha may imply that it tastes like chocolate but that's not the case. This is not a chocolate-y drink (unless you add some of your own, which is always an option). I especially like the Mocha because it has a comforting and bold taste without being too bitter, too sweet, or too strong in any particular flavor.Oh, I almost forgot to mention that it makes a strong cup of brew in my press pot so I use a bit less than I would with coffee. That helps with the savings too.One caution... If you're thinking of trying the little Teeccino bags that remind you of making tea, I'd pass. You could maybe use two bags at a time but I've definitely found that the Teeccino that you buy in the bigger (11 oz.) bags has a much better flavor. Enjoy!

I woke up one morning and was diagnosed with a severe case of GERD (acid reflux disease). I had to give up everything.  Soda, caffeine, tea or alcohol... everything causes the lower esophagial sphincter to stay open, causing the worst cases of esophagitus and other complication.  So, out with the coffee... but decaf was still effecting my reflux.  I searched high and low for an alternative and just fell in love with Teeccino.  No caffeine, great taste, close enough to coffee to not miss the flavor and they have excellent blends for flavor.  Mocha has become one of my favorites, but so has Hazelnut and their new Almond Amaretto.  Try different ones. You won't be disappointed.  It took me 3 weeks to get over the headaches caused by withdrawl of caffeine, but I don't miss it now, in fact the weird thing is, I have more energy. Go figure.So for you refluxers out there, give this a shot!

column9: Am I the only one who doesn't think Teeccino's is a god send?
column10: For a couple of years, I have been anxious to try out Teeccino. At one point, I didn't want to spend the money. At another, I didn't have a brewer nor wanted to buy one.When I started eating mostly raw foods, I decided to kick my coffee habit and pick up a Teeccino sample pack. I was thrilled when it arrived and I tried the Maya original first because it contained zero sugars. When I opened the packet, it was an earthy sort of smell, kind of like mulch or soil. It wasn't exactly appetizing. I brewed it and found the taste was NOTHING and I mean NOTHING like coffee. I tried again the next day and couldn't handle the taste of the Maya.So, I tried Mint Chocolate one day and Mocha the next of the Mediteranean blends. The mint chocolate tasted nothing like the reviews I had read - which suggested something similar to a thin mint cookie or a junior mint. I added some almond milk and stevia in order to make it taste a little better. It was tolerable, not awesome, but tolerable.I will say the mocha, thus far, has been my favorite. Is it delicious? Not by a long shot. It still has that soily taste to it and resembles coffee only in texture. It has an EXTREMELY mild, almost unnoticeable hint of chocolate - but it'll do for now.With additions, creamer, stevia, sweetener - whatever, Teeccino is indeed, very tolerable. I was highly disappointed after the rave reviews I had read, but it's still better than having no substitute in my opinion. I'm just curious as to what brands of coffee people have been buying to think Teeccino tastes anything like real coffee?

I love these little mints! They kind of taste like red hots ..yum! They are vegan and kosher! and...did you happen to see the packaging? Very sleek and nice!At this great amazon.com price, I had to buy more than one case! Not only that, but I got free shipping and they came pretty quickly! Makes a nice little gift too.I *heart* amazon and hint mints :)
This is a great salsa. It has a very robust flavor. Great with chips.Even works great as a great sauce for Hamburgers and Fried Chicken.
A delicate, quality product I've found more uses for this than I expected. It's wonderful to be able to impart such flavors without the darkness of traditional soy sauce. Highly recommended.
Takumi White Soy Sauce is an excellent soy sauce to use when eating sushi due to its lite taste which does not overwhelm the main dish.

column9: Nothing wrong with this product... but
column10: I recently discovered white soy sauce and i found this amazing brand at the 99 cent store, yeah the 99 cent store. Well i guess this other brand that i found was so popular that they were always out so i decided to do research online and stumbled onto this one. Well it's okay, it's nothing like the one i found at the 99 cent store can't find it anywhere. But it will do. It's not bad or anything like that it's just not the one i feel in love with. column9: Good, but has a different behavior than traditional 3-way mixes..
column10: I've used this product (a mcpa, dicamba, triclopyr mix) for several years now, and I find it has some pros, and some cons compared with a traditional 2,4-d/mcpp/dicamba mixes (and possibly newer mixes). Loving it or hating it will depend on your weeds.On the plus side, it has triclopyr, and because of this it does much better against wild violet, creeping charlie, and Oxalis/sorrel than the old-school mixes (which have no affect at all on the first 2).On the down side, it seems control most of the common weeds that 2,4-d does well against, but it takes a lot longer to kill them, and may require two passes to do it. (ie: dandelion, plantain, clover)My old house had wild violet problems, and my new house has creeping woodsorrel problems. I love this product because it is effective against those troublesome weeds that so few other products kill.Of course, we now in 2012 have a whole new set of "plus crabgrass" mixes coming out, based on 2,4-d, dicamba and quinclorac (and one brand adding sulfentrazone to the mix). The quinclorac gives them control of grassy weeds previously untouched by post-emergent sprays, and the sulfentrazone takes that further (nutsedge!). The quinclorac should also be at least somewhat effective against wild violet, but I suspect that the lack of mcpa/mcpp may cause them to have a different set of common weeds they won't work on. Time will tell as these are somewhat newer herbicides and a lot of detailed herbicide guides don't cover them yet..Moral of the story: No weed killer is perfect and will kill every weed without killing your lawn too. If you have a weed in your yard you can't kill, find out what it is (plenty of picture guides on the web), find out what kills it, and buy a product with the right ingredients.

This review is for PoP Oolong tea bags. My tea background was first drinking Indian milk tea using black loose tea, milk, spices, and sugar. I added far-Eastern teas (non-milk varieties) in my search for a quicker tea to brew (milk tea needs more time to prepare). I am on my 3rd box of PoP Oolong tea. The tea is not like black or green teas. Be prepared for a bitter taste but with a sweeter aftertaste. Like black teas, this produces some kind of coating feeling on the tongue, almost similar to eating an unripened banana. It is somewhat woody in taste and smell (maybe a bit flowery. It may also be slightly sour, but less than some green teas. I have tried whole leaf oolong from a Chinese shop and that was more like green tea. If you can afford more expensive oolong teas, then you might get better quality. For the price, you're getting a good deal. I also think that the batches vary so sometimes you might get a stronger, bitter flavor but if you experiment with the brewing, you might get your desired flavor.To brew this PoP Oolong tea, realize that ground tea in bags will release their flavors much faster. My solution is to boil some filtered water. After bringing to a boil, I turn off the stove and add 1 cup (237 mL) hot water to the tea bag. Then wait ~30 seconds (or golden brown color appears)and remove the bag. The first cup usually extracts most of the caffeine and is the most bitter and strong taste. Now I can brew with another cup of the hot water. I can brew around 4 cups with the colors being golden brown, golden, light green, and very light green. It is best to brew by the color and not the time. If you leave the bag in too long, it will be terribly bitter.Tea brewing is an art and science, as many other things in life are. Please refer to the science of solvent extraction for a better idea. Basically, you are extracting the tea's aromatic compounds into the water. The flavor of the brew are mainly affected by water quality, extraction time (the time in water), and water temperature. You have to experiment with this for your preferred flavor. Sugar is absolutely not necessary, if prepared correctly.

column9: Yes it does have an odor that some will find disagreeable, but it works for me and I will continue to purchase it
column10: I read some of the reviews on here and I almost didn't purchase. So I bit the bullet and purchased this at a local B&M store.  When I got home after work, I boiled some water and opened the package.  I noticed that this tea was packaged in a plastic bag so I guess it did has a pungent smell.  I opened the plastic bag and took a big whiff.  I was kind of disappointed.  It doesn't smell as bad as some of the other reviewers made it out to me but then again my nose has been wonky for some time so it could be me.  Yes I will admit that it does has a funky odor but it is not that strong to me.  To me, smells like this health food store I used to frequent in the Hyde Park neighborhood.  Very musky but weirdly comforting.  I have tried it with peppermint, turmeric (for a different affliction) and I have tried it plain with stevia and it taste okay to me.  I wouldn't say I have an iron stomach because I can easily get sick if food is left out in the open not at the proper temperature.  For me, this product took about two days for it to kick in and I am now able to sleep for a full eight hours straight instead of sleeping in fits of four hours here, wake up for about two hours, sleep for three, wake up for a hour and sleep for another four hours.  For those with sensitive noses and sense of taste, you have been amply warned by other reviewers.  For others, I say give it a shot or at least pair it with some other teas to dilute the taste a bit.  For example, mints like peppermint or spearmint will help.  Some folks will use lavender to mask the smell.

column9: GREAT ALL PURPOSE WINE MAKING YEAST, LOVE IT!
column10: I have made about 12 batches of red wine with 8 grape varitals with Lalvin EC-1118 over the last year. Every batch has started quickley and fermented to completion with no problems. I do not sterilyze my equipment or use any chemicals. I start the must at about 75 degrees and let it find it's own temperature balance after that. This yeast is so vigorus that nothing strange seems to ever be able to get started. I scatter the yeast on the must as soon as I have in in the stainless soup kettle, let it float on top for 15 minutes and then stir it in. I always adjust my sugar for 15% alcohol. About brix 26. This will take awhile to complete fermentation. About 2-3 months due to the high sugar content, but the wine has all been great. So much better then any commercial wine I have tried that I no longer want to buy wine. I went to a wine tasting recently. These were $30-$40 dollar a bottle wines. They were so far inferior to what I make that they gaged me.Larry Dennis

EC-1118Saccharomyces bayanusOriginThe EC-1118 strain was isolated, studied and selected from Champagne fermentations. Due to its competitive factor and ability to ferment equally well over a wide temperature range, the EC-1118 is one of the most widely used yeasts in the world.Oenological properties and applicationsThe fermentation characteristics of the EC-1118 -- extremely low production of foam, volatile acid and hydrogen sulfide (H2S) -- make this strain an excellent choice. This strain ferments well over a very wide temperature range, from 10° to 30°C (50° to 86°F) and demonstrates high osmotic and alcohol tolerance. Good flocculation with compact lees and a relatively neutral flavor and aroma contribution are also properties of the EC-1118.The EC-1118 strain is recommended for all types of wines, including sparkling, and late harvest wines and cider. It may also be used to restart stuck fermentations.An excellent choice for champagnes and late harvest wines. Also a very good choice for dry whites.

column9: Works for me - at half dose.
column10: I am a nurse that works night shift and travels frequently. Between the two, I have a funky sleep schedule and sometimes go through periods of extreme insomnia.Then, at the airport in Long Beach, CA I found Dream Water. I was a little shocked at the price but decided to try it anyway. Because it was expensive, I tried half a shot and it worked, well, like a dream. A whole shot makes me do weird things in my sleep, but a half shot makes me fall asleep and get a good 6-8 hours with no hangover effect - even during my severe episodes of insomnia.As a nurse, I would like to recommend that you be careful taking it every day. One of the ingredients (5-HTP) can cause serotonin syndrome in certain doses. Since we don't know the exact dose they use, I would look up serotonin syndrome and be on the look out for side effects if you take it regularly. Just in case. I haven't had any side effects, but better safe than sorry.Also, be careful mixing it with certain other meds used to adjust mood (anxiety/depression meds) or other sleep aids - even natural ones. Just a heads up.
