Jasmine tea - always a favorite and Uncle Lee's never disappoints.  Good value when purcheased in the larger 100 count box.
My kids (2 and 5 years old) love this dressing!  They happily eat their salad every night with dinner with their "purple dressing" (Annie's raspberry vinaigrette).

Love this vinagarette. It is low in calorie, yet not full of chemicals and artificial sweeteners. Great price compared to my local health food store where an 8oz bottle of the same thing is close to $4.

column9: I'm sorry to have to agree with the one-star reviewer about Annie's
column10: I have used Annie's Lite Raspberry vinaigrette for several years, and lately I've switched to another brand (Newman's Own).  Here's why I no longer buy Annie's salad dressing, with this raspberry vinaigrette being the prime example.Annie's quality on this dressing deteriorated some time ago, when I noticed that the raspberry color had changed and no longer seemed "natural".  The reason is that there's so little actual raspberry(ies) in the dressing that it no longer has the original, wonderful flavor. In fact, the color is now due to black currant "extract" and not from the tiny amount of real raspberry.The second reason that this product is not worth buying is the exorbitant price the company charges, and this is just for a small 8 oz. bottle.The third reason is that this dressing consists mostly of water, followed by  vinegar, and then a vegetable oil (the latter can or may consist of sunflower oil, which is a cheaper oil).I guess the "Lite" on Annie's label for this product ("Annie's Naturals Raspberry Vinaigrette, LITE") now means it's "lite/light in flavor and quality"!  It is really too bad that this company  has decided to cheapen its products, even though at the same time they haven't lowered their outrageous prices...

column9: Cheap, nasty garbage parading as healthy.
column10: There are dozens of organic and/or so-called "natural" salad dressings on the market, but I've never seen and tasted such garbage in my entire life pretending it's healthy. Annie's lines are comprised of the cheapest and smallest amounts of "organic" indredients possible. Keep in mind that many foods are grown organically at low prices so dont' think that because something is organic, that it is high quality, nutritious or in healthy amounts. Annie's dressings are mostly water, made smooth with small amounts of cheap canola oil, an oil which is questioned today as being good for the body. You wont' find cold-pressed olive oils or high-quality spices. Just the lowest, cheapest and smallest amounts of spice, the lack of flavors disguised by the use of vinegar, again another cheap thing to make "organically".  It disgusts me to see this dirt on the  market and to see how bamboozled the average consumer is when they see pretty label with the words "natural" or "organic" on it.  I can make a raspberry or papaya dressing myself all organic and much cheaper, healthier and tastier than this line.

Maggi sauces are pretty common, but the only one I found myself craving was the Maggi Masala Chili. It is the only Maggi sauce with some bite (it's spicy), and it's perfect with almost any fried dish.  I use it primarily for breaded and fried seafood: crabcakes, tuna croquettes, etc. It is also great as a companion to asian foods like potstickers and dumplings. There is a slight masala flavor, but it does not dominate so the foods retain their flavor; everything does NOT start to taste like curry when you add Maggi's Masala Chili. If you like hotsauces but have yet to find one that has good flavor or enough heat, try the masala chili, you will not be disappointed.
Sugar-free yet vrey flavorful.  Price is fair enough and the service superior (it even arrived early!).  A++++

I actually have tried four flavors (to date) of the Di Vinci syrups.  I like them all.  I use them in baking (you can find some recipes on the internet for using these syrups in things like muffins, etc).  Be aware that these syrups are made with Splenda.  We love Splenda - use it everyday, so we're ok with it.  (Some folks have a problem with it, though).  Currently, in my pantry, I have strawberry (I suggest using this over some low-fat frozen yogurt or ice cream!) vanilla, peanut butter and pancake syrup.  All four taste great!  The consistency of the pancake syrup is thinner than you might want, however.  I bought it because my local store did not have syrup made with Splenda at the time.  (Now they do, though).  The price listed here is good.  I've paid $17 per bottle at an online retailer!!
The best tasting Kringle ever!  I am able to freeze it, let it thaw and it's as fresh as the day baked!  Sweet indulgence!

Our 12 yr old shepherd mix has been taking this for about a year.  Our vet reccommended it, he thinks that dogs digest it better than pills.  I wasn't sure, but figured I would try it.Within a week I saw a difference in our dog.  He was a LOT more lively.  And he clearly felt better.  In fact, he felt good enough that he started stealing food off the kitchen counters again.  I was so happy to see that, it represented progress forward (instead of just holding steady, which was my best hope for his arthritis).I reccommend this product to so many of my friend with dogs.  It is really amazing what it can do and how well it works.  Best of all, the dogs love it.  I don't have to smear peanut butter on some pill and hope he'll swallow it.  If you have a dog with arthritis or hip dysplasia, this is worth trying.
This is a miracle product for older dogs.  I gives them new energy and mobility!!!

It is our dog Zoe's favorite treat.(our cat loves it too} Our Jack Russell loves is so much that she is willing to let us give her her insulin injection without a wimper knowing she will get a Jerky as a reward.

Sea Jerky - Bulk - 91 ctThis jerky is FABULOUS.  My Akita has arthritis & my Australian Cattle dog has hip dysphasia.  Since their vet recommended Nutrisea Sea Jerky, both have been without pain - they run & play as if they didn't have anything wrong.  Also, it smells divine & they love it; they think it'a a treat!
I have worked for a Vet for 9 years.  I have been witness to this product working well for many dogs.  Plus they like this---it is a great treat!!This is worth the $$!

I was introduced to this great product by a vet when our previous dog was 12. He lived to 16 and I truly believe that this product extended his life by a few months or more. We now give it to our new little guy and he loves it. It is great for their joints and coat as well as their general health. Great product!!
This is good cheap jerky.  Some people don't like the taste, but I love it.  It's not a bad taste, just different.

I was not satisfied with these walnuts. The first time I ordered them, they were excellent. The second time I ordered them, they tasted very stale, almost burnt. Absolutely disgusting. Normally, if something is not up to par I will at least eat it to prevent wasting, but these were so bad that I threw them out and considered calling amazon for a return, although I never took the time to do that. I just made the decision never to order them again.

These were good walnuts.  Not crazy about the plastic bags but these are by far the tastiest walnuts,,more expensive but they taste good and are organic.  Why must healthy food be costly and hard to find?  Anyway I couldn't find these again to re-order so I am trying another brand. I will just have to look out for these.
I kept 2 bags out and froze the rest so they would keep longer.  Didn't last long though ... these are DELICIOUS!
Sunridge Farms organic walnuts seem fresh, taste good, were not crushed, and are organically grown in the US; I think they're good walnuts.

This has been a disappointing item the last few shipments. The quality of the walnuts has been deteriorating so much so that I have cancelled the last two shipments. Has the nut crop been drastically affected by some problem? The walnuts, almonds and pistachios seem to have been affected in the last three months. Previously I have been totally satisfied with the Sun Ridge products.

These are great snack crackers.  My family first tried these in Japan and fell in love with them.  They are seasoned nicely with a salty seasoning.  I can't find them in the grocery stores here in the U.S. but found them here on amazon.  Glad I don't have to do without them.

So Hot Kid! Makes these rice crackers for infants called Baby Mumums.My brother keeps eating my daughters crackers. I must admit they are very tasty (especially the veggie flavor)So I've been searching for an adult rice cracker thats similar.These crackers were close. They are just too thick. Thats the only problem. If they were 1/2 or even 2/3 as thick they would be better. The flavor is sort of soy saucey. Its a good flavor. But i'm still searching for an adult rice cracker as good as a Baby Mumum (but hopefully less expensive by oz)
These are OK but the Big Shelley Snowy crackers are much better.  These seem quite salty to me,hence I don't like them nearly as well as others.

This is a fantastic meal in a can.  Not too spicy but not bland at all, it can be eaten alone, just heat it up. You can also add some tomato sauce and vegetarian protein crumbles (I use Yves brand) and it's a terrific chili that tastes great in whole wheat pita bread or a tortilla wrap. Low salt, low fat, it's a perfect fast food dinner when you're tired.  I ordered a case because the local supply is inconsistent.  Too bad that there are many shelves of sodium- and fat-based products, and so little room for simple, organic good food.  I will enjoy this for many meals this summer.

In general, I'm a big fan of rice and beans -- though these seemed to be a bit mild in terms of spice. A shot of hot sauce Huy Fong Sriracha sauce - 17 oz x 2 bottles and a few twists of sea salt made the flavor pop. I've also enjoyed these with a sprinkling of grated cheese. A convenient, fast meal that doubles as comfort food. Good stuff.

PROS:-The can is BPA-free.-Brown rice is healthier than white rice.-Beans are healthy.-Low sodium is healthy-All you have to do is heat up this item.-It is easy to add ground meat or sliced sausage to the rice.-It is easy to cook the cajun rice with just a few minutes of medium heat.-A fast lunch or dinner that is healthier than microwave food.-The low price on this website.CONS:-The rice is a little bland until you add your own seasoning.

So surprising for rice and beans in a can! The rice and beans both still have integrity and good flavore. If you like spicier, add hot sauce, but they have a nice spiff and are a great, easy and healthy side dish!

This is a nice, though mild, rice and bean combination. A little Tabasco makes it even better. Eden Organic makes this in different "flavors", which would be nice to get combined in one case.  A dozen of the same one takes a while to get through.

column9: On the Wish List No More
column10: I bought two cans of this product from a health food store other than Amazon and was quite dissappointed when I heated it up for a "fast food" dinner.  As far as I could tell, it had absolutely no taste except for the hot peppers, which were far too hot for me.  And as the most liked negative review said, it had a very unpleasant smell.Judging from the variability of the reviews, I'm guessing this is a work in progress.

I got a can of these from the grocery store after seeing the good reviews here, but whoa-- they are completely burnt tasting! The spices were terrible and everything was strangely dry. I could barely stand the smell as this was cooking and I ended up tossing it; adding a bit of salt and other seasonings did nothing. Very disappointing!

column9: Seriously? All of these reviews have to be fake. This stuff tastes terrible.
column10: The tomato flavor is burnt and the rice is bland. I was shocked when I bought this at the store. It was quite expensive and it was, quite bad. I compared it to an organic boxed rice and beans combination and frankly, this can almost tasted like garbage.

I bought one on a family trip a while back just for something to do while in the hotel (I usually have a tennis ball or something to bounce at the walls in extreme cases of boredom)i got it out of its package and it bounced really really high I'v kept it with me ever since it is awesome, but the fun ended cause my dog chewed it. :^(

Our pumpkin seeds arrived on June 29, 2011.  The code on our bags is 1441148, which means the production date is May 24, 2011.  It's amazing how it goes from production to my hands in a bit over a month.  The pumpkin seeds indeed look and smell fresh.  In fact, the aroma and taste are really intense.  I'm so used to Trader Joe's and Whole Food's pumpkin seeds that are drier and probably older.  (Unfortunately, my local Trader Joe's stopped selling organic pumpkin seeds and Whole Foods is so expensive that I needed to find something more affordable.)  After I open a new bag, I leave it open to dry a bit.  We are probably losing some nutrition, but it does improve the taste while keeping them raw.The Amazon webpage only says, "Processed in a facility which uses peanuts and other nuts."  The back of the package says, "May contain wheat, soy, tree nuts, peanuts, milk".  The pumpkin seeds are probably processed in a facility that processes wheat, soy, and milk too.

Great seeds! Very Healthy and organic! I do prefer roasted just due to the taste and I was roasting some of them in the oven on low.  However,  the raw seed are more nutritious and I am glad SUnridge sells them like this.

I suspect that raw pumpkin seeds (pepitas) are better for you than roasted and salted, but evidently it is an acquired taste.  Unlike some raw pumpkin seeds at the health food store, they are not bitter.  But I have to mix in 25% roasted and salted for me to like eating them.Unlike the illustration, they are the same green color as the raw ones you see in the health food store.

One of the best plant-based sources of protein.  7g per serving, without the saturated fat and cholesterol that meat and dairy have.  (this product is cholesterol-free).It is an acquired taste, but I usually throw a handful in a smoothie after working out (rarely do I eat them straight out of the bag).Champion body builder Robert Cheeke loves to eat pumpkin seeds after a workout.The only thing that I wish they would do is have bio-degradable or compostable plastic, and also have the option to buy larger bags (cut down on plastic waste).But hey you can't always get everything you want :)

Riso Carena most definitely uses real ingredients like cardamom flowers and saffron because this risotto is absolutely delicious and substantial. It contains a natural bouillon that makes it REAL easy to cook up. I added some chopped onions saute'd in a bit of olive oil and a bit of butter, then added the mix, 1/2 cup of white wine, let that evaporate, then started ladling in boiling water keeping the rice covered until it was done. I added 1-2 tablespoons of butter and grated parmiggiano, and it was my four guests delight at how delicious and satisfying this dish was.
This is a good hard crunchy treat.  It must taste great as my dog alway eagerly awaits this treat.

column9: Old, dried out and not edible!
column10: Have bought these before from a local pet food store and they were wonderful!  These however were not fresh!  My little Yorkie, who loves and never had a problem eating the previous ones from the pet food store can't even eat these!  They are horribly old and dried out!  Won't be ordering these from Amazon again just to save time! Don't buy them from Amazon!

We love our morning cappacinos made with our Delongani fully automated coffee machine. We have experimented with several diff brands of espresso coffee and found this one to be really nice...one of the best, no bitter after taste. You will not be disappointed.
DOESNT SMELL LIKE EGYPTIAN MUSK AT ALL!! WHEN I RECEIVED THE ITEM IT WAS ON A PLASTIC CLEAR BOTTLE WITH ELECTRIC TAPE NOT RECOMMEND THIS!!!

Thick, rich smell and great quality. This oil is the really great stuff. This oil remains on the skin even after shower. It also arouse and excite your senses.  Great oil. This makes a great gift for a guy/husband.
These are chewy cookie shaped brownies that are really delicious. I couldnt tell they were vegan and I think that you would enjoy these good treats.
This is the most flavorful tea I have ever had. I use chocolate vanilla stevia to sweaten it with a tiny pinch of cherry stevia. It is the most yummy drink in the Universe, and it is organic!

I bought this product for a housewarming gift along with some gourmet hot chocolate mix.  It was a huge hit.  It comes boxed exactly as pictured and the stirrers are delicious!  Such a lovely touch for a special cup of cocoa.  My friend said it was yummy in a cup of coffee too. Very nice classy touch for a creative gift.

Love the smooth and intensive flavor of this instant. Calling it espresso is to focus on the stronger flavor compared with other regular instant coffee. Great fit to mix with one scoop of Vallina ice cream,, more perfect than milk or creamer.

This espresso is not "espresso" as I am used to getting, it will work but not as good as the fine powder and does not have the taste.  Was disappointed in the quality, knowing what I know would not reorder for the purpose I use it for.  For drinking it may be fine but it is too coarse have to put it in a coffee mill to add to my batters.
The marketing propaganda on this product is wrong.  It is not instant expresso by any count.  It is simply instant coffee.

In Lancashire it's the ONLY cheese. Cut directly from the wheel, it is ambrosia whether served on crackers, in a cheese and onion toastie or used in Welsh rarebit.Very little quality seems to be lost in transit, and it's the favorite in this house.

Pay attention to the product picture. It displays the canned version, which is 23 ounces, BUT, if you order this particular entry, you will be ordering the bottled version, which is 20 ounces. Yes, technically it's listed as 20 oz., BUT it's depicting the wrong product.

just as a small warning for anyone hoping to buy this product, you should be informed that the containers that ship are 20 oz bottles, not cans. this should definitely be pictured, or at least mentioned, but it is not. if you're fine with cans, then no problem, but i was quite disappointed to open the box and find bottles where i expected cans.

I admit that I still haven't figured out what this cheese might be "ideal" for, but I'm guessing roast beef sandwiches (haven't tried that yet).  I really liked it.  Although I dislike "hot" spicy foods, featuring ingredients such as chilis or cumin, I do find that I can enjoy those "cool" spicy foods like horseradish and wasabi.  To me, while they have a bite, they also seem to have a bit of a fresh breeze quality to them.  I suppose these spices help to clear the breathing passages.In any event - this is essentially a very mild cheese, with a mild horseradish effect (not so bland that you can't taste it, but not overwhelming).  I've had this cheese by itself on rye flatbread, which is an appealing and satisfying snack; on oatcakes (crackers) - again, very tasty and filling; and also with salmon salad on rye flatbread, which it suited very well.  I think this is a good cheese for using with fish because of the horseradish.The cheese is firmish, but not hard, crumbly or "snappy" - it cuts with a bit of a soft folding quality when at room temperature.  It has a very nice, creamy, even texture, is not mushy or sticky or otherwise unpleasant.  It seemed very fresh and the horseradish taste was very fresh and natural as well - there is no weird chemical effect or aftertaste - all in all very nicely done.
I have tried several times to get a good coconut flavored coffee with little success. But this Boyer's did the trick,great coffee with a good amount of coconut flavor. Highly recommend.

Many years ago, I bought some of this Coconut Cream flavored coffee to take to a family get together at my Aunt's house.  She has bought nothing but this ever since!!  They don't stock it in the grocery stores anymore, but luckily we live near the flagship store in Denver and can purchase it there.  Since anyone can purchase it now on Amazon, it's definitely one to try!  Some of my other favorite flavors are Southern Pecan, and Creme Brulee.  Mmmmm!!!  Their regular roasts are delicious too.
This coffee is great. The taste is perfect.creamy, flavorful and a real coconut flavor, not artificial.I think it taste like an excellent coconut cream pie.I highly recommend.

I tried a coconut cream coffee in LA several years ago and really enjoyed it.  Several attempts to find a coconut cream that equaled that flavor turned out badly as they all had a chemical taste, or were poorly flavored.  The Boyer's coconut cream is very good.

column9: Great Flavor! All I've tried so far have been WONDERFUL!
column10: I don't know if the other reviewer (for the Amaretto Flavor), got a stale bag (out of date) or what the problem was, but my bags were so good I reordered BEFORE I ran out! Yumm! I also ordered This Coconut Cream flavor, while Very good, the Amaretto was exceptional! Can't wait to try more, they have a sale currently so I'm going to try some more flavors, as with the holidays coming I KNOW I'll be going through much more than usual!My daughter used to be a Barista for Starbucks (put herself through 4 years of college!) so we've tasted as much as we cared to, & I like this better than anything I've had there, or my other Fav coffee shop, Barnies!If anyone knows the difference between their Praline & southern Pecan coffee, I'd love to know as I want to try one of them on my next order!

I have tried coconut coffee I purchased at my supermarket years ago which was very tasty, so  I was excited to receive this coffee.  When I open the bag smell a bit of coconut, but the big disappointment came after I brewed it.  There is no coconut taste or smell when drinking the cup of coffee.  I ordered this bag because it came in beans so I thought I could get the maximum flavor of coconut.  This is not how real coconut coffee should taste like.  Who care if the beans smell a bit of coconut if you can't taste it when drinking your coffee.

This coffee is wonderful!! I received it a day early than expected too!! Package is air tight and coffee smells so Wonderful as it brews,and the taste is medium body and smooth.I will order this again!!

column9: Good coffee at a GREAT price...
column10: I have spent too much money on coffee and NOW I have found a brand that tastes great and i can afford !!! Thanks Boyer's and Amazon

I love the flavor of coconut coffee, so when I discovered the Boyer's on Amazon and at the time it was discounted for signing up for auto-ship (very affordable) I was very excited. However, the taste left me so sad. It is not very coconutty at all. I reground it to a finer grind and that helped some but it just doesn't have enough flavor for me. I just got my second auto-ship and will drink it but will also look for something with a little more pizzaz.
This coffee is fantastic!  I am a picky coffee drinker and this has such a nice, well blended flavor that is just so enjoyable.  Great coffee at a great price!

column9: Truth: Flavor's too artificial, roast too light!
column10: I'm not really familiar with this brand of coffee, however, I bought it because I had been searching for a decent coconut flavored coffee. I have to say, this was NOT it. People who truly know coffee and drink it on a freakish basis (like me) will recognize that the flavor here is too artificial and the roast is waaay too light!! I typically buy my coffee "whole bean" medium-dark roast but this just didnt cut it for me. I guess most people who would like this are amateur coffee drinkers, but for me I won't be buying this again. The bean itself, is not even dark brown or blackish-brown like most coffee beans. It's actually beige!! I can't even use creamer/milk with this because it will really turn the coffee to water. I recommend [...] for the best flavored coffee along with other gourmet blends. Good Luck.

Bamboo rice is very different. Unusual for a lot of people. The color makes it somewhat fun to play with. The jade color of can compliment many different kind of meals. We served it with large gulf pranws sauteed and then simmered very shortly with coconut milk and red Thai Curry.It's high content of chlorophyll causes the rice to be high on Vitamin B  and its flavor and aroma of jasmine green tea.
I love using green rice instead of normal white rice for a change. I like it with Indian food rather than just sushi like it's so often mentioned with.

Since we have to be gluten free, it can be hard to find a good variety of grains we can eat. I was so happy to find this rice. I wish it was more readily available in my area, but even with shipping, the price per pound was under six dollars and the rice was fresh and a nice change from all the white and brown rice.Bamboo rice is actually a white rice that is infused with bamboo juice, which gives it a flavor similar to fresh green vegetables. It is moist and sticky, and goes well with chicken, pork, and vegetables.

Stash Chamomile Herbal Tea is tea bags with dried, crushed chamomile flowers.Honestly, as far as I'm concerned, chamomile is chamomile.  I suppose that when you use loose flowers you get sediment in the cup and I have seen this happen with some brands of chamomile tea bags, these don't do that.I have also had organic chamomile (this isn't) but I can't taste the difference.Each bag is individually packaged and that is either good or bad depending on how and where you use it and if you are concerned about excessive packaging.If you like chamomile tea, this is a good choice.

I bought this at a store and had high hopes because their vanilla biscotti flavor is very good. This caramel drizzle, however,  is not. It has a very bad chemical flavor and after taste and doesn't taste anything at all like caramel or coffee. I have only made one cup and would be willing to try another but I was very disappointed. I really enjoy good flavored coffee and understand that there may be some artificial flavors added, but this one was just bad. K cups are not cheap and it is always frustrating when one of them is not good. I would not purchase it again.
This is the best coffee ive tried yet.I Don't even like Folgers.This says something.I have a love for caramel and it is taste-able.The only coffee I dont use milk or sugar on too!
I only drink flavored coffee, and this one is my favorite so far. It's pretty sweet, which I really enjoyed, and it has a definite caramel taste and aroma. Recommended.

First, I would like to say that I purchased this product from the STORE, not from this seller. Also that there was not a problem with the expiration date of the coffee.I am not a picky coffee drinker. I like all kinds, but I prefer stronger brews. I like flavored coffee as well, but only when it tastes like what it is suppose to. I don't think anyone wants to drink chemical flavored coffee. When I bought this product I thought it was going to be great, I am a consumer of folgers and have tried different flavors of theirs, however this was the first k-cup brand I bought from them and was VERY disappointed.  The coffee is definitely flavored and does taste like caramel, but after each sip there is an after taste of some sort of chemical.  The after taste is so strong and disgusting that you can neither enjoy the flavor of the coffee nor the caramel. For the first time was unable to finish my cup of coffee. To drink the entire cup would have been the equivalent of torturing myself.I would not recommend anyone buy this product.

This coffee is wonderful!  Everyone who had a cup enjoyed the flavor.  It was more expensive than other brands, but it is well worth the price.  If you enjoy a really good cup of coffee - this is the one!

Wow, Caramel Drizzle is really horrible... it taste like a burnt turd.  How do I know what a burnt turd taste like you ask... well let's just say that my fraternity was really unkind to me when I pledged.  Besides, don't judge me, I am trying to help you avoid making a coffee purchasing mistake!  What is "Drizzle" anyway... my best guess is that "Drizzle" is of Czechoslovakian origin and it loosly translates to "this coffee is terrible and you will wish that you didn't have taste buds".

I visited Peru back in January, and once I got home I remembered I saved some of the Inca Corn snack from the market in Lima. I suddenly became sad because I only have 2-3 oz left. I searched every hispanic store in the area and could not find it. This product was out of stock for 2 months on Amazon. Once it came back in stock, I quickly ordered it and got it in 4 days! I was so excited to open the box and eat the snack! It was like I was back in Peru again. Some pieces are a little burnt but it still is so perfect! I will continue to order this product once I run out of my current stock. Thank you AMAZON! :)

Rarely eat corn nuts but these are large kernals, just right amount of salt and big crunch.  bag is generous and I saved and ate corn for a day or two.  Flavor like frito stuff.  Fair price for me.  Gotta' try this!

If you like CORN NUTS you'll LOVE INKA CORN! And once you tried it, you won't want to settle of Corn Nuts again. I wish this snack was easier to find in grocery and convenience stores. But at least you can buy it on line now.

Not to denigrate Sunshine Cheez-It Hot & Spicy baked snack crackers made with genuine McIlhenny Tabasco brand green pepper sauce, a truly great similar product, but THIS crisp is to the other as champagne is to beer (not that I actually drink the real stuff anymore, but let's just say I had some experience imbibing.) Not too much smoke flavor, a judicious edge of jalapeno, and interestingly-textured little squares of snacking joy which do not seem squirted out of an assembly-line pastry bag sans human chef sentiment. In my well-sampled opinion, the very best of the fine line of John Wm. Macy's exquisite savory nibbles.

column9: The Best Crackers I ever had
column10: We just received these Jalapeno Cheese Crisps today. This is the first time I tried them but certainly not the last. The chips are not large and they are not uniformed size, the cheese is layered in between. They are most likely the best crackers/crisps I ever had. The jalapeno heat is nice and strong. I am somehow pretty sure that all the other flavors will be great and I'll try them all sooner or later.We had a hard time putting the box down - that's the only problem I can see. I am sure they would be great with some cool sour cream dip but we did not get to that today, we did enough damage as is. They would be great for a party - entertaining, but I am not sure I want to share them....

column9: Yummy beef stew like my mom made
column10: I made Vietnamese beef stew in my crockpot using these spices. It came out delicious and like my mom made when I was a kid! There are 4 jars in this order, each with enough spice for 5 pounds of beef. I took one star off because, unless you're making 5 pounds of beef, you kind of have to estimate what fraction of the spice in the jar you have to use since the directions are for a whole jar.

column9: Wonderful, fresh vanilla beans, reasonably priced, from a great vendor
column10: These beans come in a vacuum-sealed package to preserve freshness, and it works extremely well--all the beans that Beanilla sells are moist and plump with a wonderful texture and scent. There are multiple terrific flavors that you can get from Beanilla, but Tahitian is one that I knew well from buying it in extract form in the past. My Tahitian extract was extremely expensive, and I doled it out little by little and made it last for years. Then I discovered the fun and easy process of do-it-yourself vanilla extract, and a world of gourmet-cooking possibilities has opened up to me. My most frequent use of my vanilla extract is for homemade ice cream using my Vita-Mix. It adds an amazing extra zing to the taste that is just delicious.I had never made my own vanilla extract before I ordered from Beanilla. Their customer service is superb, and one of their representatives told me by email how to make vanilla extract when I asked, and he also explained why one might want to make his/her own vanilla extract. When you make your own, you can be 100% sure exactly what has gone into the extract, which is not always the case with some types of vanilla extract that you buy pre-made. It is also cheaper and a lot of fun to make your own.Here is the technique for making vanilla extract spelled out in detail for anyone who has not tried it before, and I have uploaded photos demonstrating these steps:1. Assemble kitchen scissors, good quality vodka, a clean, dark-glass jar (I save all my empty vitamin jars), a funnel, a spoon, something to label the jar, such as a self-sticking label.2. Remove the beans from the package. Cut each bean lengthwise in half. Then cut the beans horizontally into pieces small enough to fit in the jar and easily be covered by vodka.3. Place the bean pieces in the jar.4. Pour 1/2 cup of vodka into the jar per every 3 beans (for 10 beans, it would be a little over 1-1/2 cup). Then tamp down the beans so that all bean parts are covered by the vodka.5. Put the lid on the jar and label the jar with this information: what kind of vanilla bean you used, the date, the amount of vodka you used in ounces (or whatever measure you prefer), and the number of beans you used, then place the jar in a cool, dry place like a kitchen cabinet (I put mine with my spices).6. Every week or so shake the jar.7. After 8 weeks, the vanilla extract is ready to use.

column9: A Good Cake With A Lot That's Fake!
column10: I am a rum cake aficionado and have tried many.  Of course, the best are those you make yourself from scratch with love and lots of good rum. I gave Tortuga 3 stars because it seems to be a popular rum cake standard that consistently tastes good in comparison to similar commercial quality products within this group. Tortuga cakes are actually produced in Barbados with the company headquartered in the Cayman Islands and I imagine that this affects the steep cost of these cakes. Here is my critique of the pros and cons based on multiple purchases:PROS:1. A moist cake with a clear rum presence.2. Same brand is available in many popular flavors.3. Contains Tortuga 5 year old aged Gold rum.4. One of the most popular choices for rum cakes.CONS:1. Tortuga uses many artificial colors and preservatives-e.g. Yellow 5 & 6, sodium propionate, artifical flavors, sodium alginate, polysorbate 60, propylene glycol and aluminum sulfate.  In my opinion, this compromises the taste and integrity of the product, making it less than "natural". The box reads..."A Taste of the Islands" but it should read..."A Taste of the Lab!"2. The amount of true rum is negligible at best-less than 1/2 of 1%, which in a 1 lb. cake amounts to .0008 oz. Add your own rum more generously!3. To a discerning palate, these rum cakes taste as they are made-artificial-similar to the smell of a can of Play Dough when we were kids! A first glance at the cake tells you that the fluorescent yellow color does not exist in nature. Be sure to wear your sunglasses as you cut a slice or you will be blinded by the intense radioactive glow.4. Freshness/Expiration/Use By Date:  Another enigma! Look for the white square sticker on the side of the box. They use a Julian code to identify the date of manufacture of the cake.  For example, "12233" indicates that the cake was produced on the 233rd day of 2012 (August 20th, 2012). Better transparency for consumers would be helpful as would a clear "Use By" date. (Remember that it took decades for most US manufacturers to put easy to read expiration dates on their products.  The Islands are about 30 years behind us.BOTTOM LINE:This is a 3.5 star product in my opinion. However, I have yet to discover a better tasting commercial rum cake. Make your own using a good recipe and great rum and pocket the savings.  Hope this helps.

column9: A blend of Erythritol and Stevia
column10: On the plus side, Truvia for me is a very good tasting low-calorie sugar substitute.  Does it taste exactly like sugar? No.  But for me it tastes better than Sweet & Low, Equal, and even Splenda.The problem I have with Truvia -- and hence just the three stars -- is that it is not just a sweetener made with from a stevia extract.  The other major sweetening ingredient contained in Truvia is erythritol, a sugar alcohol.  Unlike stevia that has a history of 30+ years of safe use (with no major bad side effects) in Japan, there's nothing much known about the safety and long-term effects of taking large and repeated doses of erythritol.  Erythritol has simply not been tested a whole lot.So one is rolling the dice with Truvia, hoping that there's no long-term negative consequences of ingesting so much erythritol on a daily basis (if one is using Truvia regularly for their morning coffee or tea).If one is drawn to using a stevia-based low calorie sweetener for the known safety record of stevia (as demonstrated in Japan), then it would be wise to use a stevia sweetener that does NOT contain erythritol.  Unfortunately, Truvia does.On the other hand, if one is only concerned about the taste of the low calorie sweetener, then Truvia is a fine choice in that regard.

First of all this tea is not from Formosa. It's from India. That said the way this tea has been picked & dried has produced a high quality cup of organic Oolong tea. At a fair price. Most Oolong costs about the same for 3 to 4 oz only! Note all tea is from the same species of plant. so the growing conditions, leaf stage at picking & the drying process dictate the final cup most. together with storage & handling by the packer & you the consumer. Davidson has got this tea to me in good condition.This tea looks like green beads when dry. When brewed complete leaves unfurl with a only a small number of broken leaves. Chinese style tea does not grade by leave size, like black teas from India & Ceylon. These leaves will give 2 to three re-brewings by just adding hot water & allowing a 2nd infusion after 1st brewing has been poured. 1st brewing stronger & less sweet than 2nd brewing.This style of tea is drunk without the addition of milk, sugar or lemon.It has a faint aroma of  honey on the nose & subtle natural sweetness. However if your palate is used to drink very sweet soda then this may be too subtle.Tip put a few leaves in travel mug. add hot water & top up during the day with fresh hot water unto twice or three times. But remove the lid to smell the tea, to enjoy the subtle aroma, if safe to do so ( at your desk not traveling in a car).I am told that:This has zero calories, high in flavonoids so is a healthy alternative to diet soda etc.Some also find this style of tea aids digestion (note most chinese drink tea with food for this reason). May Help in calming a stomach, if lunch was a little too rich in fat.Other teas from Davidsons I like are:Ceylon black OP & English Breakfast These I drink with milk added.
