The consistency of the whipped potatoes is smooth and the little bits of bacon, peppers and cheese add to the explosion of flavor.  They cook easily in either the conventional oven, or on the grill when wrapped in foil!  Go ahead, treat yourself!

For christmas I ordered some coupons from my daughters school for $30.00 off Ohama steaks.  I was excited to try them as I have been bombarded with their ads for the last 2 years and I was ready to test them out.  I went on-line and looked at their packages and was so looking forward to receiving my package of fine foods and cook them.  I made my choice and fell for some of the last min. add-ons, by choice.  I went to pay and use the gift cards and well you can only use one at a time, having 2 for $15.00 I naturally thought I was getting $30.00 off the total.  With that said I was still willing to go ahead with the order.  $129.00 later I had ordered one of the package deals and the add-ons.  I received my order ups in 5-7 days packaged in a styro cooler.  packaged in the cooler were several cardboard boxes with vacuumed packaged tiny steaks.  I am a person who loves to grill and do so about 4 nights a week, so I know a little about meat, and how to cook it.  First this is not high end Dry-aged meat or wet aged this is inferior to quality meat that can be bought at a good butcher.  The steaks are about $30.00 a pound after shipping and the high prices.  The Hamburgers are tiny frozen pucks that are dry.  I am so disappointed in the quantity and quality, I really have no words to describe how disappointed I am with this whole deal.  To top everything off I received a e-mail coupon for $20.00 off my next order so the coupon that I purchased was $5.00 more than on-line deals.  Wow Do yourself a favor and spend your money in a good butcher shop of grocery store!!!

These are actually very tasty.  Pure potatoes with a great texture and no nasty filler "stuff."  No bacon, no cheese...just tasty potatoes.  They cook well in either the oven or microwave.  I add a touch of either salt & pepper or fajita seasoning to spice it up.  I rated 4 out of 5 stars because they could be a bit bigger portion.  However, this item is a fairly good value for the money.

These are actually pretty good little potato puffs, and best of all - no CHEESE!  (unless you like that sort of thing, which we don't so it's nice to actually find a potato side dish with no cheese in it).Anyways- - these are surprisingly good and they toast up nicely in the oven in like 10 minutes.  worth it for $10.
They are more potato crockets in the shape of a ball rather than Au Gratin, but nevertheless YUM YUM YUM!
Not happy with the product.  Once they were cooked the potatoes were flat and didn't look any thing like the product picture that was seen.  The shipping cost as much as the potatoes did!

column9: Now this is my kind of Potato with Steak
column10: I love to order these type of cooked potatoes and they are so great with a steak...
I really like this product.  It tasted great and only took a few minutes to make in the microwave.
Very good side dish, easy to make, easy to eat.  As others have said, needs a little spice, but other than that they are delicious!
excellent - will order again!!  It's nice to be able to order Omaha items from Amazon because Amazon ships SOOO fast, and payments are so convenient.
I was surprised at the size of these potatoes. I have bought them at my local grocery store before and was disappointed that they were so small. These are perfect!! Tasty, cook just right. Love 'em!!
These potatoes are good.  But i don't know if I'd get them again.  The garlic taste to me was off and strong.  And I LOVE garlic.  Hoping I just got an "off" batch.

Excellent and tasty though I thought not enough garlic so I added more. When I order GARLIC I guess I expect more of it.  But perfect if you have guests as it will never offend anyone. Omaha always is sure to do everything to please their customers, a premier company, hard to find anymore.
We had these along with Omaha prime rib. Both were great. Two where plenty to fill up. Made them in toaster oven in less then 20 minutes.

I received 4 of these in my first ever Omaha Steaks order that I received today. I wasn't sure what to expect, but so far, I've been pleased. I tore the plastic open, put the frozen potato on a baking sheet in the oven and put it on 350. 45 minutes later it was done and turned out being delicious. The cheese filling was crispy on-top and the potato itself underneath was nice and soft. No way would they come out as good if put in the microwave, so I'd say oven cooking these is definitely the way to go. Now, you can obviously make your own stuffed baked potatoes for far cheaper then what Omaha charges for these alone, but as long as you get a good deal on the Omaha website, these simply make a great addition to any Omaha steaks order. As delicious are they are though, I wouldn't order a box of JUST these off the site due to the added shipping costs. But like I said, as long as they're part of a nicely priced packaged deal, I'll definitely take them. Actually, I probably wouldn't order any packaged deal in the future from Omaha that didn't include these. A big plus, at least for me, is if you check the ingredients list on these, there's no partially hydrogenated oils, so there's no traces of trans fats, which is very rare with stuffed baked potatoes. Also no high fructose corn syrup, which is another rarity on a food product like this and is always a plus. If you make your own or buy them frozen from your grocery store for example, chances are, the butter used, sour cream, etc. will be full of chemicals, trans fats & high fructose corn syrup. These, not so much. So there is a definite degree of quality with Omahas stuffed baked potatoes. Each potato does have 8 grams of saturated fat, which is 42% the DRV, but that's obviously to be expected with anything that contains bacon, cheese and sour cream. I was also expecting there to be no fiber, but it turns out there's 3grams of fiber per baked potato half. Another plus. Overall, the stuffed baked potato was very tasty and actually relatively healthy, being made with quality ingredients.
These potatoes are really very good.  My husband and I both *love* them.  And way too easy.  We will be buying more of these.

column9: These are the best hash browns!!!!!!!!!!
column10: I got these in the mail today, i know right, sounds so weird to say i got hash browns in the mail, haha.  Come in dry ice cooler and were in box all in their own lil plastic bags.  Just stick them on a baking sheet for 35 min. at 400 degrees.  when you get them out of the oven you smell the cheese and it has nice crunchy outside with creamy potato inside, if you want the best side dish to your steak or other meat, hey could even use for breakfast with some eggs and sausage, your choice, this get a 5/5 for taste, 5/5 for presentation, buy these now, great price too, thanks for your time, and thank you omaha steaks, the best at great prices.

January 3, 2011I purchased these potatoes from Omaha Steaks online last week. I was not sure what to expect ... The au gratin potatoes I had seen and tasted before were sliced potatoes with globbs of gooey cheese sauce, and by the looks of them, this certainly wasn't it ... I opened the box and got out my skillet. The first thing that I noticed is that these things were huge ... like a gigantic tater tot. I browned them on both sides about 10 minutes each. To my surprise, they were very tasty. Texture was light fluffy and the potatoes tasted extra fresh .. not frozen or freezer burned. I liked them alot. I think these are perfect for kids ... none of the flavors were overpowering and great texture ... I give these 4 stars.
So so good!  Delicious, easy to prepare food!  I would definitely order again.  Had a gourmet taste, and took only minutes to get ready.  Yum!!!

column9: tasted ok.... a bit overpriced tho
column10: I like em but nothing unique about the flavor.  basically saves you from having to make them at home... a little pricey but for a treat what the heck
They taste pretty good. I eat one of these with some of the poultry selections from Omaha Steaks. It makes a great meal.
These potatoes are pretty good. They can be eaten alone or served with a meal. Really like potatoes and this is an easy choice.

Omaha Steaks 8 (5.75 oz.) Stuffed Baked Potatoes '''The Stuffed Baked Potatoes were unimpressive andlacking in flavor.I tasted no bacon or chives.However, they do make an attractive addition to ameal.

Potatoes were good. Two 12 oz trays will be enough for 4 adults so really not worth the money honestly. $10 for two little trays is a lot even for the ease and quality. Like I said they were good and easy to prepare and thankfully only four of us for x-mas dinner today or I wouldn't have had enough. 24 oz. of potatoes sounds bigger then it is lol. (not Omaha's fault)
I prepare these baked potatoes in a toaster oven. They are the perfect compliment to a hamburger, steak or chicken entree. Try them. You'll like them!

column9: Omaha Chicken and Stuffed Baked Potatoies
column10: Very good transaction and Omaha food was sent properly.  I already left one feedback.
These potatoes are very good along with all their steaks and hamburgers.  I would definately recommend Omaha Steaks to anyone looking for a gourmet dinner at a reasonable price!

I finally found a product that my dogs absolutely love. I have tried numerous brands and in several varieties but my dogs never seemed to wait so eagerly to be fed. I have tried all three flavors of this brand but they seem to like the chicken and rice flavor the best. It makes their coats shinier and it gives them a general all around healthier look about them. Now that I've found something they truly enjoy I hope they don't raise the price. A good value, in my opinion.

Red Tea Leaf's Espresso Matcha is amazing!This product has helped with the joint inflammation in my hands.  I was told I had arthritis and that it would probably get worse.  After my own research, I found that an anti-inflammatory diet could help.  Matcha Green Tea was mentioned by several sources. Red Tea Leaf teas are excellent and their customer service is fast and friendly.  I had tried several different brands, but Red Tea Leaf's variety of favors that they mix with the Matcha was what drew me to this company.I chose Espresso Matcha because I am a coffee drinker, but wanted to drink several glasses of Matcha Green Tea a day and knew I would have to forgo my coffee to drink this much (and I love coffee).  There is a subtle flavor of espresso mixed with the Matcha green tea.During a workout when a bar bell completely slipped out of my hand because I lost my grip, I decided I had to try something.  I stopped drinking coffee `cold turkey' as soon as my Espresso Matcha from Red Tea Leaf order arrived and never once got a headache.My favorite summer time way to drink this tea is to mix 1 heaping scoop of Matcha green tea into my 20 oz. water bottle the night before, then refrigerate so I `m ready to go in the morning (I make 3 of these each night when I `m packing my lunch).  Just make sure to shake it before you drink it, the Matcha tea settles to the bottom.  Within two weeks, the ache-y feeling in my hands every morning almost completely disappeared!  I am able to grip jars to open them without pain.  During my workouts, I focus completely on form and only later realize, I never thought once about my hands!  They do not hurt... at all!As for my diet, I ate very `clean' before I started drinking Matcha tea from Red Tea Leaf and I love scientific research (I know, nerdy), so drinking 3 heaping scoops of Matcha tea a day was the only change that I made.  I consistently drink 60-80 oz of water now, but even before when I tried drinking this much water to flush out my system my hands still hurt.  It was not until I added the Match green tea from Red Tea leaf that I noticed an improvement in my hand.I am so happy with this product!  Thank you Red Tea Leaf!

I'm so glad I don't live in England because if I did I would probably be twice my size from eating these all the time. My good friend introduced me to these and called them "crack". At first I thought she was kidding but, oh nelly!
It costs to much on small quantity, I am also looking for this prduct for international shipping. So the price higher than how much you can get it from groceries in uk

Is what it says, a whole mackerel in a can.  Our cats love this, much better than ground fish food in a can (and who knows what all is in that stuff.)  Plenty of juice along with the whole fish.Looks good enough for human consumption, our cats love it !!

My 7 cats like this food but it is a little yucky for the human. Pieces of mackerel swimming in a dark broth. It is billed as a "complete" food and contains carrots, peas and pasta. Why, I don't know, since these are not foods that a cat would eat in the wild. An OK alternative to go along with their dry food.

This item was purchased for my mother who really wanted them. Imagine our surprise when worry beads, something meant to be held and rubbed on , broke in less than 3 days. Then imagine when the same breads were returned and you were given 1/3 of what you paid because they are claiming you sent back something with nothing the matter with it. I love it!  Brewed with a french press and boiling water, waited 15 minutes, pressed, poured, added a touch of stevia (my favorite sweetener) and sipped to enjoy the wonderful flavor.  If you like deep flavors and dark chocolate, this is for you!
This stuff, is awfull,tried brewing it different ways, either to weak, or to bitter. I DO NOT LIKE IT AT ALL.

I used these as decorations on cupcakes for my son's birthday. They looked great but note they only fit as actual rings on little fingers. They worked as favors and decorations so I thought they were a good purchase.

I absolutely LOVE this tea! From the minute I first smelled its earthy, nutty scents (with hints of tobacco and leather), I knew it would be a delightful morning tea. I couldn't have been more right. For those who love boldly flavored and earthy teas, this is a must try.As one who has recently given up coffee (got tired of the jitters and crash), I have been searching for teas with bold and robust flavors, like in coffee. I do not exaggerate when I say that this tea has the boldest and most interesting and  complex flavor I've experienced (without the bitterness of many "bold" black teas).Coincidentally, this tea also has nearly as much caffeine as coffee. As with all teas, though, the caffeine absorbs into the bloodstream at a much slower rate, leaving the drinker jitter- and crash-free. (For the curious, this seems due to the fact that the caffeine in tea bonds with the tannins, making it much harder to metabolize.)Thus, this morning mate is not only absolutely delicious for its nutty and earthy, yet smooth, flavor, but is great for concentration and energy. I cannot reccomend it enough, particularly for those looking for boldness from their tea!

Thanks for the quick delivery.  My son-in-law does not drink coffee but this is his morning drink.  As he and my daughter were coming from California for a visit, I wanted to insure he had the Mate available and he was really appreciative.

My Morning Mate is a mix of mate, black tea, and red rooibos. Listed under ingredients are sweet cocoa, chocolate and almond bits, pistachio nuts, macadamia nuts and coriander with warm hazelnut and cinnamon.Some of the reviews on the Teavana site state that they think this tastes like coffee.  It does not taste like coffee but mate has a very distinct taste.  Although the ingredient list is extensive, I think it mostly tastes nutty.I gave it 4 stars because it is not my favorite mate tea-it is a little bitter to be 5 stars.

I grew up in New England.  We had Cake Mate sprinkles or jimmies.  They are made in Florida by Signature Foods. I still get them when I go back as they are in the grocery stores.  The CK ones are okay, and I thought they would be quite similar -- same bad hydrogenated oils and the reviews.  These are certainly fine for a cupcake.  But for ice cream or the occasional spoonful of sprinkles, you need the Cake Mate.  These are available in 32 oz. from spiceworld online.  They are listed on Amazon but not as currently available.  I plan to get some soon.

These are very colorful but not the best tasting. I used them for my sons first bday as we were having a very large party and didn't want to buy 20 mini cans but taste wise the quality was not there....the look was great. I'm sure no one knew any better after all frosting fixes all.

The Jimmies had purple in the mix.  That was exactly what I was looking for.  Since we are not planning on eating these (but throwing them instead of rice). I won't know taste.  But color is excellent!

I used these rainbow jimmies for a rainbow cupcake topper and added them to rice krispie treats for my daughter's 6th birthday.  Obviously, it was a rainbow party.  The package didn't look like the picture, but I was not disappointed in the product.  I would buy from this company again.

We chose a Thing 1/Thing 2 theme for our twins' first birthday party, and these sprinkles were the perfect color. They lean more towards turquoise than a true blue, but with our red baking cups, and white frosting, they were the perfect finishing touch!
These sprinkles make a great presentation and are tasty too!  Used them for my french chocolate balls.  Would recommend them highly.
Exactly what I thought it would be. ALOT (more then I will ever need) of pink sprinkles, that taste like... sprinkles!
Great size bag for the price! I am making a funfetti cake with just purple. These sprnkles/jimmies are exactly what I wanted. Although, the color could be darker.

Jimmies sprinkles are the best i love them because they are soft and unlike the other hard sprinkles don't get stuck in your teeth. lol But it was a great buy. You have a better deal here that anywhere else.

Good quality sprinkles.  Pricing seems pretty decent.  Love the way they make my cupcakes look - takes me back to my elementary school days, long ago!  Only gripes: the "partially-hydrogenated" ingredient and non-resealable bag.  By the way, the advertised bag looks completely different than the one you get - it's not black.  Tastes like classic Jimmies too and isn't so sweet that it'll over-sweeten your frosting.
Pros - good price for its size, fast delivery,Con - not the best tasting jimmies, still better than getting the small grocery store size
This was perfect for my purposes! I made a personalized "funfetti" cake for a bridal shower for a girl whose colors were hot pink and black, and this was awesome to get it done! Fast shipping too!
I bought these sprinkles for my cupcakes and not only are they gorgeous but you get a lot for the money. The silver is very true to color and they make a lovely accent to your cupcakes.

I bought these jimmies because I couldn't find the needed orange color in any of my local stores.  A pound of jimmies is a lot, but I went through more than I expected, probably half the bag to thoroughly coat a recipe of chocolate truffles.  The taste is, well, jimmy-taste.  My only disappointment/surprise was how short these jimmies are -- about two-thirds of the length of Wilton and CakeMate brands I have in the cupboard.If you need a special color that only CK makes, don't hesitate to get them.-- Debbie Lee  Wesselmann

Seriously, sprinkles are not just for eye pleasing aesthetics but for mouth pleasing texture.  This bag is great value compared to buying the smaller size shakers with different colors. I can use two of containers of  those colors on one batch of 24 cupcakes.  I just have to find a proper container to put the bag ones in so they are easy to shake out onto cupcakes, as that is what I use them for mostly. I'll check on amazon to see if I can find an appropriate shaker.  I may just buy a smaller one (about 10 oz) shaker and use and re-use that one.  My son and I like them also on ice cream, topped with ready whip canned cream. Gives pleasing texture to  ice cream. Yum!

I ordered these from Amazon because I can no longer seem to find them in local stores. These are an integral part of my daily lunch and I haven't found anything I like as well. Another reviewer mentioned that the rounds inside the boxes are broken and this has happened to me as well but not to the point that it ruins the product. column10: Awfully tasty for a white flour cracker snack. Perfect foil for creamy cheeses, spreads and avocados. Great value in bulk and the packaging keeps them from becoming stale.

I never tasted bagel snacks that are so awful tasting as these. Too bad I bought 2 of them. Poppy Seed flavor? I thought they have a fishy flavor to me. and like they say, they are twice baked.... just under burnt they are. YUCK.... at least my pigs do like them! They are a snack to them!!

I think these are excellent snack crackers. I eat them right out of the box. They are low in calories and fats, so it is helpful on my Weight Watchers plan. Original and Garlic flavors are also very good.

I have ordered this product twice. The product tastes fine. The problem is with breakage.The first time I ordered this product from Amazon more than 1/2 of the Bagel Snacks in all the boxes where broken into various size pieces. Since I had bought this product at the store before buying it a Amazon, and never had the contents broken into pieces like what I got from Amazon, I thought I would try to order it from Amazon again. Fans of Tyler Florence will know that this is Tyler's favorite rice for doing risotto.  He prefers it to any rice at any price when it comes time to do a risotto.  Whilst I remain unconvinced that this the absolute best rice for risotto, there can be no doubt that it makes one hell of a splendid risotto.  I wowed two different groups of guests with risottos that sprang from this rice.  I was very pleased with the results.It's very reasonably priced also.  It can be had for 31% of the price of one of it's Carnaroli rivals.  Amazon will give you four kilos for almost the same price as 1 kilo of the Carnaroli.  Does Carnaroli yield better results?  I don't think so.  This rice yields equal or better results.This is a smart buy for fine risotto.  I strongly recommend it.

column9: Antica Riseria Vialone Nano Rice, 2.2-Pound Packages (Pack of 4)
column10: There is nothing else to say: if you want a REAL risotto you have to use Vialone Nano. This particular brand is good and sold at an attractive price. I highly recommend it.

column9: The Best There Is.  Don't Hesitate.
column10: We lived in Italy for 20+ years and this is the same brand I bought over there.  In Italy they use the different kinds of rice for different dishes.  Most folks in the USA seem to know about arborio, but it is considered the lowest grade of rice and is primarily used for cold rice salad and puddings.  Carnaroli rice is typically used for seafood risotto as it is a finer grain, which is appropriate with delicate seafood.  Vialone Nano is what is used to make the best risottos whether they are homemade or in a restaurant.  Vialone Nano is a far superior grain to arborio and will make delicious, creamy risotto regardless of what you use -- sausages, mushrooms, saffron, asparagus, truffles, and yes, even seafood.  The packages are vacuum packed, which is also much better than buying the rice in bags or boxes.  We love this rice and so does everyone we serve it to.

I was surprised how sweet this cereal was, although it held up its crunchiness very well right down to the last flake. The honey taste was prominent, however I really couldn't taste the peanuts. It was good with and without milk; I tried it dry as a snack and it did a great job of stopping that sweet craving mid-afternoon. I don't know how it's really considered 'healthy' for you, as it's loaded with sugars but as an occasional treat, I'd definitely go for it. I probably wouldn't go out of my way to look for it, but if it's BOGO at the local grocery store, I'd definitely buy a box now and again.

column9: Less than the sum of its parts
column10: Important disclaimer: I like to snack on cereal without milk. Dry cereal is one of my favorite snacks, and I thought this one would be great for that purpose. Unfortunately, I was wrong. It can best be described as Corn Flakes meets Honey Nut Cheerios, which sounds great in theory, but it just didn't do it for me. It's a bit too sweet, a little on the bitter side, and they really should've used almonds instead of peanuts.

This cereal is not unlike many similar nut flakes on the market. It's sweet (not too bad, but not what you'd expect for adults), crunchy, not too bad tasting, and certainly holds up well in milk. Given that, it's still something I'd probably not buy. It seems like something marketed for adults who really want sweet and crunchy but maybe feel guilty getting something with a cartoon character on the front. Yet, if I want sweet kid-type cereal, I'd go straight for the cartoon packaging.

This is a decent tasting cereal that maintains it's "Crunch", however it's just not the cereal for me.  The first ingredient is milled corn, which is just not a good base for nutritional purposes. I also prefer a cereal higher in fiber and protein while containing more grains.I will give Kellogg's credit for creating a cereal that kids will like without having a ton of sugar in it.  This cereal has the following nutritional value per 3/4 cup;Calories 120Fat 1gSodium 160mgPotassium 40 mgCarbohydtrates 26gSugars 11gProtein 2gThere was a lot of hype surrounding the release of this cereal, I just can't figure out what Kellogg's was trying to add to their already huge selection. I'm not sure what gap this cereal fills for the brand, but it isn't one I will purchase again.

As cereals go they are not the surgery-est, but they are a very sweet cereal. The closest other cereal I thought this tasted like was frosted flakes. They are kind of like frosted flakes with a nuttiness to them. The cereal overall is good, but I wouldn't go out of my way to find it for sure.

The flakes looked like the picture on the box, except for the fact that they were smaller. I thought they were too small, which makes them get soggy quickly. They were crunchy and you could see the nut pieces on the flakes, but I didn't taste alot of honey or nuts. The cereal was sweet, but not exessively, which I liked. I won't be using this as my breakfast cereal, but I would consider using this as part of a cookie crust for a pie, or something similar.

Kellogg's Crunchy Nut Golden Honey Nut Cereal is delicious. The flavor is sweet and nutty, with a great crunchy texture. The cereal consists of cornflakes with tiny bits of ground nuts stuck to them. It's filling and only 120 calories per serving. It's great with milk or plain. I may have found a new favorite cereal. While containing quite a bit of sugars, it's definitely not overly-sweet. I think it's a perfect balance of sweet and salty.Full Ingredients:Milled Corn, Sugar, Peanuts, Honey, Malt Flavoring, Molasses, Salt, High Fructose Corn Syrup, Caramel Color, Iron, Annatto Extract Color, Niacinamide, Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C), Sodium Ascorbate (Vitamin C), Pyridoxine Hydrochloride (Vitamin B6), Thiamin Hydrochloride (Vitamin B1), Riboflavin (Vitamin B2), Vitamin A Palmitate, Vitamin B12, Folic Acid, Bht (Preservative), Vitamin D, Wheat Starch.

I have always liked corn flakes. This cereal takes your corn flakes and adds just enough honey to sweeten them and then throws in peanut pieces to add to the crunch and flavor. I have also mixed it with plain corn flakes to give them a bit more punch. It stays crisp in milk and tastes great. Give it a try and I don't think you'll regret your decision.

This is a decent tasting cereal, but it's way too sweet in my opinion. Yes, it's crunchy and stays crunchy even in milk, but it's because of the sugar coating on the flakes, not because of the nuts. The nuts are ground very fine, almost too fine, so they don't add much crunch or flavor to the flakes. The honey taste is fairly subtle. If the nuts were crunchier, more flavorful and there was less sugar in the cereal, it might taste better, as well as be healthier. Although I didn't hate it, I doubt I'd buy this one again.

column9: I tasted burnt, caramel flavoring...nice crunch though.
column10: I liked the initial crunch, similar to Honey Bunches of Oats or Frosted Flakes but more sugar coating.  Then after the taste settled in there was a burnt taste that I couldn't quite identify.  It seemed like molasses to me but my son said it tasted like burnt caramels.  I would agree with that.  It was good cereal, not great...It was just too sugary for me.  I never did get the peanut taste unless it was the burnt peanut oil taste that we were mistaking for molasses/caramels.  There was just a weird aftertaste that nobody in the family could identify.  I wouldn't purchase again.  It was OK. Not worth the price nor calories from all the added sugar.

i'm very satisfied with the taste and quality of kellogg's crunchy nut cereal. i have a somewhat wandering tastebud when it comes to cereal, never really sticking to any one particular brand. this cereal however, may become a staple in the house for a few months at least, before my wanderlust is stirred (and that's saying something, considering my habits) and i venture forth for different flavors. i love that the cereal is peppered with crunchy peanuts and the honey provides just the right touch of sweetness and kick to the mix. fantastic!

column9: Frosted Flakes with molasses-peanut flavor added
column10: I love cereal, and one of my favorites is Frosted Flakes.  Kellogg's, maker of Frosted Flakes, introduced this new Crunchy Nut cereal in 2 forms.  This type is a flaked, sugar-coated cereal with tiny chunks of peanuts on the flakes themselves.  Crunchy Nut Golden Honey Nut has two layers of flavor.  The primary flavor is exactly like Frosted Flakes, and the cereal has the same shape and even similar texture and sugary glaze.  The secondary flavors would, according to the name of the product, supposedly taste like honey and nut, but what I taste the most is molasses.  That is an ingredient in the cereal, as is sugar, honey, and corn syrup.  Lot of forms of sugar in this cereal.  Despite having honey in it, I notice no honey flavor at all.  There was another, harder to identify taste which was I finally realized was peanut, but it was overwhelmed by the other sweet flavors.  Despite little peanut bits on the flakes, it didn't immediately taste peanutty to me.  Overall, the molasses flavor left a weird aftertaste that I did not find pleasant.  These weren't flakes I could eat right out of the box, as milk was necessary to tone down the powerful, almost cloying taste.  The flakes did stay crunchy in milk for quite a while as compared to a lot of other cereals.  I think Kellogg's could reduce the sweetness by a significant amount and improve this cereal drastically.

Exactly like good old-fashioned corn flakes (with regards to crunch and lightness), with the added flavor of honey and crumbled peanuts. I'm not a fan of these with milk, as I don't like soggy cereal. Instead, I sprinkle them on yogurt, cottage cheese, or ice cream. They don't end up mushy and they add great crunch and nutty flavor to my plain boring snack.

Kellogg's Crunchy Nut is one of the few "tasty" cereals I've had that is not "go into a coma" super sweet.  At first blush I just thought it would be Frosted Flakes with a nutty taste added in, but it is far different.  Althought similar in look to Frosted Flakes, the "frosting" almost like maple and it's more like a glaze, but very good.  Also the peanut addition is wonderful with actual nuts on the flakes.  It somewhat hard to pin down a similarity to this cereal - Frosted Flakes is not a good comp as it tastes NOTHING like it.  I remember a cereal that had flakes topped with maple syrup taste and from what I can remember, this is similar, but the addition of peanuts makes it completely different.  Conversely the kids didn't really like it, although 2 of my 3 kids now have decided they don't like peanut butter, so maybe that has something to do with it...  Eitherway this is definitely something I will be buying again - if for no other reason than Dad will have a good tasting cereal in the house that is "just Dad's"!

column9: Yummy! But where did I taste this cereal before?
column10: If you ever tasted Kellogg's Frosted Flakes, then nothing new here. Same texture plus added nut bits and honey. The cereal does taste good, very sweet if thats what you like. But loses a star because there is really minimal difference in taste to their Frosted Flakes. Crunchy Nut fails to be something "NEW" from their original product.
OK, it is not the greatest nutritionally but it tastes very good and stays crunchy in milk if you don't dawdle. The honey and peanut are delicious together.

column9: Just like the old Nut N' Honey Crunch???
column10: I was excited to get the chance to try out this cereal because from the description it remind me of 'Nut N' Honey Crunch' cereal that Kellogg's had on the market about 20 years ago. I was a big fan of that cereal but I found this new cereal to be overly sweet. And even though it says it has peanuts on the flakes, and yes you can see them, I could not taste peanuts whatsoever. I am sure for those out there who never experienced the deliciousness that was 'Nut N' Hioney Crunch', they will enjoy this cereal. As for me it was just too sweet to enjoy.

column9: Heavy on flavor, light on crunch
column10: This cereal provides the great quality that is expected from Kellogg's in a new, delicious flavor. I'm a big fan of crunch in cereal, and, though this one touts its crunch, the nuts are barely noticeable. The main draw here is the flavor. It's great mixed with other cereals (honey granola, Cheerios, or even Corn Flakes), or better yet slice up a banana and add to the deliciousness.

Not the very best out there (and not the healthiest either), but I liked it.It's crunchy just like its name suggests, and the peanut flavor was quite strong. However, I don't think these characteristics justify its price premium. In many ways it tastes similar to regular honey bunches, which you can find for a lot cheaper.

This cereal is absolutely delicious!It has a slight honey flavor that is just right, not overpowering or too sweet. I am not a fan of sugary cereals, but my husband is, and we both really like this cerealEach bite actually stays crunchy which is great because I hate getting to last half of the bowl of cereal and it being soggy, this cereal really held its crunchiness! The nuts are great, they are peanuts and I have not tried a cereal like this before. I am not a fan of almonds or walnuts and those seem to be the only types of nuts that I have found in cereals.The regular size bowl of cereal fills me up and keeps me full until lunch time but also is a great snack at any time of the day or night!

This is a nice light, flaked cereal that reminds me of frosted flakes but not as sweet.  I was hesitant about the honey in the cereal but there is just the right touch of honey in it.  The crunch hold up in milk for quite awhile (I hate cereals that after a few minutes just wilt!)  I will continue to buy this cereal.

If you're wondering what Kellogg's Crunchy Nut is like, it can be summed up this way: it is basically a sweeter version of Corn Flakes . . . the flakes are crispier, slightly thicker, and coated in light honey with sprinkles of ground peanuts . . . hardly imaginative, but it's a reliable cereal making formula and works well. If you're looking to add some sweetness to your normally bland Corn Flakes, without much of a sugar/calorie penalty, this is an excellent way to do that. So why don't I give 5 stars? Eh, well, there is nothing wrong with the product, except it could be a bit denser in a variety of minerals and vitamins, and I have to be massively enthusiastic to give 5. I won't be ordering the 4-pack through subscription, as I do with Cheerios, for example. So I don't love this cereal, but you may . . . I like it, and will buy the occasional box every now and again at the grocery store.

column9: Very tasty, but needs more nutritional value
column10: Sure I love the taste of the sugary sweetness of this cereal. Tastes like frosted flakes with honey and nut mixed in. Unfortunately, with no (ok, less than 1 gram) fiber, they don't provide the nutrition that I need. The nutritional panel is basically carbs... 11 of 26 which are sugar. I kept eating, but I never felt full, but I sure did get a ton of empty calories. I can't recommend this to anyone looking to eat a hearty breakfast. If you are looking for corn, sugar, peanuts, and honey (first four ingredients) and don't care about nutrition, this cereal is for you. For everyone else, look elsewhere.Full Ingredients: (look at all the sugar)Milled Corn, Sugar, Peanuts, Honey, Malt Flavoring, Molasses, Salt, High Fructose Corn Syrup, Caramel Color, Iron, Annatto Extract Color, Niacinamide, Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C), Sodium Ascorbate (Vitamin C), Pyridoxine Hydrochloride (Vitamin B6), Thiamin Hydrochloride (Vitamin B1), Riboflavin (Vitamin B2), Vitamin A Palmitate, Vitamin B12, Folic Acid, Bht (Preservative), Vitamin D, Wheat Starch.

Crunchy Nut is really good. I was dubious at first because there are a ton of honey and nut flavored cereals out there and I didn't see how a new one would stand out. Crunchy Nut stands apart because it is VERY nutty tasting. The predominate flavor here is actually peanuts, then honey coated corn flakes. I loved it but it just isn't that good for you (hence, the 4 stars). Crunchy nut definitely falls into the sugary-cereal category but it tastes so good that one box lasted only a couple days.

I enjoyed this cereal.  I will probably get it again.I thought it tasted good and the texture was excellent.  It never got soggy in milk- although I didn't test this to any extreme.  The taste of honey wasn't prominent, but there was a "nut" flavor that I enjoyed.My son and grandson also enjoyed it- as evidenced by the fact that they just about emptied the box during their weekend visit.Now, that said, it's nothing really special- just a sweetened corn flake style cereal.  It's rather sweet- too sweet for my wife (as I'm writing this she just said that all breakfast cereals belong on the candy isle), but probably about the same as "frosted flakes."The ingredients bear this out, with the first three ingredients being "milled corn, sugar, peanuts" followed by "honey" and a bunch of various things they put in cereal- including high fructose corn syrup and salt.So, its not a health food store type product. If you're looking for a American style, sweetened cereal to enjoy, I suggest that you give this stuff a try.

The flavor was not too sweet, or too plain. We jokingly referred to it as "Corn Flakes on Steroids", due to the richness of flavor and amazing crunch. One of the first things we noticed was that it does not get soggy by the time you get to the bottom of the bowl. It's also very filling-unlike Corn Flakes, for instance, to which I always feel compelled to add some fruit to. The flavor is rich and round, and the nuts are very satisfying-it's so good, I've caught myself eating it as a snack, even without milk. Highly recommended-yummy!

Kellogg's really hit it out of the park this time. I'm not a huge cold cereal fan but it didn't take me long to wipe out this box.It stays *plenty* crunchy after pouring on the milk.It tastes terrific. Does it taste like peanuts? No, I didn't detect that but I'm sure this ingredient makes it more crunchy.The sweetness level (from honey) is just right; however, I do add a little box of raisins to a large bowlful just because I like fruit in my cereal. Bananas are great with this too.This cereal actually tops *Kellogg's Special-K Red Berries* [which I love] from my view.Total fat [daily values] = 2%; cholesterol = 0%; sodium = 10%; carbs = 11%; and, lots of vitamins including a high content of iron and folic acid. One-half cup of cereal yields 160 calories (with fat-free milk.)This will be the first food item that I've acquired [for free] through the Amazon Vine program which I plan to go to the grocery and buy more of. Terrific stuff -- I'm sold.My highest recommendation.

This is a very crispy, crunchy cereal with a mild peanut taste and a heavy molasses overtone.  It is quite sweet, the second ingredient after corn being sugar.  I have a sweet tooth and this was too sweet for me, so I guess that's saying something!It does contain a small amount of High Fructose Corn Syrup for those wishing to avoid it.  It's buried in the ingredients, so we can't know exactly how much there is, but I assume not much.  It makes me wonder why they even had to include it.It stays crisp in milk until the bowl is done (assuming, of course, you're not using an outrageously large bowl), and my cat (who also has a sweet tooth) likes the leftover milk.While I enjoyed the cereal well enough, it really was just too sweet in my opinion, so I would not repurchase.Allergen information:  Of course, if you are allergic to peanuts, you'll want to avoid this one.

Ask my husband what he wants for dinner on almost any night and you'll get one of two answers: "hamburgers", or "cereal". The man loves his cereal so much that both of our kids are sick of eating it, if that tells you anything, so who better to review Kellogg's new Crunchy Nut than a cereal lover?My husband refused to take a bite of the cereal until it had milk on it - it's a thing for him. Once he'd put it in the bowl with some milk he let it sit for a short minute before taking his first bite. And his second, and his third, and so on. Before I knew it the bowl was gone and he was debating a second one.Yes, it's that good. And better yet? He didn't put ANY sugar on it, which is not normal for him. I've seen him drown his cereals in enough sugar to make my teeth ache, so the fact that he was able to enjoy it without any extra sugar is definitely a plus!We had a problem with the company calling it "crunchy nut". While there's a slight tang of nut in the cereal, what you really get is a honey flavor. We thought they should be called something different, like Honey Flakes or Crunchy Honey.There's only one downside to this - we ran out! Time to get more!!

I live in Battle Creek, home of Kellogg's. One would assume I am predisposed to like their product. I don't work for them, but I do like most of their cereal and other breakfast food. This was my first try of Crunchy Nut. Honestly? I really, really like it. I don't eat cereal for breakfast most of the time, but I honestly polished off this box in two days. It does have peanuts, which my wife does not like, but my youngest daughter love it, as I did. Good stuff!

column9: Nice light taste, not too sweet
column10: I love cereal.  I'll eat it anytime, not just for breakfast.  I just had this for dessert tonight after dinner.  I find myself craving milk (probably a calcium deficiency) and instead of eating ice cream, sometimes a small bowl of cereal satisfies me.  This cereal tastes like cornflakes with nuts and honey.  I've always been fond of cornflakes, so I liked them.  I will definitely be buying them again.

Kellogg's Crunchy Nut cereal consists of corn flakes covered in honey and bits of peanuts.  It is somewhat crunchy, although not any more so than most other cereals.  Compared to a lot of other breakfast cereals, it doesn't have large amounts of vitamins or minerals, but it does have 25% of the daily recommended values of vitamins B6 and B12, as well as iron.  There are also small amounts of fiber and protein.The key characteristic of this cereal is that it is almost overwhelmingly sweet, with sugar making up more than 35% of each serving, by weight.  The second ingredient listed on the box is sugar, and is also contains molasses, honey, and high fructose corn syrup.  It is so sweet that I could only just make out the tastes of honey and peanuts.  There is no way that I could ever eat this for breakfast, but it does make a nice dessert in very small amounts.  If you're looking for a very sweet, sugary cereal, this might be a good choice for you, but I probably won't be buying it again.

This new cereal tastes very good, although they are a bit on the sweet side for me.  They don't have much of a peanut taste, which is fine with me.  There strongest point is that they start crunchy and stay that way in milk.  I really hate mushy cereal and these last a long time in milk.  They have a honey taste that is very pleasing.  I find them a good snack dry also.For adults, like me, they may be a bit too sweet, but for kids they are probably about right.  I'm not a nutritionist, but I suspect that they are more nutritional than frosted flakes and taste much better.  Give them a try, especially if your into sweet cereals.

column9: You'd be a Nut not to love 'em
column10: I've always been a fan of Frosted Flakes, maybe it was Tony the Tiger's stripey smile, or just the fact that they tasted like pure sugar glaze with a corny crunch. Unfortunately, my fandom only lasted until the flakes touched milk for more than a few seconds. Unless you've got speed-eating skills, the mushy sludge at the bottom of the bowl was less than appetizing.I'm not certain what I expected with this new cereal, but they were flakes, they were frosted, so what's not to like?On first bite, they are definitely a kissing cousin of Frosted Flakes, but they seemed crunchier, a bit more wheat flake taste and a bit less sugar and more almost caramelized. The nuttiness is very subtle, not a big chunk-o-almond or peanut hit, just little dots on the flakes that add to the crunchiness. And crunchy these are, from the first bite to nearly the last.They've managed to make a better flake, for sure! So, sorry Tony, your flakes are out, and the Cruncy Nut is definitely in at our house.

column9: Sweet and crunchy - great for breakfast and great as a snack!
column10: I haven't eaten cereals in years and normally ate the sugary types like Fruit Loops, Sugar Frosted Flakes, Cap'n Crunch and the like mainly as a dry snack because I'm a sugar fiend and like my cereals sweet.  When I saw this I decided to try it since I haven't binged on cereal in a few years.I really like this cereal a lot because of the nice crunch (corn flakes) and sweet but not too sweet (honey) coating and light peanut taste.  To me the peanut taste is really light but other family members noticed the peanut taste easier than I was able to.  This works out as an excellent dry snack for me but to be thorough I tried it with whole milk and skim milk for the review.It stayed crunchy during the time I ate it with milk and was pleased with the mouthfeel, taste, and texture although I prefer it with whole milk rather than skim.  I believe I'll start buying some of this cereal since I like it a lot as a snack.  I don't eat breakfast so this will always be eaten as a snack by me.If you are a cereal eater I suggest you giving this a try.  I'm pretty sure you'll like this too if you do try it.  This really is a tasty cereal with a nice crunch.

column9: Nutty for Crunch Nut Golden Honey Nut!
column10: I really like the taste of this cereal.  It tastes very much like a competitor's "Honey Bunches of Oats."I would not classify this as a health cereal by any means.  It does have a good deal of sugars in it, and the nuts are peanuts.  It's not horrible off the label though either. A serving (3/4 of a cup) is 120 calories (without milk) and contains 1g of fat, 11g of sugar and 160mg of sodium.The Ingredients:MILLED CORN, SUGAR, PEANUTS, HONEY, MALT FLAVORING, MOLASSES, SALT, HIGH FRUCTOSE CORN SYRUP, CARAMEL COLOR, IRON, ANNATTO EXTRACT COLOR, NIACINAMIDE, ASCORBIC ACID (VITAMIN C), SODIUM ASCORBATE (VITAMIN C), PYRIDOXINE HYDROCHLORIDE (VITAMIN B6), THIAMIN HYDROCHLORIDE (VITAMIN B1), RIBOFLAVIN (VITAMIN B2), VITAMIN A PALMITATE, VITAMIN B12, FOLIC ACID, BHT (PRESERVATIVE), VITAMIN D, WHEAT STARCHIf you like any of the Honey Bunches cereals you'd probably like this too.
There's not much to say about this cereal: it's about what you'd expect from the box. It's crunchy and nutty, and has a strong honey taste. I like it.

column9: Very tasty -- Frosted Flakes, move over!
column10: I found this cereal to be excellent - very similar in taste to Frosted Flakes, but without the huge jolt of sugar. The peanuts are very small - basically peanut bits that are stuck to the flakes. But, it does add a noticeable flavor to the cereal that complements the overall taste quite nicely. Although I've been a fan of Frosted Flakes forever, I would definitely pick this over Frosted Flakes 10 times out of 10 - it really is that good!Nowadays I try to eat high fiber cereals, such as Raisin Bran or Kashi, instead of the less nutritious (albeit usually more tasty) cereals. But for the occasional bowl, or mixed with a more healthy alternative, this really hits the spot. Highly recommend, especially if you enjoy Frosted Flakes.

column9: Yummy! Tastes like Kellogg's dusted your morning bowl of cornflakes with crushed peanut brittle!
column10: I just got my first box of Kellogg's Crunchy Nut Golden Honey Nut today, and as soon as I opened the inner bag, a delicious, sweet scent reminiscent of Crunch & Munch wafted out. Since I've been eying these boxes at my local Wally World for a few weeks, I was excited to see what this cereal would taste like.At first glance, it was clear that there was plenty of honey and sugar glazing these flakes and gluing the small chips of peanut to said flakes. This cereal won't be your family's health nut's new favorite, but Kellogg's is also not hiding behind any unfounded health claims here. The nutritional information is easy to find, and it's about what you'd expect for a product named "Golden Honey Nut". It's also undoubtedly as delicious as you'd hope a food product by that name would be!After getting my first whiff, I HAD to have a bowl (of course, I'll probably only be having a salad as my actual dinner now tonight, but it was TOTALLY worth it)! As other reviewers here have mentioned, the heavy sugar/honey glaze keeps these very crunchy in milk for longer than you'd have with more lightly glazed flakes. I also noticed that within about 30 seconds' time of having the milk in my bowl of cereal, it was lightly colored by the honey coating (which turned my milk a soft honey yellow). I couldn't tell that there were peanut pieces on the flakes as I ate them, which I consider to be something of a good thing - it wouldn't be terribly pleasant to me to have to deal with chunks of peanut sticking to and between my teeth as I tried to get my bowl of morning sustenance down (I'm a die-hard cereal-for-breakfast kinda girl; always have been, always will be).Nutritionally speaking, this cereal compares closely to Honey Bunches of Oats. The two are quite similar in all of the stats you'd focus on, including the added vitamins and minerals. This cereal is delicious and satisfying, but if you're looking for Kashi's cousin, this isn't it (thankfully for me, too: Kashi's healthy, but it's not terribly tasty, IMHO).Overall, I'm very satisfied with this cereal. It's sweet, delicious and crunchy, and would also make a good, lower calorie substitution for your dessert, if you're so inclined (or a great crushed topping on yogurt or ice cream). Next time you're at the store, take a look at the stats for yourself, and if you're interested, grab a box. I doubt you'll regret it!Now, I'm off to enter my consumption data to my favorite online Sparkly dietary journal site! ; )

I have been eating this by the handful. I haven't had it in a bowl of milk, but it is great just to snack on as well.Flakes are a nice size, you can see the flakes are coated with the honey and barely any peanuts. The cereal smells a lot like peanuts but you can barely taste the peanut flavor. It has a nice sweet taste, taste like bunch of cereals I have had before one of them is Frosted flakes.I think I would categorize this cereal more geared towards adults, but children would also like the flavor as well. It just doesn't have a fun mascot associated to it to get the kids but it is sweet enough for them.

I predict this will be a big seller for Kelloggs.  While I am not usually a fan of flake cereals because most get mushy too fast, Crunchy Nut stays super crunchy all the way down to the bottom of the bowl.  It really has taste, as well.  To me it has a bit of a brown sugar taste which is neither bland nor sweet.  It will probably be popular with kids and adults alike. I personally didn't taste much of the peanut taste, although it appeared there were plenty of tiny nuggets of them "glued" to the flakes.  Perhaps if this is a selling feature, Kelloggs could amp up the peanut taste a little.  Crunchy Nut could get me more inclined to eat flake cereals more often.  I hope it succeeds.

column9: Frosted Flakes With Peanuts...But Where's Tony Tiger?
column10: It could be called Frosted Flakes with Nuts because that is what it tastes like. I don't actually taste much of the nuts though, mostly the super sweet honey/sugar coating that is almost exact in flavor to Frosted Flakes with a hint of honey. The nuts seem to add crunch. This cereal is very sweet, almost too sweet. The first thought that struck my mind is that its almost like eating ice cream for breakfast. So the taste is there but is it a good way to start your day? The only wheat in it is wheat starch. The rest of the ingredients by order from the description, Milled corn, sugar, peanuts, honey, malt flavoring, molasses, salt, high fructose corn syrup, caramel color means this cereal, even though it also has some vitamins, is probably not the best choice for breakfast if you are trying to cut out empty carbs and increase whole grain foods.

column9: Not impressed with Crunchy Nut Cereal
column10: kellogg's Crunchy Nut is basically corn flakes coated with sugar and microscopically sized nut pieces.  I can't even taste the nuts on them.My key comments:1)  These are completely void, nutritionally2)  Seems like this should have been another version of Corn Flakes instead of an altogether new cereal.3)  As I alluded to above, they don't even taste particularly good.Overall, a lousy product in my opinion.

column9: Deliciously Crunchy--to the Bottom of the Bowl
column10: I was very impressed with this cereal.  It straddles the line between the healthy and the sweet/sugary.  The result is a phenomenal cereal that both the adults and children in our house were excited to eat.  In fact, my youngest even opted for this over his usual sugar-saturated brand.  Once we were through with the box, he (and I) were actively looking for this item every time we visited the grocery store.  For me, the crowning virtue of this cereal is that it remains crunchy in a bowl of milk.  Whenever I eat cereal, I tend to eat quickly to avoid sogginess.  One morning, I poured my cereal and had to focus on helping the kids with something and only came back to it after several minutes. With most cereals, I would return to a soggy mess that I poured down the drain.  Amazingly, this cereal was still crunchy and delicious.  That--and its exceptional taste--will ensure that I continue to seek out this excellent cereal.

This cereal does one thing really well -- it stays crunchy in milk.  That, if nothing else, is enough for me to recommend it to anyone who asks.  But it also passes the taste test -- it's good, and it's good without adding sugar (or really anything else; it's good right out of the box!).And it passes the kid test.  My son ate two bowls the day the box arrived, and my daughter has been eating it by the handful.  It's not overly sweet, but it has that honey flavor that lets you eat it without adding anything to it.  The nuts offer a good crunch without being overwhelming, and help the flakes to stay crunchy.  This is going on my shopping list!

column9: Yummy for breakfast or a sweet snack
column10: I really enjoyed this cereal.  It tastes sort of like a combination of frosted flakes and honey nut cheerios.  You can definitely taste the honey and the nuts.  At 120 calories for 3/4 of a cup of cereal, it's not a bad nutritional bargain either.  Good for both breakfast, and a lower-cal snack when your sweet tooth comes calling.

The kids got to this before I ever could and it did not stay long on the shelf so that in itself tells the tale. It was on the last bite (literally) that I was told it tasted great by cereal statands with the empty box in the garbage to prove it.

I'm a fan of cereals in general, but mostly those with nuts mixed in. However, most of the nutty cereals I've tried have the nuts separated from the flakes. The fact that the Kellog's Crunchy Nut Golden Honey Nut cereal has crunched peanuts on top of golden milled-corn flakes made it more appealing to me.Eating cereal is a serious ritual for me.  I like to take my time and savor the taste of the cereal as it mixes with the milk while I also get the crunchy sensation after each bite.  I tend to dislike cereals that get soggy too quickly.  In this category I place the original Kellog's Corn Flakes, Honey Bunches of Oats and Raisin Bran among others.  I have to eat these in a hurry if I want to maintain the crunchiness, and they still end up  getting very soft too quickly, leaving you with a disappointing experience.  The longest lasting cereals that I've tried include Honey-Nut Cheerios and Froot Loops, but these tend to float above the milk instead of blending in, so you end up with a lot of extra milk at the bottom.The Crunchy Nut  flakes are coated with a very sweet syrup made out of molasses.  The coating gives a very shiny appearance to the flakes, and while at first glance they seemed soaked in an oily substance, that perception went away after I tasted a few flakes coming out of the box.In terms of texture, Crunchy Nut cereal has the perfect balance.  The flakes are crunchy and very resistant to the milk and they also leave a very nice flavor to it.  I can take my time and savor all the cereal flavors without worrying about soggy flakes at the bottom. The cereal peanuts mixed with the flakes and milk give a very faint taste of Crunch `n Munch and Cracker Jax.  The crunch is very loud, which is a sign of freshness and quality.  Although sweeter than the average cereal, it didn't leave a bad aftertaste or a need to follow up with a glass of cold water, like when I eat the sweeter Froot Loops or Frosted Flakes.In terms of nutritional value, Crunchy Nut has no distinct advantage or disadvantage compared to other cereals.  Corn syrup and molasses are its main sweeteners.  It has 160 calories with skim milk (120 without), 0 cholesterol,  26g of carbs (11g of sugar, 15 of other carbs) and it's a great source of all major vitamins.Taste is simply enjoyable.  It has a very pleasant and familiar sweet taste from the combination of peanuts and molasses that's hard to resist.  It is one of those cereals you can have at any time of the day.  I highly recommend it to those of you who like peanuts and sweet cereals.

column4: Michelle L. Beck "Always the Devourer of Good...
column9: A little sweet and a little nutty.
column10: To be honest, I am not a breakfast eater, however, when I want something quick and easy, I tend to pick traditional, plain or simple cereals. My favorites are Corn Flakes (with sliced bananas), or Cheerios (original), but when I want to get fancy, I will settle for Honey Nut Cheerios (which can sometimes be too sweet), Fruit & Fiber, or Raisin Bran. So when "Crunchy Nut Golden Honey Nut" was offered, I jumped on the opportunity to try it. I must admit, I was pleasantly surprised. Each flake offers, a little sweetness (not too much) and a little crunch (not too overwhelming). And even in milk, the flakes stay relatively firm (I don't tend to let my cereal stand for long periods of time. I don't care for soggy cereal) and don't get mushy. I would definitely recommend this cereal for those who enjoy slightly sweet, with a nutty flavor, cereals.

My kids loved this.  When I got the box I gave each of my kids a bowl with cereal and milk.  The vote was unanimous - a delicious winner.  The cereal is crunchy and sweet but not too sugary.  The nutty flavor is there but does not overwhelm the rest of the contents.  My kids cut out the coupon for our first purchase of this very tasty cereal.

column9: Tastes like Frosted Flakes, stays crisp!
column10: It is kinda weird writing reviews about food products, because, well, most people have different tastes.That being said, I tore open the box, poured a bowl, and enjoyed what I tasted. If your a frosted flakes fan,try these out to see if they are comparable. They stayed crispy in the milk, and had a nice crunch to them.
Love the new Crunchy Nut cereal.  Tastes like honey drizzeled over corn flakes and nuts.  Not much more to say.  If you like those 3 things, you will love this!

column9: Frosted Flake Type Cereal with Bonus Flavors
column10: This has just the right amount of sweetness and flavor that makes for a delightful breakfast or snack.  The flakes hold their crunch pretty well and there is more flavor there than something like frosted flakes.  I think most people will know that in terms of nutrition, this is not in the league of some Kashi cereals, but most people can read the nutrition information as well. If you are a fan of sweet flake type cereals, this is right up your alley, and you will enjoy it. The nuts are a bonus though over other offerings, and they're not as hard as say some bunches of oats might be.

column9: Not my favorite way to start the day...
column10: I did not go for the taste of this cereal.  For me it was not so much as it being too sweet as it just not suiting me.  I am more of a raisin bran type cereal fan.  My kids were not wild about it either so it will never go into my cart again.  I was not overly jazzed by the ingredient list either which made me feel like it was not one of the best nutritional choices.  Do your body a favor and make another choice.

To imagine the flavor, take Frosted Flakes, substitute a honey glaze for the "frosting", and add a few thinly shredded peanuts.  It is still sweet, though a little less sweet than Frosted Flakes.  The peanuts add a light peanut taste along with the corn flakes and honey--no flavor dominates.  If that sounds good to you (like it did to me), then you'll probably love this cereal.  If not, you may be disappointed.

To do this product justice, I should tape myself enjoying a bowl of it. The cereal truly tastes like what it is: crispy cornflakes covered in honey and peanuts. The peanut flavor is quite distinct. It's good enough for dessert, but you get to have it for breakfast. What more could you ask for in life? Go get some!

If taste is your most important factor in picking a breakfast cereal, then you will like the sweet, nutty taste this cereal has. However, if like me you also want something that is nutritious and filling, look elsewhere. A serving of cereal has only 2g of protein and is loaded with sweeteners;by comparison, Special K has triple the protein and 1/3 the sugar. This cereal is also not that filling. I'll eat something else for breakfast.

Kellogg's Crunchy Nut, Golden Honey Nut, is basically Frosted Flakes cereal with peanuts.  It is very sugary (11g & second ingredient on the list after milled corn)and about 120 calories per serving (31g or 3/4 cup).  I liked how it stayed crunchy in the milk.  It is not a bad cereal but not really anything over the top exciting.  If you like frosted corn cereals with some peanut slivers infused on the flakes then you will like this.

This morning my husband, one of my granddaughters and I tried this new cereal from Kellogg's, Crunchy Nut Golden Honey Nut.  All three of us liked the cereal, but the other two liked it a little more than I did.When milk is first poured over the flakes they are, indeed, very crunchy and toothsome.  I liked the fact that I could actually "feel" the peanut pieces on the flakes, as well as see them.  The touch of honey is maybe a little over done for me, but my fellow crunchers didn't agree.  I do think this cereal is a little too sweet, but that may just be my taste preference.  The serving size is given as 3/4 cup for a count of 120 calories.  Pair that with 1/2 cup of fat free milk and you are up to 160 calories.  Certainly not bad numbers except that nobody bothered to stay within the 3/4 cup limit.  The flakes do not, alas, stay crunchy for long in the milk.  After 5 minutes they were almost completely flat and yet still very good.I have been requested to buy this cereal after this box runs out along with another new release, Crunchy Roasted Honey Nut, 10.8-Ounce (Pack of 4), and since there is a coupon printed on the box I'm sure I will do that.  I think this will end up being one of those things my grandgirls request I have on hand for their sleep over parties.  There was much discussion of how good these would be eaten as a snack without adding the milk to them.  Humm, Granny will have to be vigilant in watching these boxes.

column9: nice flavor but way too sweet
column10: This cereal has a nutty flavor to it and it would be good if it weren't for the over abundance of sugar in this. This is just corn flakes with a sprinkling of nuts and a thick coating of glazed sugar. There isn't much fiber in it either so this is basically an unhealthy cereal. The flakes stay crispy because of the thick coating of sugar takes a long time to wear off, I won't be buying this cereal, I like a little sugar with my cereal and NOT a little cereal with my sugar. LOL

My normal breakfast is cereal with fruit.  This cereal is good and kept its crunch, but it was a little too sweet for me.  I am not sure if it is the addition of the honey because the sugar content is 12% which is not really much higher than some of my other cereals, but I did find the taste a little sweeter.As far as I am concerned, the nuts were pretty much non-existent. It is basically sugar/honey and cornflakes.Caloric count with skim milk is 160 calories for 3/4 of a cup of cereal and 1/2 cup of skim milk--I guess that is pretty average.Overall, not a bad cereal, but I prefer some of the other Kellogg's cereals.

My three kids and I all were happy to try this cereal, and we all loved it. It is quite crunchy, but not so crunchy that it hurts your gums (like one or two cereals I've tried.) It definitely has a nutty flavor, too. I was worried that the honey flavor would be too strong, as I don't like extremely sweet foods, but this turned out to be a great balance. I was also extremely pleased at the corn flavor of the flakes...it wasn't over powered by the nuts and honey.The cereal held up well with milk as well, which was nice. All in all, I was quite pleased, and my kids are asking for more.

Boo to Amazon for only giving me 1 box instead of a pack of 4 for the Vine program!Okay, now that I've got that out of the way... (don't worry, didn't penalize the rating)This had a weird, strong mix of salty and sweet that I never had before when I initially tasted it.  However, with each bite after that, I got used to it, and found it tasting very good.  Pleasant aftertaste too.  I also find that it stays pretty crunchy in milk, and that it left me feeling satisfied.Still, don't they already have a cereal that has crunchy nuts and honey? Nut and Honey Crunch?  Why bother making something like this?

column9: A "Kids" Cereal Adults Will Enjoy, Too.
column10: Kellogg's Crunchy Nut Flakes are in essence Frosted Flakes (sugar glazed corn flakes) covered with peanut fragments.  While I was a bit concerned when the second ingredient listed is sugar, when I checked the nutrition info, there are only 160 calories a bowl with a 1/2 cup of milk.  I know some of Kellogg's "healthy" cereals with more calories.I found Kellogg's Crunchy Nut Flakes to be sweet but not overpowering with a hint of peanuts.  Even in milk they have a good crunch but they can be enjoyed by themselves as well.  I didn't know if the peanuts would work on a breakfast cereal but I was pleasantly surprised at the combination.  People with peanut allergies should avoid this but I think this is one of those cereals that kids and parents can both enjoy.

column9: Surprisingly tasty, crunchy, not too sweet
column10: As a lover of more hearty cereals like Grape-Nuts, I was a little worried this one might be too sweet.  Instead, I was pleasantly surprised to find that, sure, it reminded me (a lot) of Frosted Flakes, but was better.  It stayed very crunchy in milk (can't say that about the Frosted Flakes I remember), had a nice nuttiness to it - although I can't say I'd necessarily have realized it had nuts if the package hadn't clued me in.  As for healthiness - it's fortified like most cereals these days, but I was definitely hungry again an hour later and wasn't impressed by the protein or fiber content.  Overall a good cereal, but I docked one star for its dubious health value - I'll probably go back to Grape Nuts for daily eating.

As cereals go, there are plenty of choices. I tend to favor plainer ones myself, so the sweetness of the honey taste wasn't the plus for me it might be for someone else. Still, it was not bad. The bits of peanut added an extra tang. The overall effect reminded me of a cross between frosted flakes and Cracker Jacks.As an experiment, I used up the rest of the box by turning it into an impromptu snack bar mix. I melted some marshmallows with a bit of butter over low heat, and stirred in the cereal. (One cup of marshmallows to every 2 cups of cereal). I then took the mix and spread it onto a buttered baking sheet, packing it together. When cooled, I sliced it up into handy-sized servings. The result was tasty, crunchy and a bit more portable.If I were to try the experiment again, I might crunch the flakes down a bit more before mixing in the marshmallows, and try adding things like chocolate chips, butterscotch bits, raisins, craisins (dried cranberry snacks) or combinations of them all.

column9: Kellogg's Crunchy Nut Golden Honey Nut Cereal
column10: Kellogg's Crunchy Nut Golden Honey Nut is super-delicious.  The honey coating on the cornflake base has almost a caramelized flavor, and the peanut bits add extra crunch and a little extra protein.  They stay fairly crunchy in milk if you eat them reasonably quickly- in fact, they stay crunchy longer than uncoated flake cereals do, which is a good thing.But the reason I give this cereal just four stars instead of five is that the serving size is 3/4c, and that'll cost you 120 calories, before you even add milk.  3/4c doesn't amount to a lot of this cereal, so to feel satisfied and stay satisfied until lunch or elevensies, (whichever comes first), you'll either have to eat more than 3/4c (and figure on taking in more calories from cereal) or supplement your bowl of cereal with an egg or two, some fruit, a glass of juice, and maybe even a piece of toast.  I know all the cereal companies say to eat their product "as part of a balanced breakfast," but most people I know choose a box of cereal so they can pour their breakfast in a bowl, pour on some milk, bolt the cereal, and get out the door, avoiding fiddling with the egg, fruit, juice, toast, etc.  I have to say, as much as I love the taste of this cereal, I ate the recommended 3/4c for breakfast and didn't even last the hour before I was hungry again.That's not to say all is lost for Crunchy Nut Golden Honey Nut cereal.  It's also quite delicious if you mix the recommended serving size with a serving of Greek yogurt, either plain or vanilla or sweetened with honey, and the added protein and nutrients you get from the yogurt does make you feel fuller longer than just the cereal-and-milk combo.So yes, this cereal is beyond great-tasting.  It has good crunch, good sweetness- it's like eating candy!  It doesn't disappoint on the taste front.  But plan to supplement with another breakfast food so you're not running for a Snickers Bar by 9 a.m.

There are so many cereals on the market yet always something new.  When I opened the box my first thought was these smell like Kellogs Corn Pops, very sweet smelling.  As for taste, not really a whole lot of it, its almost like the milk overpowered the taste.  Its kind of somewhere between corn flakes and frosted flakes, like the cereal can't make up its mind to cater to adults or kids.I didn't find them to be particularly crunchy but really don't care too much about that.  The nuts in every bite are so small and I guess are in the flakes if that's what the different color pieces are, didn't see a real nut.  Flakes are shiny with sugar.  I have nothing against sugar and actually have Reese's Puffs sometimes, its just these are marketed as crunchy nut and they aren't really either crunchy or have nuts.  Not as fullfilling as other cereals like Raisin Bran or Special K, you'll need a banana in it.Some pros:  fairly low in calories, again taste is subjective so what's to say.  Some fibre.I wish I could write more but the cereal just doesn't give me any reason to.

This looks to be a relaunch of the old, and internationally widely available, Honey Nut Corn Flakes.The name alone should tell you most of what you need to know about this cereal as it aptly describes exactly how this cereal tastes.  Corn Flakes that are sweet with honey and sprinkled with peanuts for a slightly nutty flavor.  I would say this cereal tastes sweeter than most (and definitely sweeter than standard corn flakes ) but is still not as sweet as the traditional Kellogs "kids" cereals, e.g. Frosted Flakes, Fruit Loops, etc.A high quality cereal and recommended for those that would enjoy this flavor combination.

column9: Tastes great for what it is
column10: I personally don't care for overly sweet cereals but this has to be better than some of the kiddie cereals.I found it too sweet and prefer to mix it with an unsweetened high fiber cereal or oats. That takes the sweet edge off.If you have a young one who loves the sugary marshmallow type cereals perhaps this could help with the transition to more adult cereals.If you are trying to cut down on sugar in general this cereal isn't for you.

Crunchy Nut Crunchy cereal is great. It's very tasty. It's weird because this cereal actually tastes like a variety of sweet flavors. For it example, it sort of tastes like Cracker Jacks to me...lol. If you are one of those people who is into the healthy variety of cereals and are not used to sweet cereals you may not like this. However, if you like me, has a sweet tooth and on occasion delves back into your youth and picks up one those sweet cereals you used to like when you were a kid, this is the cereal for you.

column9: Like eating Cracker Jacks for breakfast....
column10: Kellogg's Crunchy Nut is a cornflake cereal covered with a heavy coating of caramelized sugar and tiny bits of peanuts. I swear it tastes almost exactly like Cracker Jacks - not surprising since the 3 biggest ingredients are corn, sugar, and peanuts - so it is very tasty but not exactly what I generally have in mind for breakfast.Seriously, this cereal makes an addictive snack dry out of the box, but I'd never eat something this sugary first thing in the morning. 11 grams of sugar per serving rivals my kids' sugary breakfast fare! I'll stick with my Honey Bunches of Oats.

column9: Crunchier and with more peanut flavor than I expected...
column10: I'm not a huge cereal nerd having grown up on a steady diet of mostly Müslix and Kix, with only the occasional box of Trix or Captain Crunch in the cupboard.  Though there are six million varieties of cereal products on the shelves, I pretty much stick to the occasional box of Raisin Bran or Honey Nut Cheerios, but of the brands that I do eat I have some very specific likes and dislikes.  When I picked this box of Crunchy Nut I was skeptical that it would actually deliver on it's namesake, being crunchy and nutty.  For my taste I find that the various nutty cereals usually don't have a  very strong nut taste, and the "crunchy" varieties tend to lose all their bite after a few seconds in milk.Lo and behold my surprise when this Kellogg's brand cereal delivered wholeheartedly on both accounts.  Overall Crunchy Nut has a very similar flavor profile to a box of Cracker Jacks, which in my book is a good thing.  The flakes are well enough coated with honey that they have a bit more life in milk than your typical sweetened flake, though they don't hold up as well to some of the Newman's Own cereal flakes ([[ASIN:B0040GI8YU Newman's Own Cereal - Sweet Enough Vanilla Almond 13oz 6 Pack],which are the king of crunchy in my opinion.)Overall I really enjoyed these and would probably put them into my cereal rotation.

Excellent product: good-tasting , not too sweet, with a pleasant, slightly toasted flavor. The honey-nut coating, as well as tasting nice, seems to form a protective barrier, keeping the flakes crisp right to the last spoonfull. I had to turn off my book-on-tape, as I could not hear it while I ate my cereal.The days of racing to finish one's cornflakes before they turn into a soggy ooze seem to be over at last!

column9: Taste BETTER (sweeter) than regular CORN FLAKES & stay CRUNCHY
column10: I'm not a huge fan of Kellogg's Frosted Flakes of Corn Cereal, 23-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 4) because they don't stay crunchy in milk and they leave a bad after taste in your mouth.  But I like these Crunchy flakes, even though there are only nut "specks" that have more of a peanut taste.  The Crunchy flakes taste sweeter and stay crunchier in milk than the frosted flakes.  When I first saw this cereal, I thought it would taste like Oatmeal Crisp Cereal, Chunky Almonds, 17-Ounce Box (Pack of 6) ... but it didn't.  I do like the taste of this cereal, but I prefer more of an almond taste (like General Mills) than a peanut taste (like Kellogg's).  However, I must say that the Kellogg's flakes have slightly less calories than the General Mills Oatmeal Crisp.If you are looking for a "healthy" cereal, this would not be for you ... LOTS of sugar (which I why I guess I like the taste).

column9: As a snack, this stuff is addictive! AKA "Dessert Cereal"
column10: I tried Kellogg's Crunchy Nut cereal upon arrival as it was snack time. It is truly addictive dry. I love the strong peanut flavor. However, since it is a cereal, I knew I needed to review it as such, so I poured a small bowl & here is the verdict:Pros:-It stays crunchy-Great peanut flavorCons:-Too sweet for a cereal. I do not like my milk to get sweet while I'm eating a cereal & with this the milk got really sweet right away. I wouldn't drink the milk if my life depended on it. It would make your teeth curl!I won't be buying this as a cereal. It is waaaaaaaaay too sugary to start the day with it. I might pack the remainder of the cereal up in Ziplock bags for the kids as a junky snack because it does have more health benefits than, say, a candy bar because of all the added vitamins. But I won't go out and purchase it on my own.06/21/11 UPDATE: In lieu of full disclosure, I have to admit that I've purchased this twice in our grocery store since trying the Amazon sample.
