I use it as a snack when we want something sweet but don't want to make a dessert snack. So as sugary sweet as it is, I have to admit to this being a guilty, junky pleasure once in while. I do love the strong peanut flavor.

First, Crunchy Nut is not health food. It is instead the wonderfully sweet flakes, vastly improved since my childhood.Second, food science has discovered the technique to retain crunchiness that persists throughout the entire milk saturated serving. It is a remarkable achievement and every bit as significant as E=mc2 to the consumer.I love this stuff. My wife hates it. She is in to 'healty eating'. Husbands will need to buy Crunchy Nut when we get the rare opportunity to shop unsupervised.As to the effect on the g-kids? I pre-tested it for you g-parents out there. Oh Yes! They love their g-pa.

column9: Very Sweet with undertones of peanut brittle
column10: Pros:Taste is similar to corn flakes without that wierd aftertasteStays crunchy in milkTastes very good right out of the boxOccasional bite tastes almost like peanut brittleMilk brings out the taste of honeyCons: A bit too sweet for me with milk, but kids should love this

Finally the cereal I knew and loved in England has made it across the waters to the US. I know it as honey nut cornflakes but as far as I am concerned it is the same. I am so happy that it is hear and a can now indulge a little at breakfast again.

A new cereal? Only one way to test it. Children, guess what's for breakfast this morning? My twin 8 year olds sat down and devoured a bowl of Kellog's Crunchy Nut. The earl reviews were good, alot of mmm's as milk dribbled down their chin. Crunchy, but not like granola crunchy which is good, tasty, tasty is always good and the big questions, do you want more? and would you eat it again? Two big resounding yes's, to those 2 questions. So I think we have a winner!

column9: Taste very good, healthy, not so great
column10: it's about 160 calories 1/2 cup with milk and 11g of sugar. It good and crunchy with little nuts in each flake. I eat it from the box as a snack, instead of chips or cookies, and it's very satisfying. The flakes are thick and honey coated. My 4 year old likes it a lot with milk, and he's fussy about his cereal. I will buy it again, but more for a special treat rather than a daily breakfast.

column9: Variations on a corn flake theme
column10: Crunchy Nut Golden Honey Nut is a corn flake cerial with added peanut crumbs, glued on by honey. The peanut flavor is quite noticeable at first, but less so as you get further into eating it. The flakes are smaller than those of "Frosted Flakes", but still with a light texture. It is fairly sweet, with 11 grams of sugar per serving. I enjoyed it. The easiest way to describe the cerial is that it is like "Frosted Flakes", but with added peanut flavor. There are only a relatively small number of basic ingredients that cerial companies work with and ways to combine them, and this is a pleasant variation on the corn flake theme.

This is sweet and crunchy cereal as advertised, with crunchy flakes and pieces of nuts on the sweetened flakes. They taste good enough that they make you want more - which can be both good news and bad news! It's a crunchy crunch, but it's more of a gentle crunch - I did not worry that fillings would fall off.Nutrition wise this is somewhere in the middle, however, if you are willing to make a compromise these can be great: instead of filling up the bowl with only Crunchy Nut, mix Crunchy Nut with some of the less sugary cereal like Special K, Cheerios, Total, or other nutritionally desirable cereal, and play with the portions to your liking. This also helps reduce the overall sweetness, since these are indeed sweet!

column9: Tastes like Frosted Flakes with a honey nut flavor
column10: This cereal tastes very good - similar to Frosted Flakes with a distinct honey and nut "flavor" although I didn't really taste the peanuts because the peanut flakes on the cereal are so small.I consider Crunchy Nut more like a dessert cereal than a good-for-you-type cereal because of all the sugar and high fructose corn syrup in the ingredients even though it's fortified with lots of Vitamins (A, C, Iron, D, etc.).  It's 120 calories for a 1.1 oz serving without milk.For me, Crunchy Nut has a 5 star taste with 3-1/2 star ingredients.

column9: Yummy, but not for those watching their diet
column10: Crunchy Nut, Golden Honey Nut does a good job describing the flavor.  I like to eat my cereal dry so I got a good look at the sweetend flakes.  The nuts are nearly ground up and attached to the flakes but not every flake has nuts on them so it tastes more like honey than peanuts.  A serving is only a 3/4 cup which isn't much if you meassure it out. Other nutrition facts for those that are watching their wasteline (not including milk): Calories 120, Calories from fat 10, Fat 1g, Cholesterol 0mg, Sodium 160mg, Potassium 40g, Total Carbs 26g, Fiber less than 1g, Sugars 11g, Protein 2g.  This cereal is an indulgence for me but I know my kids will like it!

This is a delicious sweetened corn flake cereal, very crispy.  The ground peanut granules are visible on the flakes. However, I could not taste any trace of peanut flavor, or notice any courser texture, due to the granules' presence.  That said, it still tasted very good.  The four stars are due to the lack of nut-perception, when it is a prominent part of the name of the product.

At first, I absolutely loved it!  It was like eating Frosted Flakes but with a more healthier side...or so I thought. It is very crunchy and has a nut cluster in every flake.  The taste is very sweet indeed.  As I went to Kellogg's website, I found a very shocking discovery:  The nutritional labels of Crunchy Nut and Frosted Flakes are almost identical!  It is they almost trying to fool adults into thinking they are eating a healthy alternative to Frosted Flakes.  Therefore it is pretty much just like Frosted Flakes but with a slightly different texture.  For the health conscious:  It has 120 calories, 26 grams of carbs(9% DV) and 11 grams of sugar per serving. A 14.1 oz box contains approximately 13 servings.  Another fine product from Kellogg's, but still too much sugar.

The Kellogg's Crunchy Nut (Golden Honey Nut) is indeed very crunchy.  It is also very sweet as other reviews have acknowledged.  In fact, its ingredient list is: (1) milled corn, (2) sugar, (3) peanut, (4) honey.... etc.  Having sugar ranks as the number 2 ingredient, you know there is a lot of sugar.  To put it in another way, in one serving size of 31 gram of this cereal, 11 gram of it is pure sugar.I really like this cereal.  It tastes sweet and delightful, and it is very very crunchy and stay fairly crunchy in the milk, just don't kid yourself in thinking this is a superhealthy food.While I do like this cereal, I don't think it is out of the world, so I am giving it a 4-star rating for being good, but not great.

Four and half stars really, but I rounded up. My family eats a lot of cereal. I'm a Cheerios lover from childhood, my daughter generally prefers the chocolate cereals and my son loves Honey Nut Cheerios.So I poured each of us a bowl. A very small one for me since it's very easy for things to taste too sweet to me.It's very crunchy. The milk doesn't seem to affect it at all in the time it takes to eat a bowl and it is very sweet. Like other reviewers have mentioned, it tastes a lot sweeter than the calories suggest. The honey taste is pretty faint. The peanut taste is just right.The reason I gave it five stars is that my kids loved it. Both of them thought it was just wonderful and it became their new favorite cereal. Since both are older, it's not a fickle decision on their part. My son's previous favorite had been his favorite for the last 10 years.It was too sweet for my tastes.I think it would make a great cracker crust or topping for a fruit crumble.I think for future servings of cereal, I'll mix it with regular corn flakes to help cut the sweet a bit.

If you like a very sweet breakfast cereal this one will do ya'.  The second ingredient listed is sugar, then on down the list you will find honey and molasses.  With all three of those in there you'd think the high fructose corn syrup might be unnecessary but alas, it too has been added.  It 's tasty but I don't detect the peanuts at all.  I'm using it as a TV watching snack at night because if I began my day with this much sugar in my bloodstream I'd be passed out by ten a.m.

Lives up to it's name.  It tastes sweeter than 120 calories and 1 gram of fat (zero saturated fat).  The crunch and the sweet taste reminds me a bit of the frosted flakes I ate as a kid.  It starts really crunchy and stays crunchy for a good while.  It's a little sweet for me as a daily cereal and it doesn't have the vitamin value of my regular cereal,  Total Raisen Bran, but will make a nice change from my daily routine.  It tastes great right out of the box as a snack.  NOTE: It does contain peanuts for those of you that are allergic to them.

Doing a food item is always difficult, individual taste and preference being a major reason why we like or dislike something.  Breakfast cereal might be one of the more difficult items.  Having written disclaimers, here is my review.This is a heavily sweetened item with 120 calories in ¾ of a cup.  In addition, there are peanut chips stuck to the flakes.  Honey and molasses are the major sweeteners.  The result is a corn flake with peanut slivers and honey that has a sweet pleasant taste.  The flakes hold up well in milk or can be eaten dry as a snack.  I think this would make an excellent base for a sweet trail mix snack.  My two-year old grandson likes them dry in his dish as a snack.This might be an alternate to the heavily sugar sweeten cereals but is not a good choice for anyone looking to control their weight.

To set the stage - I like cereal.  A lot.  :)  I tend to eat "healthy" cereals for breakfast, but I also like to get my sweet on from time to time.  I put these corn flakes squarely into the "sugar cereal" category, but you can judge the nutritional facts listed below for yourself.  They're very low in fat and not too high in calories.  I've eaten a bowl at each of the past five meals, sometimes for dessert.  Seriously, these aren't a bad choice for a relatively low calorie and low fat dessert.Taste:To quote Adam Richman of Man v. Food, "Oh, my goodness.  Ooooh, my goodness."  To help explain, from the moment that I opened the box and smelled the cereal, and through the first five bowls, I kept trying to figure out which candy these reminded me of.  Yes, _candy_.  That was the first thing that popped into my head, and it never left.  I think that I figured it out - Kathryn Beich Golden Crumbles (a fund raising candy during my childhood days in Illinois, with peanut butter coated in a candy shell).  Those were probably my favorite candy growing up, so it's no surprise that I like this cereal.As the name suggests, these taste like honey and nuts.  They are very sweet, IMO, but in a good way.  Oh, such a good way.Texture:With the sugar coating, these corn flakes have a nice crunch to them and stay crunchy for longer in milk than regular corn flakes.  I haven't had any issues with them getting soggy, but I normally finish a bowl in well under five minutes.Nutrition:At the time of this review, the ingredients are listed on Amazon, but the nutritional facts aren't.  So, I'll put them here and let you decide for yourself if it's what you want for breakfast (or whenever).  I like that they are low in fat and (relatively) low in calories, and I'm not bothered by the sugar level.  I wish that they didn't have high fructose corn syrup, but dang - did I mention that they're delicious? :)Facts for dry cereal (no milk):  Serving size = 3/4 cup, calories = 120, total fat = 1g (no saturated or trans fat), cholesterol = 0mg, sodium = 160mg, potassium = 40mg, total carbs = 26g (dietary fiber < 1g, sugars = 11g), protein = 2gBottom Line:If you like sugar cereals, honey, and nuts - then I highly recommend giving these a try if you can find them for about $3-$3.50 a box or less.  $5/box (the price that Amazon had last week) is a bit steep, IMO.

I am not really corn-flakes guy, but I realised that this is a good quickfix breakfast when I do not have enough time to make eggs and bread etc.this corn-flakes is sweet due to honey (and maybe sugar), which is good coz good calorie intake during breakfast is best way to start the day with energy.

After trying Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey, 10.8-Ounce (Pack of 4) and liking it, I was looking forward to trying the flake version next. Unfortunately it did not live up to my expectations. First of all, I could not believe how sweet this was! I could practically feel my teeth rotting away, and though it only has one more gram than the "O" cereal (11 grams to O's 10), it was far sweeter. Adding to the con list is that this particular cereal uses high fructose corn syrup in addition to sugar and honey and has next to no fiber at all (less than 1 gram according to the box). As for the pros, you can definitely taste the honey and hint of nut and it stays crunchy for a while. Yes, it has some vitamins and minerals, but on the whole, I will never get this again and can only eat it mixed with an unsweetened cereal. Since Crunchy Nut Golden Honey Nut, 14.1-Ounce (Pack of 4) is basically a waste of calories, I cannot recommend this unless you want a "dessert" cereal.

Wow!! This just may be my new favorite cereal! This version of Corn Flakes has a real bite to it. It maintains it's crunch all the way through the bowl. It may not be as "healthy" as other cereals but, for me, it's all about the taste. Annd this one has it!!

This cereal tastes wonderful.  It's vitamin and mineral enriched.  However, there are major drawbacks.It has almost 2.5 teaspoons of sugar in 3/4 cup of cereal with 1/2 cup of fat-free milk, and very little fiber.  A partial list of ingredients is as follows:  First is corn; 2nd sugar; 3rd peanuts; 4th honey; 5th malt flavoring; 6th molasses; 7th salt; 8th corn syrup.  The remaining 15 are colorings, vitamins, minerals, and wheat starch.  It has 20 grams of carbohydrates and  the milk adds another 6 for a total of 26 carbs.I would never consider this as part of a healthful diet for a child or adult.

column9: I Told You Not To Call Me That At Work.
column10: Let's cut to the chase.  This is Kellogg's Nut & Honey Crunch dressed in a new box.Pros----It tastes good (dry or covered in milk).It stays pretty crunchy down to the last bite.It smells honey nutty.Cons----It leaves an aftertaste in your mouth.It's not a healthy cereal.The first 6 ingredients go like this: Milled Corn, Sugar, Peanuts, Honey, Malt Flavoring, MolassesThat's a lot of sweetness!  So, I eat it as an after dinner snack/desert.In the end, me and my sweet tooth like it!NOTE: According to the coupon on the side of the box, they are also coming out with "Roasted Nut & Honey".  I'm not sure how different that will taste but something to be on the look out for.Search "80's Nut & Honey Crunch Cereal Commercial" on YouTube for the reference to my title.

My first thought upon opening this box was, "Whoa, this smells just like a box of Cracker Jack."And it did. Nutty with caramel and honey. Wasn't sure how that would taste, even thought maybe it might be a bit gross, but nope ... it was a good tasting cereal.Keep in mind, this is nothing out of the ordinary or special -- you've tasted this before -- but it's good. Regular cereal flakes slathered in sugary honey, a light dosing of nuts, and VERY crunchy. If you remember Nut & Honey cereal, you'll know this one.

Like it's counterpart Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey, Crunchy Nut Golden Honey is sweet and crunchy with a nutty flavor.  This version is in a flake form, which gives a different texture than the O's shape of the other.  The taste is similar, but somehow this one seemed sweeter to me.  The nutty flavor is good, and for a minute I recognized the taste from a childhood memory.  I had to think about it for a while, and then I remembered-- this tastes like the peanut brittle that my mother used to make when I was growing up!  While it doesn't have the same sugar levels as peanut brittle, it's peanutty sweet.  It also stays crunchy in milk.  I really liked it, but it's not something I'd buy for my kids.  They'd take one bite and never want to have regular (healthier) bran flakes again!

Supposedly, Crunchy Nut has been available in England for quite some time and Kellogg's finally decided to bring it over to US shores.  Kellogg's used to make "Nut & Honey Crunch", though it was discontinued a while ago. Like Crunchy Nut, they came in both flakes and "Os" versions. I have fond memories of eating Nut & Honey Crunch in the 80s, and missed it when it was discontinued. Remember the "Nothin' Honey" commercials? ;)Well, if you want to relive those days, give Crunchy Nut a try. To the best of my taste buds' recollection, the crunch and flavor are nearly identical. There is the sweet tang of the honey coating and satisfying texture of the peanut-sprinkled corn flakes. The flavor is comparable to frosted flakes, but with honey and nut flavors. It holds up well in milk, retaining it's crunch down to the last bite. Comparing ingredients and nutritional information from their respective boxes shows that they match up pretty closely there as well, though the serving size for N&H is 2/3 cup and for CN it is 3/4 cup. If anything, ounce for ounce, Crunchy Nut Golden Honey Nut Flakes looks a little healthier for you than Nut & Honey Crunch.That's not to say it truly healthy though. Sure, it is fortified with the usual assortment of vitamins and when eaten with milk you fill even more of your daily nutritional requirements. However, it is still laden with sugar, honey,molasses and High Fructose Corn Syrup. My taste buds must have changed a bit since the 80s because it is almost too sweet for me. Blame it on a steady diet of low sugar cereals over recent years. I would have a hard time eating this regularly first thing in the morning. Instead, I mimic a habit of my father's and eat a small bowl of it in place of dessert. You could even mix it with other cereals that contain less sugar (as my dad would do).Don't get me wrong, Crunch Nut tastes great on it's own, and if you have a sugar/crunch craving, it hits the spot. It even makes a good breading base for fried chicken. I just no longer have quite the sweet tooth I once did. I give Crunchy Nut Golden Honey Nut Flakes fives stars for flavor, mouth-feel and craving satisfaction. One star comes off for health impact though. If you decide to give it a try, I would shop around a little. Current 3rd party vendor prices are ludicrous. A much better deal can probably be found at your local grocer.

This cereal is some kind of awesome.  I usually eat Honey Bunches of Oats with Almonds, and this is every bit as good and maybe a little better.It's basically corn flakes coated in honey with chopped nuts.  Doesn't sound thrilling but it has a great flavor.It stays crispy in milk only for a few minutes before getting a little soggy, but I prefer a softer cereal anyway.  The thing that really stands out for me is the honey taste even more so than the nut taste.  It still is a great combination though.  I think they really hit a home run with this cereal and I'll probably buy more.This can also be eaten dry, as a snack, it tastes good on it's own with no milk too.  I think I may have found a new favorite cereal!  At 120 calories per serving, it fits into my diet as well.

If Frosted Flakes and Cracker Jack got together and had a baby, they would call it Crunchy Nut Cornflakes.  This cereal tastes great - it gets the thumbs up from my son who enjoys cereal enough he spends his allowance on buying boxes of his favorites.  Unfortunately, the reason it tastes so good is the high sugar content, which is why I am not giving it a rave review.  I whole-heartedly believe that one should not start the day with "dessert".  My own breakfast usually consists of oatmeal made with milk and NO sugar.  When my kids were little I refused to buy dessert cereals and even now that they are older, I encourage good eating habits.Cornflakes (plain) are one cereal I've never minded them eating and I thought this would be "cornflakes with a zing".  But, while they added in the honey and nut flavors, they also added in a bunch of sugar (it's the second ingredient listed on the box!) so rather than feel good about serving it, it's a cereal that I would reserve for a treat.So for a rating, here's my thought process.  Tastes great and good for you would be a 5.  Tastes bad and bad for you would be a 1.  Tastes great but not good for you then, would have to go somewhere in the middle.  So I've given this a 3.

Thanks Kelloggs for finally making what we Brits have known as "Crunchy Nut Cornflakes" for most of our lives (if you were born in 70s like I was) available in the US! The previous incarnation of "Honey Nut Cornflakes" simply didn't pass muster.Breakfast is saved!!

Nut 'n Honey is back! This was my favorite cereal in the 80's. They took it off the market, brought it back as Honey Nut Cornflakes, took it away again, and now brought it back. I don't know why they didn't revive the old name - it was a lot more memorable. Kellogg, please don't take it away, again.This is a very sweet cereal. It's closer to Frosted Flakes than Honey Bunches of Oats. Because it's sugar glazed it holds its crunch for the entire bowl. And the remaining milk is delicious to slurp!

The taste of honey is just too overpowering. Everywhere you crunched all you could taste was, well HONEY! There wasn't a hint of nut, toasted flakes, nothing just pure honey. Although, I liked the texture I didn't enjoy the taste.

This isn't anything really exciting and it's a lot like some other cereals on the market. It's a little sweet for me, but the kids like it.It's relatively healthy and it stays crunchy. I'll continue to buy this for the kids.

Overall, I would definitely recommend you try this one. It's a familiar flavor, but somehow different. It stays crunchy in milk. And it's appealing to all ages.Although criticized by others for sweetness, at 11 grams per serving, it's less than the typically sweet cereals. It has bits of nuts that aren't distinguishable flavor-wise by themselves, but add to the overall flavor. To me it's almost bittersweet because of the molasses undertones.My teenagers love it. In fact, my 15 year old saw the picture of this cereal while I'm reviewing it and told me "hey, I love that cereal."My husband didn't love it. But I'm sure he would eat it if he was hungry. He's generally very picky.I will be buying it again for my family. (Vine gave me one for free, but everyone ate it before I could get a bowl, so I bought a couple more boxes). There's another "Os" version that is good as well.

column9: Pretty good though nothing really new
column10: This cereal is pretty good, though it really tastes a lot like Honey Bunches of Oats and, consequently isn't really a new market in the cereal industry.  I gave it three stars because in addition to the lack of originality I had hoped for, I found it a bit sweet for my tastes.  My two kids, however, liked it - neither is overly accustomed to sweet cereals so maybe I am overly sensitive to the sweetness in this box.If you like Honey Bunches of Oats, you will probably like this (though this one has slightly less crunch to it).  As I said, it is "okay" but I probably won't purchase it again unless maybe I have a great coupon.

column9: ANOTHER TASTY TREAT, BUT NOTHING NEW HERE EITHER!
column10: I enjoy cereal and this cereal is like most sugar coated flakes of goodness. It's not going to win any points for originality, but it is a tasty little treat. It's like Frosted Flakes with some added sugar and nut fragments sprinkled on top....at least this time they stole a cereal profile from their own company. ;-D  I've seen this cereal much cheaper at Wal-Mart than the prices on line, so if you're looking to give it a try, buy it there.

column9: No Need to Belabor the Point ...
column10: ...these are REALLY good. I love cold cereal (okay, I also love hot cereal) and sometimes nothing hits the spot like a bowl of corn flakes. I usually like the plain ones (A&P's house brand, which I suspect is made by Nestlé, is a favorite) and add my own sugar but I couldn't resist trying Kellogg's Crunchy Nut flakes when they were offered and I'm glad I did. They're sweet without being cloying, somehow manage to stay crisp in the bowl (maybe the glaze works like armor?), and the peanut presence (crunch/flavor) was a unique and tasty addition. Granted, this isn't going to appeal to the health-conscious crowd but for what it is--mainstream cold cereal--it's very satisfying and well worth sampling if you like cornflakes and peanuts. And BTW, it makes for nice snacking out of hand without the milk, too. :)
This did not really have a memerable flavor, it was  bland and I would not purchase it again..PRefer the Special K cereals top this/

column9: Typical, overly-sweet , nutritionally void American breakfast cereal
column10: This cereal is nothing special among American breakfast cereals. It is quite sweet, very crunchy and seems more of a dessert topping than an actual healthy way to start your day.If you want to begin your day with a lot of crunchy and highly-sugared dry cereal...this is the product for you.But- do not expect this to be an item that will be healthy and provide well for you nutritionally.

column4: B. Williams ""We must be the change we wi...
column10: This might be better as an ice cream topping than as a cereal. The nutritional content of this is pretty poor, it's very sweet, and really not all that nutty.  the protein of the nuts doesn't even register in the nutrition. You're better off with Honey Nut Cheerios, IMO.  This is just another spin-off of the other sugared, flake cereals.
Crunchy sweet flakes cereal. Though a bit too sweet, ala sugar frosted flakes. The texture is good and holds in milk.

column9: cracker jack "candy in a box" cereal...very little nutritional value
column10: This is basically glazed cornflakes (instead of frosted, which is powdery-looking) with a hint of peanut sprinkled atop. The glaze has a nice caramel-molasses flavor that is maybe a little too sweet for me, but fine for other people, and mixed with the subtle peanut flavor, it really does taste like just like Cracker Jack. All it's missing is the prize!Nutritionally, like many other candy-in-a-box cereals, this one isn't so great, with only 2% of your daily value in fiber (less than 1g), 11g of sugars, and 9% of your daily value in carbs (26g). Fortified with some vitamins, it has a slight nutritional value of 10% vitamins A, C, and D, 0% calcium, and 25% Iron, Thiamin, Riboflavin, Niacin, B6, Folic Acid, and B12, but if it's vitamins you wanted in the first place, you'd probably look elsewhere.It's a nice snack if you like Cracker Jack, but I wouldn't call it a wholesome breakfast food.

This is basically sweeten corn flakes with peanuts added. They're okay and I'll probably eat them, but there's really nothing special about them.  A repackaging of flavors Kellogg's already has.  Very sweet, so if you like that sort of thing, you'll probably enjoy it.

An old favourite, that is finally going to be available in the US.This cereal is very much a Frosted Flakes type cornflake with a hint of honey flavour and shredded peanuts in the glaze. The peanut is very finely shredded and a roughly the size of finely-shredded coconut.  This small size enables it to be evenly distributed onto the cornflakes with the glaze.  The overall effect is a tasty honey-scented sweet cornflake that is extra crunchy and slightly peanuty. [See photos above]However, my SO was quite disappointed when opening the bag to not find whole, half or at least long pieces of crushed peanut, although there was a strong peanut scent. He had expected a nut & cornflake version of Raisin Bran.
I loved the taste of this new cereal. Honey-sprinkled, crunchy nut flakes. Its like frosted flakes only with honey. Would strongly recommend to anyone who loves a good cereal.

Crunchy Nut Golden Honey Nut cereal from Kellogg's is really yummy! It's all flakes that are shiny with sugar and nut granules. The nuts in the cereal are peanuts - and I love peanuts. Because of the sugar coating, it stays crunchy longer than some flake cereals. It's sweeter than I'd like, but the statistics are quite good, even so. 120 calories with only 1 gram of fat per serving. On the negative side, there are 11 grams of sugar and less than one gram of fiber. I often mix sweet cereals with others and this one would be a good choice for that. This is a very tasty new cereal for Kellogg's that I'm happy to recommend.

column9: Sickly Sweet.... The  Same Old Same Old
column10: There is nothing new about this sickly sweet cereal. It may be slightly more crunchy than other similar cereals but overloading it with sugar in lieu of real taste just does not work!Even my kids didn't like it. They had about the same opinion as me, little taste, way too sweet.I don't know who Kellogs think they are kidding with this product! It is not worth trying, their old staple Corn Flakes are way better!

column9: Just sugared Corn Flakes with nut dust on them
column10: I presumed two things about the name of this cereal:  1) there would be nuts in it, and 2) the nuts would make it crunchy.  Hmmm...not so much.Yes, they are crunchy, but that's from the thick layer of sugar coating on the flakes - and, they're just regular corn flakes.  But, it also makes it very sweet.  My teeth hurt eating this cereal it has so much sugar on it.Nuts?  Not in my bowl of cereal there weren't.  It appears that they covered the flakes with a mixture of sugar and nut dust and that's about all the nuts you're going to get in this cereal.  Unless they forgot to put the nuts in my box, you won't be finding any in yours either.Thumbs down because the last thing we need is another sugary cereal, because it's not new as the box implies, and because there are no nuts in it.

Kellogg's Crunchy nut cereal consists of Cornflakes that have been doused in a honey-sugar combo and sprinkled with very small pieces of chopped peanuts. They taste exactly like they sound -- a mostly honey-flavored variation of Cornflakes. In other words, they taste a lot like Frosted Flakes. The peanuts add very little taste-wise, and the pieces are so small that I can't imagine they contribute much in terms of protein (a serving size has 2 grams of protein). Crunchy Nut is fine but not really very distinctive.

Don't get me wrong, the cereal tastes "good"--in a bowl, or on its own; it's just that I couldn't really taste any peanuts.  No, I don't think the product is mislabeled (peanuts are the third most prevalent ingredient), just that the pieces of nuts are so small, and the honey so at the forefront of the taste that the peanut taste is completely overpowered.  (I only remember one bite that I thought I tasted something.)Is this a bad thing? Maybe not.  If they added a bunch more peanuts the caloric and fat content would go through the roof, and, as it stands now it has the same calories as a regular sugar cereal --don't let the name fool you-- it is every bit as sugary as Frosted Flakes.  You just can't see it because the honey is transparent.The cereal is also pretty sweet tasting... maybe too much for me, as I was expecting more of a Chex mix type cereal with very mildly sweet taste and nuts.  Sugar, however, is the second most prevalent ingredient, and honey, molasses, and high fructose corn syrup are in there, too.  Not a healthy cereal, per se, but not terribly unhealthy, either.  Decent but not great.  I think I would have liked it better if they doubled the nuts and cut the sugar in half.

No mushy flakes here, these keep their crunch to the bottom of the bowl.  They're  much more substantial tasting than corn flakes, and with the addition of fruit, I believe they make a healthy breakfast, DESPITE the sugar they contain. (They contain 11g of sugar, by the way, which is less than some bran cereals with raisins.)A side note: a few years ago, I read a study that said kids and adults who use unsweetened cereals actually end up eating more sugar, because they add so much of their own from the sugar bowl.Back to the taste: I didn't find anything particularly "nutty" tasting about the flakes. I could see the small, peanut flecks on each flake, but the taste didn't come through. Still, that didn't detract from the product at all, for me.Overall, I enjoyed these very much, and would recommend giving them a try.

This is a "NEW" cereal from Kellog's.The cereal tastes great but it doesn't break any new ground.There are other cereals out there that taste almost exactly the same as this one (For example, Honey Bunches of Oats by Post).Between the Kellog's version and the Post version I'd buy whichever is cheaper at the time.

I got this today and started eating it right out of the box as a treat - Yes, it's that good :)Later, I put it in a cereal bowl with sliced bananas, blueberries and whole milk and it was excellent.  Sweet, but not too sweet.  At least not for me!I stopped eating regular corn flakes years ago because it was so bland tasting and because it got milk-logged and mushy in the bowl. This Crunchy Nut cereal did not do that. I truly liked it and it will be on my shelf as a breakfast food and/or a late night snack!I would give it a try!

This was a sweet - exceedingly sweet cereal which in truth is just cornflakes with a few peanut crumbs glazed onto the flakes.  Thye do not hold up well to milk and go soggy very fast.  My 6 and 9 year old thought thay made a great treat but I would NEVER consider this nutrition.  At a guess sugar makes up 35-40% of product. 26 carbs a serving.Save yourself the money - the nuts are not tastable so buy cornflakes -a much better buy for weight and pour on all the sugar you want if that is what you are after - same result better savings.

column9: Yummy in a not too peanuty way
column10: I'm not a peanut maniac, so it was with trepidation that I opened up the box. An almost overpowering smell hit me at once, something that a peanut lover would appreciate but someone who was kind of on the fence about it would not. Suffice to say, the end product wasn't too peanutcentric. It's actually a perfect balance of sweetness and peanut taste without any huge peanut chunks. This isn't the most original cereal in the world as I'm sure there has to have been at least two or three that are similar to this. Still, I'd recommend this one to anyone looking for a cereal that fits perfectly in between a healthier type of cereal and some chocolate sugar frosted bomb atrocity that would have your kids and probably you bouncing off the wall like some speed freak on a bender. Fans of Corn Flakes, Honey Nut Cheerios and Oh's! cereals would do well to search this product out.

This answers my need at breakfast to have something tasty and at the same time good for me.I love corn flakes but always needed to put sugar on them for a little extra flavor.  This cereal takes care of that.  The honey, malt, molasses, and best of all, peanuts combine for a terrific and satisfying bowl of goodness.It even tastes good enough to eat without milk, but tastes great with milk and added fruit, bananas being one of my favorites.Push away from the drive-up window and have a bowl of this in the morning - tastes good, and better for you!

This is a pretty good tasting cereal but it is sweet beyond all get-out.  It is so sweet that it completely overpowers the nut flavors.  I get just a hint of malt through the sweetness.The best plan is to eat this with a cup of coffee by your side so you can take a sip every now and then to counteract the sugar and honey taste.11 grams of sugar doesn't seem like much, but when the company adds in honey plus molasses it hits the taste buds with sledgehammer subtleness.  Give it a try if you like sweet.AD2

I had pictured these cereals quite differently than what it really is. I am quite disappointed to find that:1) nuts are only peanuts2) I need magnifying glass to see the real peanuts3) cereal is very sweet4) a bowl of cereal and milk is not at all fillingThere is so much sugar (honey) that the flakes glisten. It is as crunchy as Kellog's corn flakes. They don't get soggy as quickly though - probably the sugar coating delays the process.Serving size is 3/4 cup and has 120 calories, 2% fat, 7% sodium, and 11g sugars. Ingredients (in order) are corn, sugar, peanuts, honey, and so on. As you can see there is more sugar than peanuts!In contrast, regular Kellog corn flakes serving size is 1 cup and has 100 calories, 0 fat, 8% sodium and 2g sugars.We will definitely not buy these cereals.

column9: WAY too sweet: Like eating Cracker Jacks with milk
column10: I'm giving this more than one star only because eating Cracker Jacks in a bowl with milk may sound like heaven to you. Personally, I think this cereal is wayyyyyyyyyy too sweet. Here are the ingreds. in order of highest content:1. Milled corn (think Cracker Jacks)2. Sugar (ditto)3. Peanuts (ditto)4. Honey (more sugar)5. Malt flavoring6. Molasses (more sugar)7. Salt8. High Fructose Corn Syrup (you know . . . sugar)It is deceptive because it says it only contains 11 g of sugar per serving. However, a serving is only 3/4 cup. I actually measured this out today, and trust me, I will be looking for something else (a doughnut?!!!) in about an hour, and if you stick with the serving size, you will be, too.  3/4 cup is probably about 6 spoonfuls. And then you're done.This is so much like candy I can actually feel it cementing itself to my teeth. So if you give this to your kids, make sure they brush brush brush (and floss).They've managed to fortify this with some vitamins (although not a whole lot), so is this better than skipping breakfast? Probably. But could/should you find a healthier alternative? Definitely.

Tasty, addictive, sweet -- new Kellogg's Crunchy Nut Golden Honey Nut cereal is delicious breakfast food, but it isn't a health food. The front of the box does not say it is. The description is  "golden flakes of corn drizzled with honey and topped with real peanuts." (That word "real" seems unnecessary.)It is obvious that the Kellogg people know how good it is. Here's what the back of the package says: "With the perfect blend of sweet and nutty in every crunchy bite, Kellogg's Crunch Nut Cereal is so delicious you won't want to wait until tomorrow to eat it. Luckily, you don't have to. It's morning somewhere."I like it as a topping on my healthy oatmeal.

column9: It's Morning Somewhere: Better Eating Than Reading
column10: When I first saw the jacket photo of this book, I was intrigued by the subtitle/teaser line "It's Morning Somewhere."  A pensive, philosophical, thought-provoking line.  So imagine my disappointment when the package arrived, and there was no book anywhere to be found... instead, the box was nearly full of what appeared to be sweet-smelling packing flakes.After also fruitlessly searching for any instruction manual for the product, I was trying to decide what to do next when my daughter came in, gave me a withering look as only a teenager can, and (indicating the picture on the front of the box, showing the packing flakes in a bowl with milk) suggested I just try EATING some.To my astonishment, this proved very successful.  The flakes had a sweet, nutty taste rather like my grandmother's peanut brittle from when I was a kid.  The peanutty taste was not really overpowering, and while they WERE noticeably sweet, the sweetness was also not excessive.  While I like peanuts and peanut butter, peanut-flavored items like peanut butter cookies are not my personal favorite.  Even so, I enjoyed the sweet-nuttiness of this stuff enough to have another bowl or two over the next few days, with just as good results.  I think anyone who particularly enjoys peanut-flavored confections (peanut cookies, peanut candies) would enjoy this product even more than I did.I might also mention that I only got to have a total of two or three bowls of the interesting flakes myself, because my wife and kids proceeded to devour them with great enthusiasm, declaring them yummy.

I am in awe of the reviewers who were able to see - much less taste - the nuts in Kellogg's Golden Honey Nut Crunchy Nut cereal.  They must have far better palates than I do, because to me these taste exactly like Frosted Flakes, if Frosted Flakes used honey.  Were I blindfolded, I wouldn't be able to tell you that there were supposed to be nuts in this cereal at all.  In fact, a blindfold wouldn't be needed given how tiny the peanut pieces are. For a cereal that has the word "nut" in it's name twice, I expected more.Overall, this cereal is fine.  Frosted Flakes (its closest cousin) are the sweet sibling of Corn Flakes, one of the most classic cereals out there.  It's hard to go totally wrong with that type of lineage. Still, it's hardly nutty, and given that's its claim to fame, I can't recommend it.

column9: A challenger to Post Honey Bunches of Oats
column10: Kellog's Crunchy Nut Golden Honey Nut cereal is (at least it seems to be that it is) designed to be a competitor of Post's Honey Bunches of Oats. This is a good cereal with a slightly stronger taste than the Post cereal, but it is close enough to be of interest to fans of the Post cereal.

column9: Crunchy, nutty and sweet, loved by kids and adults!
column10: This is a crunchy, nutty and sweet cereal, loved by kids and adults. It is sweet but NOT too sweet, you do not have to mix it with other non-sweet cereals. You can eat it like mini-cookies without milk or eat it as breakfast mixed with milk.On the top of the box, you can find some nutrition facts: 120 calories, 11g sugars, 160 mg (7%) sodium, with 10% vitamin C and 10% vitamin D, 1g (2%) total fat per serving.

column4: Penny Pinching Polly "Check out my website fo...
column10: This cereal isn't great, but it's not horrible either.  I prefer Honey Bunches of Oats Honey Roasted, 48-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 2).  Even though the cereal was well within it's "Best By" date, it tasted stale to me.  If you want a crunchy, nutty cereal with a bit of honey, stick with Honey Bunches of oats.
I really liked this cereal. it was crunchy and not too sweet! it kind of reminds me of honey bunches of oats

column9: Definitely a new one of my favorites
column10: I tried this cereal from Amazon and got hooked pretty instantly.  It's got a lot of crunch and doesn't get soggy as similar cereals, and it's on the sweeter end of "adult" cereals but isn't too sweet.  I can buy this to settle my urge for a more sugary cereal normally marketed to children, and not face embarrassment at the checkout stand when the cashier asks about my kids and I give them a sort of, "whaaaaaaat?!" look and demand a paternity test.It also has a nice honey flavor instead of fake-fruit or fake-chocolate.  It might be fake-honey too but at least it tastes more like the real deal.  There are a good ratio of nuts to flakes so there shouldn't be any major disappointment there.  How much more can I say about a breakfast cereal?  It's good!  It's good enough to add to your rotation.
Very tasty and super crunchy. This box disappeared the first morning and I was luck to get a cup full. My picky daughters decimated the box and they're dainty little things. It was a big hit.
Crunchy Nut Golden Honey cereal is yummy! The flakes are honey tasting and golden with nut clusters. I love this cereal and have purchased it several times since first trying it. 5/5 stars!!

Oh my gosh these are so good. They are really crunchy so they don't get soggy too fast, and they are sweet without being too sugary like a Frosted Flakes product can be. It's not like there are a ton of nuts, just a few little pieces now and then, which is perfect for my taste.

I love cereal.  And I especially love the honey flake cereals.  I haven't found one yet that rate 5 stars, but I'd say Crunchy Nut Golden Honey Nut came pretty darn close.With it having "crunchy" in the title, I expected it to hold up a little longer under milk.  And while it did seem to stay crunchy longer than similar types, it just didn't quite live up to the expectations associated with its name.The nut clusters are smaller than other like cereals, but it did not distract from the taste.Overall, I'd say that Kellogg's Crunchy Nut will find it's way onto my shopping list quite regularly.

column9: First flake cereal to stay crunchy for me!
column10: I have never been one to like "flake" cereals much.  Most of the time, the flakes are nothing more than soggy, limp pieces 5 minutes after pouring milk on them.  But this cereal was much different.  The flakes really stayed crunchy and the taste was wonderful.

I don't ordinarily eat cereal since I despise milk. However, certain cereals I love to munch on as a snack. I really loved the honey part-it was very sweet without overkill. LOVE the nuts, it always adds something extra to anything you are eating. Overall it has a great texture, not too hard and not too mushy.  Like I said, not sure how it all tastes with milk, though my husband ate it and had no complaints.
Nice and crunchy and very delicious!The flavor is enjoyable, similar to corn flakes but just a little nuttier and sweeter.It also does a good job of keeping you full until lunch time.

This is an ok new cereal. It tastes like a corn flake with honey and peanuts. I think it would be much better with either strawberries or blueberries. On it's own it was kind of blah. For me, there are too many other cereals that I like that are much more nutritious.

I really enjoy this cereal, but I prefer it as a mix-in to other things, such as yogurt. Alone, it was a little sweeter than I usually eat, but mixing it in balanced everything just right. The slivers of peanuts are visible on each flake. Yum!

I'm not too adventurous with my cereal choices, but I was drawn to this when I saw it at the grocery, and picked it up from Amazon.  It reminds me of Frosted Flakes, though a bit crunchier, and with a nuttier honey taste.  Like Frosted Flakes, it gets soggy fast in milk, so I tried to pour small bowls (and go back for more if I wanted it).We have continued to purchase this product, and it generally gets eaten right away.  I guess that's a good thing, but it's pretty sweet, so it may not be the "healthiest" choice out there.  Check the nutrition info and judge for yourself, I guess.Overall, I recommend you give it a try, if you like Frosted Flakes, or nutty cereals, or just enjoy trying something new.  (There is also a Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey, 10.8-Ounce (Pack of 4) variety, but we haven't tried that one yet...)

This cereal is plenty crunchy, but I'm shocked by the people saying it tastes good.  I found it to be bland, with a little bit of a nasty aftertaste.  I don't know how they managed bland and nasty at the same time, but they did.  I had two bowls, just to make sure my first opinion wasn't off in some way, but then I threw the box out.

Packaging: The packaging for this product was hassle-free, easy to open, and reasonable given the amount of product supplied.Product quality: The taste of Kellogg's Crunchy Nut cereal was very pleasing, but a bit on the sweet side. The texture was crunchy, but this did change over time in milk of course as one would expect.Overall impression: I highly recommend this cereal to someone with a sweet tooth who is not overly concerned with the health effects of a high sugar content in their breakfast.

column9: Great taste but gets soggy fast in milk
column10: I love this cereal but unless I eat it real fast, it doesn't stay crunchy for very long.  I know, there are very few cereals that stay crunchy and thats okay, but this one states on the box that it is crunchy and I cant stop it from getting at least a little soggy in 5 minutes.In fairness to the cereal, it has a great flavor and my family loves it.  I just want it to stay crunchy a little longer thats all.

We are a big cereal family around here and Crunchy Nut golden Honey really hit the spot.Within 72 hours of its arrival the boys and the family polished off the whole box, what wasn't eaten as a breakfast was munched on as a snack.This is a very good sign for a cereal there are plenty of choices out there so often one is the same as the other.  This one is not.Price wise it's a tad iffy.  but if will pay the extra buck for the box your taste buds will thank you.

column9: Pretty Good, But Best as a Snack
column10: Recently, I got a box of this cereal.  Thought I would try it, because it seemed somewhat healthier than most cereals out there.  After my first taste, I realized it was a bit too sweet for breakfast.  But it does make a pretty good snack!  So, maybe not great for breakfast, but definitely better than munching on more fattening foods throughout the day.  Perhaps not what Kelloggs originally wanted as a marketing plan for this product, but I bet it would work: "Snack on Crunchy Oat!"

I don't know if it was because I had just come off a no sugar diet, but these were very sweet.  The peanut flavor is very noticable. My family enjoyed this cereal and the 2 boxes were gone in as many weeks.  I don't think I will buy these only because of the sugar content.

column9: You might like it; I didn't
column10: Reviewing food is always a dicey thing because taste varies so much from one person to another.  So whether I like or dislike something is irrelevant to whether you will.That said, I couldn't finish the first bowl of this cereal that I tried.  It wasn't that it was gross or disgusting or anything; it simply didn't appeal to my pallette.Maybe your experience would be different.

column9: Everyone in the family liked it, but we seemed to tire of it fairly soon
column10: This cereal has a good taste. Crunchy, as advertised. A taste of honey, again as advertised. Everyone in my family liked it. When we were done with this one, we bought the companion cereal and tried it too. It too was good.But we seemed to tire of the cereal fairly soon. We're back to our old favorites already. This one just did not make the cut.

My husband loves these. I think they are just ok. They are reminiscent of Frosted Flakes only much crunchier and they didnt get soggy in milk which is a plus for me. The thing I didnt like was that with each bite the taste of peanut butter got stronger and stronger. This wasnt a problem for my hubby. My 8 year old liked them but went back to her kid cereals and only ate them once. My husband finished the whole box in a few days so I would buy them again but only for him. I couldnt get my mind off of feeling like I was eating Skippy with milk.

column9: So glad they are here but pricey
column10: After quite a few years living here in the US this was my favourite cereal that I missed from the UK. Friends and relatives would bring me it over when they visited. Very very tasty !Although I must say it is also widely available in the grocery stores now so after paying over $20 for 4 boxes from Amazon  I then discovered them at my local store for $2.86 each or a special 2 for $5 so I paid over double !
GREAT TASTING. CRUNCH LASTS. IDEAL WITH OR WITHOUT MILK, FOR BREAKFAST OR SNACKING IN FRONT OF THE TV. GOOD ALTERNATIVE FOR POPCORN.
This cereal was great! It held it's crunch to the last and final bite. It was just the right sweetness and without lots of artificial junk. Good job on this one, Kellogg's!

column9: Best for those who love honey.
column10: They are ok. We (me and the family) were not as wild about them as we thought we might be at first. They definitely are crunchy, I will give them that.Perhaps it's because they are basically just corn flakes with a new twist on the taste. They do a nice job of distributing the nuts throughout. They are able to get the peanuts into each bite because they seem to stick to the corn flakes, which makes sense. If it was any other way, they would just sink to the bottom of the box.I prefer the taste of the frosted corn flakes a bit more over the honey. I guess it's just a different kind of sweetness. But I believe that for those who's favorite cereals are ones with honey flavors in them, they should try this out, since I think they would be perfect for them!

column9: You'd Have To Be NUTS Not To Like Them
column10: I like just plain ol' Cornflakes, so I did dig these.  Basically they're honey glazed Cornflakes with tiny bits of chopped nuts on them.  I'm sure you can envision that, so judge accordingly.

Absolutely delicious cereal!  It's my new favorite and the kids liked it also.  While it doesn't appear to be especially good for you, it is at least average as far as calories and nutritious content goes.  I tried the same cereal that comes in "O" shapes and did not like it at all.  In the flake form though - hands down the tastiest cold cereal I've had in a long time.

This new cereal by Kellogg's is comparable to Honey Bunches of Oats in shape and texture.  While not off-putting, this cereal takes a sweetness flavor to the max.  Some will find it too much; others might enjoy it.  Also, I'm kind of surprised Kellogg's used high fructose corn syrup in a new cereal, given the current stigma of that additive.  This flavor is okay, but I recommend the Roasted Honey Nut first.

This is sweeter honey coated version of Kelloggs Cornflakes,  It was more sweet than nutty,  you get very little nutty taste, it is overwhemled by the honey coating.  It would be great if it had more nuts since it will help increase the "Crunchy" texture.  It does not stay Crunchy long, like regular cornflakes it becomes very soluble after three minutes.I would recommend eating it with any unsweetened milk, or you will be getting an extremely sweetened concentrated milk when you finish the cereal.  I like drinking the left over milk and it was just gaggingly sweet when you use vanilla or chocolate milk.  I tried it with Fat free, 1%, 2%, chocolate and whole cow's milk.  I also tried it with Soy Milk (vanilla, unsweetened, chocolate), Rice drink (vanilla and Plain), and Almond milk (vanilla, chocolate, and Plain).  It tastes the best with plain almond milk, you get a better nutty flavor and the honey coating mixes well with the milk.Plain dry "Crunchy Nut" cereal makes me cough so I think it would be hard to make this into a portable dry snack. I would definitely recommend this cereal to a sugar junkie, but the honey coating is too sweet for me.
I got this cereal on a whim, and was actually surprised by how good it was.  My kids keep asking for more!

This is a good cereal, but relatively high in sugar. Of course my girls enjoyed it because it is sweet. Taste and consistency similar to frosted corn flakes. It is, after all, toasted cornflakes -- of course with nuts. If you like sweet cereals and don't mind the extra calories of the higher sugar, the taste is good. If you are looking for a lower sugar alternative, good old Product 19 from Kellogs is far healthier. If you are looking for flakes and nuts I would recommend one of higher fiber alternatives like Kirkland Signature Cinnamon Pecan which is also available on Amazon.

column9: Misleading photo but still very tasty!
column10: My kids really enjoy this cereal probably because it so sweet. If you have had Nut & Honey Crunch, it tastes very similar.The image on the box shows each piece coated in nut flakes, far from accurate! You will find a few nut flakes on most of the corn flakes, some with none at all.The cereal stays crunchy for a decent amount of time in milk and is very satisfying to eat.I have't tried them but I imagine these would be a good coating for adding crunch to foods that can handle a sweet flavor. Perhaps over salmon, chicken, sweet potato casserole, etc.

Our family liked Kellogg's crunchy nut cereal very much for that extra crunchy feeling with a coating of nuts on the top and it was not too sweet. It was tasty like the other kellogg's brand cereals even more crunchy than their own cereals. Kids can eat as a morning cereal or as a snack even. I wish they had mixed some other nuts, other flavors or dried nuts to even taste more good. I think anyone would like this cereal. Its worth trying once and see if you like it too.

I really liked Kellogg's Crunchy Nut Cereal. It has a nice honey taste, but isn't overpoweringly sweet like Frosted Flakes. At the risk of repeating the obvious, it has a sweet nutty taste and is nicely crunchy. It makes for a very satisfying breakfast.I usually don't bother with milk in my cereal, but I tried a bowl and it was great. Some cereals get soggy very fast, but this one stayed crunchy long enough for me to finish the bowl.I was hoping to have a few more bowls so I could write a more detailed review, but my wife and kids polished off the box too quickly. That in itself is an endorsement. :)

I really enjoyed this cereal and am looking forward to buying more.  They're corn flakes with a hint of honey and roasted nut sweetness and crunchiness.  I had also tried the Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey, the ones shaped like 'O's and that had much more of a roasted peanut taste which wasn't what I was looking for in a cereal, although if you're a real peanut lover it would be right up your alley.  For just a bit of honey/roasted nut taste I highly recommend the flakes.
Liked the taste and they held up well in milk. I also tried the other variety, Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey, 10.8-Ounce (Pack of 4), which I preferred  by an edge.

. . . to this new cereal from Kellog's.  Five of my children devoured the box within 2 days.  Four really enjoyed it; one was "so-so" -- hence the four stars.From a father's perspective, the response was good enough for me to go to the store and actually purchase it again.  For a review of a food item -- that spells success!

column9: how nutty and sweet do you want to be?
column10: After hearing that this cereal has been a long-time favorite in England, I was eager to give it a try.Kellogg's Crunchy Nut - Golden Honey Nut does have a lot of flavor in every bite - you can taste the honey and nuts, in good balance. Make no mistake, this may not be the full-on sugar taste of Frosted Flakes, but this is a sweet-tasting cereal.I was surprised to read afterwards that the nuts are actually peanuts, because there certainly isn't a strong peanut flavor. But people with peanut allergies be warned!I'm one who likes my cereal a bit healthier and less-sweet, though. If you compare this to plain, unsweetened Cheerios, at the same 3/4-cup serving size you're getting 50% more calories (120 vs. 80). It would take 3 teaspoons of sugar to equal that with the Cheerios!Although it stays crispy, Kellogg's Crunchy Nut does get soggy fairly quickly, which is not my taste.So I guess the question is - when choosing your first meal of the day - how nutty and sweet do you want to be?

When you open the package of this cereal, you can definitely smell a nutty aroma.  The flakes are light, sweet, and nutty, and stand up pretty well to milk.  The flavor is both sweet and nutty, though not overly so.  I feel it is definitely different than what is already out there.  If you like nutty, sweet cereal, this is a good one to try!

column9: A wonderful, crispy and flavorful breakfast treat
column10: This product isn't anything like I thought... it is so much better.  I had anticipated a heavy peanut flavor, but it appears that the peanut honey coating is there to help keep the cereal crispy in milk for a longer period of time.  No sugar is required as the honey gives you just the right amount of sweetness.  The flakes stay nice and crispy for the entire eating process (unless you are playing in-between or working the morning crossword puzzle).  The taste combination is fantastic.  I remember a similar product from some years back, also made by Kellogs that was named something like "Nut and Honey".  While they were similar, this product doesn't have the heavy nut of the heavy honey flavor from the older product.  Instead, it provides a very smooth mix that makes for a very pleasant breakfast experience.  I recommend this product.

My girls love trying out new breakfast cereals, and we go through three to five boxes of cold cereal each week.  They were excited about this one, since it smells sooo yummy.  But the first bowls that I poured went uneaten (I was a good sport and choked mine down) and they've never reached for it again.  I'm personally surprised that Kellog's thought a cereal covered in peanuts would be a good idea in this day & age, what with fatal peanut allergies springing up everywhere. That's not my problem, though.  My problem is simply that the cereal is not good.  It is horrifyingly sickly-sweet!  Although the flakes do stay crispy in milk for a good long time (this might be part of the problem... a little bland mushiness would be welcome), this cereal is too sweet to stomach.  And the aftertaste is no improvement.  As my 7 year old daughter remarked, very accurately, "It smells better than it tastes."  This box of cereal tastes exactly like a Payday bar.  Maybe there's an audience out there of people who were already going to eat candy for breakfast, but I would rather not.  Skip this one.

column9: Isn't this just "Nut N Honey Crunch?"
column10: I used to love Kellogg's Nut N Honey Crunch as a kid. When I tasted this cereal, my first thought was, "Oh my! They've repackaged Nut N Honey Crunch!" Because that's essentially what this is. Granted, I haven't had that cereal in over a decade. But I'm pretty sure that this is that old cereal, repackaged.And since I loved that cereal, I really liked this. Over the years my tastes have changed a bit, so this struck me as a bit too sweet, but still delicious.
Looks like frosted flakes but tastes betterIt just a yummy crunchy cerealProbably not too good for you but when we eat sugared cereals we don't expect health foodWorth buying

This is my first time trying these they are very tasty and I would recommend them. That being said, if you are trying to loose weight or simply watching your diet you probably wont want to eat too much of these outside of occasional use it not for the health-conscious. The young ones and even my husband enjoys these they are very very yummy even to eat dry as a snack.

For those who grew up with Kellog's Corn Flakes and still like them, Crunchy Nut Golden Honey Nut provide an alternative that avoids one of the faults of its long standing predecessor:  this cereal does not get soggy in less that five minutes!  Despite the "Golden Honey" title, this is not a super-sweet kids cereal that will give you sugar shock with every bite.  It is tasty, has the flavor of real cereal and not sugar coated cardboard, and is an enjoyable morning eat.

column9: Crispy, sweet cereal with a nutty taste
column10: I have always loved sweet cereals growing up. As an adult, I still have a kid-like love for certain cereals. Frosted Flakes, however, was not on my checklist of cereals that I loved growing up. Kellogs now introduces Crunchy Nut, which, in my opinion is a modified version of Frosted Flakes which add nut bits onto the flakes. So if you love Frosted Flakes, there is no reason why you would not like this brand of cereal. Stay crunchy in milk and sweetens the milk as you go. There is nothing entirely new or original here, but its tasty and you wont be disappointed.

Kellogg's Crunchy Nut cereal doesn't come packaged as a kids' breakfast item, but it sure was a hit with the under-10 crowd in my house.  One bowl revealed the reason why:  it bears a striking resemblance to Frosted Flakes.  The crunchy nut aspect of the cereal comes from tiny nut bits on the flakes themselves, not from any sort of separate clusters.  For that reason, their appearance is actually hit-or-miss from bite to bite.  However, that sweetness is in every spoonful, and if you're not searching for a lot of that flavor, then this may not be the cereal for you.  It's strange to me that the box gives the impression of a wholesome, possibly even healthy cereal and yet the taste is pure kids' Saturday morning treat.

Our whole family enjoyed this new cereal.  It's very tasty and not overly sweet, which is a big plus for me.  Sweet enough for my kids to like.  Crunchy, satisfying and delicious.  I realize there are a lot more healthy cereals out there, but getting my kids to eat Kashi is an impossibility.  If you want something refreshing and new, try this.  It is yummy!

This is your typical corn flake cereal with small peanut chunks on them.  It is a good balance of nuts to cereal, and what makes it stand out is a nice hint of molasses.  It is about 1/3 sugar, so it is a little on the high side, but similar in sugar content to Honey Nut Cheerios.

column9: High School Favorite Makes a Comeback in Disguise
column10: In high school I found my perfect cereal. It was sweet enough to satisfy my sweet tooth, it sated my desire for cornflakes and, as an added bonus, it had peanuts. That cereal was called Nut & Honey Crunch. I used to buy it in bulk and sometimes, when I felt like mixing things up a bit I'd add some Rice Chex.And all of a sudden Nut & Honey Crunch was no longer on the grocery store shelves. I missed it. Then this came along and I decided to give it a shot. The first time I tasted it, Nut & Honey Crunch came to mind moments before I did a little happy dance. It has fewer peanuts and is not as sweet, but it's close and gives me a similar flavor when I mix it with Rice Chex.Since I prefer my cereal a bit on the squishier side, I like to let it sit for about 5 minutes first to soften up the flakes and flavor the milk (yes, I'm a slurp the milk from the bowl kinda gal), but it still stayed relatively crunchy while I ate.Now, if you're watching your caloric intake or are trying to maintain a healthy diet, I'd be more inclined to call this cereal dessert rather than a wholesome nutritious breakfast, so it should definitely be consumed in moderation.Note: Watch the price because it may be (much) more cost effective to purchase directly from the grocer.

column9: Sweet & crunchy, but not a great breakfast cereal
column10: I like cold breakfast cereal and usually have four to five different boxes in the kitchen cabinet most of the time.  I also like the flavor of peanuts, so I figured this product would be worth trying.The flakes reminded me of Kellogg's Frosted Flakes -- very crisp, very sweet.  I tried it with milk for the first time for breakfast. I found the flavor of peanuts at breakfast was not very enjoyable.  The next day, I tried eating some as a snack, right out of the box.  It was in the late afternoon.  As a snack at this time of day, the product was far more enjoyable.  I also tried it sprinkled on vanilla ice cream, which was good.The combination of ultra sweetness and peanuts didn't work for me early in the morning.  But thinking of it as a snack and using it apart from its traditional intent, I found it tasty and satisfying.

Though not a picky eater at all, I am fairly choosy when it comes to my cereal. I like low calories and sugar, high protein and fiber, and a great taste. For a sweetened cereal (great for a dessert at night) 11g of sugar isn't too high. It's not fabulous, but not horrible either. There are 120 calories in a serving...again, not bad, but the serving size is only 3/4 of a cup, rather than the 1 cup most cereals measure by. Protein and fiber are almost non-existent. The taste, however, is fantastic!I would definitely recommend the cereal in moderation or for a dessert rather than the main source of breakfast. It probably won't keep you or the kids full for very long because of the lack of protein and fiber.If you're looking for a suggestion of a delicious cereal that's also good for you, I would try the Kashi GoLean Crisp in Toasted Berry Crumble. 9grams of protein, 8grams of fiber, and 10grams of sugar per serving. And very yummy! Amazon sells that by the 4pack as well.

I would not buy Kellog's Crunchy Nut cereal because it does nothing to distinguish itself from any other flake based cereal out there.  Its pretty sweet (too sweet for my taste and probably most adults), gets soggy pretty quickly and makes no relative health claims.  Its has almost no nuts and could really use some granola clusters or something else.  Unless its on sale, or you only eat flake cereal (of which there are definitely better options) then I really don't see any reason to try this.

column9: They got it right this time.
column10: The last time Kellogg's attempted a "honey nut" cornflake I was not impressed.  While the flavor was good the flakes were extremely "crunchy", bordering on hard.  I had to let them soak a bit before the texture would be acceptable.  They were not the "Frosted Flakes" with a honey nut flavor I was expecting."Cruncy Nut" is what I expected the first time.  The smell of honey hits your nose every time the package is opened.  The flavor is moderately strong honey with a hint of nut on a flake that is crunchy but *not* hard.  The texture is very similar to "Frosted Flakes" and the crunch holds up in milk similarly to "Frosted Flakes".This one's earned a regular place on my cereal shelf.

This cereal has a good flavor, reminiscent of nuts and honey.  There is also an underlying flavor of malt and molasses.  However, it is much too sweet for my tastes.  Perhaps if it was sweetened simply with the honey and not the additional high fructose corn syrup, I would have liked it better.A box of cereal is typically eaten within 4 or 5 days in my home.  However, this one is still half full after 3 weeks because no one in the family likes it.  If you are a fan of very sweet cereals, you would probably like it much better than my family and I did.

If you like peanut flavor with your sweetened corn flakes, you will probably like this cereal.  They are sweet (too sweet for me) but not overly sugared; a 31 g serving has 11 g of sugar.  There are more sugary cereals on the market than this one.  This cereal contains High Fructose Corn Syrup, sugar, molasses & honey.  A smorgasbord of sweeteners!The peanuts bits are very small of course - I wouldn't expect whole peanuts if they're going to be stuck to the flakes.  They do add a nice peanut flavor & texture.It stays crisp just slightly longer than regular corn flakes.  I actually like that they become soggy because I prefer soggy cereal...I know, it's weird.I would only buy this cereal to top off my unsweetened shredded wheat - it adds a little interest to a plain bowl of cereal but it's too much sugar for my taste to eat a whole serving of this cereal alone.  But if you like a sweeter cereal & peanuts, you will probably like this just fine.

A very flavorful cereal with or without milk.  The sweetness of the honey and the lightly salted peanuts were a tasty combination.  Crunchy Nut didn't last a week in my household.I would definitely purchase this item in the future.  If the price was right.

I'm always on the lookout for cereal that isn't too sweet, both for my husband and my children. And besides the usual suspects, it can be surprisingly difficult to find a tasty cereal that isn't loaded with sugar. So, when I saw this one, I thought we would give it a try (not being privy to the ingredient list beforehand).The flavor is really good - I don't find it overly sweet, and there is a definite overall nut flavor. It tastes delicious both with milk and straight out of the hand. It doesn't appear to get soggy overly fast, which is a huge criteria for me. My husband said he finds it a bit too sweet (he prefers Corn Flakes), and my daughter (who is 4) ate about 3 bites before asking for something else.However, what absolutely ensures that I will not be buying this cereal in the future, is the ingredient list. Out of the first 8 ingredients, 4 of them are a form of sugar. This is how it reads:"Milled corn, sugar, peanuts, honey, malt flavoring, molasses, salt, high fructose corn syrup...."I attempt to avoid HFCS whenever I can - I'm not of the "it's completely evil" mindset, but I believe that it's hard to have moderation when it is in absolutely EVERYTHING. And with 3 other kinds of sugars, where is the need? 11g of sugar in one 3/4 cup serving of cereal is far too much - both for me, and for my children. So, while I really enjoyed the flavor, once this box is gone there will be no repeat purchases.

column9: Too sweet, not as nutty as it would seem, but still tasty
column10: I enjoyed the cereal despite the fact that it felt too sweet, and was not nearly as nutty as I expected, given the name and the picture on the box.Cons:- Too sweet, it seems a bit too much, every bite is quite sweet. And though I think most cereals go over the top with sugar, I thought this one might be a little less so. To my surprise it was sweeter than most of the ones I eat.- I love peanuts. The cereal promised lots of nut crunch. It was not to be, it doesn't have that many, and the honey/sweet flavor over powers the nut flavor, so you just get a hint of peanut flavor. It tastes more just like a honey cereal.Neutral:- The picture (like every other cereal box cover) is misleading. You get about 20% -at best- of nuts it portraysPros:- Overall the flavor is good (your mileage may vary), and it is nice and crunchy.1 star off due to the sweetness, and another star off due to it not being/tasting as nutty despite all the advertising pointing that way. You may still enjoy it - I did - but it did not live to the expectations and I am unsure I would buy it again.

I think this is an older recipe of cereal that I used to love and then it was all of a sudden gone from the shelves.  I was so happy to see it again and my family loves it.  It's cornflakes with a sweet coating and peanut pieces on the flakes.  Not too sweet which I'm happy about and really delicious!

I could smell the nuts right when I opened the box of cereal.  It smelled quite tasty.  The cereal itself is also pretty yummy, not too sweet not to NOT sweet and just nutty enough.  The only thing that would make it better is it it stayed crunchy in the milk longer, but most cereals have this problem.  The flakes are small, just the right size.  I would definitely buy this again!

I've always liked Kellogg's cereals, so Crunchy Nut was an easy choice for my breakfast needs.First impressions:I could smell the peanuts as I opened the box, so I knew I'd be in for some tasty goodness! I tried a couple of the flakes before the milk was added and it had the same texture and taste as Frosted Flakes. These were a little crunchier because of the peanuts.Taste:Once the milk was added, that's when the taste kicked into overdrive. The milk released the honey drizzle flavor, so each bite was sweet, crunchy, and delicious. Strangely enough, the peanuts felt like more of an aftertaste, even though you can clearly see them on the flakes (see the picture I uploaded in Customer Images).This is one of those cereals you have to eat fast, since the milk saturates the flakes pretty quickly. However, there is a plus - when there's no more flakes to eat and you get to the leftover milk, there's a swirl of honey flavor mixed in to make it extra sweet for your taste buds.Conclusion?This cereal isn't going to meet any daily nutritional requirements (you'd need 4 bowls to get the nutritional value in one bowl of T....umm, another cereal!), but it is definitely a yummy way to start your morning.I think of them as Frosted Flakes for a new millennium.Definitely recommended!

column9: I like it, but family LOVES it.
column10: This cereal is very sweet and very crunchy - almost too crunchy. It reminds me of Bit O' Honey candy in cereal form, and with a peanuty flavor additive. I really like honey and just about all nuts so I was anxious to try this. If you like them too, then you won't be disappointed. I just thought both flavors were a little too intense and it was defintely too crunchy, almost hard. My husband doesn't mind soggy cereal and I questioned if this would get soggy. I watched one morning as he did his normal routine of pouring milk on his cereal and putting the dogs out in the backyard.  He made coffee, situated the newspaper on the table, and let the dogs in.  When he finally started eating, I could hear his lound crunching all the way in the living room.

My Jamaican ginger arrived before time - very prompt delivery. My only complaint is that this did not taste like Jamaican ginger.  The Jamaican ginger that I purchased in NYC several years back had a rich robust flavor and was a little darker in color.  This ginger had a light color and tasted no different than the regular ginger you could purchase in any vitamin store.  Very disappointing.

As the item says  Ground Jamaica Ginger Root, That is what I wanted so I ordered it, What I got was regular Ground Ginger that you can pick up at any store. There is a slight difference in taste. So if your wanting the Jamaica Ginger dont waist your time

Yes the packaging was different than they show on the advertisement but, the flavor was outstanding. I've had several types of pista over the years and this one is fresh and good tasting. Very hard to get Indian Sweets here in the St.Louis area, and this company will get my repeat business! Lightning fast shipping and quality products. I was very pleasantly pleased. The taste was a bit "mild" (IE: Not strongly nut flavored) but yet very good as well, not at all to "mushy" or hard.Warmly,Jackie

my first time trying this dessert but it was delicious- the presentation is alittle different than in the picture- it comes packaged more like a block of it (not in individual pieces)- but very tasty! and quickly delivered. i would reorder it- not terribly sweet but pistachio is very nice.

English Double Devon Cream - pack of 3 This is a bit of pure heaven. I love the product. I made scones,took them and the English Double Devon Cream to work to share with coworkers. Coworkers were actually moaning as they ate. Had to order the 3 pack to give jars to coworkers that are now hooked.Cheryl Lynn

I've purchased this flour from Amazon in order to make pita bread. It's wonderful!  Atta flour is ground finer than other whole wheat flours and so gives excellent results.  I also use it to make no-knead bread, and the loaves are turning out lovely.Also, I've successfully substituted it for unbleached all-purpose flour in pancakes, and muffins with excellent results. Only difference is that the batter seems to see rise and bubble up when it sits but I just stir back together to smooth it before pouring/scooping into trays, and it bakes and rises beautifully.  I'm still experimenting with it and will try it with cakes next.  Highly recommended!UPDATE: I noticed a little later that the flour was sent to me past its "better if used by" date of December 27, 2009.  My item was shipped to me on January 30, 2010.  Amazon's customer service was wonderful, and I received a prompt full refund from them since they couldn't guarantee that an immediate replacement from the seller would not have the same problem.  Unfortunately, I could not change my positive review of the seller (India Connect) to outline the problem and express my displeasure at being sent a food item past it's "better if used by" date.Of course I realize that flour does not immediately expire, and thankfully I had it stored in the fridge.
