It adds flavor to your water and nothing else. This is a great way to get you to drink more water, which is important for your health!The sweeteners used here are sucralose and acesulfame potassium. The amounts are so tiny (under 2%) that I really wouldn't worry about that and, again, if you're currently not drinking enough water and this will help you do that, then I'm all in favor of that.Well recommended!

column9: handy, no calorie flavoring for your water...
column10: I try to drink at least 8 8 oz. glasses of water a day, and I don't know about you, but water can get a little boring.  So, occasionally I like the flavors you can buy to put in the waters to make them more fun.  If they taste great I'm more apt to get my water in.  I have never tried a liquid version of a water enhancer, but thought these looked interesting.  The container is small, small enough to fit in the palm of your hand and if you do a squirt of flavor for every 8 oz. you should get 24 uses out of the container.  The nice thing though is that you can tailor it yourself, more if you like a deep flavor and less if you just want a hint.  That's one thing you can't do neatly with the dry versions.  I also like that the size is small.  With this size I could have it in my desk at work to pump my water up a notch or two.  The flavor, mango peach is delicious-not too sweet, just perfect and smells tropical.The only drawback I could see is that you need to be careful in using it and have it right over your bottle, the color I'm sure would stain and the liquid comes out pretty forcefully with a squeeze.  Other than that, I was pleased I had a chance to try this and would definitely consider buying this and telling others about it.Great idea in a little package!

column9: Decent product, good tasting, but doesn't seem that cost effective
column10: I really liked having this product and adding it to water and tea.IT tasted very good, was easy to use, but given how much they recommend using it is expensive.  I used even more to get the flavor I wanted, and so my biggest reservations are that 1.  it is not cost effective, and 2.  if you don't close the lid, you have a much bigger mess than with a powder.Still, good stuff.

I'm not sure if I was just not using this correctly or if the flavor was just too weak.I tried this in sparkling water and tea and although it left a flavor, I couldn't tell that it was Mango-Peach.It also left an aftertaste.If you like the flavor this makes, then you would probably enjoy the product but for me, I would not purchase this again.

I want to like this product, but I can't say I would buy it after trying it.Taste = 5 stars. It does taste GOODPrice = 2 stars. At ~$5 a bottle, it is not a good value.  The recommended few drops just don't add enough flavor.  It takes 2 long quirts to add sufficient flavor.Portability = 2 stars.  While this is a small and easy to pack bottle, it's not really user friendly for travel.  The amount of dye in this product must be quite strong.  If you get the liquid on something porous, watch out - it might as well be food coloring - it stains.  Since it is a liquid, it is much more likely that you will encounter a leak than a small package of drink crystals.  I would never consider keeping this in my purse to flavor water on the go.

column9: It's better when I mix it with something else
column10: There are a lot of my friends who love this stuff, all of the flavors.  I don't really care for it.  I didn't care for it by itself flavoring water that is.  I did, however, like it when I added it to slightly flavor my tonic water.  I do realize that I'm apparently in the minority because as I said, everyone else I've talked to about this stuff absolutely loves the MIO flavors.
Mio Mango Peach flavor is just delicious.  Calorie free and aspartame free, these little drops can flavor anything from plain water to coffee.  You'll like it!

The Mango Peach flavor of MIO is great!A few drops go a long way in a bottle of water, but for a stronger flavor can add more (or less to taste)Like how portable it is, no need to measure just drop into a bottle or glass of water.Tastes better than flavored waters you can purchase and cheaper!

column9: A nice light addition to your drink
column10: Overall, I liked the Mio product and would recommend it.  I found it easy to use and I liked being able to control how much to add (this is more challenging with the Crystal Light packets I've used before).  And it's not as overly sweet like Crystal Light.  Just a little shot of Mio gave my water a light, refreshing taste that wasn't overpowering.The only negative was that I thought it smelled a little odd in the package, kind of a plastic-smelling/fake peach/chemical smell, but I didn't get that same feeling with it mixed in the water.  It diluted right away in the water and I didn't get that smell in the mixture, but I was somewhat hesitant when I first popped the container open.
Received one via Vine program.Product is "ok".  We prefer the Propel powder's taste and because we prefer to avoid artificial coloring.

column9: I like this even better than Crystal Light!
column10: I really like this product - it's nice because with the packaging, you could easily keep it in your purse, car, or gym bag.  I don't like keeping Crystal Light packets in my purse because I have had them open up, then had to get all the powder out.  I also like the fact that you can put as much or as little flavoring in as you want.  Sometimes we have the smaller bottles of water in our house, and then you have to try to estimate half of a packet, and often end up too little or too much - and then you have to keep the halfway full package around until you need it.  With this, you could have any size serving of water and flavor it just as much or little as you like.  I also particularly like this flavor.

MIO makes a wonderfully tasty product that is simple to use and flavor plain water.  Unlike prepackaged granules, this liquid will let you adjust the flavor, so if you don't want to be overpowered, you can just add a few drops.  This is incredibly concentrated so I recommend that you start with one squirt for 8 oz. of water and add more until you figure out exactly how strong you want it to taste.  I also discovered that this is great to add to plain ice tea since it will flavor and sweeten it at the same time.

Yeah, mango-peach.  That's as good a description of the taste as any.  All I know for certain is that I like it.  I'd probably like it better if it were more tart, but that's my personal taste and most people like sweeter flavors than I do.  Something really nit-picky is that there is a very slight saccharine after taste.  Very slight.  The color of the undiluted liquid in the little squeeze package is surprisingly red.  I guess this stuff can be used for some tasty zombie make-up too.  I've been using Mio as a coffee replacement.  It has flavor and it's easy to mix to control how strong the taste is.  Actually, easy to mix isn't a good description.  Squirt some Mio into a cup of water, carry it down the hall, and it's mixed just fine when you get where you're going.  The packaging makes it super convenient too.Anyways, my note-to-self is to try the other flavors and hope to find one less sweet.Now, as a drink mix...  Rum or vodka, toss in something sour to get that sweet/sour thing going.  If you want a specific recipe, 1 shot vodka, 2 shots water, 2 dashes lime juice, stir and serve, then add 2 or 3 squirts Mio.  It'll mix itself soon enough and the swirlies are fun.

column9: Tasty and and little goes a long way
column10: I love this stuff.  I mix a long squirt of it in a 3 quart water bottle and it flavors to my liking.  The main key with this stuff is portion control. It is very concentrated so for smaller amounts of water, it does not take very much to flavor it.

column9: Like having concentrated kool-aid in a bottle!
column10: Oh goodness this is so delicious if you like these flavors and love kool-aid! I can't believe there are no calories in this and I love the fact it can fit into my purse to take with me when I need a little sweetness in my spring water. I am not one who likes water so this is a great alternative to buying sugar-laden, or nasty sugar-free energy drinks. The flavor is strong or weak depending on how much you use in your water. I like it fairly sweet so 2 semi-long squirts is just right. It's kinda addicting since it reminds me of drinking kool-aid! The only reason I give it 4 out of 5 stars is the price, I can not believe what they charge for this considering it is not an energy, vitamin enhancer, or health increasing kind of drink. Just some yummy flavor to perk up your water now and then : )

column9: Everyone in my family likes this stuff
column10: I selected the Mango Peach to review because I like those flavors, in general.  I used it in a small bottle of Aquafina water.  When I put in one squirt, the water tasted very light, like a flavored water that had just a hint of the flavor. With two squirts, it tasted stronger, like a "fruit tea".I can see that it would be handy to have around, especially if you need a little flavor to encourage you to drink the water.The bottles are small, convenient, seal well (they double click shut) and seem durable. I will be trying other flavors, although this one tastes good.My wife and daughter tried it as well.  My wife liked the flavor.  My daughter said, "Oh, I love that stuff, especially the pomegranate."Mio contains a significant amount of artificial sweetener. The sweeteners used are sucralose and acesulfame potassium.  Note that they are not using aspartame, which is a big advantage to me - I dislike the taste of aspartame.And since the only diet soda you can get at fast food places is flavored with aspartame, I'll be carrying this stuff so that I can get a cup of water or a bottle of water and flavor it myself.

I drink 64-96oz of water per day. I live in Las Vegas and it is necessary because of the sun and heat to get as much hydration as possible. I feel better, eat less, and my skin looks amazing the more water I drink. I always have a NALGENE Tritan 1-Quart Narrow Mouth BPA-Free Water Bottlewith me and re-fill it as many times a day as I can swallow. Any product that helps me drink more water, I am interested in trying.Growing up my mom always bought Crystal light for the same purpose of drinking more water. I think this is an updated-version, better-tasting alternative for Crystal light.MIO Mango Peach did not help me drink any more water. I actually found myself avoiding my water bottle because I didn't like the aftertaste of the product. I tried adding less MIO, I tried adding more. Nope. Didn't change. I still didn't grab for more water with MIO. I prefer plain old water, it's easier to drink and more satisfying.With that said, I do like the flavor of this drink. I prefer it as a drink with a meal. It solves the aftertaste issue and with ice it is a pleasant, refreshing drink that does not add calories. I also enjoy adding a splash to plain Greek yogurt and for mixing low(er) calorie mixed-drinks.I cannot see myself purchasing more of this product unless it was on a super sale.

The Mango Peach Mio is tasty, but for the price I would say it's not worth it. I've seen it for 4-5 dollars at grocery stores and it's even more here at Amazon. Because of Amazon Vine, I decided to give it a try.I like how you can add as little or as much as you like to your water, instead of it being in little packets like some other brands do. I used about 4 squirts of it in a 16 oz bottle of water. However, I highly doubt you can get 24 servings from this unless they are very watered-down servings. You can taste both mango and the peach in it. Although it tastes good, you can tell it is artificial and it also has a slight aftertaste.Overall, a good product, just not one I would pick up myself if given the chance.

column9: Tasty, but with an artificial aftertaste.
column10: I was really curious about this item. The Mango Peach is not bad, but there's this really fake aftertaste. I think I would try other flavors out the the same curiosity, but I can't say that this would be a staple on my shopping list.

column4: There's No Stopping Space Vikings T. Edwards!
column10: I've had several of the MiO flavors and don't have much bad to say about them in general.  The convenience and price makes for a pretty desirable little flavoring product.  A little bit will go a long way, I stretch them much further than the 24 servings they're marked with, and they're reasonably tasty (personal leanings aside).If I had any qualm with them at all it's that they are decidedly 'artificial' in their sweetness and to a lesser extent in their flavors.  The flavoring is supposedly not artificial according to the packaging so perhaps it's more of the sweetener skewing my perception of the flavor. While probably pretty obvious given the nature of the product it should be noted for those that really hate artificial sweeteners or have a particular dislike of a particular artificial tasting flavor (I'm giving you the stinkeye banana Runts and all your ilk).This particular flavor, mango peach, is pretty middle of the road for my tastes.  Definitely mango and peach in flavor but I far prefer the berry pomegranate and fruit punch but that's just me.  If you're bonkers for peach and mango this will probably not disappoint.

column9: Good stuff, but not worth the price
column10: This stuff is straight-up delicious and with 0 calories what's to complain about? Well, the cost for one. These are like $4 each at our local walmart and even more expensive on amazon.com. I can also testify that while this MIGHT make 24 servings in a lab, those are very watered down servings. To get a flavor profile I was happy with I ended up getting more like 6 1-liter bottles of water dosed to appropriate flavor intensity.If it was 1/2 the price I might consider it, but as it stands right now. I won't be picking these up anymore.

...but don't add too much. In a 16.9oz. bottle of water, 3 squirts is enough for me and I like sweet-ish drinks. The first time I tried it, I over did it and it had that overwhelming sugar substitute taste to it. Also, although it's Mango Peach, I personally taste more peach than mango which is unfortunate because I prefer mango flavor to peach. Overall, this is a tasty low-cal, low-carb alternative for those who are looking for a drink that won't cause them to rack-up calories throughout the day.

column9: Great new way to add flavor
column10: I am really enjoying the MIO products. In a tiny package you can add interesting, sugar free flavors to either plain or sparkling water.  I have now tried several of the flavors and have enjoyed them all. You do have to play around with them to find the right amount to flavor and sweeten to your taste but the beauty of the product is that it's easy to do. Great product -- I hope it sticks around

column9: tastes great, very convenient, and no aspartame!!
column10: We started using Mio for a couple of reasons.  First, we wanted to cut out excess calories, and second, we wanted to save on the high cost of beverages in restaurants.  Drinks cost about $3-4 each at most casual dining places - that adds $20 to the bill for a family of four.Most flavored water "enhancers" contain aspartame, which I am highly allergic to.  However, Mio is sweetened with sucralose and contains NO ASPARTAME!  Another plus is that Mio is a liquid and not a powder - "add a little or a lot."  My husband prefers his drinks strong, I like mine milder. Mio allows you to choose how much, without worrying about what to do with the excess.  I used to use 4C mixes (which also have no aspartame), but ended up with powder in my purse when I didn't need a whole packet in my drink.  These little bottles are a convenient size that fit easily into a purse or backpack.  My grocery store sells them for about $4 each and they are definitely worth that.We have tried many flavors, and our favorite is the Berry Pomegranate.  The mango peach is a little too sweet for us, but still a good flavor.  My mom usually only drinks lemon flavored iced tea.  The sweet tea flavor is too sweet with no lemon, but she found that the peach tea is a great substitute.  The fruit punch tastes a lot like cherry Cool Aid.  I hope that Mio expands the selection with some new flavors - I'd love a green apple, or lemonade flavor.  Overall, highly recommended!

I really do like this Mango Peach flavor, but after drinking about a cup or two, I could definitely notice an artificial sweetener taste. It's not strong, but it's apparent.It's a really cute design and I like the idea of using this concentrated liquid to make drinks. It's much easier than using powder and it's handy to carry around. Unless I can find one where the artificial sweetener taste isn't there, I most likely won't purchase it again.

This super-concentrated flavoring is so convenient.  One small squeeze into my water glass is plenty for a full 12 ounces of water.  The flavor mixes in instantaneously without any gritty sediment at the bottom of the glass.The flavor is comparable to other water flavorings (like Crystal Light, etc).  It's not exactly natural tasting, but it's not offensive either.  I defnitely taste the mango and the peach.  This is more convenient that the flavored powders for making water more interesting without added calories or caffeine.  A good product!

I've been using MIO for several months now and I really like it! When I want a sweeter flavor, I add a dash of Truvia (stevia based sweetener). I love the Mango Peach flavor, but have found most of the others quite good, too. In fact, I'm hoping they start introducing even more flavor choices. The only one I don't like is the Sweet Tea flavor (although the Peach Tea flavor is great).The packaging is well-designed. There's no dripping when you use it, and since the cap snaps down tightly, it doesn't leak if you throw it in your pocket or purse. The bottle is also small enough to get through security at the airport, so I don't have to drink all the sugary and caffeinated drinks they offer on the plane. MIO has become a staple in my house. Price-wise it's a better bargain than the powdered packets.

column9: Marvelous, especially with added lemon juice
column10: I'm a water drinker and I still drink a lot of it straight from the filter. But water can get boring...it is nice to occasionally use an enhancer to add some zest. At various times, I've tried all the commercial products out there. None come close to matching the flavor and convenience of MiO. This is truly an original and outstanding product and it has become a regular part of my food life.I'm an extremely health-conscious eater. I eat a mostly plant-based diet of whole grains, vegetables, and fruits. I grow a large portion of my own veggies and buy the rest from local farmers' markets. I try to avoid processed food and cook almost everything from scratch. MiO's ingredient list shows artificial colors, sweeteners, and preservatives...so you might wonder why would I even consider drinking it. Well, I don't use that much and I don't worry about this one little misdemeanor in my pantry. My diet is so healthy in so many other ways that I consider MiO a small indulgence.I've tried to go natural with water enhancers--for example adding pomegranate juice. But truthfully, it is not nearly as flavorful and far from convenient or cost-effective.What I frequently do use to make my MiO drink more healthful is to squeeze a real half a lemon into it. The artificial sugars used in MiO are so strong that they sweeten the lemon, too...and the lemon enhances all the MiO flavors. Lemon is extremely healthful! I could fill up this review page with medical and nutritional information showing the beneficial qualities of lemon juice. I've known about this for a long time but rarely fixed lemonade for myself because I dread using all the real or artificial sugars that it needs to take away the intense sourness. The artificial sugars used in MiO are 600 times sweeter than sugar...they do the trick with a little squirt and nothing more added. So, by using MiO with a half a lemon squeezed into it, I find that I am drinking more liquid per day than I did before I discovered MiO and I am incorporating lemon juice into my daily diet. In the balance, MiO has been a health improvement.Yes, I am aware of the propylene glycol used in this product...but it does not cause me great concern. I am more fearful of coming into contact with bad chemicals from insecticides, common home cleaning products, factory-farmed meat and fish, and the tons of processed foods that I avoid when cooking my own meals from scratch.Taste is a matter of individual preference. I keep all the flavors on hand for variety's sake, but seem to prefer the Berry Pomegranate and the Mango Peach.The MiO bottle is a marvelous invention that should win some kind consumer prize. There is a double-locking lid and little membrane over the opening. The membrane creates a tiny vacuum within the bottle as you squeeze, so you'll never fear dripping the contents on clothes, carpets, or tablecloths as you remove it from your glass. The double-locking lid is so secure that I have no fear carrying a bottle in my purse.My personal wish list for MiO is that they'd remove the artificial coloring. That would make is more healthful and not detract from the flavor in any way.

column9: Mix with the plain greek yogurt, So yummy!
column10: Just came out an idea about mixing Mio with plain yogurt. I added one squeeze into a 2lb of greek yogurt, stirred for a while. Taste just like the fruit flavor yogurt on the market. Has a creamy texture with less carbs and lots of protein. Yummy!It seems a little too sweet for me, so next time I'd add half squeeze and try.As a water flavorant, as far as I tried, I like this flavor and the fruit punch.The sweet tea and peach tea taste far less satisfactory than snapple or lipton brisk (my favorite brand). But after adding some lemon juice, those two taste better.

column9: Mango Peach :A Fun, flavorful water enhancer
column10: I love the Mio line. The portable package is sleek and stylish. The concept behind using as much or as little as you like is wonderful, and for the most part the flavors are awesome.The Mango Peach is my sons favorite. For him this product became a most convenient money saver. During the school year  he would leave the house in the morning and have class until the late evening hours. So he was buying many juice drinks and flavored water drinks at school, and spending a ton of money. With the ability to tuck a bottle of Mio right into his pocket, he was able to bring a water bottle with him and refill it,  add the Mio,and have flavored drinks any time he liked. And he saved a nice amount of money in the bargain.I like the creativity that Mio affords me. I can have it mixed in a little seltzer or Pellegrino for an elegant faux cocktail. Or I can add a few drops to my regular home brewed iced tea for a fruity, tropical twist on an old favorite. It is so nice being able to find multiple uses for a product. I am glad I found this.

column9: No Calories But Tastes Like It's Naturally Sweetened
column10: A little bit goes a long way.  A few drops of MIO Mango Peach, 1.62 Ounce (Pack of 4) into a glass of ice cold water makes for a delicious and refreshing beverage.  And, to boot, it is calorie-free.  It tastes like it is naturally sweetened but it is not.  I made a pitcher of this Mio and I love it.  It's a great drink and especially helpful for dieters.  An additional benefit is that it comes in such a small container that you can carry it in your purse or pocket.

I received my bottle of Mio Mango Peach flavoring free from the Amazon Vine Program, in exchange for writing a review.I have a girlfriend who loves Mio and had been encouraging me to try it.  I think the flavor she likes is sweet tea.  So when I saw it offered on the Vine website, I jumped at it.  I drink a gallon of water every day, and sometimes it gets a little monotonous.  What would be nicer than a no-calorie peach/mango flavoring to add to the water, right?I'm sorry to say that I won't be buying Mio in the future.  I had to add 3 or 4 squirts to a glass of water to get any recognizable mango or peach flavoring.  And then it had a very strong saccharine-type aftertaste, and an almost perfume-y smell.  The Mio website claims that it uses sucralose and not saccharine, but whatever it was I didn't like it. Unfortunately, sucralose can also cause diarrhea and gas if enough is ingested.A look at the ingredients on the bottle confirmed my suspicions that this was just another way to ingest unhealthy ingredients masked as "natural".  Propylene glycol - a type of mineral oil, can cause allergic skin reactions.  Yellow #5, Blue #1, and/or Red #40 - these have been linked to ADHD, hyperactivity in children, and lymphoma. Acesulfame Potassium, an artificial sweetener, aggravates hypoglycemia, and has been linked to breast and lung tumors. That's quite a chemical cocktail we're adding to our water!It does come in a cute little bottle that would go well in a purse or backpack.  And if you are counting carbs or calories, or are diabetic, these drops could be a nice way to flavor plain old water.But for me, I'll just continue to add a squirt of lemon or lime juice to my water.  I'm actively trying to eliminate unneeded and harmful chemicals from our diets and Mio won't be something we buy again.

Well, since some other user decided they'd paste their review on to each flavor allow me to give my short but sweet review:MiO is delicious. I like that I can just put in the tiniest of splashes in my drink and just have a hint of flavor... or splash a lot in and get a real flavorful experience. It's a quick and easy thing to use. It's also fun to watch it splash into the water. I've also found it's good to flavor different types of alcohol.In regards to the criticism by other reviewers for it containing propylene glycol - don't be in a panic like them. propylene glycol is harmless unless ingest massive quantities of it. Using a canard like "it's considered harmful to pets so humans shouldn't ingest it!" is just alarmist behavior. Chocolate is harmful to dogs. Better not eat that then!Lastly, in regards to it having so many "food colorings" - well, if you don't like anything that flavors your water to have anything artificial in it, squeeze a lemon into it. Put a dash of sugar. Or just drink the water plain. You know what you're getting into when you buy this stuff.Bottom line: This is my new favorite drink flavoring. I will be buying from them again and again.

column9: Flavor needs improvement, scores points for convenience
column10: I've tried this flavor of MIO, as well as the strawberry watermelon, and my main reaction to both has been that the flavor is not natural tasting and is far too sweet.  MIO mixed with water creates a flavor not unlike a kids' juice drink, which is not something I prefer.  The taste is sticky sweet and very artificial.  Obviously, something like this is highly subjective, so I'm sure many people love it...it's just not my style.  I will say that MIO is very convenient.  The packaging is small and easy to keep in a desk at work, for instance, or a purse.  Also, there is no need to really stir the liquid, so it has an advantage over Crystal Light or other similar powder products.  Nonetheless, I would need to see major flavor changes before I would buy this again.

I'll preface this review by saying that as artificially flavored soda products go (most of what you will find on your supermarket shelves fall under that descriptor) this one is not bad... at least in terms of taste.  It is cleaner and truer than most. (Note: my kids liked this flavor better than the peach, but said the peach flavor got a bit lost). But, except for the environmentally-friendly packaging and convenience, that is where the good ends.While the cute branding is what is put forward, this is a heavily marketed chemical stew (to quote the web site from which I retrieved the actual ingredients) from Kraft foods.  In case you are wondering what is in it, here is the list:Water, Citric Acid, Propylene Glycol, Malic Acid, Contains Less than 2% of Natural Flavor, Sucralose and Acesulfame Potassium (Sweeteners), Potassium Citrate, Red 40, Blue 1, Potassium Sorbate (Preservative).I personally go well out of my way to avoid artificial sweetener knowing that most are carcinogens which were given a fast pass because the FDA believes that America needs artificial sweeteners. (I learned this in graduate school from a woman who did independent, unbiased research, and if you knew half of what I know... you would avoid them too!)So we tried these without the understanding that it is an artificially sweetened, as well as artificially flavored beverage.  I am really hoping Amazon will provide full information on the ingredients in their packaged foods soon! (By which I mean simply reporting what is on the label as I have above).I will note as i did in my other review that htis concept is not novel.  My kids have been making "Italian sodas" for years using Torani Vanilla Syrup 750mL syrpus for years.  I do something similar with a bit of juice (but am generally happy enough with fizzy water).  If you like a bit of flavor, I would recommend trying the Italian syrups: much better, much much healthier, or... just add a little juice ;)  (That adds instead of subtracting from the nutritional value).I would give this drink 4 stars for flavor, 5 for convenience, 4 as an overall "green product" from reduced packaging to minimal transportation costs... but a -5 for nutrition.  I am frankly not sure whether this mix of chemicals is better or worse than high fructose corn syrup (my family does not have weight problems) but, personally would rather side-step the entire issue of what is worse for them.  they don't drink Coke, or Pepsi, and I will be limiting this to a very occasional (is it right to call it a treat?)  Frankly I would rather hand them each a sugar cane (which I can get from the local farmers market).  That is a much healthier treat (and I do not have to question whether or not sugar cane qualifies as a treat.)I would recommend instead, trying one of the brands of Italian syrup which Amazon carries, and can personally vouch for many varieties or Torani.  If they ever go to packaging it in luch box squeeze bottles, this product is dead in the water. IMO, that is all it offers.

I added the recommended amount of Mio to a glass, then filled it up with water.  The flavor was pretty strong, but I thought it tasted better than kool-aid.  If you're one of those people that can't stand drinking water because it's tasteless, then this would help you get the water you need without sacrificing taste.  Some people may also want to use less than the recommended amount if they want the taste to be more subtle.  This would make the bottle last longer, too.  The reason I didn't give it five stars is because I think it's kind of pricey for being what it is.  There are 24 servings in each container, but if you drank a few glasses of water a day and used this every time, then that would add up.  Water flavoring shouldn't be expensive.

I have to admit that I was already using this before it was offered to us on Vine. MiO Liquid Water Enhancer, Mango Peach is my favorite flavor.  And the directions are accurate - just add as much or as little to your water as is to your taste.  I find it's better cold, so I keep it in the fridge so it doesn't warm up the water.Out of the other flavors I like the MIO Liquid Peach Tea and MIO Berry Pomegranate. I didn't care for the MIO Sweet Tea, personally, probably because I grew up in the South where Sweet Tea is considered ambrosia, and I have never cared for any MIO Fruit Punchso I haven't tried that flavor.So I totally recommend Mio Liquid Water Enhancer. I've gotten my step-dad hooked already! I think it's great for water drinkers who may want a change in taste.Now I see there's a Black Cherry flavor - I look forward to trying that!

column9: Water flavoring - add a little or a lot to make it "your way"
column10: My daughter is a ballet major in college and she dances about 6 hours or more each day. The fluid needs are tremendous to keep the joints lubricated and to prevent dehydration, but she doesn't really like to drink plain, boring bottled water. I got her this MiO Liquid Water Enhancer, Mango Peach 1.62 fl oz (48 ml) to try so she might be encouraged to get the fluids she needs.She added one squirt to her water as the directions indicated and found that the flavor was not quite as strong as she had hoped so had to add more to really get a good mango peach taste. Perhaps other flavors are stronger? At around $6.00 for a small container, it can get expensive since it really doesn't give enough flavoring to make the 24 8-ounce drinks as it advertises on the product label. It is a nice size, however, to carry in a purse or bag so that you can always have it with you. This water enhancer provides no vitamins so it is not nutritive as some other products are. It adds no calories to the water -- which is an important consideration for many.It's good enough that I'd like to try more flavors, but the price is the main drawback since a person will actually likely need to add more drops if they want a strong taste of the flavoring.

Don't get me wrong, this adds nice flavor to your water.  The price per ounce is outrageous!  The Mango Peach required quite a few squeezes to get a good flavor in a 16.9 oz bottle of water.  I'd be willing to try other flavors but I doubt I'd buy this flavor, I'm not a big fan of this one.  I don't want my water to just have a faint flavor, I'd rather have just plain water than that.  You have to use too much of this flavor to get a good tasting water.

I've seen the ads for MIO many, many, many times, but never considered it as anything but another gimmick.  After receiving the MIO Mango Peach, and the Peach Tea from Amazon Vine I can testify that these are actually wonderful.  The ease of use and taste is excellent.  We go through lots and lots of drink products and, in general, they take up enormous amounts of shelf space when we buy them in bulk to save money during sales.I haven't calculated the cost effectiveness of MIO yet, but I could store several bottles of this in very little space.  Normally we buy Arizona Tea either in the cans or the gallon jugs, and using MIO would be a great alternative.MIO will now be a favorite at our house along with Crystal Light Lemonade.

column9: I hated it. My roommate loved it.
column10: Immediately upon adding this product to your water, your water turns red. Fairly bright red, even with just a little bit of the product. Next, your nose is greeted with a slightly artificial, slightly sweet, vaguely peach scent. Finally, upon taking a sip, your taste buds are met with... kind of nothing. A slight bit of a hint of flavor, but very very fake and a little bit chemical-ly. That was my review.I had high hopes for this product. I don't like drinking water, and anything that can turn water palatable for me is excellent. BUT, I didn't like it. It basically takes perfectly good water and turns it into a glass of chemicals. The one good thing is that you can add as much or as little as you want (for a very red, very fake flavor, or for a very pink, very watered down flavor - with no in between that I can find).All that said, I quickly gave the MIO to my roommate and he loved it. Absolutely loved it. I think he had four glasses of water this evening alone, and he commented that the bottle wasn't going to last the week. So I guess it's not for everyone, but it is for some people!

I drink a lot of water.  In the summer I drink a lot of fizzy water -- I even have my own water fizzer -- and sometimes I want it to have some flavor.  Not sugar, I don't want soda, just a little something to break up the monotony of water, water and water, with water on the side.I've tried a couple of flavoring products and remained unimpressed, but I have to say that MiO surprised me.  The flavor is really clean and natural, and the sweetness, though from artificial sources, (Sucralose) isn't off-putting.  I'd prefer it unsweetened but it's not horrible; I'm fine with it.I've tried it in water and in hot and cold tea, and in each case, MiO enhanced the beverage.  It's easy to use and each bottle looks to have a fairly generous amount of flavoring in it. (At least it does for me; I use one squirt for anything up to a liter of liquid.At this price point, MiO is a very good alternative to soda, in my opinion.  There are a lot of different flavors, so if mango-peach doesn't suit, you have other choices.  I liked this one so much I'm tempted to try some of the others.  How much more of a recommendation could you ask for?

Most of the flavoring products I've had always leave an aftertaste that seem to bother me. MIO Liquid does not, so that already made me happy. The mango peach is a good blend that I found enjoyable, and I'd be interested in sampling the other flavors that they have to offer. The fact that it comes in a liquid form is nice too, because powder can be so messy. I also like the small packaging size which makes it each to pack when your traveling.

I am one of those people who adds the flavor packs to her water...well,sorry 'Crystal' you and I won't be seeing one another again...I have aNEW best friend! Meet MIO!  I love this stuff!  Easy to use, a squeezeplease...and you control the strength of the flavor of your water, notsome little flavor packet =)A bonus on days that you want less or moreflavor in that H2o...or if you are using a smaller or larger glass...just add another little squeeze...or...you get the idea...LOL  I willbe trying other flavors, I really am sold on this fun and tasty product!

We are thrilled with this MIO product!  The mango peach is delicious.  We do not just add it to water.  We've really enjoyed it inside of our protein shakes.  It adds a very unique fruity flavor to the otherwise dull drinks.  The MIO products are delicious, but this peach is one of our favorites.  We really like how you can determine how much to put in your drinks based on your taste.  It's not in a single-serve canister or sleeve which determines how much you get.  This unique squirt bottle allows us to determine the precise amount that we enjoy.  I can't say enough great things about this product.  It is a big hit in our house.

column9: Great taste for just a Squeeze
column10: Just a little squeeze brought a flavor splash in a 16 ounce bottle of water. It was just enough peach mango flavor to perk me up. Considering how large the container is, I know that I can get more than 24 servings from it. I think that is a conservative estimate.I am thinking how great this would be for a car trip. Take several flavors and you can skip the drink machine, I really like that there are no calories. It is in a sturdy plastic bottle that when you snap it shut will not come open by itself. So, I could put it in my purse and carry it with me. Actually, the package is kind of cute, it is shaped like a drop of water when you turn it upside down to get the splash.I have been buying the powdered tubes at the store but they can be messy when you open them. I sometimes lose some of the flavor powder on the counter top.So portable, tasty and easy, this is a great product.

So I have to confess - I absolutely LOVE these things.  I love almost all the flavors, and this Mango Peach is at the top of my list, next to Strawberry Watermelon.  I love that I can put in as little or as much as I want into my reusable water bottle and I'm off!  I usually put 2 short squirts into my 64oz Nalgene, and I feel that is plenty for me.  At that rate, it usually last a few weeks for me.  Some may want it stronger, for me, it's quite enough sweetness.  I don't get headaches from this like I do from Crystal Light, so the fake sugar is better for me.  It's also recyclable in my community.  My only hope is that this never gets discontinued - I can't go back to the powder stuff!!!!

column9: It's OK but I think I like my water un-enhanced.
column10: I ordered this from the Vine selections just out of curiosity since I have nothing against the taste (or lack thereof) of plain old water and if I want something else it'll be juice (the real thing from real fruit) or tea.  I do concede that this stuff tastes like peach; no false advertising there.  The mango flavor is overwhelmed, however, by the peach and doesn't come through very well to my tastebuds.  That's OK.  Peach is nice.  I add it to coconut water and it makes for a pleasant drink.If I were to ever voluntarily buy this, I would prefer no sweetener added so that I would have control over the level of sweetness to my drink.  This stuff is really too sweet for me.  When I reduce the amount of Mio enhancer to reduce the sweetness, that also reduces the fruit flavor too much.  Another thing I would prefer is no artificial coloring.  It makes for an unappealing, unnatural look to the drink.Bottom line:  I doubt I'll look for more Mio liquid water enhancer unless I can find some that is unsweetened and has no artificial coloring.

Mangos are a favorite fruit of mine and I find peaches to be delightful whether raw or cooked. Never having had them in combination left me a bit aprehensive when I received the Mio. I opened an eight ounce jar of bottled water and squeezed in a shot of Mio. The result was a bottle of water with a barely distinguishable flavor. I gave it a second shot and the taste was just right. There is no one formula that fits all. It depends on individual taste and how hard you squeeze the Mio bottle and the length of the squeeze. With a little fine tuning you can achieve a welcome diversion from plain water. This is a tiny bottle but it can bring a big dose of enjoyment.

I absolutely love peach tea. I was happy to try Mio Liquid Peach Tea and Mio Peach/Mango Tea to see if it would be better than real peach tea or other peach tea brands. The idea is simple, make a syrup to add to your glass for some delicious tea wherever you are. No messy packets to mess with; No clouds of powder to smell. However, getting it to the right flavor took a lot of shots. The directions say one shot per each 8oz of water. I filled two glasses with 8oz of water. This review deals only with the peach/mango.On the first shot, you couldn't taste anything other than water though the glass did have a tint to it. The second shot still gave no hint of a flavor. The third shot definitely had flavor, but not identifiable as peach or mango. The fourth shot was definitely better and the fifth finally had a nice taste to it. However, 5 shots into what ended up as a 6oz glass of water seemed a bit much. With each pack having 24 shots (one shot per 8oz serving as recommended on the directions), and one glass taking 5 shots to taste good - you are lucky to get 4 glasses of tea out of one Mio Liquid 1.62oz container. Granted tastes differ and you might get by with less shots. I also used tap water instead of bottled water to test it out to get an exact 8oz measurement of water.

My daughter introduced me to Mio while we were visiting her last summer.  Since then I have gone through a few of the flavors, with Mango Peach being one of my favorites.  Recently I added a Strawberry Watermelon to the mix and have found it is also good, especially in water.  The Mango Peach is a favorite mixed with Turkey Hill Green Tea and is a daily drink for me (ie. why I bought 4 at a time).Now I must have my daily fix or I feel like the day is not complete.  Do I love it, YES!
I have been using the MIO varieties both at home and at work. Not only do I love it both for the taste and ease of use but I flavor our tea and water with it when family comes over for bridge.

This is my favorite flavor, and I decided to purchase from Amazon rather than grocery store because it's better priced.  Everyones taste buds are different, so I recommend trying one first before buying multiple quanitites.  The others are good too, but I find this to be my ultimate favorite.  Love the fact that it's zippo calories.

Yet another item that we have added to AutoShip as mu husband goes thru 3-5 bottles per week at the office and traveling. this and the peach iced tea are his favorites. So far the Sweet Tea has been the only flavor that we have not really enjoyed.

I had bought this at a local store and tried it it out. This is my review.For a small bottle (less than 2 oz)if you use it right this can actually last a long time. Just a little bit of it in a water bottle goes a long way. But be careful not to press on it to much or to much will come out and it will be grossly sweet.. Seriously just barely pinch it and it will really be enough to flavor the water...The only other negative is the additives in it... They are not very good for you...But then again what diet sweetener really is?But other than that it is not bad!

I somewhat enjoyed the MIO Mango Peach flavoring for water.  It adds a little flavor to water and is easy to use.  My only complaint is that is has a bit of an aftertaste like many calorie free drinks have.  I didn't care for that.  I will definitely drink what I received from Amazon Vine but am not sure I would buy more on my own.  I have to think about that.

I can't really tell you much about these from personal experience, but my daughter is just bonkers about this stuff.  We have a ton of these packs in the cupboard, and she takes them with her everywhere.  So, I guess it's either really yummy or really addictive.

column9: Reasonable taste if it keeps you away from sugary drinks
column10: This MIO Mango Peach is a reasonable alternative to sugary drinks. If it keeps one away from sugary drinks, it does its job. It is not going to win a taste contest against fresh fruit or fresh fruit juice but it has zero calories. I use one squirt each time, on cups 12 to 20 ounces of water. The squirt has enough power that it can almost reach towards the bottom of the cup.In my case, I occasionally use it to give the water a little flavor, so it's not just plain old water, and keeps me away from the sugary drinks. Squirting this is faster than brewing tea and icing it or slicing lemons and limes, although the latter are probably healthier choices :)

As with all of the MIO products, this is so delicious that it is hard to believe it contains no calories.  I love the ease of portability and how securely the lid closes.  I never worry that it will accidentally open in my purse.  I am saving a ton on soft drinks because I can order water in the drive-thru and then add my MIO to the water for a delicious drink.
This liquid packs a flavor punch to water.  You had as much as you want to a desired potentcy.  And it's zero calories!!! Can't beat that!

column9: Horrible taste, would rather just drink water...
column10: I couldn't taste any mango peach, just tasted like I added plastic to my water with food coloring.  I liked the idea of a little flavoring for my water, but I guess I thought this would be a little more natural, which it is definitely not.

I usually drink coffee, ice tea or plain water. Once in a while I use  individual tubes of no calorie flavors. I find Crystal Light is usually too sweet for me & prefer the store brands.  MIO isn't nearly as sweet as Crystal Light, but I'm not crazy about this flavor. I used two squirts in a 10 oz. bottle of water, then shake to mix. It's hard for me to judge how much I'm squirting into the water. A serving size is 1/2 tsp. so you might want to measure your squirts to get an idea of how much you're using. Of course, the sweetness & strength of flavor will be up to you..just use more or less squirts.When I mix MIO Mango Peach into a glass of water, I don't like the smell. I prefer to mix it into bottled water, the bottle opening prevents the smell from getting to my nose.ProsNot as sweet as Crystal Light0 CaloriesCan use more or less according to your taste preferenceConvenientIn BetweenThe flavor of MIO Mango Peach is so, so...taste improves when it's coldConsIt's hard to get the flavor consistentI don't like the smell of MIO Mango Peach (it's better to use this in a bottle, not a glass or cup, etc.)

column9: A little flavor or a lot, the choice is mine
column10: I've been using MIO in my water for quite a while now. I like that it allows me to give my water that something extra, so that it makes me more inclined to get my daily intake of water in. Additionally being able to choose how much or how little flavor you add is nice too; me I found that with most of the flavors I like 2-3 quick squirts in my water bottle which holds 24 ounces. Mango Peach is by far my favorite, with MIO Sweet Tea as a close second. For some the taste may be unappetizing and I admit at first I wasn't sure I liked it, but it grew on me and now I use MIO on an almost daily basis.

When mixed perfectly, the MIO Mango Peach iced tea tastes like a diet version of Chili's Mango iced tea which I am a big fan of.The problem is that it is next to impossible to get a consistent strength. I try for 2 medium squirts for the right flavor, but there is no practical way to measure how much mix you are putting in your glass. It squirts out too hard to measure with a measuring spoon. So, some days it is too strong, and I end up dumping the whole thing. Other days, it starts too weak. Of course, adding more makes it too strong. Like Goldilocks, some days, it ends up just right, and it tastes great.The bottle says that it has 24 servings. I haven't been counting, but it seems like a lot more than 24.

Probably the best thing about MIO is its portability and sharability. The problem is that the flavor  may not be outstanding enough for anyone to want to share.I don't particularly care for the phony label "Water Enhancer". Adding an artificial color, artificial sweetener, and an unnatural taste that only approximates the flavor created in nature does not seem like an enhancement to me.The MIO is easy to use - flip open the cap, squeeze some MIO into the water for an explosion of color, taste, squeeze again, taste, squeeze again if necessary, continue squeezing and tasting until satisfied, and then clip the lid shut.The inexact nature of the squeeze is a sticking point for me because it's almost impossible to duplicate the exact amount squeezed each time. One could measure half a teaspoon of liquid first but that defeats the design of the product. I've only tried the Mango/Peach. It has great color but only average taste that tastes slightly artificial. There is a chalky aftertaste after each swallow, but not an obtrusive one.  I much prefer Crystal Light for taste though I also find it tedious to mix just the right amount of product into the water with the CL.Anyone so inclined might find it easy to shoplift such a small handful of a container, but the taste of the product might preclude such shenanigans.

Sorry, but everyone in my famiy thought this stuff was nasty. If you just use a few drops, it tastes like watered down Kool-Aid, but if you put in a few more drops, it tastes so sweet, you almost need an insulin shot after! No happy medium there. Won't be buying this stuff anytime soon, sorry, might be a great conveinience for some, but why bother if it's gross!

I took my Mio to work to flavor up water at lunchtime. I try to drink 6-8 cups of water while at work, and sometimes I get real tired of plain ol' water. Yay for Mio!It's much more convenient than keeping a jug of juice in the work fridge -- the Mio does not need to be refrigerated, and is small enough I could take it with me on the go to restaurants and forgo the overpriced soda.The Mio `liquid water enhancer' (honest advertising, there) is not really tasty, but if you want a little more flavor than water, it works. The flavor is no worse than most, say, energy drinks, or zip-fizz like concoctions.I found the Mango Peach to be decent. The flavor is pleasant enough, not strongly mango or peach, very sweet. It takes a bit more of the Mango Peach to flavor a whole glass than it does the Berry kind, I think, but I do like the Mango flavor better.The bottle design is simple. Instructions on the side tell you to open, squirt, enjoy (I paraphrase). I think it would be better in a bottle of water, if you were carrying it around (on a trip, maybe? This is getting better and better.), thus you could shake it, as with a cup of water I found the flavor to condense a bit at the bottom.The packaging is secure enough I don't think it would open by accident, or leak, should I be carrying it in my purse.I would make a couple comments on the labeling. One, and this is just funny: under the flavor it explains that it is Mango peach `Natural flavor with other natural flavor'. Ok. Two, the Nutrition Facts are listed for 1 serving -- so 1/24 of the bottle. This makes a lot of sense, except that then all the values are 0. That only tells me there is perhaps something of sugar and protein in there but not significant enough to be 1% -- or the values are just 0. I don't pretend to understand Nutrition labeling.Know that this flavor-enhancer is not a significant source of things like calcium, iron, fiber, etc. (They're missing the part about it not containing peanuts.)Ingredients include malice acid, propylene glycol, citric acid, less than 2% of natural flavor (...ok), potassium citrate, sweeteners, coloring, and preservatives.It contains 0% juice, does not need to be refrigerated, but should be used within a month of opening.Size effective, yes -- Mio is awesome. Price effective, well, that depends on what you are doing and what you want.

column9: Did not care for the aftertaste.
column10: I love peach drinks and was excited to try this but what a letdown!  It tasted okay at first, sorta, then the aftertaste kicked in.  Maybe the other flavors are okay but this one is a definate will not buy again!

column9: Tastes great, but too artificial for my tastes.
column10: Though this product is touted as a "water enhancer", it is nothing less than just artificial sweeteners with "natural" flavor and artificial coloring. The third listed ingredient is propylene glycol, which is the main ingredient in most antifreeze and gel deodorant sticks. Apart from the inventive concept of delivering it in concentrated form in a squeeze bottle, it is nothing more than re-marketing of sugar-free Kool-Aid for adults.

I drink lots of water and really don't have a problem with how it tastes. Still, I'm trying to stay away from sodas and thought this would be a good alternative to carbonated diet beverages. The first time I used it the darn thing squired all over the place. Okay. Definitely user error but still aggravating.The taste is more peach than mango and frankly tastes very artificial. I thought I'd like this more than I did. I'm glad it's low calorie, but I don't see myself buying it in the future.UPDATE: I have been drinking this product for a while now and have grown to like it. I especially like to mix it with my Emergen-C in a glass of water. I doubt it'll be something I buy--I think it's expensive for what it is, and I prefer drinking something that has vitamins or something that will be beneficial to my body--but it has grown on me.

The bottle says to use one squeeze per bottle of water. This gives you about 24 uses per MIO bottle.  This comes out to twenty-five cents per $6 MIO. In most cases a bottle of flavored water isn't more than twenty to thirty cents more than a bottle of plain water.  So you don't really gain anything unless you use it to flavor tap water.  That would be fine if you don't mind the same flavor each time.As to the flavor, Mango Peach would not be my choice but it tasted fine and had just a little aftertaste.  But this might have been because I squeezed too hard on the bottle.  Of course if you use less it just flavors the water a little and has no aftertaste at all.  For me I think I'll just drink my water straight or with a squeeze of 'Real Lemon'.Zeb Kantrowitz

I didn't know what to expect when I first tried MIO Mango Peach. For the most part, I was pleasantly surprised. My first try was too strong though. This stuff is potent. After adjusting the amount used, I got it to where I really like it. Less is definitely better. The flavor isn't all that natural tasting, but it is very pleasant when you don't use too much. I highly recommend you start out with only a drop or two, until you reach your desired level of flavor. I like MIO Mango Peach, but I only recommend it if you're a fan of fruity diet drinks. If you're more of a juice drinker, and/or someone that does not like diet soft drinks, you may want to look elsewhere.

column9: Way too sweet if you slavishly follow instructions
column10: Summary: Possibly less expensive way to have flavored drinking water versus pre-mixes and bottled. Too sweet for my taste at the concentration specified on the label.Pros: Nice aroma. Tastes somewhat like mango and peach.Cons: If you follow the directions, it's too sweet. I would cut the concentration by about half.Summary: Not a horrible product, but I don't think I will buy any after the Vine sample runs out. This may be as much because I am not a consumer of the ready made flavored waters to begin with as any specific issues with Mio. Perhaps it would be better with soda water?

MIO Mango Peach comes in a handy dental-floss looking bottle, and has 24 servings in a bottle. Basically you squirt some in plain water, and this enhances the water with a semi-artificial peach/mango taste. It also seems to contain food-color, since it tints the water a light peach color.I was curious to try Mango Peach Mio, but I confess it really isn't something I care to repeat. The drink does enhance the water with a semi-fake artificial peach taste, but I confess I prefer my water straight and without the extra fake-flavoring and acid.While the taste was appealing, I don't need the extra chemicals or food dye in my diet, and as the main ingredients are: water and malic acid and contains zero fruit juice, you aren't really getting anything healthy here. I also found the ingredients in this drink mix irritating to my bladder, so those with painful bladder syndrome should be aware this drink contains acid.If you like artificial drinks of the crystal light variety, this might appeal to you.  For me, while the idea was innovative, I would like it to be more healthy to consume and without the food dye and acidity.

column9: Nice Taste In A Handy Format
column10: This is the second flavor of MIO that I've tried. The Peach Tea was good but I think the mango Peach is even better. It tastes like Peach with a slight taste of Mango. There is no need for additional sweetening. It claims that that each glass should get half a teaspoon mixed in but I found that to be too weak. I'll not be getting 24 servings from the container... maybe half that. For the home I see no use for this product but on the road or at work I can see where this would come in very handy. I'll be buying more of this product especially for backpacking. Good for the workplace or a roadtrip too.

Have tried a few different flavors. They were good but I ended up using the bottle in 2 days. Not many "servings" in the tiny eyedrop-like bottle.Try it for yourself ... generally the flavors aren't anything new. Convenience = 5, the whole unit maybe = 3.

I don't like most drinks with artificial sweeteners, so my expectations were not very high for the MIO Mango Peach, which contains Sucralose.  I must say, I was very pleasantly surprised.  When I added it to my filtered water (filtered with 3M Filtrete Water Station it had the thirst-quenching qualities of plain water, and it tasted lightly of real mango and peach.  It didn't taste artificial, and it wasn't too sweet unless I accidentally added too much MIO to my water.  When that happens, I merely add a bit more water.  Because of the Sucralose, I won't buy this often, but I will definitely buy it occasionally.Amazon doesn't list the ingredients.  Here they are:  Water, Malic Acid, Propylene Glycol, Citric Acid, Contains less than 22% of Flavor(s) Natural, Sucralose and Acesulfame Potassium Sweetener, Potassium Citrate, Yellow 5, Yellow 6, Red 40, Potassium Sorbate Preservative.  Definitely not a health drink, but tasty enough that I don't care.

This is a pretty simple complement to water - squirt it in a glass, and it will add some decent flavor to 'normal' water. Quick and easy, and a good product to carry around if you're on the go. If you had it at a restuarant, you could probably do fine with just the water, and the flavoring the MIO provides.I think the 24 drinks per container is a little optimistic. It takes a decent amount to get strong flavor, so if you need your water sweeter, you'll probably go through the containers more quickly than the packaging's estimate. But, if you just need a little flavor, you'd be fine. It's also not instant flavor - you do have to stir it, or give it a minute to settle in.The flavor itself is okay. It does get sweet at the higher doses, but not overwhelmingly. There is no medicine-y taste, like you'd get with some of the cheaper powder drinks. Like another reviewer noted, it's "adult Kool-Aid."

column4: Mrs. K "From the wilds of the Mojave"
column10: This is adult Kool Aid, sans the sugar. But the concept of easily controlling the level of flavor is interesting.The mango peach is okay. The flavor doesn't stand out - it's orange and sweet. I think it needs a little more tart.I wish there was a way to turn up the flavor and turn down the sweetness.

MIO Mango Peach is pretty good, and, unlike other flavors, it's good mixed with water. I was a little surprised, however, at the strong coloring; I don't object to coloring for its own sake, but the redness made the kids ask questions. This is something I'll consider buying again, and I really like the bottles. They're a good size for pocket or purse, and they don't seem to leak or drip.

column9: Really great - though it definitely won't make 24 drinks
column10: The MIO Liquid flavors are really, really good. In fact, they are vastly more flavorful than the many powdered water additives that I have tried. I loved the Mango Peach and tried a coworker's Pomegranate, and fully intend to explore other flavors in the future. But it is simply hogwash that these make 24 drinks. They will if you only want mildly flavored water, but for a fuller flavor you will only be able to make perhaps 16 drinks. This is still a good price for such a convenient way of making something to drink, but perhaps some will feel misled.What I like about this in addition to its taste is that it makes me drink more water. I'm a coke addict. The brown, sugary cola kind. I drink far more cokes than are good for me and they undoubtedly lead to some mild dehydration. If for no other reason than that, I plan on trying out all of the MIO flavors.

I love the MIO products.  They are cute, portable, and really tasty.  The Mango/Peach isn't my favorite flavor, but it's still pretty tasty.  My favorite is the Berry Pomegranate, it's so good!  The absolute best thing about MIO is that it makes me drink a lot more water.  I look forward to my water drinking when it used to be almost a chore.  These little containers hold a lot too!  You'll be happy with this purchase.

column9: MIO Excited To Try - Disappointed In Taste...
column10: I had wanted to try MIO ever since it came out in the Spring of 2011.  Priced it and always passed it up since I found it nowhere on sale and/or no coupons were available. Howsomever, Amazon sent me a sample through the Vine Program so that I could review the product.  I found the taste and aftertaste to be more than a little offputting.  I love mango and I love peach but I tasted no "tea" flavoring in this product.  MIO is such a handy product but if I were the company, I would go back to the drawing board and re-release MIO with hopefully a better taste and outcome. I would not recommend this product since it misses the mark on so many different levels.

I was excited to try this "water enhancer" with the mango peach flavor, as I love mango flavored anything (well almost).  I squirted this Mio Liquid into a glass of cold water and was hoping for the best.  It just tasted like a melted popsicle or similar.  I thought the squirts would be more measured, but they are not, so I don't know how you can know if you got enough flavoring or not.  I squirted a few more squirts into my glass, hoping that I didn't put enough in.  With more flavoring, it wasn't any better.I don't have any, but I wondered if using this stuff in sparkling water would work better.  This flavoring in regular drinking water just doesn't work for me.  I would rather drink plain water than this.  Another scenario that this may or may not work in is the water at Disney World.  The water there tastes like sulfur, and it is something awful.  Don't know if this would mask that taste or not.

In a nutshell: MIO Mango Peach tastes like Crystal Light On The Go Metabolism Plus Green Tea Peach Mango without the little green flecks (or pro-ported benefits of green tea). And somehow, MIO has managed to turn water in to a drink that doesn't make me less thirsty. It's kind of amazing that way.If you enjoy fruity drinks with a strong "diet" aftertaste, you're going to love MIO.

Yikes.  I feel like the odd woman out, but I really did not like the peach mio.  I like the idea of adding as much of it (or as little as I want).  I don't like my flavored water to be too overwhelmingly flavored if that makes sense.  However, the little I used it made it taste like a watered down glass of Koolaid to me.  I tried it again and used more and it still tasted like a watered down drink, but with a bite on the end that was not mango peach flavored.  It was just not very good which is a disappointment.  This little container would have been perfect on the go.

Wow, I have to say, I did not enjoy this drink additive at all.  I've tried several other brands, some I liked some I didn't, but this was my first opportunity to enjoy a MIO, and it didn't speak well for the brand.My biggest problem with this product would probably be the taste.  It's supposed to be mango peach and honestly it didn't taste like either of those things.  The suggested serving is 1 squeeze per 8oz serving so I tried that at first in my water bottle.  It tasted like extremely watered down indeterminate flavored gatorade.  Not so good.  So the next time I amped it up and did 3-4 squeezes into my water bottle.  This time the flavor was stronger but it still didn't taste a thing like mango or peach and actually I felt like I was drinking that sugar water they place in hummingbird feeders.  The color was about the same too come to think of it.  It was kind of disappointing not only for the taste, but for the fact that I needed to use 3x the amount suggested to actually taste anything.  This means there probably won't be the 24 servings it says it has.  Not that I'll probably finish it.The only thing this had going for it was that the ingredients were somewhat natural.  But then they through a bunch of red and yellow dyes to bring that down.  It also has an attractive bottle that it comes in, easy to tote around.  But that only goes so far.  This product is supposed to flavor water and since it fails in that area I can't really recommend it.Review by M. Reynard 2011
I like it, easy to carry,does not taste bad...I checked the internet and propylene glyol is a chemical that is used in a ton of stuff...

column9: Not mango or peach or anything recognizable as such
column10: I tried this in water, and it took a lot more than I expected to be able to get a strong taste. I am accustomed to Crystal Light and was a little surprised that this MIO took so many drops to get the strong taste I wanted. But the more I put in, the sweeter the water became; it seemed to get sweeter a lot faster than the mango taste amplified. I just couldn't drink it.Next I thought maybe it would brighten up my Diet Sprite; well it did make it pretty! But the MIO seemed to fight with the sweetener in the Diet Sprite in a way that created a funky chemical off-tasting residue in my mouth. So dumped that.One last attempt to redeem the MIO: iced tea! How can you mess that up? Easily! Add some MIO! The tea went from delicious, to tasting like someone had dropped perfume into it. I can't even begin to describe what happened when my tea and the MIO mixed; every sip not only smelled like my bath lotion, but it also faintly tasted like maybe the lotion had been dumped into my tea. Just an unpleasant, shudder-giving experience. Dumped that glass.No matter what I mixed the MIO into, it also left a slimy feeling in my mouth, kind of like snails had been living in there awhile.Not a purchase or even a recommendation for me.

This is a great concept, period.  Small container of concentrated flavor that you can add to your drink until you get the flavor profile you want.  Infinite possibilities!  I also like this particular flavor a lot as it doesn't seem "fakey".

.... was the Dr's. command."You can't get enough water !" Next she tells me I'm going to the bathroom too much. Hmmmmmmm.MIO is a great product to carry around in your pocket for every time you buy a bottled water. OPen you water , drink some straight out of the bottle , to make room for the MIO , squirt in how much flavor you want, shake and enjoy.Available in many flavors , the portability of this is the true selling point. Flavor in your pocket.And darn great tasting too !
It gives your water a mild flavor.  The small packaging is very good, handy to carry with you or keep in your desk.  This was fun to try, but I prefer my water straight.

The entire purpose of this product is for it to flavor water and on the commercials they make it look like it will create a drink similar to Crystal Light Peach Tea Drink Mix (12-Quart), 1.5-Ounce Packages (Pack of 4) but in reality it falls very short. We followed the instructions and after adding the proper amount of MIO to the water we tasted it. The flavor was barely detectable so we tried adding more drops. I think we ended up adding three times the required number of drops and still did not have an adequate flavor in the water. Therefore, we can no recommend this product. The only reason we are giving it 2 stars instead of 1 is that we wonder if this problem is with the entire product or just this flavor.

column9: Absolutely Delicious Mix I Won't Be Purchasing
column10: What a great tasting drink mix!  It's by far the best I've ever tried, but I won't be buying or using it because of its ingredients.  Here are the ones that trouble me:1. Propylene glycol is a humidifier used in corexit, anti-freeze, deodorants, and many other products you don't want to eat (although it is approved for use in human and dog foods). Sensitive children may have an allergic reaction to this ingredient.2. Sucralose is an artificial sweetener that combines sugar and chlorine.  Although the manufacturer claims many studies show the safety of Sucralose, I have not been able to locate or read those studies.3. Acesulfame potassium is a sweetener often used in combination with Sucralose.  A 2010 study from Drexel University (find it in PubMed) indicated that safety studies were not sufficient to prove the safety of this ingredient.4. MSG has been given new names, among them "natural flavoring."  Could it be that this mix contains MSG?5. Red and blue dyes tell me that this product is aimed at children, and its great flavor means it will probably be a favorite among youngsters, the ones most likely to show effects from these ingredients.I had hoped that this drink mix would not be a chemical cocktail.  I was wrong.

column9: not for those who like flavor
column10: This is a good product if you can't stand to drink regular water.I'm not sure who doesn't like water, but I can think of several occassions during which I drank wanter that was so unpleasant, that masking it with something equally not pleasant but colorful might've convinced me that I was drinking something satsfactory. For example, when camping or when in Mexico, one is usually faced with the choice of drinking detestable, diarhhea-causing water. During such occassions it's useful to trick one's body to drink the water by adding a product that contains preservatives and dies (yellow-6). A product that in tongue-in-cheek way lists "natural flavor with other natural flavor" on its bottle, and proceeds to list "less than 2% natural flavor" on the back cover in the ingredients list.Still, if you are into coloring your water, this product comes in a BPA-free container that's great for on-the-go -- it is really lightweight and can fit in the palm of your hand, yet is good for 24 cups. According to the directions one quirt of the substance is enough to color 8 oz of water. In fact, the design of the bottle is one of its better selling points - it's very sleek.How does it taste? Like sugar water. To me, regardless of how little or how much I add, it doesn't taste like mango or peach. It's color is very light red, as if you put blood oranges into your cup and diluted them with about 1907897807850 gallons of water.Also, I'm not sure if this is indicative of the brand or amazon, but my bottle has a relatively fast expiration date - February 26, 2011. Moreover, according to the product label, once opened the contents of the MIO bottle should be consumed within a week.

column9: One of my favorite new products!
column10: My Dad is a diabetic so I am always on the lookout for Sugar-Free items that he can enjoy. Mio is now one of those products that our whole family enjoys. It's easy to use, the taste is fantastic, and even the kids think this is cool. You control the amount of product in your drink so everybody can get their desired strength of flavor. I also love the fact that I can take this along in my purse and enjoy it any where I go. So far Sweet Tea is my favorite flavor, but I plan to try all of these.  Thanks Amazon!
I really like the MIO mango peach.  I add it to club soda for a nice light spritzer drink.  The MIO berry has a funny chemically aftertaste but this one is just delicious.  Perfect for summer.

column9: convenient and it tastes good - easy to dispense & no spills
column10: Very convenient for travel; we keep several in the car.  Also great for hiking.  Simply flip the top, tip it over the top of your bottle, and squeeze.  It has a flexible, rubber-type opening which holds the liquid in until you squeeze.  Very easy to use even in a moving vehicle.  No spills!  Variety of flavors available and we like them all.  Do with they had one that was sweet but unflavored, for adding to tea and coffee!  Calorie free.  My kids love them.  The mango peach is one of our favorite flavors, and isn't often found in other similar products.

Both my husband and I liked this product. I didn't notice the artificial sweetener but he did. He still thought it was good and that's saying something. I cannot emphasize how much he hates artificial sweeteners. But he liked this enough that he's planning to buy some for his office at work.Depending on how much of a sweet tooth you have, you might go through this at a different rate. It's very easy to use. You just squirt in your preferred amount of flavor. I did a small glass at first and didn't even have to stir.It has no carbs so it will be great for a low carb diet.
eBay to use mix that is liquid. Allows you to mix the amount you like. True Peach Tea flavor. I add three streams into a water bottle and it tastes great.

I wanted to like MIO. The peach mango taste was disappointing. I tried more concentrated taste, which was only more disappointing; and less, which was faintly disappointing. Other members of my family also tried it, to see if it was just a taste thing I lack, and no one liked it enough to take a second sip. The flavor reminds me of the smell of a sweaty steam sauna.
MIO Mango Peach is a winner as well, I have tried the Sweet tea which is also good. Drinking with MIO flavor liquids makes drinking water so easy for the kids! Great item, no need for the soda.

column9: As good as the Berry Pomegranate flavor
column10: My local grocery has four different flavors of the MIO liquid, but not this flavor. Out of the those that they have, the Berry Pomegranate is the clear winner. (The sweet tea tastes "off", the watermelon is weak, and the Fruit Punch tasted a bit too much like dye.)  So I was eager to try it this one.It came, and the kids and I all had fun trying it...and we all liked it, just as much as the Berry Pomegranate! It's got a nice amount of sweetness, and it's natural-tasting as well.These little things really are nice for those who know they don't drink enough water but who (like me) don't care for the taste of water all that much. I like to keep one in my purse, so if I'm at a fast-food place and I want to be good and avoid soda, I can just ask for a cup of water, then squirt a bit of flavoring into it. These are also great for masking the plastic taste that bottled water all-too-often has.The only reason I don't give them 5 stars is because somehow, if you drink two or three glasses of water with this, or if you squirt too much in, then your mouth can feel slightly dry. I'm not sure why that is, and I don't notice it with just one glass of water.Yum!

Rounding out the (thankfully now expanding) lineup of flavored drink options for those who can't or don't want to go with something sugary comes Mio, which offers a clever twist by giving you control over how strong your drink actually ends up.The Mango Peach flavor is light and refreshing, and isn't an overpowering taste at all.  If anything, the "mango" aspect isn't even very prominent, landing more on the "peach" side. For those who didn't like the Peach Tea flavor, this one has much less of an artificial chemical taste.Because the Mio flavors are liquid instead of powder, it's easier to experiment with different types of drinks.  I've used it in Airborne or similar vitamin C mixes that don't taste great on their own, and it can even work well if you let loose a few drops into a shot of clear liquor like vodka.As with all the other varieties of Mio, your particular mileage may vary depending on how much is used in any given glass of water.  It's not hard to go through the entire bottle quickly if you like a lot of flavoring added, but on the flipside the bottle may lost forever if you only put a few drops in at a time.

column9: Not appealing at all.  Will stick with Crystal Light and Snapple
column10: I am a Crystal Light peach tea fan so I was anxious to try this. My gold standard is Snapple diet peach.  Occasionally they come out with a Mango/Peach which has been excellent.Crystal light relatively closely approximates the Peach version.It seemed like Mio it would be convenient to use.First I had trouble with the packaging.  It was hard to appropriately tear the plastic cover off.  I also had trouble with the directions.  I am 49 and my near vision is going the way most people in their 40s goes... I can't read the directions without finding reading glasses.  Could the manufacturers possibly consider their over-40 customers valuable and print just a little bigger?!My first squirt of the liquid went past the glass.  Ok.  So that will only happen once but..
