They satisfy the craving for sweets, without doing terrible dietary damage, and give us good advice. What other snackfood does that? Oh...and they're yummy!

This is a fun gift to send, 96 individually wrapped La Choy Fortune Cookies with free shipping, hard to beat, and good fortunes inside, I was told.  This is a real stress reliever for an office of people.  Add the words, "between the sheets," after each fortune.

column9: Made the difference on my sugar cookies!
column10: I read on Allrecipes.com that this made sugar cookies taste better than regular vanilla. I used my Aunts tried and true recipe but used this vanilla. I really feel it made them taste a lot richer. I was very happy with the delivery time from the vendor as well.

I found a bottle of this at a discount store, but oh boy, was the flavor priceless. It is great for flavoring merengue, hot chocolate, or even add a dash to strawberries, when you mix them up for topping (strawberries just don't taste as good as they used to). My personal favorite is hot milk with some white-chocolate syrup and a dash of butter vanilla. Even my sister likes this flavoring and wanted to use it in her cupcakes she baked for church.Butter vanilla is my new must-have flavoring. It is a great addition to any baker's cupboard.
Totally replaced my regular vanilla for baking my sugar cookies. Since I have a cookie business, I'm super particular about flavor and value. I'm sold on the Butter Vanilla Emulsion!
I bought this to add to my protein shakes. It makes my shakes taste so great. I love butter flavor and vanilla.
Love the apple cider wish you could get it in stores.  I would drink more but have to order by mail and hate the wait.
This is one of the best hot drinks I have ever had.  Would recommend it highly. Lovely for relaxing - especially in cold weather.

column9: Nice Change for a Hot Drink, With Cinnamon
column10: I was hoping this would taste wonderful on a cold night and it didn't disappoint! I also like that it is a natural mix so there are no harsh chemicals or preservatives. I could happily have one every night, but I save it for a treat!

My wife loves it.  Me not so much.  It's just a taste preference thing.  I think I've been ruined by the apple ciders that are loaded with sugar, so this one tastes a little bland to me.  But it's probably how apple cider is meant to taste.  It smells great though!

This flavor is sooo good.  Light and refreshing... and a great alternative to a morning tea without caffiene.  My daughter loves to take a cup to school with her every morning.  I will definitely keep this in stock!
I really like this k-cup flavor.  Natural is right!  Sure seems fresh and exactly as described...not too sweet, an intense apple flavor with a touch of cinnamon.
I don't know what I expected when you add water to apple you get weak apple.  If you put a cinnamon stick in all you'd taste would be the cinnamon.
This is one of my favorite teas.  The vanilla gives the tea a very smooth taste, it is very enjoyable.

column9: Good veggie replacement when you do not have the time!
column10: Some times you cannot cook vegetables for dinner. This is a great alternative when pressed for time and want quality I sometimes use raemen (sp?) noodles WITHOUT THE SEASONING PACK to add more body! I like it because the salt content is low, and that is why I do not add the noodle seasoing pack. Easy to heat in the microwave.

column9: Dang. I like healthy, but these are NASTY
column10: Man, where's the sugar in this thing? Sugar cane and agave are part of the paleo diet right? Damn, my tastebuds are spoiled by sugar and oil and this just didn't cut it for me. So much for trying to be healthy. I really thought I was eating dirt. I can't even share it with others. No one in my office will touch this snack.  Sorry Caveman team. Not a fan of this one.
The chocolate is not sweetened at all, so I didn't like it.  The berries were very good.  They looked dry and hard, but were soft like raisens.

column9: Five Star Product, One Star Box...
column10: Having used Beyond Gourmet unbleached parchment paper for years, I was unhappy when the price got so high and began purchasing the white parchment which our grocery store carries.  The white parchment was several inches wider than Beyond Gourmet so I often had more waste than when using the unbleached product.  Further, I wasn't particularly happy with it as it tended to scorch more easily than the unbleached, brown paper.  The last drawback for me was that the white paper was not as easy to "mold" into the shape of the pan.When I saw this four-pack of unbleached parchment paper, I decided to give it a try.  Even though each roll held the same square footage of paper, the cost was significantly less than Beyond Gourmet.  I am very pleased with this purchase.  The paper works very well; it is heavy enough to use several times, but flexible enough to be molded easily to the baking pan.  Product releases easily and the paper can be wiped off for more uses.Yes, the box is too flimsy and has no metal cutting edge, but that seems to be a drawback with all unbleached parchment papers.  So, "If You Care" receives five stars for the paper and one star for the box.

column9: Even more useful than regular parchment paper
column10: I originally bought this just because it was cheaper than the regular parchment paper in the grocery store. I was therefore very pleasantly surprised to find out that it's actually much more useful than regular parchment paper.The silicone non-stick coating is no joke. Before I got this, I would often line pans with aluminum foil and spray them with oil to roast peppers, cook frozen samosas, etc. Now, I instead just lay the food on top of a piece of parchment paper, and the non-stick coating makes oil unnecessary. And, this paper is *much* cheaper than aluminum foil.Two things to note: at 13" wide, it's a couple of inches narrower than most regular parchment paper. Also, unlike most grocery store brands, it doesn't have a metal band to help you tear off sheets. (They claim that you can use the cardboard edge to do that, but it doesn't work.) But 13" is plenty for almost everything I do. And using scissors to cut the paper is a small price to pay given how well this paper works.

column9: For cooks who love to COOK!
column10: About 5 years ago I discovered the "secret" to better baking -- parchment paper.  This little kitchen miracle worker makes baking so much easier and healthier.  No more having to grease cookie sheets or clean up the mess from a pecan pie that "bubbled over" when cooking.  A piece of parchment paper does the trick while keeping unecessary fats and calories out of your foods!The one problem with parchment paper is the variety you find in most stores is 1)  Expensive and 2)  bleached with chemicals.  "If You Care" has solved both of those problems in this 4-pack of parchment paper that your kitchen will love (hint:  it also makes a GREAT gift for a friend who is into cooking -- trust me!).  For the price you will pay for 4 boxes of this parchment paper you will get over 8 times as much as you would have gotten in the grocery store!  Plus you can rest easy knowing you aren't harming the environment by using paper that was bleached (can someone tell me what the purpose is to bleaching parchment paper -- it just seems silly!)I can't stop recommending this paper enough.  This is my 4th purchase from Amazon over the years of this exact same paper and while you may think that 4 boxes is a lot -- trust me, it will get used!  Once you discover how much easier it makes cooking you will be using it for everything!

In recent years, parchment paper has become as essential to my cooking supplies as resealable bags and aluminum foil.  I use it to line the bottom of the pan for all kinds of baking - breads, cookies, pizzas, etc. - it's an essential item.  The typical grocery store parchment paper is usually too wide, so there is waste, it is bleached (ugh), and it is not silicon-coated. These other papers use quilon, which isn't as safe and doesn't withstand as high a heat because of the chrome in it (try baking hearth breads at low enough temps for that stuff).  'If You Care' parchment paper IS silicon-coated on both sides and can safely withstand temperatures used in baking hearth breads.  I also like that there is enough (70 square feet) parchment paper in a box of 'If You Care' (compared to 30 square feet of the other - and lots of it wasted, since it's too wide).  Buy the 4-box package of 'If You Care' from Amazon, and you'll save a bundle!So, if I like it so well, why do I give it only four stars?  It's because I have to get my scissors (or a knife) out to cut a piece of it.  The edge of the box (with no cutting strip) will maybe work one or two times for helping tear a straight edge - then it breaks down. Even folding a sharp crease along the tear-line doesn't yield a good tear.  I know the lack of a metal tear-strip is part of the recycling benefit of the packaging, but I wish there was an easier solution than cutting with scissors or a knife.  Still, the product itself is good enough for me to overlook this one flaw.  I wouldn't use anything else.

This parchment paper is unlike any I have ever used before.  Previously, I hated using parchment paper--it seemed to get a funny smell in the oven (like a burned smell), baked goods still stuck to it, etc.  Normally I would use aluminum foil instead, but now try to avoid using aluminum foil for cooking in high heat.  This unbleached parchment paper has been an excellent substitute.  No weird smell, food slides off effortlessly, and as others mentioned, I can use it at least twice before I have to replace it, so less is wasted.  Plus since no chlorine is used, I can feel good about helping the environment in a small way.The only negative is that there is no easy way to tear it out of the box.  You can try to use the edge of the box to tear, but it's an imperfect solution.  I use scissors.  A small hassle overall, really.

This is a wonderful product and I have been using it for several years now.  I usually can get two usages out of each sheet.  I use it to line glass, enameled, and stainless pans, and it works great. I would like to find out how safe the silicon coating really is.  From the research I have done online it seems OK, but if you know of a problem please post.

I use this product mainly to roast garlic for my seasonings business. I love the parchment paper. My only complaint is that it's a bit tough to tear since there is no sharp edge on which to tear the paper. Otherwise, great product!

column9: Good product stuck in a horrible box renders it difficult (at best!) to even use.
column10: I agree with the other reviews--great product.BUT, when the product is packaged in a box so useless, i wont ever buy again.  The parchment is supposed to be ripped along the side of the box.  You know: where other boxes have a jagged edge?  This has NOTHING.  Seriously, they expect you to rip the parchment along the bare edge of the flimsy cardboard box holding it.  It never works...i've had friends and family take shots at it.  So far NO ONE has been able to get a straight tear...So if you get this, be sure to have scissors nearby!  :(
For those who take their baking seriously andprefer the unbleached parchment paper, this isthe real deal. I recommend this product for priceand quality.

column9: nice way to bake+super easy cleanup
column10: Stumbled on to this pan liner while making a last minute stop at a green products store in Seattle. Now after using for everything from tortillas to roasting chicken simply amazed. I thought I had tried out parchment paper until finding this,now rarely use any oil when baking.Just spray off outside edge of items to be baked with a thin oil coating and wallah. Product feel is sturdy,no odd smells from oven at higher heat temps.Just bought a second box today,just love the low or no clean on pans.Bakeware surface life expectancy I can imagine is greatly enhanced too.Says made in Finland on box, fins have been known for their ingenuity in mfg

The parchment paper was purchased for our chef at our Center, and he stated that not only was the price great on the parchment, but baked items do not stick to the parchment like the previous parchments he had used.  He was very well pleased with the product.
This is a very good product and value, it was even better last year when you got 5 rolls for the same price, what happened to deflation?

column9: Great product and price with Subscribe and Save; If you need a cutter edge, simply replace this box with a used saran wrap box
column10: I'm a BIG fan of parchment paper in general (based on all the scares about using commercial cooking sprays, non-stick sheet trays with coating that eventually peels away, microwaving in plastic or saran wrap etc.)and it actually works better than absolutely any other non stick methods out there (including the "non-stick foil"Teflon Non-Stick Foil Sheet, 16" X 24".  And with this brand, if the food you're cooking isn't too wet or messy (e.g., I used it on top of a cookie tray when baking bread), you can use the sheet quite a few times (I know, at .07 a sqr foot, you can splurge and use a fresh sheet each time). This brand of parchment paper also seems sturdier than most others (hence the ability to use a sheet more than once) and it has a slight silicone coating on it that makes it absolutely 100% stick proof.  I've also had no burning whatsoever on the bottom of the bread and I've stopped using commercial spray oils. The coating also makes this a good choice to make food cooking packets for wet foods without making a big mess (I wrap a piece of salmon with yellow and red peppers or a sprig of rosemary with lemon and then fold/seal the packet before cooking in the oven. Perfect! Some liquid does seep through onto the cooking dish, but not a lot. Clean up is a quick rinse with soap and water.Although the parchment paper in a roll form does roll up a bit (as opposed to using the pre-cut flat sheets), I don't really find that to be a big deal (or worth the extra money to buy the pre-cut sheets)....I simply fold about 1/3 of an inch of the paper around the bottom of the tray and it stays put. Also a lot of people complain about a cutter not being on the box...while I do agree it's a bit more work using a scissor or trying to tear the sheet using the cardboard box edge, I get around the problem by simply replacing the original box with a similar sized saran wrap box (or wax paper box etc.) that has the saw tooth cutter edge. Problem solved!

This is the first time I used parchment paper for my baking.  I just love it.  Pastry came off easily and no messing around with grease the pan.  It kind of expensive but worth it.  The only complaint I have is it's hard to cut, the teeth along the box is very dull; it curled up on you and it slided.  My trick is to dab a little of shortening here and there on the baking sheet before putting parchment paper on top.  It worked.

My wife likes to bake cookies now and then, especially for parties and such. She's tried all kinds of ways to get cookies that don't stick to the baking tray. Nothing works completely. Then one day she read in the Martha Stewart Living Magazine, that parchment paper was the thing to use. Parchment paper? I'd never heard of such a thing. Neither had she. Well, I was dispatched to the local supermarket with the instructions to get some. First of all, I had no idea where to look or what to look for. I asked a couple clerks and it baffled them too. Finally. one knew. It was over with the waxed paper and occupied a tiny space on a top shelf. "If You Care" was the brand. "If You Care"? I might expect Betty Crocker or something like that. Anyhow, I brought a 70-foot roll home. My wife reported that it worked perfectly. Not a single cookie stuck. She'd never bake cookies again without parchment paper. That was almost four years ago.Gary Peterson

I was used to the bleached white parchment paper and wasn't sure how the unbleached stuff would perform. Turns out that it's a little heavier than the commercially available stuff, and also coated with silicon. I'm not sure it needs that, since I've never had any kind of sticking problem with plain parchment paper.That said, you can use it several times, as long as it doesn't get oily from whatever you're baking. So it's economical -- I bake at least twice a week and it looks like the three pack will last a year or so.You can tear the paper using the box if you're careful to hold your thumb near the edge so you get a good rip started. It's worth two seconds of extra time to save that blade from going through the waste cycle.So far, I like it, recommend it and will purchase it again.

column9: Another good item to live healthier
column10: I use this paper for a while now and never had a problem with tearing it. I love that it is healthier for my family and I will keep on rebuying as needed. Another great item to get rid of toxins in our life and live healthier.

column9: Best way to bake stuff in the oven!
column10: I don't cook much but I do love to bake my tofu and vegetables, especially when my hubby declares that he won't cook some nights. And I've learned from him not to use aluminum foil so much but to use parchment paper for oven cooking! This item was much cheaper in this packaging than any others at the store and it arrived very quickly. Also this is the best brand of parchment, and it makes cleanup after fact much easier too.

Just received this parchment paper and it is wonderful stuff.  The comments on the box being flimsy is true, but I saved an old parchment box and just transferred it.  I tried tearing the paper the way the directions said on the box and had no problem with it.  I think holding the box firmly and tearing the paper at the correct angle is the key.

While I don't love the paper teeth to rip paper...I do like this parchment and the value for my money. I'm on my third box, and it lasts a good bit longer than Reynolds since you have more length. It's a little annoying to rip the paper, but it works best to tuck the flap inside the box and rip UP, rather than down like you do to tear foil.

Great product, no bleach on my food! Use it to bake, freeze and cover my food. It is a large purchase but I can find it at any of the health food stores in my area so I rather have 2 much than none at all.

I have used this parchment paper for a long time and am very please with it.  I Bake a lot of bread and line my pans with it.  I put the dough to rise on a paper lined rimless baking sheet and when ready to bake, I slide it onto the baking stone, paper and dough together.  I have reused the same sheet over and over.

I have roasted, baked, and decorated with parchment paper.  I have a silpat mat too, but I find that parchment is so much more convenient for cleanup since I just throw it away afterwards.  I also prefer to bake my cookies using parchment instead of silpat for a chewy texture.  An extra plus is that the parchment can be reused if you have more than 1 batch of cookies to bake.This parchment is also great for decorating baked goods.  I've wrapped brownies and cookie bars with strips of this brown parchment paper and tied with twine for a rustic look.Like others have mentioned, there is no easy way to tear the parchment.  You have to use the sawtooth cardboard but otherwise this is what I was looking for at a great price.

I received this parchment just in time for some loaves I was about to bake. Talk about timing! The paper worked perfectly. I particularly like the fact that it is much more environmentally friendly than the grocery store paper I usually purchase. Who needs bleached parchment anyway? Not having a cutting edge on the box might seem inconvenient but we all should have some utility shears in our kitchen anyway. I think it makes the product better. If you have ever cut yourself on one of those boxes you know what I mean.In summary this is a great option for those of us that want a quality and economical product that happens to be a little bit better for the environment. I will purchase again.

column9: BEST parchment paper and eco-friendly, too!
column10: I LOVE this parchment paper. It's so much better than  the typical Reynolds or whatever store brand kind that's white. First, it's longer, so it fits the baking sheets better. Second, it's eco-friendly, made of unbleached paper--who even knows what they put in that other stuff to make it white? Third, it's better at absorbing grease than the other kind. I highly recommend this if you're serious about baking--you won't go back to the el cheapo store brands again!

This is by far the best parchment paper I have used. Previously I was using Reynolds, which is the only brand in most stores, and thought it was working well. It had a tendency to cook on the edges, especially if using it multiple times. While shopping in my coop I decided to splurge on this envrio friendly brand, being at double the cost. I am certainly glad I did because this product Outperforms the Competition in every way. It is even more non-stick, lasts through multiple cooking cycles, is even tougher. With the multiple uses I can make several batches of cookies on the same sheet. In the end I think it will likely end up being cheaper. My next purchase will be the muffins liners. By far and away you will not be disappointed.
excellent product for my Excalibur dehydrator - glad I saw someone's comment about using it...cleanup is easy and I am being green!

I'd become a convert to baking with parchment paper a couple of years ago, and in that time period I've gone through a couple of different rolls - generally just whatever brand was available at the store, none of them being particularly better or worse than the other. Until I decided to try this brand one day. As someone who makes a point to try to shop local & eco-friendly whenever possible, I was really glad to find a more environmentally-friendly parchment paper and really didn't mind paying a little more for it than for the conventional brands. That is, until I used it for the first time. For starters, it's not sized to fit a standard cookie sheet, so to get coverage for a whole pan, you have to use one and a half or two sheets, where the other kinds I've used have just required one sheet to cover the entire pan. Lastly, there's no easy way to tear it - no handy jagged aluminum edge like on most kinds of parchment paper that makes it quick and easy to use. I have no complaints about the quality of the product itself (once I've finally got a patchwork cover made on my cookie sheets), but then I never had a complaint about the conventional brands, either. Really, for me, it's just not wort the hassle. In the future, I'm just going to save myself the frustration and annoyance and just go with the regular kind.

We love this product but the last time we ordered six bottles they sent in very poor packaging and one bottle was broke.  Even after complaints and a request for a new bottle - because it is not a cheap product - we did not get an answer or a replacement bottle!!  It would be really nice for the company to at least reply to complaints!
We've been using this product for years.  The flavor is rich and delicious.  Spicy, but not overwhelming.  I've used it as a condiment, as a glaze and in recipes.  Highly recommended.

These peanuts are marked to be priced 2/$1.00 however Amazon is selling them 108 for $56.47. That's more then 50 cents a pack and you are buying in bulk! Whats up with that Amazon? You would get a better deal going to your local gas station...
I love these peanuts. They are really easy to put into my child's lunch and for me to take to work as a snack. I love that they are packaged because then I won't eat the whole can.

column9: If Costco member, buy from costco
column10: This product is available at Costco (Business Costco) and is a fraction of the price..its about $36 if you buy 6 packs of 18 (1.75 0z) . But nonetheless a good product. Tastes great.
I love the size of the individual packets. Can throw in purse, lunch box or backpack for snack during the day.  Gives high energy, and great taste.
This frosting is great, especially if you want to use black but don't want it to taste bitter.  The only thing I don't understand is the price.  This frosting is $1.50 a tube at Wal-Mart.

column9: Does not dry overnight; thick gel hard to apply evenly
column10: Wilton's Black Sparkle Gel icing looks and tastes good, but the thick gel is difficult to apply evenly.  I used it on sugar cookies to make "ladybug spots and antennae," which worked out fine, but the applicator and thickness of the icing made drawing fine lines (e.g., for piping ladybug "heads") very difficult.But the biggest drawback for me is that this icing does not dry quickly (I left my cookies on a cooling rack for 8 hours overnight, at which point the icing was still wet.  After putting the cookies in the oven for 10 minutes at 200 deg. F, and cooling them, the icing was less wet, but still tacky and not ready for bagging.)  I have since read from reviewers elsewhere that this icing takes 2 to 3 days to dry.  It would've been helpful to see this noted on the packaging.  I would not recommend this for decorating cookies; after 2 to 3 days for drying, your baked goods will have lost much of their freshness.

column4: J. Smith "Just let me finish this chapter...."
column9: Why make black icing at home?
column10: I hate making black icing at home, there's always an after taste from the food coloring and it ends up being a big mess. The Wilton tubes of black icing are great for frozen buttercream transfers when I decorate a birthday cake and much easier to handle.
I started making fondant cakes a few months ago.  This works great for the finishing touches to the cakes without having to mix up your own colored frosting, which saves a ton of time!

Another top brand began tasting funky long before oil spills, so I've used only Bumble Bee for years. With the best reputation, they dont even seem to advertise-best tasting tuna that can be used for salad or in any recipe requiring tuna fish. Amazon's case sale price made this a no brainer purchase. Thanks Amazon!!

What ever happen to TUNA in the can. SOLID use to mean SOLID. WHITE use to mean WHITE. The cans are smaller the price is more expensive. My biggest complaint is the ADDITIVES. Soy proteins or something has been added, you can't just drain the water off anymore. You have to rinse and rinse and when you done you have a miserable mess of NOT SOLID, NOT VERY WHITE tuna. This brand is not as bad as COS or STARKIST. I am going to try a natural Tongol tuna next time. A little more expensive but ......... hopefully better that this.
Great tuna, great price...doesn't smell fishy like some other brands! Love it! Fast delivery to your door! Five stars from me!
Second time I have ordered this.  About 1/3 of the cans arrived dented.  Amazon will not allow returns.  Stuck with damages and no way to get credit.

column4: The Best Music Ain't on the Radio
column10: Same exact tuna that I buy in the store.  Even though it's labeled "solid white", sometimes when I open the can it looks more like chunk white, but that's a problem I have whether I buy cans from Amazon or my local supermarket, and whether I buy Bumble Bee or Starkist (although I find Bumble Bee is much better at delivering the stated "solid white" than Starkist).  So whether to buy online from Amazon is just simple math.When I bought on 5/18/12 these were the prices:24 pack for $30.72 = $1.28 per can (and no sales tax).Or with subscribe and save it's $26.11 = $1.09 per can (and no sales tax).Now I'm looking on 5/29/12 and the price has jumped:24 pack for $35.76 = $1.49 per can (and no sales tax).Or with subscribe and save it's $30.40 = $1.27 per can (and no sales tax).*Update, price on 7/9/12 down to $30.48 (or 25.91 with subscribe and save), but price on 8/2 went up to 35.76 (or 30.40 with subscribe and save). Price may fluctuate, so just got to watch it.I've ordered this twice from Amazon, both times at much cheaper prices then what I normally pay at the supermarket.  Both times, none of the cans came dented, all were in perfect condition, just like what I get at the store.My family eats a lot of tuna, and since tuna takes years to go bad, buying in bulk from Amazon can be a good deal as long as the price is cheaper than what I get at the local supermarkets (where I live, I typically see Bumble Bee Solid White for $1.55 to $1.89).Just do the math and you'll know if this is a good deal for you or not.

This product should not be allowed to be labeled "Solid" in fact is doesn't even resemble what is sold as chunk tuna in other brands.  This is not my usual brand, I was shocked when I opened the can!  First off if you shook the can it sounded like it was full of water.  The tuna didn't even resemble tuna it looked like a wet mess. I had trouble touching it.  Bumble Bee should be made to mark this for what it is.  Check out Three Diamonds Solid and  you will see what solid tuna should look like.

Every time I've had Bumblebee tuna in the past, it's been pretty awful.  Lots of the 'mud line' (red muscle) included and very few *solid* chunks.  I went to the local grocery store and picked up a single can of this (Albacore) by Bumblebee thinking their Albacore should be better and it was the cheapest at the store. The American Stockyard line is handcrafted using all-natural ingredients, premium spices, and no high fructose corn syrup, and it's gluten-free.KC Pitmaster- This sweet sauce has a heavy dose of dark brown cane sugar with a hint of tangy mustard and a touch of spice. Brush it on your ribs or drizzle it on your brisket in the last few minutes of cooking time and you will have your own secret BBQ weapon.Harvest Apple- This unique sauce is a creative blend of tart Washington apples, brown sugar and a special blend of spices, a perfect complement to any BBQ meal.Memphis Red- In Memphis and places further East, they prefer their sauce to be plenty tangy but also just a little sweet and spicy. This sauce combines apple cider vinegar, pure cane sugar and a special blend of spices to give you the right combination for your pulled pork or just about anything that goes on a BBQ grill.Red Raspberries- Sweet red raspberries from America's northwest, bbq spices, honey and a touch of smokey chipotle peppers to bring you this unique sauce that is perfect for chicken, beef or pork.Smoky Mustard- More than 250 years ago, German immigrants settled in present day South Carolina and introduced their version of BBQ sauce to a hungry nation. There are no tomatoes in this sauce. Instead you will find premium whole grain mustard, tangy yellow mustard, brown sugar and a touch of hickory smoke. This sauce pairs perfectly with pork and is also outstanding with beef or chicken.Smoky Sweet- Kansas City was home to some of the largest stockyards in the country and has a well-earned reputation as one of the premier BBQ cities in the world. This sauce exemplifies the sweet, spicy, and smoky tomato-based sauces that Kansas City is known for. From ribs to chicken, brisket to burnt ends, you will not run out of uses for this versatile sauce.Southern Blues- This sauce is as sweet and sultry as its namesake musical style. Slather some of this sauce on some ribs and watch it glaze to perfection on the grill. Brown sugar, apple cider vinegar and more than 20 spices and seasonings combine to create championship BBQ flavor that you can enjoy at home.

I've only tried the Southern Blues and it was amazing on Ribs. I have to say this was THE best BBQ sauce I've ever had to date. I wish Amazon starting selling this brand because it is very hard to find locally.

My kids were so excited to get their favorite suckers in the mail!My son wanted me to separate out the cherry lollipops for him, so I started to sort the candy by flavor. To my dismay, only a few were cherry (10/157 in canister #1, 6/155 in canister #2). The majority of the lollipops were watermelon (61/157 in canister #1 and 47/155 in canister #2). Unfortunately, this is the one flavor that nobody in my family likes.By my calculations, with 8 flavors in a 150 item canister, there should be approximately 19 (about 12%) of each flavor. I understand that these candies are probably packed mechanically, so the numbers will not be exact. However, one of the canisters was 39% watermelon flavor, which to me is not acceptable.The three star rating is for the uneven flavor assortment. The flavor I give five stars.

column9: Flavors you receive may be different than product description!
column10: This review is for the YummyEarth Organic Lollipops, Assorted Flavors, 30-Ounce Container.I'm only giving this a one-star, bad review until they change this description and get it right. Beware before you buy! I've been ordering these lollipops for 2 years now, and I LOVE them, I totally recommend them actually, but I am annoyed that the current item description vs. what you will receive in the mail IS DIFFERENT. How hard is it for someone to update this thing correctly? Someone's lazy or dropping the ball.Under *Product Features* it reads, "Mix of Sour Apple Tart, Pomegranate Pucker, Mango Tango, TooBerry Blueberry, Googly Grape, Strawberry Smash, Very Very Cherry, Wet-Face Watermelon".Then, under *Product Description* it reads at the beginning of the paragraph, "Includes: Pomegranate Pucker, Razzmatazz Berry, Cheeky Lemon, Orange Squeeze, Wet-Face Watermelon" and ends the paragraph again with, "Mix of Sour Apple Tart, Pomegranate Pucker, Mango Tango, TooBerry Blueberry, Googly Grape, Strawberry Smash, Very Very Cherry, Wet-Face Watermelon".  ???  So which is it??VERY confusing. Now, if you don't care what flavors you get, say you're just giving these away as Halloween candy, order away. But if you're like me, I look forward to having at least some certain flavors for myself and so I'm annoyed when what I'm expecting isn't what I get.I also used to be annoyed that the ratios of the variety mix were VERY uneven, you'd get like one apple and 25 blueberry lollipops (the worst flavor in my opinion), but they claim to be changing that. And apparently it depends on WHO you buy them from (yummy earth or a 3rd party vendor thru Amazon). I don't think product consistency and an accurate description, no matter who you buy it from, is too much to ask!This is also happening in the Vitamin C 30 oz container of pops as well. I ordered what I thought was the usual variety mix it claimed to be, and it arrived with now only having blueberry, razzmataz berry, and very cherry. Lame! Just get the desciption right and be consistent. It's not fair to order and pay for something you expect to get and then get something else. It's a hassle to complain, call customer service, write this stupid review, etc. and waste everyone's time. I'm only writing this to warn you and save someone else the trouble, and also get the description fixed.I personally think the best flavors are apple, strawberry and watermelon and I give the rest away. These have been my Halloween candy for three years now and are a big hit. But if this inconsistency continues I'm going to move on to some other natural/organic candy.
